author: Esperanza
title: Entrevista a Martin Curiche, Camila Huaracan y Sofía Dietz: Operación Huracán, a 9 años aún no hay justicia
content:
Para este registro, nos reunimos con Martin Curiche ex-preso político mapuche incriminado en el montaje de la llamada «Operación Huracán 1» en septiembre de 2017, junto a otros siete dirigentes mapuche y no mapuche, mediante una serie de pruebas falsas implantadas y manipuladas por Carabineros y un civil.


«Cuando se dio toda la operación fue por un tema específico, por dos temas en este caso: estaba el juicio

Luchsinger Mackay

 y a la vez, el

Caso Inglesia

. Fue en ese entonces cuando nos reunimos amigos, pu lamngen y familiares de los presos y decidimos que podiamos hacer algo, podíamos romper ese círculo mediático que la prensa no estaba dando, en conjunto con una red de secundarios y la red de apoyo infantil. El dia 100 de huelga de hambre, porque los peñis del caso inglesia para poder anular un tema que era la asociación ilícita, nosotros empemos a hacer movilizaciones y decidimos levantar un punto de reunión permanente a las afueras de la cárcel». Relata Martin.


El dia 23 de septiembre de 2017, luego de producirse un segundo desalojo en el punto de reunión fuera de la cárcel, Martín Curiche es detenido bajo una orden emanada por el Tribunal de Temuco.


Curiche fue acusado de «asociación ilícita,incendio territorista y de estar en un supuesto grupo de WhastApp donde se comunicaban para comenter ciertos detilos». Imputaciones que finalmente fueron desacreditadas al quedar al descubierto la implantación de pruebas falsas por parte de funcionarios y altos mandos de Carabineros con el apoyo de un civil.


Han pasado 9 años desde la Operación Huracán 1 y Martin, cuenta que hasta la actualidad existen recupercusiones. La exposición mediática y el papel de las grandes cadenas nacionales de comunicación influyeron en la opinión pública de manera negativa.


«Cuando ya se descubre que fue un montaje de todo, el tema de buscar trabajo se vio difícil… (9 años después) Pensando que ese tema estaba zanjado hasta la fecha sigue con réplicas. Cuánto tiempo más tiene que pasar para que eso se borre del expediente de uno, del curriculum en este caso, porque es lo primero que se muestra cuando uno postula a un trabajo».


El otorno familiar y de la comunidad también ha quedado marcada, dice Martin «se empieaza a ver más visitas de carabineros en ese tiempo, para mi zona era escaso ese tema pero después que sucedió eso, la visita de carabineros en el territorio fue excesiva en ese período que duró la famosa Operación Huracán».


Camila Huaracan, una de las abogadas de Martin, quienes actualmente están el en juicio «Operación Huracán 2» como querellantes, comenta:


«trabajamos en el mayor fraude procesal sistemático en el cual se pudo acreditar que los altos mandos realizaron obstrucción a la investigación, también falcificación de prueba y esto netamente, fue perpetrado por altas esferas de Carabineros de Chile, a través de la dirección de inteligencia de la Dipolcar y también de Uioe; Unidad de Inteligencia Operativa Especializada».


Las representantes en este juicio donde Curiche, ahora en calidad de víctima, se refieren al grave hecho de cómo altos mandos de carabineros actuaron para encarcelar injustamente a dirigentes mapuche y la lentitud para encontrar justicia. «Vemos con preocupación cómo ha existido, un obstáculo para acceder a la justicia… vemos cómo acá se ha retrasado a tal punto de que ocurrieron casi 7, 8 años para que recién se comenzara la preparación de juicio oral y ahora vamos a los 10 años y tenemos una sentencia condenatoria en pimera instancia, pero aún así tampoco se condenaron a todos los carabineros…»

«Por ejemplo el General Blu, el capitán Marín o también Teuber, que ellos participaron en estos montajes, no van a ir a la cárcel, van a estar con libertad vigilada y a muchos de ellos igual se les abonó todo el tiempo que estuvieron en medida cautelar… Vemos que la justicia sí funciona de manera distintas cuando los imputados o las víctimas son mapuche o son altos mandos de Carabineros. author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Sastre sin fumigaciones: “Lo que debería venir es la agroecología para las futuras generaciones”
content:
Por Mariángeles Guerrero


Desde Santa Fe


Siete líneas en una hoja membretada de la Corte Suprema de la Nación pusieron punto final a la batalla judicial que emprendieron, en 2018, vecinas y vecinos de la localidad de Sastre y Ortíz (Santa Fe). Los jueces Horacio Rosatti y Carlos Rosenkrantz desestimaron un reclamo de la municipalidad y convalidaron la decisión que ya había tomado la Corte santafesina: se deben establecer mil metros de distancia para las fumigaciones terrestres en relación a toda esa ciudad. El ministro Ricardo Lorenzetti se excusó de intervenir. Tras conocer el fallo, Sonia González, una de las impulsoras de la causa, pide: “Que no se dude ante la salud”. Asegura que ahora irán por la reforma de la ordenanza local, de acuerdo a lo establecido en los sucesivos fallos favorables que tuvo el expediente.


Sastre y Ortiz es una ciudad de 6.000 habitantes ubicada en el sudoeste santafesino, zona núcleo del agronegocio. A lo largo de la provincia, pueblos y ciudades conviven a diario con las avionetas y los mosquitos. Santa Fe cuenta con una ley obsoleta, que data de 1995, cuando aún no se había aprobado la soja transgénica en Argentina. La soja modificada genéticamente implicó un mayor avance de la frontera agrícola y un mayor uso de herbicidas, principalmente el glifosato. Pese a urgir una actualización, la Legislatura provincial cajoneó varios proyectos de reforma impulsados desde 2010 por organizaciones socioambientales.


En 2018, Zoe Giraudo tenía dos años y un diagnóstico: linfoma linfoblástico tipo T. Estaba internada en Rosario pero, al momento de poder regresar a su casa para continuar los tratamientos de quimioterapia desde allí, los médicos advirtieron a la familia: no podía estar cerca de los venenos. En la localidad ya se venían reuniendo vecinos para intentar que el Concejo local y de que la intendenta, María del Carme Amero, tome alguna medida preventiva ante los mosquitos que fumigaban a menos de cien metros de las viviendas. A fin de ese año se presentó el amparo colectivo que ahora concluyó en la última etapa procesal posible con una nueva sentencia a favor.


La demanda se presentó contra la Municipalidad tras varios intentos de diálogo con el Ejecutivo y el Concejo para que se reformara la Ordenanza Municipal 951/2004, que fijaba el límite de fumigación a solo cien metros a partir de la finalización del área urbana. En el juicio se presentaron como terceros interesados la provincia y una decena de productores. Si bien en 2020 el juez Francisco Hail, de Rafaela, dio la razón a los vecinos, la municipalidad apeló. Y siguió apelando hasta llegar a la Corte Nacional.


Desde la Capital Federal se puso fin al litigio alegando que el último recurso de queja presentado por la Municipalidad de Sastre carece de “fundamentación autónoma”. Cuando refiere a esta falencia, el máximo tribunal indica que una queja determinada no cuenta con un relato prolijo de los hechos y una crítica ordenada al fallo que se busca impugnar. En este caso, el de la Corte de Santa Fe.


El fruto de la lucha colectiva


En el contexto de una provincia donde se plantea la tensión entre salud y modelo productivo y se priorizan los intereses de los grupos concentrados que están detrás del glifosato, de los transgénicos y del monocultivo de commodities, vecinas y vecinos iniciaron un camino que no abandonaron. Y lograron un fallo que ahora implica un precedente relevante para las localidades de Santa Fe y para otros pueblos fumigados del país. Hoy Zoe Giraudo tiene 10 años y su mamá siente que, con esta resolución, deja de cargar una mochila que llevó por años. “Estamos orgullosos como grupo y yo como mamá, porque siento que hice un montón por mi hija”, dice González.


—¿Cómo comenzó la movilización en Sastre?

—La lucha de los vecinos empezó hace muchísimo tiempo, porque había muy pocos vecinos que estaban tratando de alejar estos venenos que ya se sabía que hacían mal. En 2018, una vecina que vive a una cuadra vio un mosquito que estaba fumigando a 70 metros de su casa. Y coincidió con el tiempo en que yo tenía a Zoe, mi nena, internada en Rosario. Esa vecina empezó a buscar soluciones: yendo a la municipalidad, a juntar firmas, a levantar publicaciones en las redes. Zoe se estaba atendiendo con los mejores médicos, pero al final no tenía resguardo con respecto a los venenos. Ellos se juntaron como vecinos, juntaron firmas, fueron al Concejo Municipal y nada. No hubo soluciones. Eso pasó en marzo. Los vecinos …

title: Comunicado público ppm Caso Grollmus
content:
Frente a las exuberantes condenas y tras un viciado proceso declaramos:

Mari mari pu machi, pu lonko, pu werken, kom pu che. El día de hoy nos dirigimos a la sociedad en general, a todos y todas quienes nos han brindado su apoyo y respaldo en este proceso denominado “Caso Grollmus”.

Actualmente a nosotros como comuneros mapuche se nos ha condenado a penas que marcarán un precedente como obscenamente políticas, se nos condena por decisión política, por ser mapuche que vivimos y recuperamos nuestro territorio.

Tras el gigantesco despliegue comunicacional, y tras el espectáculo montado por el Ministerio Público y la PDI, la familia Grollmus demanda al estado en busca de indemnizaciones y reparaciones.

La fiscalía con el aval del tribunal logró su objetivo: condenar a una pena que ponderada resulta en 1055 años de prisión contra nosotros. La prensa vociferó la sentencia y el poder político respaldo, claridad absoluta.

Les decimos, su ocupación contra nuestro pueblo y su territorio apenas tiene 143 años. Nuestro pueblo resistió al imperio español casi 300 años.

Hoy Chile soberbio y republicano nos condena a más de 1000 años. Por el único motivo de luchar por nuestra soberanía, por nuestro buen vivir y dignidad. Lo anterior tendrá la más necesaria respuesta: continuar con el legado de nuestro pueblo, luchar por nuestra dignidad y libertad.

Los Grupos de Tarea y la BIPE de la PDI recorren los penales de forma morbosa buscando testigos a quienes poner corbata de protegido y sin rostro. Sólo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos” se dictó sentencia y veredicto. Nuestro territorio se militariza y vuelven a saquear nuestros recursos naturales, vuelven las concesiones mineras, CMPC y Mininco cual mecenas entregan dinero y donaciones a Postas y Escuelas.

Queremos manifestar nuestro agradecimiento por todo el respaldo de nuestros hermanos y hermanas en otros territorios y ciudades. No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso.

Nos movilizaremos por nuestra libertad y juicio justo.

Finalmente los invitamos a sumarse a la próxima movilización articulada en distintos territorios para este 12 de octubre, Día de la resistencia de nuestros pueblos.

¡NULIDAD Y LIBERTAD! ¡NO MÁS TESTIGOS PROTEGIDOS! ¡UNIDAD EN EL WEYCHAN! ¡LIBERTAD A TODOS LOS PRESOS POLÍTICOS MAPUCHE!

Presos Políticos Mapuche del Caso Grollmus de la Franja Lavkenche, CP Biobio, CERECO Coronel, Cárcel Llancahue de Valdivia.

title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

title: Two young Kurdish women athletes arrested by Iranian forces in Saqqez
content:
Iranian forces have arrested two young Kurdish women athletes, Rojan Ebrahimi and Aida Ghaderi, in Saqqez, Kurdistan Province, in recent days.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Ghaderi, a swimming coach, was arrested on 4 October after forces from the Ministry of Intelligence raided her family home in Saqqez without presenting a warrant.


Ebrahimi, an MMA athlete from Saqqez, was arrested a day earlier, on 3 October, after Ministry of Intelligence forces raided her family home.


Both arrests were carried out without warrants.


Any charges against the two women, as well as their current whereabouts and status, remain unknown.

title: ‘We can’t report anything against AP govt’: National media silent on Tirumala Tirupati controversy after ED and CBI probes debunk false claims of ‘beef tallow’ use
content:
In a press release on 17 September 2026, eight months after the Supreme Court-appointed CBI Special Investigation Team (SIT) explicitly ruled out the presence of animal fats in the ghee used for manufacturing the Tirumala Tirupati temple’s prasadam, the Enforcement Directorate has arrested a promoter of a private food company allegedly involved in contamination after lab forensic analysis revealed the presence of seven adulterants. Notably, none of them are animal fats, specifically ‘beef tallow’, the allegation of whose presence triggered outrage and investigation in the first place, and cemented a political upset in the state by amplifying communal tensions.


 


by

 Mouli Sharma


 


On 19 September 2024, Andhra Pradesh’s Tirumala Tirupati temple had taken over national and regional news by storm for an unsavoury reason: an allegation of the presence of animal fats in the temple’s

prasadam

 (consumable offerings to Hindu deities given as blessed alms to devotees), specifically the accusation that ‘beef tallow’ was used in the rendering of adulterated ghee used to make the temple’s laddus. Unverified accounts of ‘lab reports confirming the allegations’, which were amplified by TDP’s CM Chandrababu Naidu himself, eventually led to an FIR about the same being registered on 25 September 2024, followed by a PIL being filed in the Supreme Court by one Dr. Subramanian Swamy.


Over a year later, the allegations were debunked by a Special Investigative Team constituted by the CBI to investigate the case, whose forensic examination categorically ruled out the use of animal fats, though the presence of synthetic adulterants was confirmed.


On 17 September 2026, almost exactly two years later, the enforcement directorate reproduced the same findings. Seven adulterants were listed in an ED press release announcing the arrest of a food promoter allegedly involved in multi-crore transactions behind the procurement of the adulterated ghee—Refined Palm Oil, Palm Kernel Oil, Palmolein, MG-90, Monoglycerides, Myvacet Soft 400 and Acetic Acid Ester—none of which are animal fats of any kind, let alone fats of particularly polarising animals, like cows.


 


On 17 September 2026, almost exactly two years later, the enforcement directorate reproduced the same findings. Seven adulterants were listed in an ED press release announcing the arrest of a food promoter allegedly involved in multi-crore transactions behind the procurement of the adulterated ghee—Refined Palm Oil, Palm Kernel Oil, Palmolein, MG-90, Monoglycerides, Myvacet Soft 400 and Acetic Acid Ester—none of which are animal fats of any kind, let alone fats of particularly polarising animals, like cows.


In the light of both revelations, the dozens of mainstream media outlets across the country who expounded the now debunked claims without any evidence of their legitimacy back when the controversy had first surfaced, fanning communal sentiments within the country’s dominant caste-Hindu population, triggering a rise in hate speech, and cementing the popularity of the then newly elected NDA government in the state, have remained conspicuously silent.


“Unfortunately, we cannot use any news content against the AP government. I cannot say more than that,” he said.


Major newspaper outlets with the largest circulation rates in India; channels with the highest viewership statistics, and websites at the top of Search Engine Optimisation and provenance score rankings—The Times Group, The Express Group, Firstpost, The Hindu, Dainik Bhaskar, NDTV, and many more—all solicit their newsdesk items from this agency. This is possibly why the only visible headlines currently in the public domain that acknowledge this debunking, are the opposition party’s own social media posts, and an article by The News Minute, an independent alternate online news portal focusing on the South.


 


A noteworthy aspect of the entire controversy was that the allegations, from the outset, were being made in retrospect. Though the Telugu Desam Party had already come to power by the time the FIR was registered, with Naidu having replaced YSRCP’s Jagan Mohan Reddy (who was then targeted for his Christian identity) during the Legislative Assembly elections in May 2024, the complainant made it clear that his accusations were about procurements made during the preceding government’s tenure.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Recent Incidents Highlight Chinese Transnational Repression in Taiwan
content:
A NUMBER OF recent incidents illustrate new tactics in China’s playbook for transnational repression.

For one, a comedy club in Taipei–known as Comedy Club or Comedy Plus +–had its entrance smeared with a mixture of feces and white paint. It is thought that this occurred due to performances by comedian Huang Yi-hao. Huang previously mocked Chinese president Xi Jinping during a stand-up routine in December 2025, clips of which recently went viral online.

A 35-year-old man surnamed Kuo was reportedly paid 50,000 NT by a 33-year-old man surnamed Liu to carry out the attack. It is unclear whether the two were acting at China’s behest.

Past similar incidents include when Hong Kong pro-democracy singer Denise Ho and bookstore owner and publisher Lam Wing-kee, one of the Causeway Bay booksellers, were splashed with red paint by attackers. Some of these attackers were linked to Taiwanese pro-China organized crime groups such as the Bamboo Union gang.

Likewise, Aegis, a restaurant that assisted Hongkongers seeking refuge in Taiwan, and a gym owned by a pro-democracy Hongkonger who had previously stood as an electoral candidate, had faced similar incidents. Aegis was splashed with chicken feces by men who were paid by a Chinese national to carry out the act.

The gym in question was splashed with red paint by two individuals who arrived from Hong Kong. The two individuals departed back to Hong Kong before they could be caught.

Nor would this be the only case in which China has apparently flown individuals to Taiwan to carry out actions that they try to quickly flee from in short order. This was also the case when political commentator Akio Yaita was attacked in a Taichung hotel where Yaita was giving a speech, with the individual in question having been flown in for the attack from Hong Kong, and subsequently attempting to flee abroad. The use of Taiwanese and Hongkongers, or Chinese nationals with Hong Kong passports, for such attacks, however, allows for plausible deniability that avoids being directly traced back to the Chinese government.

Still, the attack serves as a reminder of what Taiwan stands to lose if it were to fall under Chinese control. Even the simple act of mocking one’s political leaders in a comedy show could lead to violent reprisals.

To this extent, reports indicate that cases of Chinese impersonation seem to be on the rise. The distributor of the documentary State Organs, which details Chinese organ harvesting of members of the Falun Gong, has reported cases of individuals attempting to pose as him to carry out threats using his phone number. Kuan Chien-chung is the head of Lion Movies Culture Company. This seems to follow up on preceding reports of individuals connected to civil society groups receiving suspicious e-mails with interview requests from people that they were often already connected to.

author: rti_admin
title: The Algorithm of the Ballot: How Data Decides Democracy Before We Vote
content:
Elections used to be loud. Street-corner rallies, hoarse loudspeakers, campaigners going door to door, entire neighbourhoods gathered around a television for the evening debate. That version of democracy is dying, and most of us haven’t quite noticed the funeral. The real contest now happens somewhere quieter — inside a smartphone screen, in the space between a thumb and a feed. Political persuasion doesn’t shout at crowds anymore. It whispers to individuals, one at a time, and the whisper has been tested, refined, and timed with a precision no rally could ever match.

This isn’t speculation about some AI-run future. It’s already part of how political communication works in India and elsewhere with widespread mobile internet access.

Campaigns describe their own methods as “smart” and “surgical,” and for once the marketing language is accurate. Nobody is addressing an anonymous mass anymore. Every voter is a profile being built in real time — every scroll, every pause, every like or skip can become another data point feeding a model of who you are and what might move you. Linger two seconds longer on a video about unemployment, and your feed may begin showing you more content like it, each one worded slightly differently, until what started as manufactured content starts to feel like your own settled opinion.

What makes this so effective is precisely that it doesn’t feel like anything is being done to you. A curated feed never announces itself as curated. It just feels instinctual — as if the device has learned to think alongside you rather than manipulate you. Two people can work in the same office, live in the same city, share the same friend group, and still inhabit completely different informational worlds. One sees hope where the other sees decline. One sees progress where the other sees collapse. The algorithm isn’t necessarily lying to either of them. It’s simply reflecting their inclinations at them, amplified, until the reflection becomes impossible to distinguish from the self that’s supposedly thinking.

Try this yourself, and it gets uncomfortable fast: spend one full day deliberately engaging with the opposite side of your politics. Like the arguments you find weak. Click into the topics you usually scroll past. Within hours, your feed may begin to recalibrate. The old version — the one that felt so personal, so obviously true — can start to look different, as if it never existed. That should bother you more than it probably does. If a belief can be reshaped in an afternoon just by changing what you click, how solid was it to begin with? Political conviction, it turns out, isn’t always bedrock. Often it’s just a data point that hasn’t been nudged yet.

A Global Infrastructure of Influence

None of this is a local phenomenon. In the United States, campaigns use predictive modelling, experimentation, and targeted advertising to identify voters and test which messages are more persuasive. In China, the digital infrastructure is subject to extensive state regulation, including rules governing algorithmic recommendations and the presentation of information. In the European Union, regulators have moved beyond drafting rules: new regulations governing the transparency and targeting of political advertising became fully applicable in October 2025, imposing significant restrictions on the use of personal data for political targeting.

Different governments, different justifications, same underlying playbook. None of it necessarily depends on coercion, because coercion is visible, and visible things get resisted. The real method can be subtler: build the environment so precisely that a person mistakes the nudge for their own free judgment. Nobody feels manipulated when they’re convinced the idea was theirs all along.

There’s a specific kind of unease in standing inside a polling booth and asking yourself a plain question: was this decision actually made here, in this moment of privacy — or weeks ago, in a server room, by a system that had already modelled the outcome? When results appear close to pre-poll forecasts, “good analytics” is one explanation. Successful engineering is another. At a certain level of precision, the two can start to look identical.

This matters more, not less, in a country as vast and unequal as India. Behavioural targeting doesn’t treat every citizen the same way. Voters with less digital literacy, fewer alternative sources of information, or less social capital to question what their …

title: Labnotes | Ang kontradiksyon ng renewable energy transition sa Pilipinas
content:
The 54MW Pililla Wind Power Project in Pililla, Rizal is operated by Vena Energy. Photo by Chantal Eco

Sa kalagitnaan ng krisis sa klima, ibinibida ng gobyerno at ng mga malalakihang korporasyon ang transition sa renewable energy bilang solusyon — na ang mga solar, wind farm, at iba pa ay susi sa mura’t malinis na enerhiya. Pero habang kinakalbo ang mga kabundukan para itayo ang wind turbines, solar panels, at mga dambuhalang dams, ang bill ng kuryente—palagi pang tumataas!

Ang mga dapat itanong: sino ang may-ari ng mga planta, sinu-sino ang may kontrol ng transmisyon at distribusyon, at para saan ba talaga ang Electric Power Industry Reform Act o EPIRA?

Patuloy ang pagdami ng mga wind at solar farm sa Pilipinas. Noong 2022, 1,530 megawatt (MW) na kuryente ang mula sa solar, at nadoble ito noong 2025 sa 3,003 MW. Umaabot na ngayon sa 3,892 MW (3.9 GW) ang kapasidad mula sa solar, habang ang wind farm o kuryenteng mula sa hangin ay nananatili sa 427 MW lamang.

Sinasabing malinis at mas mura ang kuryenteng nagmumula sa modernong teknolohiyang Renewable Energy (RE) tulad ng solar at wind farm. Ang RE ay teknolohiyang gumagamit ng mga likas na yamang halos di-nauubos tulad ng araw, hangin, at tubig. Mahigit 22 porsyento ng kuryente sa bansa ang galing sa RE — nagmumula ito sa geothermal plants (9.1%), hydroelectric dams (8.7%), solar farm (2.2%), wind farm (1.1%), at iba pang planta ng enerhiyang hindi umaasa sa petrolyong rekurso.

Sinasabi na kapag nagtayo ka ng RE tulad ng solar farm, ito ay mas mura kaysa sa paggamit ng coal power plant na karaniwang itinatayo ngayon ng mga pribadong korporasyon sa enerhiya. Nasa P2.99 kada kilowatt-oras (kWh) lamang ang gastos sa kuryente kapag solar ang gamit, habang PHP3.50/kWh naman kapag hangin ang gamit. Malaking mura ito kumpara sa paggamit ng karbon o coal na may presyong PHP3.80–5.50/kWh, o sa imported na diesel na umaabot sa PHP15–28/kWh. (Tingnan ang Talahanayan 2.) Hindi na rin bumibili ng panggatong tulad ng langis, diesel, o coal ang mga pribadong kumpanya upang paganahin ang kanilang mga planta, dahil tuloy-tuloy at libre ang suplay ng rekurso tulad ng hangin at araw.

Kung kaya ito ang paborito ngayon ng gobyerno at ng mga monopolyong korporasyon sa enerhiya tulad ng MERALCO at First Gen ni Manny Pangilinan, ng Aboitiz Power ng mga Aboitiz, San Miguel Global Power ni Ramon Ang, Prime Infrastructure ni Enrique Razon, at ACEN ng mga Ayala. Sinasabi ng mga korporasyon na magpapababa ito ng singil sa kuryente. Sa ilalim ng Philippine Energy Plan 2023–2050 ng gobyernong Marcos Jr., layunin nitong pataasin ang suplay ng kuryenteng nagmumula sa RE hanggang 35 porsyento sa 2030 at 50 porsyento sa 2050. Sa kasalukuyan, tumaya ang DOE sa 16,337 MW na solar farm at 5,377 MW ng wind farm na proyekto sa buong bansa — lahat ng ito ay pag-aari ng mga pribado at dayuhang korporasyon.

Kung mura ang teknolohiyang RE, bakit patuloy pa ring tumataas ang singil sa kuryente? Bakit hindi nakikinabang dito ang mga mahihirap at maliliit na konsumer? Sa kasalukuyan, nagbabayad ang mga konsumer ng P13 hanggang PHP16 kada kWh sa mga distributor ng kuryente. Ang Pilipinas ngayon ang may pinakamahal na singil sa kuryente sa Asya, habang isa naman ito sa mga bansang may pinakamababang minimum wage sa rehiyon. Mahal na ang kuryente, mababa pa ang kita ng mga ordinaryong pamilyang Pilipino.

Kailan lamang pinayagan ng Energy Regulatory Commission (ERC) ang MERALCO na magdagdag ng singil sa kuryente. Kalakip dito ang pagtaas ng FIT-All (Feed-in Tariff Allowance) mula P0.2011 patungong P0.3359 kada kWh. Ayon sa batas, garantisado ng gobyerno ang pagbayad sa mga korporasyon para sa kanilang mga proyektong RE sa loob ng 20 taon — dagdag na mabigat na pasanin sa mamamayan sa loob ng dalawang dekada.

Hindi pa rito natatapos ang pangongotong ng mga kumpanya sa elektrisidad. May nakaambang dagdag na singil sa tinatawag na GEA-All o Green Energy Auction Allowance, na nagpopondo sa mga inaprubahang proyektong RE ng gobyernong Marcos — ilan sa mga ito ay nabanggit na sa itaas. Ibig sabihin, ang mamamayan mismo ang pinagkukuhanan ng puhunan para sa pagtatayo ng mga bagong proyektong RE. Mamamayan ang magpopondo sa mga proyektong ito, at sisingilin pa tayo ng mahal na presyo ng kuryente. Ginigisa tayo sa sarili nating mantika!

Ayon sa mga taunang ulat ng mga kumpanya, kumita ang MERALCO ng P38 bilyon, P45.86 bilyon, at P51.13 bilyon noong 2023, 2024, at 2025, ayon sa pagkakasunod-sunod. Samantala, kumita …

author: Jessa Agad, Mira Bueno at Jenelle Nuqui
title: Ano ang papel ng US sa krisis sa langis?
content:
mga kuha nina Jessa Agad, Colline Nobleza, Mira Bueno

“Itigil ang gyerang agresyon ng US sa buong daigdig”

Iyan ang panghuli sa anim na hiling ng mga tsuper mula sa ikinasang dalawang araw na transport strike sa bansa noong Setyembre 29-30.

Sa patuloy na pag-atake ng US-Israel sa Kanlurang Asya, apektado ang pangunahing industriya ng langis na nagpaparalisa sa pag-aangkat ng suplay sa iba’t ibang bansa. Ngunit sa Pilipinas, paano nga ba ito nakakaapekto sa karaniwang mamamayan?

Nang sumiklab ang giyerang agresyon ng US-Israel laban sa Iran noong Pebrero 2026, naging malaki ang epekto nito sa daloy ng langis sa iba’t ibang rehiyon, partikular sa Strait of Hormuz, isang mahalagang ruta ng mga pandaigdigang kalakalan.

20% ng pandaigdigang suplay ng crude oil at liquified natural gas (LNG) ang dumaraan sa Strait of Hormuz. Dahil sa matinding tensyon at mga banta ng pag-atake sa rehiyong sakop ang ruta, naantala at bumagal ang trapiko ng mga barkong pang-kargamento na siyang nagpalaki ng pangamba sa suplay ng enerhiya at nagtulak sa presyo ng krudo mula $65 patungong mahigit $100 bawat bariles sa pandaigdigang merkado.

Bukod sa Strait of Hormuz, inatake ng Iraqi drone ang East-West oil pipeline ng Saudi Arabia noong Setyembre 11 dahilan para pansamantalang isinara ang naturang pipeline na kilala rin bilang Petroline.

Ang imprastraktura ay direktang nag-uugnay sa mga pangunahing oil fields ng Saudi Arabia sa Silangang Lalawigan patungo sa port terminal ng Yanbu sa Red Sea, ito ang nagsisilbing pangunahing alternatibong ruta ng bansa upang maiwasan ang Strait of Hormuz.

Sa katunayan, ginagamit ito upang iangkat ang humigit-kumulang 4 milyong barrels ng langis kada araw na katumbas ng halos 4% ng pandaigdigang suplay.

Ayon sa pinakahuling datos mula sa Department of Energy (DOE), ang Pilipinas ay pangyunahing umaasa sa pandaigdigang merkado dahil halos 98% ng crude oil imports ay nagmula sa Middle East, partikular sa Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates (UAE), at Iraq.

Bukod sa krudo, ang mga pinong produktong langis na ginagamit sa mga sasakyan tulad ng diesel at gasolina ay 97 porsyento na inaangkat naman mula sa mga karatig-bansa sa Asya gaya ng South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, at Japan. Gayunpaman, ang mga refinery ng mga bansang ito ay umaasa rin sa krudo na nagmumula sa Middle East na kailangan dumaan sa makitid na ruta gaya ng Strait of Hormuz.

Hindi lingid sa kaalaman ng nakararami na 50% ng industriya sa bansa ay nakaaasa langis. Sa halos pitong buwang pagpapatuloy ng giyera, nagpapatuloy pa tumitinding krisis sa global supply chain na higit na nakaapekto sa presyo ng langis tungong $200 kada barrel.

Ayon sa Department of Energy, umabot na sa P73.68 kada litro ang netong pagtaas ng presyo ng diesel mula sa unang kwarto ng taon. Samantalang sa loob lamang ng Setyembre, tumaas pa ng P18.31 kada litro ang presyo ng diesel, bunsod ng magkasunod na dagdag-presyo.

Sa ulat ng IBON Foundation, 65% ng suplay ng langis ay napupunta sa sektor ng transportasyon, sumunod ang services (11.9%), industriya (7.6%), gamit pangbahay (7%), at sa agrikultura (1%).

Kaya naman sa bawat pagtaas ng presyo ng langis, tsuper at operator ang unang umaaray.

“Sa maghapon naming pamamasada, nag-uuwi na lang kami ng mahigit P200, pinakamataas [na ang] P400. Sa kinu-krudo namin sa isang araw mahigit P3,000. Kaya kakapiranggot na lang ang aming kinikita sa aming pamilya.” ani Tatay Mario, jeepney driver-operator sa Novaliches,

Noong Setyembre 28, ipinatupad ng LTFRB ang minimum na pamasahe sa tradisyunal na jeepney mula P13 tungong P14 para sa unang apat na kilometro. Ayon sa PISTON, insulto ang baryang dagdag-pasahe para sa mga tsuper at operator na gumagastos ng P3000 kada araw para sa langis.

“Dahil sa ganitong presyo ng langis grabe eh, hindi kakayanin. Kasi yung piso na dinagdag nila, wala rin epekto yan dahil sa sbrang taas [ng presyo].” dagdag ni Samuel Soria, driver-operator ng Don Bosco-Delpan-Divisoria route.

Sa kabilang banda, dalawang ‘oil giants’ sa Pilipinas ay nag-ulat ng paglaki ng kita ngayong taon.

Ang Petron Corporation, na pagmamay-ari ni Ramon Ang, ay nakalikom ng P3.8 billion kita sa unang hati ng 2026. Habang ang kampanyang Shell Pilipinas Corporation naman ay dumoble sa P1.62 billion ang kita kung ikukumpara sa P743.6 million nilang kita noong 2025.

Ayon sa PISTON, ang pabago-bagong dikta ng pandaigdigang merkado ng langis ay pakana ng US kagunay sa nagpapatuloy na giyerang agresyon sa Kanlurang Asya na …

author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)

title: Sleeper-Cell Report July 2026 – Global Coalition reports 0 confirmed ISIS attacks
content:
An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside


 


Key Points


– Six sleeper-cell attacks recorded by RIC, but the Global Coalition claims 0 attacks were officially claimed by ISIS


– One military personnel was killed, and a further five injured


– A minimum of seven alleged ISIS members were arrested


– A total of 36 civilians were injured, two killed


– An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in Deir ez-Zor


–

Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS mercenaries repatriated from Roj camp


 


In-Depth


In July of 2026, RIC

recorded six sleeper-cell attacks which some publications have attributed to ISIS, according to


North Press Agency

 one of these attacks was claimed by ISIS whereas the


Global Coalition


reported that July was the first month since the territorial defeat of ISIS in 2019, where they claimed 0 attacks. Also this month at least 7 members of ISIS cells were arrested.


On July 7, Bombings struck central Damascus near the Ministry of Tourism and the Four Seasons Hotel, during the visit of Macron the president of France to Syria. Ministry of Interior has attributed the attack to ISIS, the bombing resulted in the killing of one civilian and injury of 36.


On July 8, three attacks happened during the same day and the are believed to have been carried out by ISIS members.

Unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle used machine guns to target an oil truck in Abrahyah town in eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, killing the driver.


Similarly, unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle, attacked a checkpoint of the Internal Security Forces near al-Baserah city bridge.


According to North Press Agency, also on July 8 ISIS

claimed responsibility for the killing of Rashad Khalaf al-Ghurair in the northern countryside of Deir ez-Zor.


On July 15,

unknown gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire on a member of the 72nd Division on the road linking al-Arimah and Manbij in eastern Aleppo countryside, injuring the him.


On July 18,

two unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle opened fire directly on member of the Defence Ministry


near al-Awsajli junction in eastern Manbij city.


On July 9,

Syria’s Interior Ministry announced its security forces had dismantled several ISIS cells in southern Syria, arresting a senior leader and several members accused of involvement in assassinations and financing terror.


On July 28,

Syrian Internal Security Forces and the General Intelligence Service in Aleppo announced the arrest of individuals allegedly affiliated with the ISIS, during a security operation in Aleppo and its surrounding countryside.


An ISIS flag was raised on a school building in al-Zubari, eastern Deir ez-Zor countryside, in an incident that sparked widespread concern among residents.


During July, Two Tunisian families linked to ISIS were repatriated from


Roj Camp, which houses families of ISIS members, and returned to Tunisia. Additionally, Tunisian citizen Bilal Chawachi was sentenced to 55 years in prison after being convicted on terrorism-related charges, specifically traveling to Syria and fighting alongside the extremist organization.


Germany sentenced an Iraqi man to life imprisonment and his former wife to nine years and six months in prison after convicting them of enslaving and torturing two Yazidi girls while they were members of ISIS in Syria and Iraq between 2015 and 2017.


Three U.S. citizens pleaded guilty to terror charges, prosecutors said the defendants communicated through encrypted messaging applications between July and November 2025 and planned to travel to Turkey before crossing into Syria to join ISIS. 


* Due to the low rate of confirmed ISIS attacks RIC has decided to stop publishing monthly sleeper-cell reports and instead share a bi-annual summary of ISIS activity throughout Syria.

author: groundxero
title: ‘The Struggle Continues’ for Today’s Generation of French Students
content:
The French student movement has a long history of political activism based on organized protests and occupations not only for the improvement of their learning experience and school conditions but also against capitalism, consumerism, imperialism, and police repression.


 


By

C.J. Polychroniou


Common Dreams


 


France

 is presently in the throes of nationwide student

protests

 that have turned increasingly violent as the police crack down on students, using tear gas and heavy-handed tactics as students blockade entrances to their schools and even set fire to several schools across France.


 


The students, aged between 15 and 18, are protesting over poor school conditions (overcrowded classrooms, crumbling

infrastructure

, heavy workloads, teacher shortages) and demand increased funding for schools. Thousands have been

detained

, mostly minors, and dozens injured, including some 50 law enforcement officers.


 


The high school protests begun in Aubervilliers, a low-income Paris suburb, but quickly spread nationwide, as usually happens with students protests in France. University students have now joined high school schools across France, thus creating an even more volatile situation for the French government. Incidentally, the student protests are unfolding alongside massive public-sector protests over pay and working conditions.


 


French students have also shown that they are always on the side of the workers’ fight for better working conditions and in their struggle for an alternative socioeconomic and political order.


 


France is indeed in crisis mode, economically, politically, and socially. Weak growth and deteriorating public finances have been the norm for several years now, while

austerity

 is being advanced by the political establishment as the only available solution to the country’s economic problems and financial misery. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu presented an austerity-driven government

budget

 on October 1 that proposes 43 billion euros in new fiscal measures to reduce the deficit.


 


However, the

budget

 bill is surely expected to face a rough ride as France has a deeply divided parliament that has repeatedly rejected austerity-driven budget proposals, forcing in fact several prime ministers since 2022 to step down. Lecornu’s government may very well be the next one to collapse as it is highly unlikely that either Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party or Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s left-wing France Unbowed (LFI) party (which France’s

Interior Ministry

 has actually classified as far left) will make compromises, especially in light of the fact that France’s next presidential election is scheduled for April 18 and May 2, 2027, and looks like the

run-off election

 will be between Le Pen and Mélenchon.


 


In addition, France’s

bond market

 is under growing pressure as its 10-year yield has reached the highest level since 2002. With the cost of borrowing money hitting a peak, France, which has faced sluggish growth for years, is likely to see even slower growth in 2027 than in 2026. This situation seems to be serving the far-right RN party particularly well, which has already scored a “

historic victory

” by securing enough seats in the recently held Senate election to establish its own caucus for the first time.


 


In the meantime, the student protests are being used both by Le Pen and government officials to

target

 Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s party for allegedly deploying agitators and using rhetoric to stoke students’ anger.


 


There is little doubt that the concerns of French students are legitimate. Their grievances with the poor state of schools have been building since this summer’s

heatwaves

, which exposed “the poor state of schools, with poor insulation and no air conditioning,” according to

Vincent Latour

,

 a professor of British Studies at the University of Toulouse-II-Le Mirail. Moreover, the president of Union Syndicale Lycéenne (USL), 19-year old

Ryad Rani

, said that student grievances had elicited no response from the government and that the movement will continue with the protests until its demands are satisfied.


 


The French student movement has a long history of political

activism

author: Emily Lassam
title: French high school students on the march
content:
“I like this kinda thing because it’s revolutionary”, a 16-year-old high school student told me as we stood out the front of her school in Nice at 7am on the last Wednesday in September. As we talked, students started arriving from across the city to join the blockade of the school, the Lycée Parc Imperial, the largest in the area.

Hundreds of students trickled in, and suddenly it was hard to tell where the sea of high schoolers started and ended. Some carried things to help build the barricades to stop anyone from entering the school.

I asked the 16-year-old if she knew all the students or whether they were from other schools. She pointed out a group of high schoolers who must have travelled from another school and said: “I don’t know them, but we are all comrades”.

This wasn’t the first blockade she had been part of at this school, but she said it was different to previous blockades. This time, it isn’t just one school but more than 1,000 being blockaded.

Videos and photos of French students holding Palestinian and Algerian flags, calling for revolution, chanting against the far-right National Rally and fighting against intense repression are sweeping social media.

This comes at a moment when a growing wave of student protests and revolts is sweeping across the world. Last year, there were the Gen Z revolts that were led by students and swept across Nepal, Indonesia, Madagascar and a whole series of countries in the Global South.

In July, hundreds of thousands of students in India joined huge protests and forced the education minister to resign. At the end of August, tens of thousands of students in Germany struck from school to protest the introduction of forced military conscription. Across Chile in early October, thousands of students and teachers took to the streets to protest possible education cuts. And in Australia, high schoolers have been at the forefront of the fight against Pauline Hanson, organising two successful school walkouts in opposition to her.  

French students are protesting the terrible conditions in their schools, for both students and teachers. Schools are forced to deal with inadequate funding, large class sizes, decrepit facilities and low staff pay and morale. To make matters worse, further cuts are planned in the upcoming national budget. And it’s not just schools facing cuts.

President Emmanuel Macron has announced the budget will include £54 billion in cuts and a fourth wage freeze for the public sector. On 29 September, thousands of public sector workers went on strike in anticipation of these cuts, with many strikers visiting high schools to show their solidarity with students. Teachers are also planning to strike on 6 October.

Students at Parc Imperial said their school was far from the worst, but even here the conditions are terrible. Class sizes often exceed 35 students, and the classrooms meant to accommodate them are too small and have limited, if any, heating and cooling. Temperatures can reach 40 degrees inside in summer and are freezing in winter. During the day, they said, students often do nothing for long periods because there aren’t relief teachers to cover absent teachers, often because the conditions are so bad. Students are also angry about the competitive Parcoursup system that pits them against each other to get into university.

While students and teachers struggle to manage in these conditions, the head of Parc Imperial lives on campus in luxury with his own gym and “wine cave”. Bad as this is, the main enemy, the high schoolers said, is the government. Macron puts billions into the military and police but refuses to adequately fund schools.

The cops’ crackdown on the high schoolers has been severe. The 16-year-old Imperial Parc student showed me the gauze, disinfectant and cream she had brought in her bag in case any students were injured. She hadn’t expected to use it, but ended up caring for a number of people whom the cops had tear-gassed and injured. She said she had been “naive to think the police would do nothing because we are minors. I am 16, most people are 17, 15, 14 we are very very young”. Across the country, police have injured hundreds and arrested thousands of high schoolers.

One of the first schools to start the blockade movement was Paul Éluard in Saint Denis (north of Paris). Saint Denis is a poor and migrant area that has been particularly neglected by the Macron government. Students report that the food there is inedible, rats and …

author: AWSM
title: Why I Won’t Vote ~ A SYMPOSIUM #1
content:
Anarchy 37, March 1964, Why I Won’t Vote

Voting : “The instrument and symbol of a freeman’s power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country”

The saying that ” only a fool would put a loaded gun into the hands of an idiot ” is an especially apt analogy of government. An idiot (usually well-meaning) considers himself clever enough to run the affairs of a large number of people by taking a seat in parliament. A large number of people, acting like fools, vote for his party’s policy then spend the next few years grumbling about the results. The error in approach is that the voter thinks that he will get what he voted for. If he could vote for those who in fact control the country, say the Governors of the Bank of England, the directors of the industrial corporations and those behind the ministries, the illusion of democracy would be more understandable.

The real centres of power lie far beyond the people’s influence at elections. These remain constant whatever Party is ” in power “. In the terms of centralised ” democracy ” the only possible argument to justify voting is that marginal benefits may be gained. The state only incidentally attends to the well-being of its subjects. Its main concern is its power relation to other states, of which the most perfect expression is in war.

I am on the side of people anywhere who are prepared neither to live nor die for something that in the long run can only militate against survival and the conditions that make life worth living. Our immediate action must, by its nature, be to oppose that pathetic gesture, voting. It must be direct and direction. We can learn to live as free men and women only by organising against the condition we are in.

The Tenants Association, Consumers Association, and Direct Action in industry all provide opportunities for people to experience directing their own lives in positive ways towards positive ends.

Only by direct involvement in society can the individual hope to transform himself and his world. Freedom cannot be given, it must be taken; and the free society can only grow from experiments in the problems (ethical and organisational) of community.

Voting does not, and cannot, mean government by consent. By voting, one acts on the assumptions that certain men are fit to govern, and that a majority is necessarily right. Also should the state, acting in the name of a (frequently fictitious) majority, declare war, the individual loses the right to live, if he ever had it.

To me, voting is complicity with the State and a negative action, therefore I do not vote.

author: Cormac Mills Ritchard
title: Demolishing the idea of public housing
content:
The United Nations’ special rapporteur on adequate housing, Koldo Casla, usually deals with slum demolitions in third-world countries. Last month, he took aim at the Victorian Labor government, claiming its demolition of Melbourne’s 44 public housing towers and the “forced evictions and mass displacement of approximately 10,000 residents” could be a violation of their

human rights

. This follows a Victorian parliamentary inquiry in December, which called for an

immediate pause

 to the demolitions, and a class action against the demolitions filed by Inner Melbourne Community Legal (IMCL), which has been granted special leave to

appeal

 to the High Court on 7 October.

Despite growing challenges, Premier Ben Carroll is ploughing ahead with the demolition of Melbourne’s public housing towers. Of course, Labor doesn’t characterise what it’s doing as “eviction” and “demolition”, but “renewal” and “redevelopment”, which it claims will increase the number of residents on the estates from 10,000 to 30,000, and replace towers that have “reached the end of their useful life”. There is no truth to this.

If Labor’s multi-billion-dollar project is aimed at addressing the waiting list for social housing, it’s missing a couple of zeros. Only 11,000 of the new residents will be in social housing, an increase of just 1,000. As of June this year, there were 58,021 people on the Victorian Housing Register’s

growing waiting list

, of which 33,253 have been assessed as “priority”—mostly those who are currently homeless or experiencing family violence. The redevelopments will mean that just 1,000 more people will have places in social housing ... by 2051.

The redevelopment won’t help others affected by the housing crisis, either. The other 19,000 residents of the new mixed-tenure developments will live in a combination of build-to-rent, a model that the

 Age

 has found to be between 20 and 70 percent

more expensive

 than the market rate, and “affordable housing”, which is not that affordable and does not provide long-term security, as exposed by a recent

Four Corners


investigation

. 

The North Richmond public housing precinct is a telling example. In September, the state government briefed the City of Yarra on its plans for the tower at 139 Highett Street. The

Age

 reported last month that the tower, which currently has 220 public housing units, will be replaced with a development that has

only 150 social housing units

 and 650 build-to-rent units.

Simon is a former resident who grew up in the North Richmond precinct after his parents emigrated from Vietnam. After the latest announcement about the precinct, he attended a community meeting of public housing tenants who demand the towers be refurbished rather than demolished. He told

Red Flag

 that his parents, a labourer and kindergarten worker, were both poorly paid. Living in the public housing tower allowed them to escape the anarchy of the private rental market. “We knew what the rent was next week and didn’t have to worry about eviction or not being able to afford food. I could attend school and university without many issues. That security meant you could plan your life”, he said.

“Social housing” is an umbrella term that covers both public housing, run by the government, and community housing, run by not-for-profits. When Labor talks about social housing, it usually means community housing—so its claim to be replacing 10,000 public housing places with 11,000 social ones actually represents a huge cut in public housing.

Public housing rent is capped at 25 percent of a household’s income or the market rate, whichever is lower, while community housing providers can charge up to 30 percent. However, community housing organisations (CHOs) are entitled to 100 percent of any tenant’s Commonwealth Rent Assistance and can charge extra fees on top. In its

submission to the inquiry

, IMCL notes that some of its clients pay up to 50 percent of their income to a CHO through “rent, utilities, lift fees, concierge and management fees”. Community housing residents also have fewer rights than public housing residents; West Heidelberg Community Legal found that “long-term community housing tenants were 3 to 5 times more likely to face eviction than public housing tenants”.

Worse still, unlike the government, CHOs don’t have to allocate places based on need, which means that the more the social housing waiting list is serviced by community rather than public housing …

author: Jordan Humphreys
title: Germany’s far right surges
content:
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) made significant gains in several state elections across Germany in September. In Saxony-Anhalt, the party won a frightening 44 percent of the vote and fell just three seats short of forming government. Two weeks later, it won 38 percent in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, doubling its vote share from the previous election. Even in liberal, multicultural Berlin, the AfD vote went from 9 percent to 16 percent.

The results have sent political shockwaves across not just across Germany but the whole of Europe. It is no wonder why. The AfD is on the extreme wing of the broader far-right surge worldwide. Founded in 2013 as a Eurosceptic opposition to Chancellor Angela Merkel’s bailouts of the Greek government, the party has moved radically to the right over the last decade.

Today, the AfD calls for mass deportations and a strict blood-based concept of German citizenship, while opposing the right to political asylum. It also campaigns for separate schools for the children of migrants. The party also argues that focusing on the crimes of the Nazi period encourages national humiliation and therefore opposes Holocaust memorials. In 2023, AfD leaders attended a secret meeting in Potsdam with wealthy donors and prominent neo-Nazis to develop a plan to expel from the country millions of migrants and refugees and hundreds of thousands of German citizens of non-German background.

The AfD is riddled with veteran neo-Nazis. While the party initially placed barriers on fascists joining, these have been loosened as the AfD has moved further right. Björn Höcke, leader of the AfD in the eastern state of Thuringia, has been a key figure driving this shift. Prior to his public rise with the AfD, Höcke wrote articles under the pseudonym “Landolf Ladig” for neo-Nazi publications, praising Hitler and the Nazi regime. 

At campaign speeches, Höcke has repeatedly used the slogan “everything for Germany”, which was the official motto of the Nazi paramilitary wing (the

Sturmabteilung

, known as the Brownshirts or Storm Troopers). In an infamous 2017 speech in Dresden, Höcke sparked outrage by calling the Holocaust Memorial in Berlin a “memorial of shame”. The AfD branches in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern are closely associated with Höcke’s faction in the party.

A 2024 investigative report by Bavarian Radio found that AfD parliamentarians employ more than 100 individuals with ties to far-right extremist organisations. Numerous former activists and staff from the National Democratic Party—an openly neo-Nazi party since renamed The Homeland—are employed as strategy writers, social media managers and advisors. The AfD’s youth wing is effectively controlled by Nazis.

The AfD is so extreme that other European far-right leaders like France’s Marine Le Pen, Italy’s Giorgia Meloni and Britain’s Nigel Farage have broken ties with the party, expelling it from their European Parliament coalition. However, the Trump administration and Elon Musk in the US and the Putin regime in Russia are all friendly with the AfD.

While the AfD has been gaining ground for some years, the latest results are a significant step forward and confirm that, despite the ebb in support for some figures like Trump, the fascist right has firmly entrenched itself as a permanent feature of contemporary capitalist politics across the globe.

That the AfD is so extreme only reinforces the seriousness of the situation. It also raises the question of why people in Germany, after the experiences of the Nazi period, would support such a filthy, bigoted party.

The primary driver behind the AfD’s rise has been the collapsing social base of the traditional parties in the German government. In a story repeated across the world, decades of support for neoliberal economics and centrist politics by the centre-right and centre-left have alienated millions of people from the establishment parties. The shift to the right in mainstream German politics in recent years has created plenty of kindling for the AfD fire to burn.

After all, it was not the AfD that invented the demonisation of Muslims and Arabs in Germany. Both the centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU) and the Social Democratic Party (SPD) have stoked racism for years, promoting harsher border control regulations and punishing refugees and migrants in the process. A key turning point came when Angela Merkel surprisingly allowed more than 1 million Syrian refugees into Germany in 2015. In …

author: Deaglan Godwin
title: Student Union independence under threat at Sydney University
content:
The University of Sydney has announced its intention to intervene in the student union and potentially undermine democratic elections.

The announcement follows a controversy, concocted by the right-wing Murdoch media, about an election ticket contesting this year’s Students’ Representative Council election. The ticket, called Globalise the Intifada, drew hysterical condemnation from Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, federal Education Minister Jason Clare and a spokesperson for NSW Premier Chris Minns. Albanese told Sydney’s

Daily Telegraph

 the slogan “is an absolute outrage that has no place in Australia”. 

Vice-chancellor Mark Scott and chancellor David Thodey joined the chorus of condemnation.

In a statement released on 29 September

, they said: “We deplore the manipulation of the recent election campaign to spread hurtful and distressing language across campus”. 

The university also said it will commission an independent review of the SRC’s “current affiliation and funding arrangements ... to ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and psychosocial safety requirements”. The review will also focus on student and staff codes of conduct and on campus security. 

Behind closed doors, Scott and Thodey floated even more drastic measures. A source present at last week’s University Senate meeting

told

Honi Soit

, the student newspaper, that Scott raised the possibility of the university taking control of student elections and conducting them online. A university spokesperson refused to answer

Honi Soit

’s questions about the discussions. 

The university’s investigation rests on the spurious claim that phrases in support of Palestine, such as “globalise the intifada” and “from the XXXX to the sea”, threaten the safety of Jewish people. 

In Arabic, “intifada” simply means “shaking off” or “uprising”. It commonly refers to the First and Second Intifadas, mass movements of Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank against Israeli apartheid and settler-colonialism. The phrase denotes the steadfast resistance of the Palestinians to decades of ethnic cleansing and apartheid. 

Governments, corporate media and university managers spend huge amounts of time and energy painting these phrases as calls to violence. Meanwhile, they turn a blind eye to the very real violence that Israel is committing in Gaza and the West Bank. New satellite imagery of the city of Rafah in Gaza illustrates the scale of Israel’s assault. Before 2023, the city looked like any other: houses, public squares, parks. Today, the city is a wasteland, all the buildings reduced to rubble. 

Our government and our universities are complicit in this violence. Many universities maintain research partnerships with weapons companies that sell arms to Israel and conduct exchange programs with Israeli universities. Yet we are expected to believe that student activists campaigning against racism and genocide are the violent actors!

These attacks on student political organising don’t come from nowhere. This confected crisis is taking place in the context of the sham royal commission into antisemitism. Vice-chancellors grovelled before the commissioner as they were grilled about why they allowed Palestine solidarity protests on their campuses. The conflation of anti-Zionism with antisemitism has been a constant of the entire affair. 

Universities are under significant pressure from both the government and pro-Israel organisations to clamp down on free speech and solidarity activism on campus. This aligns with their own self-interest in squashing mounting criticism of their complicity in Israel’s genocide in Gaza, and their desire to attract funding from arms companies and the broader corporate sector, which by and large supports Western imperialism and Israel. 

Widespread hostility to university ties to Israel among students and staff has been on display recently at Sydney University. The controversy around the ticket has distracted from the fact that the election also included a referendum on the administration’s complicity in Israel’s genocide. More than 4,000 students voted, and an overwhelming 92 percent of students voted in favour of breaking the university’s ties with arms companies and Israeli institutions.

Anyone who supports Palestine, who supports student unionism or who supports freedom of speech must speak out against Sydney University’s recent decision.

author: Jessica Corbett
title: Another Trump Administration Boat Strike Claims 4 More Lives
content:
“Where is Congress to stop the horror?” asked Amnesty International USA.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

US President Donald Trump’s boat-bombing spree continued on Sunday despite condemnation from around the world, claiming four more lives and bringing the death toll from the 13-month campaign to at least 238.

Sharing a video of the strike, U.S. Southern Command said on social media late Sunday that “under the direction of SOUTHCOM, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean.”

“Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking,” SOUTHCOM continued, without offering any evidence, as with at least 70 previous strikes since September 2025. “The operation killed four narco-terrorists.”

Citing a federal memo that it aims to keep concealed from the public, the Trump administration claims to be at war with drug cartels and that the killings in the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean are justified. Legal experts and human rights advocates argue the bombings are at least war crimes, if not outright murder.

Sunday’s strike was the administration’s first confirmed boat bombing since Ben Saul, the United Nations special rapporteur on human rights and counterterrorism, said last month that even if the targeted vessels were engaged in drug trafficking, there are no “international legal rights to unilaterally use military force” to counter cartels.

After SOUTHCOM’s announcement, Gizmodo reporter Matt Novak declared, “We murdered four more people in a boat today.”

Brian Finucane, a former State Department legal adviser who now advises the U.S. Program at the International Crisis Group, called it “more performative killing at sea.”

Nearly 240 dead in this illegal campaign of extrajudicial killings, i.e., murder at sea. Where is Congress to stop the horror? https://t.co/yYQdIVkjTE

Highlighting the rising death toll from Trump’s “illegal campaign of extrajudicial killings, ie, murder at sea” initiative, Amnesty International USA asked, “Where is Congress to stop the horror?”

The Republican-controlled Congress has declined to pass war powers resolutions intended to stop the strikes — though the odds of passage could change if Democrats reclaim one or both chambers in next month’s midterm elections.

Trump’s bombing spree has apparently been not only illegal but ineffective. The Washington Post reported in July that a Drug Enforcement Administration analysis concluded that the boat-bombing campaign has not “reduced the amount of cocaine entering” the United States.

We now have three full months of data since Google changed its search to feature AI results. The numbers are worse than we anticipated. Overall readership that comes to Truthout through Google is down 54 percent against last year. The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

The only way we can keep publishing is with strong reader support. We are asking you to start a monthly donation to Truthout today — anything you can do, whether $5 or $25, makes a difference.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: El martes movilización a Tribunales y el jueves a la Secretaría de Industria
content:
El martes, las dos CTAs, ex combatientes de Malvinas, movimientos sociales, partidos de izquierda y organismos de Derechos Humanos marcharán al Palacio de Tribunales en rechazo del fallo de la Corte Suprema que permitió la derogación de la Ley de Tierras.


La CGT confirmó una movilización para el próximo jueves 8 a las 15:30 hacia la sede de la secretaría de Industria -antiguo ministerio de la Producción- en la avenida Roca 651, en el centro porteño, “contra la política económica” del gobierno de Javier Milei.


Foto:

Mat ((i))


Calentando motores


Por Mario Hernandez


La ñata contra el vidrio


El secretario de DD HH del CECIM La Plata, Ernesto Alonso, denunció que la resolución de la Corte deslegitima tanto a los ex combatientes como a todo el pueblo argentino, dejando vía libre a un “plan sistemático de entrega”. Advirtió que el fallo busca dejar a la ciudadanía “con la ñata contra el vidrio” mientras corporaciones transnacionales y magnates tecnológicos se apoderan de los recursos estratégicos.


Foto: Agencia Andar/CPM


También la CTA Autónoma y la CTA de los Trabajadores acusaron a los magistrados de “complicidad cipaya” y de firmar un “cheque en blanco” al gobierno de Javier Milei. Advirtieron que eliminar las restricciones de la Ley 26.737 de 2011 que fijaba un máximo del 15% a la propiedad extranjera, límites por nacionalidad del 30% del cupo, un tope de 1.000 hectáreas en zona núcleo y la prohibición sobre cuerpos de agua, habilita la compra ilimitada de suelos, fuentes de agua dulce y zonas de frontera por parte de fondos especulativos.


En una asamblea en Parque Lezama el viernes pasado, Gabriel Solano, dirigente del Partido Obrero, reclamó “voltear todo el DNU 70/2023” señalando que la norma desregula también prepagas, alquileres y tasas financieras.


En tanto, las fuerzas con presencia en el Congreso tratan de fortalecer su posición de cara a la sesión especial del próximo jueves 15. Con su sentencia, la Corte Suprema podría generar la derogación total del DNU 70/23, lo que significaría un golpe demoledor a la gobernabilidad del presidente Javier Milei.


Foto: Indymedia Trabajadoras/es


CGT: sin paro general y con plan de lucha escalonado


Bajo el lema “Las Malvinas son argentinas, la industria también”, la CGT marchará a la secretaría de Industria el próximo jueves. Será la cuarta acción coordinada con otras organizaciones: 22/7 por los jubilados, 7/8 por San Cayetano y 20/8 por los endeudados.


Estará emparentada con la que una semana después se realizará en el Congreso convocada por los docentes y estudiantes universitarios a la que se sumó el rechazo al fallo de la Corte Suprema.


Al respecto, la CGT acusó a los jueces supremos Horacio Rosatti, Carlos Rosenkrantz y Ricardo Lorenzetti de poner en venta al país y ratificó que se sumará a la movilización del 15 de octubre.


Cristian Jerónimo


Paro pospuesto


Pese a las presiones internas, la conducción pospuso una huelga inmediata. Cristian Jerónimo, uno de los triunviros de la CGT, argumentó que un paro perjudicaría a los representados, mientras que otro, Jorge Sola, secretario general del Seguro, garantizó una huelga general antes de fin de año “si no hay respuestas”.


Sectores de izquierda sindical calificaron la movilización del jueves como una “medida raquítica de la burocracia sindical” y que la cúpula cegetista fue complaciente al convalidar contrarreformas laborales como los bancos de horas y el Fondo de Asistencia Laboral (FAL). Según este sector, la marcha busca alianzas con un empresariado liderado por Techint para pedir proteccionismo para el capital, en lugar de aumentos salariales o la derogación de la reforma laboral.

El martes movilización a Tribunales y el jueves a la Secretaría de Industria

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

title: Fransa’da daha iyi eğitim için 413 okulda eylem
content:
Fransa’da eğitim koşullarının iyileştirilmesi talebiyle düzenlenen lise eylemleri devam ediyor. Fransa Eğitim Bakanlığı bugün ülke genelinde 413 okulda eylemler olduğunu açıkladı. Eylemlere yönelik polis şiddeti de devam ediyor.

Fransa'da öğrenciler niye eylem yapıyor, ne talep ediyor?

Ülkenin önde gelen lise sendikalarından USL Genel Sekreteri Marius Mesnil, katıldığı bir televizyon yayınında, hükümetin liselilerin taleplerine ilişkin adımlarını yeterli bulmadıklarını yineledi. Mesnil, lise kuşatma eylemlerinin kararlılıkla sürdürülmesi çağrısı yaptı.

Fransa'da daha iyi eğitim koşulları talebiyle başlatılan lise eylemleri büyüyor. Ülke genelinde 413 okulda protestolar sürerken, Fransa'nın en büyük işçi sendikası CGT de öğrencilere destek vererek iş bırakma çağrısında bulundu @RevPermanente/X https://t.co/eSlFa4u7Xe https://t.co/2TqmWX4Z2G

Ülkenin en büyük sendikası CGT Genel Sekreteri Sophie Binet de liselilerin eylemlerine destek vereceklerini açıkladı. CGT ve diğer işçi sendikaları bugün iş bırakma ve lise öğrencileriyle birlikte protesto gösterilerine katılma çağrısı yapmışlardı.

Fransa’da 6 Ekim çağrısı: İşçiler gençlerin yanında olacak

Lise öğrencilerinin 17 Eylül’de Créteil’deki Saint-Exupéry Lisesi’nde başlattığı eylem, kısa sürede Paris banliyölerinden ülke geneline yayıldı.

Öğrenciler öğretmen ve personel eksikliği, kalabalık sınıflar, aşırı yoğun ders programları, bakımsız okul binaları ve bazı dersliklerde masa gibi temel ihtiyaçların dahi bulunmamasını protesto ediyor.

Öğretmen açığının kapatılması, daha fazla personel, daha az kalabalık sınıflar, yenilenmiş okul binaları ve daha iyi öğrenme koşulları için somut adımlar atılması isteniyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Γιάννης Βολιάτης
title: Επιστολή εργαζομένων της Βιολάντα – Καταγγελίες για εκφοβισμό από την εργοδοσία
content:
Επιστολή εργαζομένων της Βιολάντα – Καταγγελίες για εκφοβισμό από την εργοδοσία


Με το αίμα των πέντε νεκρών εργαζομένων από την έκρηξη στο εργοστάσιο της εταιρίας τροφίμων Βιολάντα στα Τρίκαλα να μην έχει στεγνώσει καλά-καλά ακόμη, με τον ιδιοκτήτη της εταιρείας, Κωνσταντίνο Τζιωρτζιώτη, να έχει ήδη αποφυλακιστεί εδώ και παραπάνω από έναν μήνα και εν μέσω

καταγγελιών για εκδικητικές απολύσεις

, μερίδα των εργαζομένων της εταιρίας απέστειλε επιστολή στα ΜΜΕ, κάνοντας λόγο για ψυχολογική πίεση, εκφοβισμό και bullying από μεριάς της εργοδοσίας, προκειμένου να υπογράψουν συγκεκριμένα έγγραφα.


Ακολουθεί η επιστολή:


“Επικοινωνούμε εκ μέρους σημαντικού αριθμού εργαζομένων της ΒΙΟΛΑΝΤΑ, οι οποίοι αισθανόμαστε την ανάγκη να δημοσιοποιήσουμε μια κατάσταση που βιώνουμε καθημερινά και μας προκαλεί έντονη ανησυχία.


Σύμφωνα με τις αναφορές εργαζομένων, το τελευταίο διάστημα επικρατεί στον χώρο εργασίας ένα ιδιαίτερα πιεστικό κλίμα, με περιστατικά που οι ίδιοι βιώνουν ως ψυχολογική πίεση, εκφοβισμό και bullying.


Εργαζόμενοι αναφέρουν ότι τους ζητήθηκε να υπογράψουν έγγραφο σχετικά με τις αποδοχές και τις συνθήκες εργασίας, ενώ ορισμένοι υποστηρίζουν ότι αισθάνθηκαν πως πιέστηκαν να το υπογράψουν, καθώς τους μεταφέρθηκε ότι η άρνησή τους θα μπορούσε να έχει συνέπειες ακόμη και στην εργασιακή τους σχέση.


Παράλληλα, σύμφωνα με τις ίδιες αναφορές, εργαζόμενοι που έχουν προχωρήσει σε καταθέσεις ή έχουν εκφράσει παράπονα φέρεται να δέχονται λεκτικές πιέσεις και συμπεριφορές που τους δημιουργούν φόβο και ανασφάλεια.


Ιδιαίτερα σοβαρό είναι ότι ανάλογες συμπεριφορές bullying και ψυχολογικής πίεσης φέρεται να βιώνουν και οι επιζήσαντες, άνθρωποι που έχουν ήδη περάσει μια εξαιρετικά δύσκολη και τραυματική διαδικασία και θα έπρεπε να αισθάνονται ότι προστατεύονται και όχι ότι βρίσκονται αντιμέτωποι με νέες πιέσεις.


Ζητάμε να ακουστεί η φωνή μας και να διερευνηθούν με σοβαρότητα και ανεξαρτησία όλα όσα καταγγέλλονται.


Θέλουμε να μπορούμε να εργαζόμαστε με αξιοπρέπεια, χωρίς φόβο και χωρίς να αισθανόμαστε ότι η έκφραση μιας καταγγελίας ή η κατάθεση της αλήθειας μπορεί να έχει προσωπικές συνέπειες.


Απευθύνουμε έκκληση προς κάθε αρμόδιο φορέα, την Επιθεώρηση Εργασίας και κάθε ανεξάρτητη αρχή που μπορεί να εξετάσει την κατάσταση


Ακούστε μας. Ερευνήστε όσα καταγγέλλουμε. Προστατεύστε τους εργαζομένους και τους επιζήσαντες.”

Alerta.gr
