Dossier


„

Die hessische Polizei geht systematisch alle Personen in ihren Datenbanken durch, bei denen sie einen Hinweis auf eine „Psychische und Verhaltensstörung“ gespeichert hat. Damit will sie Risiken für Gewalttaten erkennen und etwa Gefährderansprachen oder Überwachung planen. Um Betroffene zu unterstützen, bräuchte es andere Maßnahmen.

„Psychisch Auffällige, Vielschreiber, Gewalttäter“ lautet der Name einer Taskforce, die es seit Februar 2025 beim hessischen Landeskriminalamt gibt. (…) Einen PSYV-Vermerk gibt es aktuell zu rund 1.600 Menschen in Hessen, schreibt das dortige Innenministerium auf Anfrage. (…) Laut Robert-Koch-Institut erhielten im Jahr 2023 40,4 Prozent der Erwachsenen in Deutschland eine Diagnose für eine psychische Störung

…“ Aus dem

Beitrag von Anna Biselli vom 08.07.2025 in Netzpolitik


 („Hessen: Polizei überprüft 1.600 psychisch erkrankte Menschen“ mit weiteren Infos zu geplanten Stigmatisierungen – siehe mehr dazu wie auch beginnende Proteste in immer mehr Bundesländern:


Erneuertes Psychisch-Kranken-Gesetz in NRW soll nicht nur der Polizei, auch der  Ausländerbehörde Informationen über Klinikeinweisungen von Geflüchteten liefern


„

Ein neues Gesetz in Nordrhein-Westfalen soll nicht nur der Polizei mehr Informationen über Menschen liefern, die in eine Klinik eingewiesen wurden. Auch die Ausländerbehörden sollen mehr über Geflüchtete in Psychiatrien erfahren – damit sie Abschiebungen besser planen können.


Nordrhein-Westfalen will sein Psychisch-Kranken-Gesetz (PsychKG) erneuern. Darin geht es zum einen darum, wann Menschen unfreiwillig in eine psychiatrische Klinik eingewiesen werden können. Zum anderen aber auch um Hilfsangebote und Unterstützung für Menschen mit einer psychischen Erkrankung. Das ist in Deutschland auf Ebene der Bundesländer geregelt.


In NRW wie in anderen Bundesländern steht allerdings noch ein anderes Thema im Mittelpunkt der Diskussionen: der Austausch von Daten über Menschen, die in eine Klinik eingewiesen werden. Insbesondere dann, wenn die Einweisung wegen einer festgestellten Fremdgefährdung erfolgte, also weil die Sorge besteht, dass eine Person aufgrund ihres Zustands anderen gefährlich werden könnte. Und in NRW geht es auch um Abschiebungen.


Am Donnerstag sprachen im Gesundheitsausschuss des Landtags Sachverständige über den Gesetzentwurf. Zahlreiche Stellungnahmen von Kliniken, sozialpsychiatrischen Diensten, Verbänden und Betroffenen äußerten Sorgen.


Eine Klinikeinweisung ist keine Strafmaßnahme


„Hier bekommt die Polizeibehörde in medizinisch psychiatrischen Zusammenhängen ein erweitertes Mitentscheidungsrecht über den Datenfluss bis hin zur Entlassung“, schreibt etwa die Freie Wohlfahrtspflege NRW. Sie ist eine Arbeitsgemeinschaft, der unter anderem das Rote Kreuz, die Caritas und die Arbeiterwohlfahrt angehören. Eine Klinik-Unterbringung nach dem PsychKG sei „keine strafrechtliche Maßnahme“. Die Kritik der Freien Wohlfahrtspflege bezieht sich auf eine neue Regelung, wer bei der Entlassung einer zuvor zwangseingewiesenen Person von den Kliniken informiert werden muss. Neben Vertrauenspersonen oder dem sozialpsychiatrischen Dienst soll künftig in bestimmten Fällen auch die örtliche Polizei in Kenntnis gesetzt werden. (…)


Dass im Gesetz überhaupt der Eindruck erweckt wird, man müsse psychisch Erkrankten mit Gefahrenabwehrmaßnahmen begegnen, darin sehen viele Fachleute ein Problem. Das bediene, so die Freie Wohlfahrtspflege NRW, „das Narrativ der ‚gefährlichen psychisch kranken Gewalttäter’. Eine psychische Erkrankung und Gewalttaten stehen jedoch nur in einem geringen Umfang in einem direkten Zusammenhang.“ (…)


Die Ausländerbehörde soll immer wissen, wo eine geflüchtete Person sich aufhält, damit sie sie jederzeit abschieben kann. Fachleute sind empört.


Psychiatrische Kliniken sollten „nicht zu Orten werden, von denen aus regelmäßig Abschiebungen erfolgen“, schreibt dazu die Aktion Psychisch Kranke. „Die Krankenhäuser sollten geschützte Räume bleiben“, heißt es in der Stellungnahme des Vereins, in dem sich Bundestagsabgeordnete und Fachleute aus der psychiatrischen Versorgung zusammengeschlossen haben. (…)


Ärzt:innen sind keine Abschiebehelfer


Abschiebungen aus Krankenhäusern passieren schon heute. Bei einem Abschiebeflug nach Afghanistan im Juli 2025 waren mindestens drei der 81 Betroffenen unmittelbar davor in einer psychiatrischen Klinik. Anfang 2025 holte die Polizei einen suizidalen Geflüchteten aus einer Klinik in Osnabrück …

author: Peter Boyle
title: Malaysia deports 1476 refugees to Myanmar
content:
There was outrage from refugee and human rights groups when Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced in July that his government had made an agreement with the military coup regime in Myanmar to deport 5000 Rohingya refugees who fled the regime's genocidal attacks on this Muslim minority.

The United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) has registered 126,000 Rohingya refugees in Malaysia and there are more unregistered. Over the past year, these refugees have been targeted in a campaign of hate by figures in the conservative United Malays National Organisation, a component of the coalition federal government in Malaysia.

Green Left's Peter Boyle spoke to Madhavi Madhu, a member of the Socialist Party of Malaysia (PSM) and a longstanding refugee rights activist.

There have been reports that the Malaysian government has begun its promised deportations of refugees back to Myanmar. What is the actual situation?

The government deported 1476 Myanmar nationals (including women and children) on September 29 aboard two navy vessels and a hospital vessel. These individuals were detainees from various immigration detention camps. Large numbers of refugees remain in these detention facilities following continuous, large-scale raids that have taken place throughout this year.

What has been the response of refugee rights and human rights groups?

Amnesty International and Asylum Access have issued strong condemnations of the deportations. The UNHCR also raised concerns, stating that while authorities claim the returns are voluntary, those returned had been held in immigration detention. This raises serious questions about whether the decisions to return were genuinely free and informed.

Additionally, on 24 September, a coalition of NGOs — including Gegar, AKSI, Activist Network, and Beyond Borders — protested in front of the Home Ministry’s office, demanding a halt to these dangerous deportations.

What has been the government’s response to warnings that such deportations may amount to "refoulement" under international law?

The government has not directly addressed these warnings. Instead, it has maintained its narrative that the repatriation is voluntary and conducted in coordination with the Myanmar government to ensure the returnees' "safety".

However, Myanmar remains under heavy martial law, and no clear or transparent program has been outlined to guarantee "safe and dignified" returns. Refugees cannot safely return because their villages and homes have been destroyed. Furthermore, they face a high likelihood of forced military conscription, while those suspected of anti-coup activities risk immediate detention and torture.

Have any Rohingya been deported, and is the online hate campaign against Rohingya, and physical attacks on them, still taking place?

Because the government has not shared an ethnic breakdown of the detainees, there is no official information confirming whether any Rohingya refugees were among those deported on September 29.

Notably, Myanmar Foreign Ministry official Han Win Aung explicitly stated that this repatriation framework is strictly for "genuine citizens". Because Myanmar does not legally recognise the Rohingya as an ethnic group or grant them citizenship, this statement raises a major red flag. It suggests that if any Rohingya are deported, they will be systematically excluded from any legal protections or reintegration plans promised to "citizens".

As for the online hate campaign, it remains highly active. Xenophobic and hostile comments continue to flood the comment sections of news portals reporting on the Rohingya or refugees in general.

title: Κινητοποίηση αλληλεγγύης στον απεργό πείνας και πολιτικό πρόσφυγα Soner Inanç, Παρασκευή 2/10, 09.00 στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Εργασίας
content:
Από Solidarity with Migrants:


ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΚΙΝΗΤΟΠΟΙΗΣΗ/CALL TO DEMO [GR/ENG]


Κινητοποίηση στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Εργασίας την Παρασκευή 02/10 09:00 (Λεωφόρος Θηβών 196-198)


Ο Soner Inanç πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες είναι από τις 27 Αυγούστου σε απεργία πείνας σε καθεστώς κράτησης, ενώ κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση λόγω της ενδεχόμενης απόρριψης της αίτησής του για άσυλο. O πολιτικός πρόσφυγας Soner Inanç αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για τη δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park. Μετά την απορριπτική απόφαση ως προς το αρχικό αίτημα ασύλου του, Soner Inanç κατέθεσε αίτημα ακύρωσης και ακολούθησε όλες τις σχετικές διαδικασίες. Τέλη Ιουλίου, συνελήφθη και βρέθηκε σε διοικητική κράτησης στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου.


Ένα μήνα μετά, μεταφέρθηκε στη Θεσσαλονίκη με σκοπό την απέλαση του. Μετά από τέσσερις εβδομάδες στέρησης βιταμινών, αναγκαίων για την μη ύπαρξη μόνιμων επιπτώσεων, το αίτημα αυτό άρχισε να καλύπτεται όπως όφειλε εξαρχής μετά από συνεχή πολιτική κινητοποίηση και δημοσιογραφική κάλυψη για τον κίνδυνο τον οποίο διατρέχει αν δεν του χορηγηθούν. Το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου οφείλει παράλληλα ως απεργός πείνας ο Soner Inanç να παρακολουθείται από ανεξάρτητη ιατρική επιτροπή για να διασφαλιστεί η απρόσκοπτη άσκηση της ως πολιτική δράση με συγκεκριμένα αιτήματα: τη συνέχιση της διαδικασίας απόδοση ασύλου, την μη απέλαση του στην Τουρκία και την απελευθέρωσή του. Ο Soner δηλώνει αποφασισμένος να συνεχίσει στον αγώνα του, αφού κρατείται άδικα, περιμένοντας νέα απόφαση για το άσυλό του.


Ως Solidarity with Migrants, γνωρίσαμε τον Soner στο στρατόπεδο προσφύγων Οινοφύτων όπου πάντα προσπαθούσε με όλα τα δυνατά μέσα να υποστηρίζει τα δικαιώματα όλων των προσφύγων με μια βαθιά διεθνιστική προσήλωση. Η “λογική” των αποφάσεων της υπηρεσίας ασύλου καταδεικνύει τις συνέπειες των μεγάλων αλλαγών που έχουν επέλθει στο καθεστώς ασύλου τα τελευταία έτη καθώς έχουμε να κάνουμε με την καταστρατήγηση της έννοιας του πολιτικού ασύλου. Γι’αυτό και ο αγώνας του Soner είναι και αγώνας για το πολιτικό άσυλο γενικότερα και χρειάζεται τη στήριξη όλων μας.


Στηρίζουμε σε όλα τα επίπεδα την άμεση απελευθέρωση και απόδοση πολιτικού ασύλου. Σε αυτήν την κατεύθυνση καλούμε σε:


κινητοποίηση στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Εργασίας την Παρασκευή 02/10 09:00 (Λεωφόρος Θηβών 196-198)


Solidarity with Migrants


English


Soner Inanç, a political activist for workers’ rights and democratic freedoms, has been on a hunger strike in detention since August 27, while facing the threat of immediate deportation due to the possible rejection of his asylum application. Political refugee Soner Inanç was forced to flee Turkey because he has been targeted by the Turkish state for his activism and has already been imprisoned in the past for his participation in the Gezi Park movement. Following the rejection of his initial asylum application, Soner Inanç filed an appeal and followed all relevant procedures. In late July, he was arrested and placed in administrative detention at the Lavrio Police Station. A month later, he was transferred to Thessaloniki for the purpose of deportation.


After four weeks of being deprived of vitamins, which are essential to prevent permanent health consequences, this request began to be met as it should have been from the start, following continuous political mobilization and media coverage of the risk he faces if they are not provided. At the same time, the PROKEKA center in Paranesti must ensure that Soner Inanç, who is on a hunger strike, is monitored by an independent medical committee to guarantee the unimpeded exercise of his political action, which has specific demands: the continuation of his asylum proceedings, that he not be deported to Turkey, and his release.


Soner states that he is determined to continue his struggle, as he is being unjustly detained while awaiting a new decision on his asylum case. As Solidarity with Migrants, we met Soner at the Oinofyta refugee camp, where he always strove by every means possible to support the rights of all refugees with a deep internationalist commitment. The “logic” behind the asylum service’s decisions highlights the consequences of the major changes that have taken place in the asylum system in recent years, as we are witnessing the undermining of the concept of political asylum. author: daniel
title: hätte, hätte, menschenwürde
content:
Mit El Hishri ist ein ganzes System der Gewalt angeklagt

Das Komitee für Grundrechte und Demokratie ringt seit mittlerweile 46 Jahren mit den vielfältigen Fragen rund um Menschenrechte, radikale Demokratie und Menschenwürde – und wie diese von unten immerzu neu erkämpft werden müssen. In der Kolumne „Hätte, hätte, Menschenwürde“ schreiben die Komiteeler*innen ab sofort in jeder Ausgabe über aktuelle Ereignisse und Auseinandersetzungen, die sie umtreiben.

Am 16. Juli 2025 vollstreckten deutsche Behörden einen Strafbefehl des Internationalen Strafgerichtshofs (IStGH). Der Libyer Mohamed Ali El Hishri wurde am Flughafen Berlin-Brandenburg von der Bundespolizei verhaftet. Der Prozess soll am 4. Mai 2027 beginnen. Der IStGH verfolgt Einzelpersonen für Völkermord, Verbrechen gegen die Menschlichkeit und Kriegsverbrechen, wenn der Staat des Tatorts oder des Täters nicht willens oder fähig ist, zu ermitteln. Die Vollstreckung von Haftbefehlen des IStGH durch Deutschland ist keineswegs selbstverständlich: Friedrich Merz hatte bezüglich des Haftbefehls gegen den israelischen Ministerpräsidenten Netanjahu angekündigt, im Falle eines geplanten Deutschlandbesuchs dessen Ein- und Ausreise ohne Festnahme zu ermöglichen. Im Falle El Hishri ist die Anerkennung des IStGH für die Bundesregierung jedoch opportun.

Laut Anklage des IStGH soll Khaled Mohamed Ali El Hishri als hochrangiger Funktionär der bewaffneten Gruppe Spezialeinsatzkräfte (SDF/RADA) zuständig für den Bereich des Gefängnisses Mitiga in Libyschen Tripoli gewesen sein. Das Gefängnis in Mitiga zählt zu den staatlich anerkannten Gefängnissen, obwohl es faktisch von einer bewaffneten Miliz betrieben wird. Dort sind Frauen und Kinder inhaftiert. El Hishri werden Verbrechen an Gefangenen vorgeworfen, unter ihnen libysche Staatsangehörige sowie Migrant- *innen und Geflüchtete. Die Anklage umfasst Folter und andere unmenschliche Handlungen, Vergewaltigung und andere Formen sexualisierter Gewalt, Mord, versuchten Mord und Versklavung. Im Dezember 2025 wurde El Hishri nach Den Haag überstellt.

Insbesondere Schwarze Menschen aus den Ländern Afrikas werden in Libyen versklavt und sind systematischer Ausbeutung und Misshandlung ausgesetzt. Durch Erpressung, Zwangsarbeit, Lösegeldforderungen und Menschenhandel werden sie zur Ware degradiert. Das Geschäft mit Flüchtenden ist ein äußerst profitabler Wirtschaftszweig, das Mitiga-Gefängnis ist Teil davon. Mit offizieller Anerkennung können Gefängnisse zudem Hilfsgüter und Gelder von Organisationen wie IOM (Internationale Organisation für Migration) beziehen. Sie sind Teil eines Systems gewaltvoller Rückführungen (Pull- bzw. Pushbacks), das die EU-Mitgliedstaaten mittels Institutionen wie der Europäischen Grenzschutzagentur Frontex und Milizen der sogenannten Libyschen Küstenwache erschaffen haben, um die Migration nach Europa zu minimieren. Die EU-Staaten, darunter Deutschland, finanzieren, unterstützen und trainieren die sogenannte libysche Küstenwache, die Überwachungsflugzeuge von Frontex informieren diese über Boote, die sich von Libyen aus über das Mittelmeer in Richtung Europa bewegen. Auf diese Weise werden Flüchtende aufgegriffen und zurück nach Libyen in eben dieses Gewaltsystem gezwungen, von dem das Mitiga-Gefängnis ein brutaler Baustein ist.

Bislang haben sich bereits 120 Überlebende des Mitiga-Gefängnisses beim IStGH gemeldet, um Zeugnis abzulegen über das, was sie unter El Hishri in Libyen haben erleben müssen. Für viele von ihnen bietet eine Anhörung in Den Haag die erste Gelegenheit, das Erlebte offiziell zu schildern. Für sie alle ist es außerdem von entscheidender Bedeutung, dass in dem Prozess nicht allein El Hishri anklagt wird. Die Überlebenden wollen, dass deutlich wird, wie die EU-Politik zu der Gewalt beiträgt, der sie in Libyen ausgesetzt waren, nachdem sie durch die libyschen Milizen auf dem Meer aufgegriffen, zurückgeschafft und inhaftiert wurden. Sie fordern, dass die Verantwortung der Europäischen Staaten ermittelt wird.

Folter und Misshandlung dauern an

Während El Hishri Verbrechen aus den Jahren 2014 bis 2020 vorgeworfen werden, gehen Folter und Misshandlungen in Mitiga und anderen staatlichen und in den nicht-offiziellen Gefängnissen Libyens bis heute weiter. Wir müssen zur Kenntnis nehmen, dass diese Gefängnisse faktisch längst das tun, was die EU-Staaten mit GEAS und den Return Hubs planen: das Festsetzen von Migrant*innen im Vorfeld der EU-Außengrenzen mit beschränktem bis keinem Zugang zu …

Λευτεριά στην Παλαιστίνη, λευτεριά στον Λίβανο.


Η

7η Οκτωβρίου

 ήταν μια πράξη αντιαποικιακής και αντιιμπεριαλιστικής αντίστασης. Μια συνέχεια της αντίστασης που χρονολογείται από τη στιγμή της ίδρυσης του κράτους του “Ισραήλ” το 1948, αλλά και ακόμη νωρίτερα, κατά τη διάρκεια της βρετανικής αποικιακής κατοχής. Ήταν ένας λαός και ένα κίνημα που ξεσηκώθηκαν ενάντια στην κατοχή. Η ημέρα αυτή θα συνεχίσει να τιμάται ως τέτοια για τις επόμενες γενιές, ακόμη και αν οι σιωνιστές και οι ιμπεριαλιστές προσπαθήσουν με κάθε μέσο να ελέγξουν και να αλλάξουν το αφήγημα. Τα αλεξίπτωτα πλαγιάς που πετούσαν πάνω από τον φράχτη προς την κατεχόμενη Παλαιστίνη, ο φράχτης που περιέκλειε τη Γάζα και γκρεμίστηκε από τους ανθρώπους που εκδιώχθηκαν από τη γη τους πριν από δεκαετίες: αυτές οι εικόνες δεν θα ξεχαστούν και θα παραμείνουν στη μνήμη μας ως σύμβολα της αντίστασης του Παγκόσμιου Νότου.


Η απάντηση της σιωνιστικής οντότητας, με την υποστήριξη των ΗΠΑ, υπήρξε ανελέητη. Η Γάζα έχει ισοπεδωθεί από τους βομβαρδισμούς και, παρόλο που γίνεται λόγος για κατάπαυση του πυρός, συνεχίζουν να βομβαρδίζουν και να πυροβολούν αδιακρίτως. Ο Λίβανος και η Συρία τελούν υπό κατοχή και δέχονται συνεχείς επιθέσεις από τη σιωνιστική οντότητα. Οι κυβερνήσεις αυτών των περιοχών καταστέλλουν την αντίσταση και την εναντίωση στη Δύση και το “Ισραήλ” στα εδάφη τους, ενεργώντας ως εντολοδόχοι των ΗΠΑ. Όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν ενώ το “Ισραήλ” καταλαμβάνει όλο και περισσότερα εδάφη, αποσταθεροποιώντας περαιτέρω την περιοχή.


Το κράτος του “Ισραήλ” και οι ΗΠΑ καταστρέφουν ορισμένες από τις αρχαιότερες περιοχές με συνεχή κατοίκηση στην ιστορία του πολιτισμού, στην Παλαιστίνη, τον Λίβανο, τη Συρία και το Ιράν. author: Monthly Review Press
title: In Amsterdam in November? Head to Pakuis de Zwijger for Chris dePloeg’s “The Exterminating Empire”
content:
Join

Pakuis de Zwijger

 for a conversation with author Chris de Ploeg about his new book, a radical and urgent indictment of the global capitalist system and the imperial violence it unleashes upon people and planet alike. At its core, the book argues that genocide and ecocide are not tragic byproducts of capitalism – they are its fundamental features. Together with renowned climate author Jason Hickel (in person), frontline Palestinian surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah (joining online) and our moderator, climate justice activist and researcher Harriët Bergman, we will dive deeper into the interconnections of the great challenges of our time–and more importantly, how to fight back. There will also be cultural performances from Chihiro Geuzebroek and brothers Chris and Max de Ploeg, tying their ancestral struggles in Bolivia and Armenia to the global struggle for liberation.


REVIEWS:


Counterpunch

, “

Resisting Annihilation: Reviewing “The Exterminating Empire”

, by Seth Sandronsky


“…de Ploeg, who does far more than compile lists of atrocities, draws parallels between the American holocaust of the native inhabitants’ relations with buffaloes and Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and their farming of olive trees. Land theft and separating those living on the land from it are nothing new. The author has skin in the game, given his family survived the Armenian genocide and Nazi holocaust…”


Counterpunch

, “

Capitalism is Waging War on Palestine While Creating a Burning Planet

” by Daniel Falcone:


Daniel Falcone:

What is the central argument of

The Exterminating Empire

 and how is the book structured? It looks as though the book serves as an intervention as well as an addition to current scholarship.  


Chris Kaspar de Ploeg:

 I open the book with some jarring facts that seem paradoxical at first sight. We need about 30 percent of our productive capacity to

give everyone on the planet a good life

. Not just the basics like housing, clothing and healthcare, but also modern appliances like refrigerators, laptops, access to the internet and more. At the same time, that standard of living is denied to about

80 percent of the world population

. Green energy has been cheaper than fossil fuels for years, yet climate breakdown is only accelerating. We could

solve world hunger

 with about 0.03 percent of global GDP, but hunger is only increasing.


That looks like an extraordinarily wasteful system, and it is. The point, however, is that under capitalism, these are not paradoxes at all. In fact, they are signs of capital’s success. Under our current economic system, the primary goal, ruthlessly pursued, is

profit maximization

. That profit maximization is reached through pushing down costs–and we are those costs, our labour, our environments, our lives–and by conquering markets, often through a mix of military and economic warfare. That essentially puts

capitalism on a warpath against life

. The system is working exactly as it is supposed to.


We see, for example, that profit rates are higher in the fossil fuel industry because it essentially

functions through monopolies

, despite the higher costs. We see that the military-industrial complex is growing exponentially, targeting any vestiges of resistance against

US-led global hegemony

, which globalized harsh budget cuts in social welfare, healthcare and education. These very conditions of

structural impoverishment

 then create the conditions of desperation necessary for people and countries to accept their status as sources for cheap labour, resources and land for global corporations, mostly centered in the Global North.


In the book I write about a dialectic between slavery and genocide, and between structural genocide and active genocide. A good way to understand that relationship is by going back to the

We Charge Genocide petition

, which was presented in 1951 at the United Nations by William L. Patterson, on behalf of the

Civil Rights Congress

. He estimated that, since the abolition of slavery, some 10,000 black people had been lynched, often for something as small as looking a white woman in the eyes. These lynchings were not hidden affairs, but were a

public spectacle

, for which neighbors came together, and pictures were spread on postcards across the country.


Patterson

 goes on to argue that this kind of active violence serves a deeper purpose. It was meant to intimidate the black masses to accept lower living standards …

Et si nous reprenions le pouvoir sur le travail, la production et la valeur

 

?


Le groupe lyonnais de Réseau Salariat vous invite à son apéro de rentrée : une rencontre ouverte à tous.tes, pour faire connaissance, échanger et discuter autour d'un verre.


Cette soirée sera l'occasion de découvrir ou d'approfondir les propositions portées par l'association : salaire à vie (salaire attaché à la qualification personnelle), extension de la Sécurité sociale, démocratie économique et communisme déjà-là.


Ces réflexions s'inscrivent notamment dans le prolongement des travaux de l'économiste et sociologue Bernard Friot, figure la plus médiatique de l'association Réseau Salariat.


L'association se présente comme un mouvement d'éducation populaire qui cherche à penser et à diffuser des alternatives au capitalisme à partir des conquêtes sociales existantes, en particulier le régime général de Sécurité sociale.


Que vous connaissiez déjà les thèses de Réseau Salariat, que vous les découvriez ou que vous ayez simplement envie d'en discuter, vous êtes les bienvenu·es.


Rendez-vous mercredi 7 octobre à partir de 18 h 30, aux Clameurs, à Lyon.

author: ROAPE
title: What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?
content:
John Molyneux’s classic statement of Marxist theory and practice

What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? was first published in 1984. The short book provided an incredibly sophisticated description of Marx’s method, and his relentless and insistent focus on the core agency of the working class.


Only the working class – however it is interpreted, described or labelled in social theory – can deliver a revolutionary anti-capitalist project. There cannot be, Molyneux argued, any substitute – no enlightened project of state development, or ‘socialist’ military leadership who deliver socialism on behalf of working people. Molyneux – in restating Marx’s central tenet – emphasised the role of the working class in their self-emancipation. Marx was the original prophet of the self-emancipation by working people. Without this class, and this project, there is simply no Marxism, no socialism, and no possibility of international revolution.


For an African audience the book speaks to multiple failed projects of socialism delivered by military coups, ‘enlightened’ governments and guerrilla movements. Each of these movements at different times dressed themselves in the language of Marxism, class and anti-imperialism but systematically broke genuine efforts at working class power.


What is the Real Marxist Tradition

? speaks directly to those on the continent trying to find a way to a genuine and emancipatory theory and practice of liberation.


Molyneux’ brilliant short book has now been reissued by the UK based publisher Bookmarks, and the Ugandan publisher Editor House Facility (EHF) who focus on readers across the African continent.


The new issue of the book comes with a major new introduction by the Ghanian socialist Gyekye Tanoh. Tanoh writes about the development and transformation of the working class on the continent since Molyneux wrote the book, and the continued capacity of this class to bring about socialist and revolutionary transformation across Africa.  


Join us for the launch of the African edition of

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 on 22 October at 18.30 (BST) with Gyekye Tanoh, Tafadzwa Choto

, 

Martin Empson and Mark Thomas. Reserve your place 

here

.


For readers based in Africa, John Molyneux’s 

What is the Real Marxist Tradition?

 can be purchased through Editor House Facility


here

. 


Endorsements of the book:


‘John Molyneux cuts through a century of distortion to recover Marxism’s authentic, revolutionary essence. This classic work distinguishes between living theory and dead orthodoxy, showing that Marxism is not a relic of the past but a vital method for understanding and transforming the world. It is essential reading for anyone seeking to understand capitalism and how to change it. For young activists and students alike, it is a must-read as it offers a powerful weapon for today’s struggles.’ 


Tafadzwa Choto

, International Socialist Organisation, Zimbabwe


‘In this book, John Molyneux undertakes a principled exercise by applying Marxism as a “method of analysis” to Marxism itself. He thereby provides not just a description of what Marxism is, but a method for detecting what isn’t. His application of this exercise—in the form of an autopsy of the interests and classes represented by three self-proclaimed Marxist tendencies—provides a valuable model for defining Marxist politics and organizations in our own contexts while enabling us to avoid the “hybrid ideologies of the petty bourgeoisie.” This is crucial, for us in the Global South, where reality differs greatly from that of Europe, thereby demanding a Marxism of contextualized design, not rigid imitation. The method offered is therefore a vital tool in enabling Marxist projects capable of fulfilling its role in “guiding revolutions to victory.” Such is true whether in the Global South or in global contexts marked by increasing economic complications and the co-option of Marxism by bourgeois ideologies fighting for survival amid the clear failure of neoliberal models … One need not agree with all of Molyneux’s conclusions to find his method a timely and indispensable resource.’


Muzan Alneel

,Marxist researcher and writer from Sudan

What is the Real Marxist Tradition in Africa?

ROAPE

title: "If Bolsonaro wins, they kill us; if Lula wins, they let us die.” : On the 2026 Elections in Brazil
content:
In Brazil, the third term of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers’ Party is drawing to a close. Lula could win a fourth term—making him the most-elected politician in the country’s history—if he defeats the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. However, Flávio Bolsonaro—son of the man dubbed the “Trump of the Tropics,” who attempted

a
coup d’état in 2023

 strikingly similar to the one Donald Trump attempted in 2021—is dangerously close to taking the lead in the polls.


It is time to assess the threats that a new Bolsonaro administration would pose, as well as the risks that will remain or emerge under a continuing center-left government. We spoke with fellow Brazilian anarchists active on a variety of fronts about the challenges that both scenarios could pose to human beings, the environment, and social movements resisting capitalism and colonialism.


Flavio Bolsonaro in a photo-op with Trump in May 2026 during a meeting at which he lobbied for the US to designate Brazilian drug cartels as “terrorist groups.”


What the 2026 Elections Mean for Brazil and the Americas


The 2026 election will determine to what extent the gains achieved through hard-fought social struggles are stripped away. Just as Trump returned to power via the 2024 election, there is a risk that Flávio Bolsonaro could resume his father’s attacks on the working class, marginalized groups, women, Indigenous peoples, and the environment. The Workers’ Party and the left in general have not managed to produce new figures to succeed their charismatic leader; without Lula, they appear doomed to electoral defeat.


There is a risk that the left will fail to field an effective new candidate for 2030, when Lula will no longer be eligible for reelection. It is also likely that, if elected, Lula could fall victim to the so-called “

incumbency
crisis

“—a pattern that has emerged in elections worldwide this decade. Leaders on both the left and the right see their public standing erode after taking office, as they fail to address the inexorable impact of capitalism on the lives of ordinary people. Symbolism and abstract ideology carry significant weight in the increasingly polarized political landscapes of bourgeois electoral politics, and around the world, the ruling class is relying less and less on the carrot and more and more on the stick.


Therefore, it is likely that the far right will soon return to power. This is a reality we must face. It could happen in 2030, but it could occur as early as 2026.


This is taking place in a context in which Trump’s United States is attempting to reorganize the world order through force, showing everyone what anarchists have always known: that representative democracy, international law, and institutions like the United Nations exist at the pleasure of the ruling class and will not protect us. In the course of its first fourteen months in power, the second Trump administration toppled two heads of state—killing the Iranian leader and abducting the Venezuelan president. In both cases, there was open talk of seizing the oil from these territories; in Venezuela, the administration successfully stole billions of barrels, which are now under Washington’s control.


As head of state, Flávio Bolsonaro would voluntarily hand over Brazilian workers, forests, and land to US imperial interests. We are already in a dire situation under the neoliberal arrangement that Lula manages; with a fascist who is beholden to the US in power, the struggle for survival would become even harder. Furthermore, the oil, minerals, rivers, and forests in the territory known as Brazil would serve to fuel the technological, military, and nuclear arms race that endangers life across the entire planet.


The United States is openly attempting to interfere in Brazilian elections to favor Bolsonaro by sending “observers” to

question
election results

 and threatening to impose further tariffs on Brazil. At the same time, the US-based company Meta—which controls much of the content circulating on social media—is

blocking
Lula’s campaign content

 just weeks before the election without explanation. The same elites with the same reactionary agenda control both military power and the companies that dominate technology and digital communication.

title: Die Welle der Ultrarechten in Lateinamerika: Das Wirtschaftsprogramm der Libertären ist kein Weg zur Freiheit, sondern zur Entfremdung und Unterdrückung
content:
Dossier


„… In den letzten Jahren sind die Regierungen in mehreren lateinamerikanischen Ländern von einer Welle rechtsgerichteter, liberal-konservativer politischer Akteure übernommen worden. Auf der Grundlage klassischer neoliberaler und konservativer Programme gewannen Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, Daniel Noboa in Ecuador, Jair Bolsonaro in Brasilien und Javier Milei in Argentinien die Präsidentschaftswahlen in ihren Ländern. Obwohl es Bolsonaro 2022 nicht gelang, seine Amtszeit als Präsident zu verlängern, befürworteten rund 50 Prozent der brasilianischen Wähler seine ultrarechte Agenda. Dadurch steht die politische Macht des siegreichen Sozialdemokraten Lula da Silva auf wackeligen Füßen. Im Falle Perus wurde der linksgerichtete Präsident Pedro Castillo durch seine frühere Vizepräsidentin Dina Boluarte ersetzt – mit der Zustimmung und der unmittelbaren Allianz der Ultrarechten im Kongress…“

Beitrag des Redaktionsausschusses Minga

in der Übersetzung von Susanne Schartz-Laux am 22. März 2024 in amerika21


 und mehr daraus/dazu:


Was die extreme Rechte in Lateinamerika so stark macht


„Auf dem lateinamerikanischen Kontinent schreitet eine reaktionäre Welle voran. Mit Ausnahme von Mexiko und Brasilien – den beiden Großmächten der Region – sowie Uruguay und Guatemala haben die übrigen Länder (Argentinien, Chile, Kolumbien, Bolivien, Peru, Ecuador, Paraguay, El Salvador, Honduras, Panama usw.) autoritäre rechtsextreme Regierungen gewählt, auch wenn teilweise in Stichwahlen und mit knapper Mehrheit. Dabei handelt es sich um Regierungen, die eine Bevölkerungsstimmung der Feindseligkeit und der politischen Aggressivität zum Ausdruck bringen. Es ist nicht dieselbe traditionelle liberale oder „republikanische“ Rechte, die den triumphierenden Neoliberalismus der 1980er Jahre prägte. (…) Die extreme Rechte von heute verspricht keine Zukunft des Weltfriedens auf der Grundlage der Märkte, sondern eine apokalyptische Säuberung von den Gottlosen, die sich den „natürlichen“ Hierarchien widersetzen: Arbeitgeber:innen über Arbeitnehmer:innen, Mann über der Frau, „weiße“ Hautfarbe über alle anderen people of colour und Reiche über den Armen. (…)


Im Gegensatz zu früheren Phasen des Aufstiegs der extremen Rechten in Lateinamerika, die jeweils 30 Jahre andauerten, stützen sich die aktuellen Kräfte jedoch auf ein unvollständiges und kurzsichtiges Gesellschaftsprojekt, das wirtschaftlich gesehen den weltweiten Trends zuwiderläuft. (…)Doch wenn diese extreme Rechte kein hoffnungsvolles Wirtschaftsprogramm vorlegen kann, wieso verfügt sie dann trotzdem über eine beträchtliche Wählerschaft? Eine Ursache ist sicherlich die Enttäuschung über die progressiven Kräfte, die die Wirtschaftskrise (Inflation, Versorgungsengpässe, Rezession) nicht überwinden konnten. Doch diese Erklärung allein reicht nicht aus.


Die radikale Rechte zieht mit zwei Schwertern ins Feld, die ihre hohen Zustimmungswerte erklären: Zum einen ist es das Versprechen, einige der wichtigsten Gründe der Wirtschaftskrise zu bekämpfen, und zum anderen das Versprechen, den von der Krise Geschädigten moralische Wiedergutmachung widerfahren zu lassen. Das erste Schwert zerfällt rasch und unwiderruflich; das zweite jedoch wird mit feuriger Geschicklichkeit geschwungen. Der rachsüchtige Hass der neuen Staatsräson gegen Menschenrechte, Migrant:innen, Linke, Kommunist:innen, die Kirchnerist:innen, Indigene, Feministinnen oder jeden Anflug von sozialer Gleichheit spielt die Rolle einer kollektiven Buße, die vom gescheiterten Wohlstandsversprechen ablenkt. Wenn es schon keine glückliche Zukunft gibt, dann soll es wenigstens das Vergnügen an der Grausamkeit geben. Opfer sind diejenigen, die sich als unversöhnlich anders betrachten. Diese moralische Perversion der Hoffnung zerreißt das soziale Gefüge. Und auch wenn sie nur von kurzer Dauer ist, werden ihre Folgen für den gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt lange anhalten. Man kann ihr nicht allein mit umgekehrter Wut begegnen. Auch wenn in Krisenzeiten eine Personifizierung der Schuldigen für soziale Missstände notwendig ist – nur dass sie sich in diesem Fall auf eine winzige Minderheit der Mächtigen konzentriert –, ist vor allem eine mutige Wiederherstellung einer glaubwürdigen Hoffnung auf ein produktivistisches und auf soziale Gerechtigkeit ausgerichtetes Projekt erforderlich. author: Julius Gavroche
title: The subject, the proletariat, anarchist organisation and other nostalgias
content:
Barricade in Seville, Summer 1936


by Laura Vicente


It is quite possible that no one will pay much attention to this brief piece, but just in case, I will say in anticipation that my aim is modest and that I do not intend to be polemical, although I would not mind sharing arguments and thoughts, moving beyond the stereotypes we all hold that lead us to be obtuse and, at times, blind.


There are comrades who have been pondering the existence, or lack thereof, of the proletariat for some time, searching for the lost revolutionary subject, building “the” anarchist organization capable of developing “a” program, “a” strategy, and concrete tactics that will lead us down the path of revolution. I have not read all their writings, I am sorry to say, because I am exhausted by anarchism’s difficulty in imagining a way out of capitalism that does not involve returning to the past and to nostalgia, even melancholy. This is how two authors, Julie Graham and Katherine Gibson [who go under the pen name J. K. Gibson-Graham] perceive it in their book

A Post-Capitalist Politics

. They claim that a lack of imagination is a pathology of the left, something that reminds me of the “melancholy” of the left, applicable to anarchism, which Wendy Brown discusses in her essay on this topic. Leftist melancholy is a stance in which attachment to an identity or a political analysis of the past is stronger than interest in current possibilities for mobilisation, alliance, or transformation. The melancholic subject identifies with lost ideals and experiences their absence as feelings of desolation and dejection. This fixation on the past has a clear connection to the total paranoid theory that says nothing can happen. Fisher calls it a “severe Leninist superego”.

[1]


The proletariat, the working class, was the subject of the revolution in another era of industrial development that ended in the mid-20th century, not because there were no other subjects, but because of the power of the narrative that championed the proletariat. When we speak of workers’ consciousness as the foundation of their “being a subject,” it seems we’re talking about something pre-existing that simply needs to be awakened, discovered. But consciousness-raising, in reality, is a practice of collective discussion that underscores the inequalities under which people collectively live. Consciousness does not pre-exist, it is not given, but rather it must be constructed from our place within a structure of inequality (capitalism, patriarchy, white supremacy, colonialism). The way to construct it is with other people who share a similar material existence.


Class consciousness has receded because the idea that there is no alternative to capitalism has advanced; the narrative has fallen apart.


On the other hand, holding closed seminars, waiting for the right information, the advanced political and ideological discussion that shapes a well-defined strategy to “awaken” the revolutionary subject, bringing to the surface a situation capable of awakening action by the people or any other subject, does not fit with what I have learned in history, either today or yesterday. No theory has ever transformed reality.


I have not forgotten of the need to “organise anarchism” as if it were not already organized. It gives the impression that the real aim is to impose order on anarchist diversity and multiplicity, transforming these interconnected, horizontal, decentralised, and non-hierarchical networks into parts of a whole that must be “the” effective, hyper-organised anarchist organization with strong militancy, etc.

[2]


I recently said in an anarchist space that this debate is a men’s debate. The reality is that, even with women involved, the writings I have seen are by men. Reflecting on this, I concluded that women, and those perceived as such, have long known that there are other revolutionary subjects (think of

Mujeres Libres

, creating their own revolution between 1936 and 1939 and being ignored by the world, which is why I want to highlight them).


The struggles and events of the feminist movement were able to mobilise social transformation on an unprecedented scale, without resorting to a vanguard party or any of the other “needs” we have associated with political organisation (strategy, tactics, ideological narratives, modelled revolutions, etc.). title: Spencer Beswick - Building the American Anarchist Movement
content:
Author

: Spencer Beswick

Title

: Building the American Anarchist Movement

Subtitle

: Radical Collectives and Continental Convergences in the 1980s

Date

: 2026

Notes

: Journal for the Study of Radicalism (2026) 20 (1): 29–51. https://doi.org/10.14321/jstudradi.20.1.0029

Source

: Retrieved on October 4, 2026 from https://anarchistnews.org/content/building-american-anarchist-movement


 “Bowl a strike, not a spare—Revolution everywhere!” Members of the Revolutionary Anarchist Bowling League (RABL) chanted bowling-themed slogans as they marched against President Ronald Reagan's threat to invade Nicaragua in 1988. Acting within a broad progressive coalition, RABL helped shut down major sections of downtown Minneapolis for three days in an outpouring of rebellion against the Reagan administration's covert wars in Central America. Events reached a dramatic climax when a masked protester threw a bowling ball through the window of a military recruitment office.

[1]

 The crash of the broken glass marked the beginning of a new era of anarchist militancy in the United States. The rage of a generation of young people raised in Reagan's America threatened to explode.


 Reflecting this mood, the pilot edition of what became the

Love and Rage

 anarchist newspaper (published from 1990 to 1998) was simply called

RAGE!

 The pilot, which was distributed at an action at the Pentagon in 1988, reflected growing anger at the Reagan administration's wars at home and abroad, including the war on drugs. Promised a “new morning in America,” a generation of disaffected young people raised in the alienation of the suburbs found themselves shut out of political life. Many of their parents lost their unionized factory jobs to neoliberal outsourcing or were kicked off welfare. They grappled with the reality of skyrocketing inequality, precarious jobs, and violent policing. The hopes of social democracy—not to mention the liberatory movements of the 1960s and 1970s—appeared dead, and mainstream society seemingly offered little worth saving. Meanwhile, Reagan crushed the dreams of a better world in Central America by funding and training Guatemalan death squads, Nicaraguan Contras, and violent Salvadoran elites.


 But dissidents emerged out of the cracks of the new society. A rising generation of young people encountered anarchism in mosh pits at punk shows and in street fights against fascists and police. A core group of anarchists across the country began to build a continental revolutionary movement. This article explores how several key collectives—including the Revolutionary Anarchist Bowling League, the Revolutionary Socialist League, the Youth Greens, and the Vermont Family—revitalized US anarchist theory and practice in the 1980s. Together, they formed a pole around which the diffuse anarchist scene began to cohere into a movement capable of coordinating strategic action across the country. Activists coming from these diverse groups (and many more) would expand the anarchist milieu in the 1990s and shape the turn-of-the-century antiglobalization movement.

[2]

 Members of each group became involved with Love and Rage, an organization that used its widely distributed newspaper as a catalyst to build first an anarchist network and then a membership-based Revolutionary Anarchist Federation that shaped the movement's direction. But first, local anarchist groups needed to encounter each other, exchange ideas, and build connections across North America.


 This encounter occurred in large part through a series of four continental convergences that took place from 1986 to 1989 in Chicago, Minneapolis, Toronto, and San Francisco. Very little has been written about these gatherings. Sociologist Lesley Wood posits that social movement theorists tend to ignore these kinds of convergences in part because the disciplinary norms of what counts as social movement activity reduce them to the level of cultural background to the “real” organizing.

[3]

 Beyond the gatherings, historians have written little about anarchism in the late twentieth century. Anarchist history typically focuses on earlier periods, and the burgeoning history of the United States in the late twentieth century has generally dealt much more with the rise of the Right than the evolution of anarchism and the Left.

[4]

 Yet it was in this period that anarchism was reborn as a major tendency on the American Left since marginalization in the early twentieth century …

title: Le Projet-Evasions a besoin de ptis sous
content:
Pour qu'on puisse continuer notre agitation sociale on se lance dans un mois de recherche de fonds.


Le Projet-Evasions c'est un réseau multilingue d'amitiés anarchistes qui existe depuis 2019. Après sept joyeuses années à mener nos petites activités*, le temps est venu pour nous de faire appel à votre soutien.


Par « petites activités » on veut dire : faire des trucs dans lesquels on voit du sens, un potentiel émancipateur, révolutionnaire et des perspectives anarchistes. Par « trucs » on parle de création de plein de contenus (livres, brochures, articles, podcast, capsules audio, stickers, revues, cartes postales, jeux, expositions, affiches),

d'ateliers et de présentations

, de création d'outil pour se former à l'antirep et d'un gros travail de diffusion. Tout ça dans plein de langues différentes paske, l'a-t'on-dit, on est un projet multilingue à cheval entre plusieurs zones linguistiques.


On crée souvent du contenu qu'on a envie de partager mais aussi des outils dont d'autres personnes peuvent se saisir. La majorité du temps on crée notre contenu nous même et quelques fois on collabore avec des personnes externes. On diffuse toutes les versions papiers à prix libre, chaque personne peut décider librement, en fonction de ses propres capacités, de ce qu'elle peut et veut nous donner en échange. En parallèle, toute les

versions digitales

 de ce que l'on produit sont disponibles gratuitement sur notre site internet.


L'argent qu'on a est majoritairement utilisé pour payer les impressions. Même si on travaille principalement avec une imprimerie camarade qui nous soutien de ouf, les frais d'impression restent notre dépense principale. En deuxième place se trouvent les frais d'envoi qui augmentent chaque année. Quand on envoie à l'étranger, les frais de poste et de douane sont souvent plus élevés que les frais d'impression de la publication que l'on envoie. À côté de ça, on achète aussi régulièrement des livres et d'autres publications auto-éditée qu'on rediffuse à prix libre. À l'âge d'or de notre trésorerie (désormais revolu), on a plusieurs fois pu soutenir des anarchistes en prison, des projets en quête de thunes et quelques rares fois défrayer un peu de nos voyages et du travail que l'on fait. En dernière position dans nos dépenses se trouve les frais de notre site internet et deux trois bricoles logistiques.


À l'heure où l'on écrit ce texte notre caisse comporte exactement 741 francs suisse et 123 euros et si l'on souhaite la remplir à nouveau c'est qu'on a plusieurs projets qui seront bientôt prêts pour à être envoyé à l'impression. Comme élément de comparaison : l'impression des 1000 exemplaires de

Illégal élégance

 nous a coûté 3000.- soit 3.- l'exemplaire et l'impression des 4000 livres sur les

interrogatoires

 nous avait coûté 16'000.- soit 4.- par livre.

content:
Συνέντευξη με τον Αρτάν, μέλος της Αναρχικής Συλλογικότητας

Smokva

 των Σκοπίων, που διοργάνωσε το προ ημερών 18

ο

 Βαλκανικό Αναρχικό Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου. Διατυπώνει μια πρώτη αποτίμηση, που επικεντρώθηκαν οι συζητήσεις, σε τι συνεισέφερε στα ευρύτερα ζητήματα και κυρίως ποιες αποφασίστηκε να είναι οι άμεσες δράσεις.


>Πώς αποτιμάται το 4ήμερο Βαλκανικό Αναρχικό Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου στα Σκόπια;


Όπως είχαμε την ευκαιρία να συζητήσουμε, είχαμε μια πολύ ιδιαίτερη εμπειρία αυτού του φεστιβάλ στα Σκόπια. Αποτελεί μια από τις σημαντικές συνεισφορές στην περιοχή.


Τρία ή τέσσερα χρόνια πριν δεν θα είχαμε τέτοια δυνατότητα. Αλλά επειδή στο προηγούμενο ΒΑΒ στη Θεσσαλονίκη που ήμασταν περίπου 20 ακτιβιστές από εδώ γεννήθηκε η ιδέα να διεξαχθεί στα Σκόπια, κάτι που αποτέλεσε κίνητρο για εμάς και αμέσως αρχίσαμε την προετοιμασία του.


Έτσι άρχισε να ενεργοποιείται ένας κόσμος, ιδιαίτερα νεολαίοι που πριν δεν είχαν κάποια εμπλοκή με τα κινήματα. Κάτι που το είδαμε όλοι μας αυτές τις ημέρες με τη συμμετοχή τόσων ανθρώπων από την πόλη, εδώ.


>Σε ποια θέματα επικεντρώθηκαν οι εκδηλώσεις και συζητήσεις;


Ξεκινήσαμε από τοπικά ζητήματα της περιοχής αλλά και ευρύτερα διεθνή ζητήματα, όπως η γενοκτονία στη Γάζα και η διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη στην Παλαιστίνη, η αντίδραση στον νέο μιλιταρισμό ιδιαίτερα στην Ευρώπη, η καταπίεση και καταστολή κα. Έτσι είχαμε αρκετές συζητήσεις πάνω σε αυτά τα θέματα και πώς θα οργανώσουμε την αντίστασή μας.


Επίσης, είχαμε συζητήσεις για τις πολιτικές, τους τρόπους οργάνωσης και τις κινητοποιήσεις ενάντια στον φασισμό στα Βαλκάνια, αλλά και στην Ευρώπη, και θα συνεχιστεί η συζήτηση μέχρι το επόμενο ΒΑΒ. Κάτι που αποτέλεσε συνεισφορά των συντρόφων που ήρθαν από ευρωπαϊκές χώρες, να μην περιοριστούμε στα Βαλκάνια αλλά ευρύτερα διεθνώς.


Άλλωστε τα Βαλκάνια σήμερα αποτελούν σημαντικό σημείο επικέντρωσης των αναρχικών διεθνώς. Και αυτό είναι ένα στοίχημα το πως μια βαλκανική οργάνωση μπορεί να συνεισφέρει ευρύτερα, κάτι που αναγνωρίζεται. Ήταν πρόκληση 14 χρόνια μετά την προηγούμενη διοργάνωση εδώ στα Σκόπια.


>Ποια μπορούμε να πούμε ότι είναι το σημαντικότερο χαρακτηριστικό αυτού του ΒΑΒ;


Νομίζω ένα από τα σημαντικότερα ήταν η μεγάλη συμμετοχή στις συνελεύσεις πάνω σε ζητήματα δράσης. Δεν μείναμε μόνο στο επίπεδο της κατάθεσης πολιτικών ιδεών αλλά στην επεξεργασία συγκεκριμένων βημάτων δράσης και όχι μόνο στα Βαλκάνια. Έτσι ελήφθησαν 3 συγκεκριμένες αποφάσεις.


Μια περιφερειακή και διεθνής αντιμιλιταριστική οργάνωση και μία ημέρα διεθνούς δράσης κατά του μιλιταρισμού. Όπως επίσης συζητήσαμε και για τον τόπο διοργάνωσης του επόμενου ΒΑΒ που θα καταληχθεί στον επόμενο μήνα.

Саверио Мерлино пишет в первом номере этого журнала[1]: «Анархисты всегда страдали и остались бессильными вследствие разногласия, никогда не прекращавшегося в их среде между индивидуалистами и коммунистами, которые так же далеки друг от друга, как северный полюс от южного, и сходятся лишь в одном пункте: в ненависти к парламентаризму».

По моему мнению, Мерлино преувеличивает, приписывая бессилие анархистов разногласиям между коммунистами и индивидуалистами. Когда случаи оказывались благоприятными для действия и, главным образом, когда хотели и могли сделать что-либо практическое, забыв о разногласиях, коммунисты и индивидуалисты (я говорю, конечно, о тех, кто были действительно анархистами и, следовательно, верными принципу «ни господ, ни рабов») снова боролись бок-о-бок. Бессилие анархистов зависело от множества других причин, особенно от отсутствия немедленно годной к применению практической программы, за исключением, конечно, тех общих обстоятельств, среди которых они были вынуждены действовать. Иными словами, дело заключается в том, что они смотрели на идеал, опережая этим своё время, и поэтому, вместо того чтобы воплощать свои идеи в жизнь, считали себя обязанными своим апостольством приблизить тот час, когда осуществление станет возможным.

Мерлино еще преувеличивает, когда пишет, что идеи коммунистов и идеи индивидуалистов (я все время говорю, конечно, об анархистах искренних и сознательных) диаметрально противоположны: так могло бы показаться, если принять литературные и «философские» уклоны некоторых лиц всерьез; но на самом деле речь идет, чаще всего, о словесных недоразумениях.

Анархический индивидуализм потерпел несчастье излагаться часто лицами, которым не доставало какого бы то ни было анархического чувства: буржуазными литераторами, желавшими при посредстве парадоксов привлечь к себе внимание, чтобы иметь возможность с подобием успеха вступить в лоно официальной литературы; полуграмотными и полунеграмотными, которые хотели произвести впечатление; больными, которым чтение непонятной литературы повредило рассудок; наконец, и хуже всего, злодеями более образованными, и чтобы точнее выразиться, смышлеными, чем обычные преступники, чувствовавшими необходимость оправдать свои преступления теорией; в Италии эти последние, главным образом, кончали фашизмом. Буржуазия, правительство и различные политические партии пользовались этими заблуждениями, чтобы клеветать на анархизм и слишком часто им удавалось вредить нам и дискредитировать нас в глазах масс. Недоразумения и личные вопросы срывали дискуссии и часто приводили к расколам даже среди самих анархистов. Но все это не мешает тому, чтобы в своем существе, то есть в своих моральных движущих силах и в своих окончательных целях, анархизм индивидуалистический и коммунистический не были бы одним и тем же или почти одним и тем же.

Я настоятельно рекомендую прочесть книгу Армана «Введение в анархо-индивидуализм»[2], которая скоро выйдет в переводе на итальянский язык, сделанным товарищем Меникони (смотреть в конце этого номера журнала). Это – важная и добросовестная книга, написанная одним из наиболее признанных среди анархо-индивидуалистов писателем, получившим среди них общее одобрение. И что же мы видим? Читая этот труд, спрашиваешь себя почему Арман говорит постоянно об анархическом индивидуализме, как об особой доктрине, в то время, как он только то и делает, что излагает принципы общие для всех анархистов, каково бы ни было их направление. Арман, любящий называть себя аморалистом, на самом деле написал нечто вроде руководства по анархической морали – нисколько не «анархо-индивидуалистической», а анархической вообще. Даже более того, не просто по анархической морали, а по морали общечеловеческой, так как она основана на …

author: Unknown
title: Синтез христианства и анархизма в свете западного богословия
content:
Издательский кооператив «Напильник» предлагает ознакомиться со статьей магистра теологии Александра Питыка, который рассуждает о возможных путях синтеза анархизма и христианского вероучения.

Начав с разбора взглядов на религию, встречавшихся в работах анархистских теоретиков, Питык переходит к рассказу о религиозных деятелях, стоявших на анархических позициях: одном из основателей «Индустриальных рабочих мира» католическом священнике Томасе Дж. Хагерти, католическом священнике Айта Патси, выступившем на стороне Республики во время Гражданской войны в Испании, и английском священнике и анархо-социалисте Грешеме Киркби, боровшемся за ядерное разоружение.

Многим обсуждение христианского анархизма кажется таким же непривычным, как и обсуждение анархического христианства. Тем не менее, политико-религиозное движение христианского анархизма, проявляющееся в различных формах, существует уже давно. Многие движения и личности, как в прошлом, так и в настоящем, придерживаются идеи либерального христианства и решительно заявляют, что анархизм и христианство не обязательно должны быть взаимоисключающими идеологиями. Напротив, если найти определённый подход, они скорее сходятся в содержании, чем расходятся. Жак Эллюль в своей книге «Анархизм и христианство» так и пишет:

«Считается само собой разумеющимся, что анархисты враждебно относятся ко всем религиям […]. Также считается само собой разумеющимся, что набожные христиане ненавидят анархию как источник хаоса и отрицания установленной власти. Именно эти упрощённые и неоспоримые предположения я намерен оспорить».

Попытка определения анархизма сталкивается с проблемой его стереотипного образа. Представление о том, что анархизм — это отсутствие порядка, а не правительства, что он является синонимом хаоса и бессмысленного насилия, сохранилось с викторианского периода и стало известным благодаря таким произведениям, как «Секретный агент» Джозефа Конрада. Конечно, существуют некоторые формы повстанческого анархизма, которые, по-видимому, соответствуют этому стереотипу — достаточно вспомнить деятельность Неформальной Анархической Федерации (Federazione Anarchica Informale, FAI) — но, вопреки распространенному мнению, использование насилия для большинства анархистов есть неприемлемым в виду подавления личности человека, даже если откровенный пацифизм является позицией меньшинства. Далекие от бессмысленности и деструктивности, большинство анархистов считают себя вовлеченными в конструктивный проект, состоящий из новые представления о будущем, политика, которая воплощает это будущее в настоящем, и самостоятельная организация людей.

Известно также, что и большинство христианских церквей традиционно скептически или даже враждебно относятся к социалистическим идеям. Анархистские и социалистические движения часто определяли себя через атеизм и материализм; они считали себя просвещенными и прогрессивными именно благодаря отказу от религии и Церкви. Можно посмотреть на любого классика анархизма конца XIX или начала XX вв. В XIX веке критика Церкви и религии была незаметной, поэтому негативное отношение к религии часто считается «обязательным» для анархиста. Возьмём, к примеру, одного из самых известных анархистов Михаила Бакунина: в книге «Бог и государство» он предупреждает, что религия «отупляет и развращает народы» и что она убивает в людях разум, который «есть главный инструмент освобождения человека». Он приходит к выводу:

«Если Бог существует, человек — раб; но человек может и должен быть свободным: следовательно, Бога не существует».

Эрих Мюзам рассматривает религию и государство как взаимосвязанные инструменты угнетения и пишет в «Освобождении общества от государства», что «Бог и государство […] являются двумя полюсами власти», которые «основаны на отрицании равенства, взаимности и личной ответственности. Пётр Кропоткин — один из важнейших представителей коммунистического анархизма и, безусловно, далёкий от христианского анархизма, — например, признаёт, что христианство было испорчено институционализацией, когда он описывает христианство как «восстание против имперского Рима», которое было подавлено «тем же самым Римом, принявшим его принципы, обычаи и язык» и ставшим, таким образом, «римским правом». Кропоткин пишет, что «в христианском движении, несомненно, были серьёзные анархистские элементы». Однако «анархистское содержание», которое он находил в «истоках» христианства, исчезло для него, когда «это движение постепенно превратилось в церковь»10. Эта аргументация на самом деле …

author: By Elvis Takahashi Mantello, Contributor
title: Nikos Romanos Acquitted As Greek Government Pushes Terrorism Cases
content:
Athens, Greece — Testing Greece’s controversial terrorism law, Greek anarchist Nikos Romanos, alongside Argyrios K. and Dimitris P., was acquitted of terrorism charges earlier this year in connection with an explosion in an apartment in Athens in October 2024.


For the same case, Marianna Manoura was sentenced to 19 years in prison on explosives and terrorism charges, while Dimitra Zarafeta received an eight-year sentence.


The charges against Romanos were centered on a partial fingerprint found on a plastic bag where the accidental explosion occurred in the Ampelokipi neighborhood. The investigation turned into a terrorism case and renewed attention on Romanos who previously gained notoriety in 2008 after witnessing the

police kill his friend Alexandros Grigoropoulos

, which triggered weeks of unrest across Greece.


A mural of Alexandros Grigoropoulos in Exarcheia, Athens, at the corner of Messologiou and Tzavella streets, near the site where he was shot. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.


Greece’s Terrorism Law & A Partial Fingerprint


During the trial, anarchists and supporters gathered against riot police outside the courthouse while defendants inside faced terrorism charges under Article 187A of Greece’s Criminal Code, with penalties up to life imprisonment. 


Article 187A, the Criminal Code provision concerning terrorism, was amended seven years ago and requires more than the commission of a serious offense. For an act to qualify as terrorism, it must create a “serious danger” to the country or an international organization and be carried out with a specific purpose, such as seriously intimidating a population, coercing public authorities, or seriously harming a country’s fundamental constitutional, political or economic structures.


Evangelia Kontaki, a lawyer who reviewed Article 187A for Unicorn Riot, argues that the provision’s language leaves significant room for interpretation. She points to requirements that an act create a “serious danger” and be intended to “seriously harm” a country’s fundamental constitutional, political or economic structures, questioning what objective criteria determine when those thresholds are met.


Kontaki argues that criminal liability should be grounded in an identifiable action rather than a person’s thoughts, beliefs or intentions. “A crime requires a physical action or an unlawful failure to act,” she said.


During the trial, many questioned how a partial fingerprint led to a terrorism prosecution, and what role Romanos’ political history had played in his prolonged 17-month detention.


Outside the Athens Court of Appeals on April 24, 2026, riot police advance to disperse supporters of Nikos Romanos and other defendants gathered during the trial. Photo contributed by Elvis Takahashi Mantello.


The partial fingerprint became a key point of contention and the defense challenged what the print could infer.


Romanos denied any involvement, arguing that the fingerprint could not establish when, where or under what circumstances he had touched the bag. Although a weapon was found inside the bag in the apartment, his fingerprints were not found on the weapon itself.


Prosecutors argued that the fingerprint connected Romanos to the apartment’s occupants and the site where explosives were being prepared. The prosecutor eventually raised doubts about the fingerprint evidence, noting that other unidentified fingerprints had been found on the same bag. The court acquitted Romanos.


‘Political Revenge’


Romanos described the case as “political revenge” and argued that his political past and continued activism influenced the authorities’ decision to return him to pre-trial detention.


Speaking by phone, Anny Paparousou, a lawyer for Dimitra Zarafeta in the Ampelokipi trial, pointed to what she viewed as signs of bias in the investigation, both the decision to send the anti-terrorism unit to the apartment rather than forensic investigators and the absence of a police witness at trial.


Paparousou said the proceedings were problematic from the outset and has been vocal in her criticism of the application of Article 187A, challenging its use in the case.


She argued that Greek authorities have historically treated anarchists and left-wing movements as political threats.


Cynthia Bousiou covered the trial for the independent news outlet

The Press Project

 and said prosecutors can often rely heavily on assumptions about what defendants knew or intended …

title: Sacco e Vanzetti. Assassinio di stato e solidarietà internazionale
content:
“Se l’anarchismo era la punta più avanzata di questa lotta per la libertà contro la tirannia, la documentazione più concreta di una battaglia-simbolo combattuta proprio dagli anarchici, quella sul caso Sacco e Vanzetti, rappresentava simbolicamente uno dei riferimenti più avanzati di questa forma di pensiero, che pertanto avrebbe potuto essere colpita in maniera tanto pesante quanto letale” – L.Botta Le carte di Vanzetti Aragno ed. Torino 2019 pag 42.


E ancora:


 “La salute è in voi” – lettera di Bartolomeo Vanzetti ai compagni nel 1927 – a cura di Robert D’Attilio ed. Il Picconiere – El Paso – Villafalletto Cuneo 2007.


Centosette anni fa, il 24 dicembre 1919 a Bridgewater nel Massachusetts, alcuni individui tentarono una rapina ad un blindato. Vanzetti fu accusato di questo. Era un militante anarchico conosciuto alla polizia, si era occupato di scioperi, aveva volantinato, diffondeva pubblicamente idee sovversive, scriveva ed era stimato tra la sua gente, immigrati italiani che quel giorno erano da lui al porto di Plymouth a comprare pesce secondo una atavica tradizione natalizia. Quando insieme con Sacco fu anche accusato della rapina a South Braintree del il 15 aprile 1920, era già ritenuto colpevole della tentata rapina di dicembre, non per sentenza di tribunale, ma perché anarchico, immigrato e renitente alla leva. Tutti reati, questi ultimi, che gli verranno rinfacciati nei 7 anni di tortura processuale iniziati dall’arresto, il 5 maggio 1920. Dei reati attribuitigli, nella requisitoria dell’aprile 1927, a sentenza definitiva, rivendicava la verità e la logica: “Se io potessi rinascere due volte, per due volte rifarei quello che ho fatto finora. Voi mi condannate perché sono italiano, ed in effetti io sono italiano, e voi mi condannate perché sono anarchico, e io sono anarchico”. Lo disse in piemontese “Mi sun anarchic!” e qualcuno tradusse.


Quindi, una volta conosciuta la cronaca del caso Sacco e Vanzetti e la loro innocenza sui reati specifici, si smetta di rimarcare il vittimismo di due anime innocenti, si smetta di fare feticismo degli eroi e si parli del perché della loro condanna: essi erano colpevoli di anarchismo e le loro idee erano incompatibili con la Red Scare americana. Ed erano colpevoli di essere stranieri. In effetti il caso Sacco e Vanzetti attraversa tutti i temi che sono comuni alla emigrazione. Temi tuttora attuali. Il motivo per cui si abbandona il proprio paese, il  cammino, l’attraversamento, l’arrivo al porto, la selezione ai confini, il respingimento o la detenzione provvisoria in attesa di essere o meno accolto, il mercato del lavoro, la ricerca della casa, che era abbinata al lavoro – se lo perdevi perdevi anche la casa. E poi le lotte per un contratto, il riconoscimento dei diritti civili, il movimento operaio dell’emigrazione, soprattutto della Costa Atlantica, nel quale era presente il movimento anarchico, l’anarchismo di Luigi Galleani, al quale Nick e Bart aderirono fin dal 1912, prima con contributi al giornale di Galleani “Cronaca Sovversiva”, poi con articoli, ma soprattutto con opera di agitazione, propaganda e partecipazione agli scioperi e alla controinformazione. Ricordiamo che quel sabato 5 maggio del 1920, quando furono arrestati, avevano volantini che informavano dell’assassinio di Andrea Salsedo da parte della BOI, che poi diventerà FBI, con la stessa modalità della morte di Pinelli. Nel 1917, i nostri erano stati insieme nel Messico, renitenti alla leva della prima guerra mondiale. Ed ancora il Caso Sacco e Vanzetti riguarda la giustizia di stato, la repressione, il circuito carcerario, la pena di morte. E durante il processo tutta la xenofobia dei funzionari bianchi – polizia e magistratura – verso gli emigrati, negando credibilità ai testimoni italiani, creando o nascondendo materiali processuali, e indirizzando i testimoni d’accusa.


Solo 50 anni dopo il governatore del Massachusetts, Michael Dukakis, figlio di emigrati, dichiarò a nome dello stato che quel processo era inficiato da razzismo e che ogni onta andava cancellata dalla memoria di Sacco e Vanzetti. Ricorda quella scena del film di Roberto Benigni in cui Johny Stecchino si chiede perché il boss Cozzamara ce l’avesse con lui: “Vabbeh, gli ho ammazzato la moglie, ma poi gli ho chiesto scusa. E che sarà mai!”.


Ne parlammo a Villafalletto, paese natale di Bart, nel sessantesimo dei fatti, nel settembre 1987, con la F.A.I., il Centro Studi Pinelli, lo storico Luigi Botta e l’Istituto Storico della …

title: Adam Gary Lewis - Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism
content:
Author

: Adam Gary Lewis

Title

: Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism

Subtitle

: Considering Anarchist Prefigurative Possibilities for the Future

Date

: 2026

Notes

: *A text edited for the workshop “Cultures of Anarchist Anti-Colonialism” at the 2026 Hamilton Anarchist Bookfair. **Note: This zine is a heftily edited version of chapters, ideas, and discussions that appear in the 2026 PhD dissertation. I have aimed to condense this work, and dispense with some of the excess academic referencing, language and theory. This is not to suggest that these elements cannot be useful to anarchists, but in the spirit of generating wider forms of discussion I present this initial edited version. The interviews referenced here come from my conversations with 17 anarchists in Southern Ontario, that span a range of cities, communities, and scenes, and encompass a range of complex social identities. In particular, I highlight the words and perspectives of Indigenous participants. Pseudonyms were used to help to maintain some aspect of anonymity. I hope these ideas further some of the ongoing and important conversations on anarchism and anti-colonial politics both here in Southern Ontario, but also further afield as well. My heartfelt and ongoing thanks to all who participated and supported this project over many years, and all the anarchist crews in Southern Ontario. Of course for those with more academic and theory oriented desires I invite you to check out the full dissertation work as well: Adam Gary Lewis. 2026. Cultures of Resistance, Cultures of Potential: Anarchist Value-Practices, Settler Colonialism, and Indigenous Resurgence. PhD Dissertation. York University.

Source

: Retrieved on October 4, 2026 from https://anarchistnews.org/content/cultures-anarchist-anti-colonialism


Someday, somewhere, today’s empires are tomorrow’s ashes.


—Propagandhi


 Commitments to resist settler colonialism and articulate affinities with Indigenous struggles carry potentials for greater forms of anti-colonial politics within anarchism. Such commitments are important points of resistance and action within anarchism, but they are often limited, and require greater expansion in both theory and practice in order to actually generate disruptive forms of anarchist anti-colonialism.


 Anarchists have long named settler colonialism as a key form of oppression and domination that needs to be opposed, alongside more standard anarchist oppositions like the state and capitalism. This is most readily visible in intro to anarchism books, zines, and discussions. Opposition to colonialism is nestled alongside the wide range of opposition to all forms of oppression and domination that characterizes contemporary anarchist politics. In many of these accounts, and especially those that are more theoretical in nature, there is little discussion as to what this sort of anti-colonial opposition might look like. There may be vague nods to support for Indigenous resurgence, or wider histories of complicity with international forms of anti-imperialist struggle, but rarely is there more detailed discussion of how committed form of anti-colonial politics might be enacted in here and now –in specific places at specific times– and with direct reference to the histories and flows of struggle that might disrupt anarchism for the better.


 This results in a tendency to leave colonialism among a wider laundry list of things to be opposed, and lacking in greater qualification and consideration of what this means as practical forms of politics. How, then, are anarchists actually seeking to practically, materially, and intentionally oppose settler colonialism, and support Indigenous resistance and resurgence? This zine attempts to shed light on some of the everyday ways that anarchists in Southern Ontario are engaging this work, and how they are thinking about the relationship between anarchism and anti-colonial politics.


 I consider how spirituality, history, relationships to land and place, and prefigurative imaginations for the future interact with anarchist anti-colonialism. I begin with spirituality as a tension that is perhaps even less discussed amongst anarchists, but which intersects directly with Indigenous resurgence politics, given the centrality of Indigenous cosmologies, grounded normativities, and relationships to land. The limited anarchist approach to spirituality is a stumbling block for anarchist affinities with Indigenous struggles, as well …

author: Joshua W.J. Brown
title: The New Native Needs a Theory of Obligation, Not a Blood Test
content:
The New Native should not become the old Native with a better genealogy.


That is the danger I keep hearing underneath the question

The Elephant

 has been asking this year. The “New Native” in this series is not a newly discovered ethnic group. It is a political figure emerging from a Kenyan public that has begun to act as though citizenship might mean more than being represented upward by an ethnic kingpin, disciplined by a church, managed by a civil servant, or frightened back into the inherited categories of the colonial state.


Akal Mohan sees the consolidation of a Kenyan identity beyond old orders of tribe, clan and denomination. Wangui Kimari traces the state’s fear of the “detribalized native”, then and now: the urban African who does not stay where authority says identity belongs. Joe Kobuthi reads the 2024 rupture through theology and the failure of a state that has demanded something close to sacred obedience. Across the series, the New Native becomes legible precisely when older intermediaries stop being able to explain the citizen to himself.


But once “native” is liberated from colonial administration, a second problem arrives. What is it going to mean?


If native means only ancestry, the term can become a blood test. If it means only citizenship, it can become historical amnesia. Neither answer is adequate for a country in which people can be equal citizens while communities still possess radically unequal historical relationships to land, dispossession, state violence, migration and political power.


Kenya’s own constitution already knows this, even when political language forgets.


One country, more than one kind of right


Chapter Three of the constitution does not grade citizenship by antiquity. A Kenyan citizen is a citizen. Citizenship may be acquired by birth or registration, and citizens possess the rights, privileges and benefits of that status. The constitution does not say that a person becomes more Kenyan because his ancestors arrived first, or less Kenyan because a grandparent crossed a border.


Then Chapter Five does something equally important: it refuses to pretend that equal citizenship has dissolved collective history. Article 63 recognizes community land, including ancestral lands and lands traditionally occupied by hunter-gatherer communities. The Community Land Act recognizes customary rights and gives them legal force. Article 56 requires affirmative measures for minorities and marginalized groups.


These provisions are not an embarrassing inconsistency in the constitutional order. They are a clue.


Equal citizenship and historically specific rights can coexist because they answer different questions. Citizenship asks: who belongs to the political community, and on what civic terms? Ancestral land rights ask: what relationship does a particular community possess to a particular place, and what happened to that relationship? A remedy for dispossession is not a superior passport. A passport is not a land restitution programme.


Conflate those categories and the state gets two convenient escapes. It can tell a dispossessed community that everyone is equal now, therefore the old theft no longer requires a specific remedy. Or it can tell citizens descended from later-arriving populations that they may live under the law but can never fully belong because history placed their ancestors in the wrong column.


Both moves turn time into an alibi.


The Ogiek case is about more than recognition


The Ogiek litigation makes the first danger impossible to romanticize away.


In 2017, the African Court on Human and Peoples’ Rights found Kenya responsible for violations involving Ogiek land, property, natural resources, culture and development. In 2022, the Court ordered reparations, including compensation and measures to secure Ogiek ancestral land rights. In December 2025, after years of implementation failure, the Court found Kenya had still not made the ordered compensation payments, had not completed the identification, delimitation, demarcation and collective titling of Ogiek ancestral land, and had not begun the consultations required to resolve concessions and leases affecting that land.


That matters to the New Native argument because it shows why a purely civic vocabulary is insufficient. “We are all Kenyans” cannot do the work of a title, a payment, a boundary, a consultation, or the restoration of a legal relationship to ancestral land.


Universal equality is not the …
