author: Chris Walker
title: At Ohio Campaign Rally, Trump Threatens to Withhold Aid If Democrats Get Elected
content:
“I’m not going to help” if an Ohio Democratic candidate for governor wins, Trump said.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In a campaign speech in Vandalia, Ohio, on Saturday, President Donald Trump suggested he would withhold federal funds from the state if voters elect Democratic politicians in this year’s midterm races.

Trump appeared to conflate two different political races, discussing U.S. Sen. Jon Husted’s (R-Ohio) Senate reelection campaign and Democratic candidate Amy Acton’s campaign for governor in the same statement. (Husted is running against former U.S. Senator and Democrat Sherrod Brown, while Acton is facing off against Republican candidate for governor and Trump ally Vivek Ramaswamy.)

“Jon Husted…calls me all the time. He always wants money,” Trump said during his speech. “If Amy Acton got in, I don’t know anything about her.”

“I’m not going to help her, probably, she hates me, I guess,” Trump added.

Trump’s speech also featured vulgar attacks against Democrats in general. At one point, he encouraged those in attendance to “just get out and vote” for Republicans.

“If you do that, we’re going to win, and we’re going to win big, and we’re going to shove it up their ass,” Trump said.

The president made a number of bizarre claims during his Saturday night speech. He claimed that he has one of the highest IQs “anywhere in the world,” telling the audience it was around 1,775. Such an IQ would indeed be the highest, as no IQ test has ever measured above 300. He also said that polls are “fake,” complaining that they didn’t take into account his plans to campaign in the final weeks of the race — a statement that is technically true but misleading, as polls question respondents about their current attitudes. And he reiterated an unlikely (and legally dubious) promise to deliver $5,000 checks to every American adult if Republicans win the midterms.

Trump has already withheld disaster aid from states for seemingly political reasons. In a series of Truth Social posts in late June, Trump announced hundreds of millions of dollars in disaster aid funds going to states that backed him in 2024, while ignoring some requests from states that backed his opponent, Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris.

An analysis from the Urban Institute around that time showed that, since Trump reentered the White House, over 84 percent of requests from states that voted for him won approval, as opposed to only 41 percent of requests from states that didn’t back him. Approvals, when they did occur, happened twice as fast for red states as for blue ones.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

author: dev
title: La mobilisation lycéenne à travers les yeux d'une professeur du 93
content:
J'voudrais écrire avec mes tripes, mon corps, ses joies et ses dégoûts, loin de toute moraline (Nietzsche) parce que les tribunes de circonstance, les communiqués, syndicaux ou autres, les déclarations d'intention, les mots creux, les rodomontades resteront lettre morte et ne sont que vétilles en considération de ce qui se joue en ce moment dans les lycées de toute la France, et au-delà (universités, monde du travail, perspective du 17 octobre…).


DÉGOÛTS !


L'intersyndicale nationale, au soir du 2 octobre, après plus de 5000 interpellations en 5 jours (pire qu'au plus fort du mouvement des Gilets Jaunes) et des centaines de cas de violences policières avérées, n'est pas même foutue d'appeler à la grève et à manifester le mardi 6 octobre (date posée par le mouvement lycéen pour une grande journée d'actions). Elle préfère en effet le « dialogue social », soit la complicité avec les pouvoirs en place, à la solidarité et aux véritables changements… L'intersyndicale qui précise encore dans ses communiqués qu'il faut que le gouvernement

entende

 les revendications lycéennes, déclaration totalement hors sol, comme si, de là où nous en sommes, le lion affamé allait entendre la plainte de l'antilope… Bref, l'intersyndicale, avec ses éternels atermoiements, c'est le maintien du système tel qu'il est, or certain.es ne le comprennent toujours pas, ce qui est bien désespérant, alors même qu'elle s'est évertuée à faire perdre tous les mouvements sociaux conséquents des dix dernières années (au moins), à commencer par la mobilisation contre la contre-réforme des retraites.


La liste des exactions de la police est tellement longue qu'un recensement exhaustif ne peut en être dressé : tentative de noyade à Belfort par un flic en civil, tentative d'écraser des élèves, par un flic à moto au Blanc-Mesnil, tentative d'homicide à Troyes : une voiture de police fonce à vive allure sur une foule de jeunes, calmes, réunis dans une rue, tout en les gazant depuis les vitres ouvertes du véhicule, étranglement d'une lycéenne de 14 ans à Alençon, éborgnement d'un lycéen de 16 ans, à Argenteuil du fait d'un tir à bout portant de LBD. À Tours, Maël, 16 ans a aussi été éborgné, Mâchoire brisée du fait d'un tir tendu de grenade en plein visage d'Eden, 15 ans, dans le Val d'Oise

 [

1

]

.


Etc.


Une copine me raconte : présence de flics avec des chiens à Carnot (collège-lycée à Paris 17è), mouvement de foule à l'intérieur du collège, son fils de 11 ans blessé au genou dans la panique. Bah au moins, il détestera la police, et pour longtemps !


Dans mon lycée du 93, au terme de deux jours de blocus, on dénombre 5 élèves placés en garde-à-vue dont l'un, mineur, sera peut-être déféré au tribunal ; des blessures : une jeune fille, à l'œil, ayant reçu un projectile suite à l'envoi de gaz lacrymogène par les forces de l'ordre, d'autres présentant des contusions dues à des coups de matraques ; des mises en joue d'élèves par des flics armés de LBD et moult tirs de gaz lacrymo ; des insultes, évidemment ; des intimidations : un flic en mode prêcheur qui déclare à un élève : « tu sais, ce que tu fais là, à la mosquée, même si tu le confesses, on t'le pardonnera pas »… Et aussi une voiture bélier fonçant à vive allure dans le tas, pas de blessés mais une catastrophe aurait pu avoir lieu.


À noter que les élèves embarqués l'ont été alors qu'ils n'étaient plus devant le lycée mais sur le chemin les reconduisant chez eux, par des keufs en embuscade aux environs du lycée, bel exemple de crapulerie et veulerie.


On les pensait bien soumis, pour toujours


Dociles à souhait


Esclaves, sans fin


Dominé.es sans répit


Qui ça ?


Les sauvageon.nes des banlieues, les relégué.es des quartiers populaires… mais ils n'en peuvent plus et relèvent la tête !


Dans mon lycée du 93, depuis des années, on « joue » aux chaises musicales, il n'y a bien souvent pas assez de chaises pour les classes à 35, il faut donc aller en chercher dans d'autres salles qui, de fait, connaîtront à leur tour le même sort, le problème n'est donc pas réglé et se poursuit sempiternellement. Les chaises, en outre, de piètre qualité, sont pour beaucoup endommagées, s'entassent dans les salles et ne sont pas jetées


Depuis l'an passé, Pécresse a fait installer des systèmes bloquant les fenêtres qui s'ouvrent donc à peine maintenant, empêchant toute réelle ventilation ; système anti-suicide paraît-il, mais les élèves peuvent allégrement se jeter dans le vide depuis les passerelles menant …

author: Unknown
title: Mobilisation lycéenne : infos pour la semaine du 5 octobre
content:
Appel de la coordination lycéenne.

RDV

 de mobilisation. Répression, arrêtés préfectoraux...


Lundi 5 mobilisation dans les lycées. Mardi 6 octobre manif 14h République et assemblée lycéenne 17h


Samedi 3 octobre on était 300 lycéens de toute la région parisienne réunis en assemblée de coordination.


La colère a commencé parce que c'est la casse sociale dans les lycées de banlieue. Le tri des pauvres et des riches à lécoale, c'est mort on refuse. On revendique la fin de Parcoursup. On revendique des moyens, des professeurs et des

AESH

. On veut des classes qui ne sont pas à 35, du respect pour tous les élèves, des bourses qui arrivent à temps, des lycées où il n'y a pas de rats, ni de plafonds qui s'écroulent, ni de l'amiante, ni des salles à 40° en été.


On revendique un avenir pour les lycéens de banlieue. On sait que la méritocratie c'est un leurre. Y'a pas de raison que nous, on ait une éducation et un avenir de seconde-zone comparé aux lycées privés ou des beaux quartiers. Et derrière, on sait qu'on n'a pas d'avenir dans ce système où ce sont les riches qui décident. On veut savoir où va l'argent et on veut qu'il aille là où y'a besoin

 

! Le gouvernement il met des milliards dans l'armée, dans les patrons, dans la police. C'est ça la violence. Alors nous, on ne se laissera pas diviser par les discours contre les casseurs, on est tous ensemble.


Le gouvernement, l'extrême-droite et les grands médias, ils ont tout tenté pour nous faire taire. Toute la violence de la police on l'a vu. les fermetures de lycées, on les a vu. Ceux qui disent qu'on est insctrumentalisés ou qu'on est bêtes, on les a vu. Ok, noté. Ok, ils ne veulent pas qu'on se mobilise. Ok la répression a pour but de faire peur, que notre colère s'éteigne et de nous diviser. Les 5000 lycéens arrêtés doivent tous être relâchés sans aucune poursuite.


On va continuer de se mobiliser. Et on ne s'arrêtera pas au lycée non plus. On n'est pas seuls. Les gens du monde du travail se joignent à la mobilisation. Et notre colère, elle peut parler à tous les jeunes, même en dehors de la France.


Alors nous, on va construire la grève lycéenne

 

! On appelle tout le monde à nous rejoindre et à se mettre en grève : les profs, les parents, les étudiants, les pompiers, les autres travailleurs. ils nous la mettent à l'envers

 

? On leur remet 68 et on ira plus loin. Les syndicats appellent à la grève mardi, il faut que tout le monde nous rejoigne

 

! Et si ça sort les gilets jaunes avant même le 17 octobre tant mieux

 

!


On veut prendre notre lutte en main : c'est les lycéens mobilisés qui doivent décider de leur mouvement, et c'est à personne d'autre de décider à notre place. Donc sur chaque blocage, devant chaque lycée, il faut prendre la parole, so'ganiser nous-même et décider ensemble.


Dès lundi, partout on se mobilise. Et mardi, on doit tous aller en manifestation à République à 14H. On y sera en tête de cortège de la coordination lycéenne Paris x Banlieues. On appelle tous les lycées à venir, à se préparer leur banderole. Et derrière, rendez-vous pour tous les lycées mobilisés en assemblée de la coordination lycéenne Paris x Banlieues à 17h. Parce qu'après mardi bien sûr qu'on va continuer

 

!


Un communiqué de parents d'élèves d'Aubervilliers


Parents d'élèves : une présence solidaire auprès des lycéen·nes mobilisé·es


Depuis une dizaine de jours, des milliers de lycéennes et lycéens, dans toute la France mais en particulier dans le 93 et à Aubervilliers, manifestent leur colère.


Cette colère est aussi la nôtre : contre le manque de moyens, la dégradation du bâti scolaire, l'exposition aux canicules, les absences d'enseignant·es non remplacées, le manque d'infirmières, d'assistantes sociales, de psychologues et de médecins scolaires, les emplois du temps surchargés, l'inertie de l'Éducation nationale face aux agressions sexuelles, sexistes et racistes, la sélection arbitraire et inégale de Parcoursup…


La colère des lycéen·nes d'Aubervilliers s'exprime la plupart du temps de manière pacifique, joyeuse et déterminée. Elle n'est bruyante que pour ceux qui ne veulent pas l'écouter.


Rien ne justifie la répression policière, les gaz lacrymogènes qui pénètrent jusque dans les écoles primaires alentour, ou les violentes interpellations dont nous avons été témoins. Ce ne sont pas des «

 

casseurs

 

», ce sont nos enfants

 

; ce ne sont pas des «

 

violences urbaines

 

», mais un mouvement social portant des revendications …

author: anred
title: Claudio Katz: «hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei»
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico. Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.

Por Indymedia Argentina.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de 

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el 

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam 

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: – 

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy 

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto: 

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.


Indymedia: –

 ¿Por qué importa ese dato?


Claudio Katz: – Porque conforma el escenario en el que actúa la izquierda. Desconociendo ese hecho es muy difícil desenvolver estrategias para derrotar a Milei, revertir el ajuste y reconquistar los derechos populares. Ese camino transita por llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder, mediante frentes comunes y acuerdos de lucha con los sectores dispuestos a reconstruir el país, apostando a un gobierno que en sus primeros días de gestión revierta de un plumazo todo lo hecho por Milei.


Foto: 

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Ese es el eje el debate actual. Si derogaremos o no de inmediato las leyes laborales, el RIGI, los Glaciares o la impunidad de la Corte …

title: Blocchi nei licei in Francia: la protesta continua e si espande
content:
Da meno di una settimana in Francia tutti i licei di periferia di Parigi e di altre grandi città sono bloccati dai picchetti degli studenti che, insieme a professori e assistenti all’educazione, hanno messo al centro la questione della formazione.


Tutto è partito da Créteil dove i professori hanno organizzato uno sciopero e gli studenti si sono uniti alle rivendicazioni. 


Ciò che viene espresso è una mancanza di mezzi e di risorse per i licei di periferia, l’insufficienza di personale oltre agli edifici degradati, ma viene anche portata una feroce critica sulla qualità della formazione e sulle possibilità lavorative inesistenti a seguito del diploma. Queste proteste hanno visto immediatamente una diffusione significativa, anche le università si sono unite ai blocchi, inoltre i sindacati confederali e, ancorché il governo, sono stati obbligati a prendere in considerazione le rivendicazioni. 


La risposta muscolare delle forze di polizia non si è fatta attendere con arresti, fermi e feriti gravi, oltre a cariche all’ingresso delle scuole da parte dei CRS. E’ interessante notare anche la presenza di diversi consiglieri di La France Insoumise sui blocchi, a partire dal sindaco Bally Bagayoko di Saint Denis. 


Ne abbiamo parlato con un professore di un liceo di periferia di Parigi.

title: AYM, Tayfun Kahraman kararının gerekçesini açıkladı, mahkemeyi uyardı: Yeniden yargılansın
content:
Anayasa Mahkemesi (AYM), Gezi Parkı davasında 18 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırılan Tayfun Kahraman’ın adil yargılanma ve bireysel başvuru haklarının ihlal edildiğine hükmederek yeniden yargılama yapılmasına ve Kahraman’a 100 bin TL manevi tazminat ödenmesine karar verdi. Kararı uygulamayan mahkemeyi uyaran AYM, "Kararların bağlayıcılığının sorgulanması ve uygulanmaması hukuk devletini işlemez hâle getirir, kaçınılmaz bir şekilde hukuk sistemini kaosa sürükler" dedi.

AYM, Temmuz 2025'te Kahraman'ın adil yargılanma hakkının ihlal edildiğine karar vermiş ve yeniden yargılama için kararı İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'ne göndermişti. Mahkeme, AYM'nin "yetki gasbı" yaptığını belirterek yeniden yargılama talebini reddetmişti. AYM, bu kez bireysel başvuru hakkının oybirliğiyle, hakkaniyete uygun yargılanma hakkının ise oyçokluğuyla ihlal edildiğine hükmetti ve yeniden yargılama için kararı aynı mahkemeye bir kez daha gönderdi. Kahraman’a ayrıca 100 bin TL manevi tazminat ödenmesine hükmedildi. Ödemenin Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığına başvurudan itibaren dört ay içinde yapılması, gecikme halinde yasal faiz uygulanması kararlaştırıldı.

Yeni Parti Grup Başkanvekili Gökhan Günaydın, AYM'nin kararının akıbeti benzer olan çok sayıda siyasi tutuklu için emsal teşkil ettiğini belirterek "Böylece Anayasa Mahkemesi, ilk derece mahkemesi niteliğindeki ağır ceza mahkemesine ve temyiz mercii olan Yargıtay’a bir kez daha Anayasa’yı hatırlatmış oldu" yorumunda bulundu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Ritchy Thibault, premier prisonnier du mouvement lycéen
content:
Interpellé en pleine rue jeudi dernier, l'écrivain et voyageur Ritchy Thibault a été emprisonné. Il lui est reproché un discours prononcé à Saint-Denis lors d'une assemblée générale de lycéens. Une audience se tiendra ce lundi à 13h au tribunal de Bobigny qui statuera sur sa libération dans l'attente d'un procès ou son maintien en détention, ce qui serait un très mauvais signal envoyé aux lycéens plus que jamais mobilisés.


Il y a des fabricants de destins qui l'aimeraient clandestin.


Certains commencent dans des amphithéâtres, d'autres dans les caravanes ou sur des rond-points de campagne. Celui de Ritchy Thibault semble, lui, avoir trouvé un drôle de raccourci : viré de l'hémicycle en tant qu' attaché parlementaire, on le retrouve forcément dès le premier jour de la mobilisation aux abords d'un lycée de banlieue et de nouveau devant les tribunaux pour sa prise de parole.


Le voilà érigé en quasi responsable de la contestation, incarnation autocentrée pour le Parquet - proclamée d'une jeunesse qui ne supporterait plus rien — ni l'ordre, ni l'autorité, ni les institutions, et encore moins ceux qui prétendent les représenter. À chaque mobilisation son cortège, à chaque polémique sa réponse proportionnée, à chaque interpellation sa détermination sauf qu'à chaque fois ou presque il y a un mort, qui un voyageur traîné sur 100 m par la Municipale qui un maire véreux cloitrant une aire de « gens-du-voyage ».


Voir en Ritchy Thibault une sorte de porte-parole naturel des populations opprimées semble se dessiner assez fiablement au fil des mois et parfois des semaines, au fil des émeutes, et manifestant en première ligne pour la fin des coups et des étranglements sur la voie publique jusqu'au fond des mitards.


Chatgpt dirait : c'est là que le personnage devient intéressant. Il se retrouve quasiment à chaque procédure a établir un rapport de force - comme un rapport de farce - une variante de la fameuse Défense de rupture. On le voit à chaque fois argumenter - dans ce régime de parole qui est le sien à des joutes assez réussies et brillantes de tentatives d'auto-désarrestations (désarrestation = lorsqu'un groupe de personnes tentent de libérer physiquement un•e camarade au prise avec la Maréechaussée.) Dans cette nouvelle économie de la contestation, l'arrestation devient parfois une ligne de CV, la convocation une médaille et le passage devant la justice un épisode supplémentaire dans le récit héroïque du rappel historique - à chaque fois situé des personnes, persécuté (génocide des voyageurs, parquages, apartheid de l'Etat français envers des populations).


L'atout de Ritchy Thibault, ce n'est pas qu'il parle trop. C'est qu'il a fait de la confrontation avec le pouvoir une méthode, un médium — et que le pouvoir judiciaire, lui, a les moyens de transformer chacune de ces confrontations en procédure, le transforme en tribune.


La vraie question devient : justice qui protège l'ordre public ou justice qui finit, volontairement ou non, par devenir un instrument de mise au pas d'une parole et se prendre les pieds dans le tapis d'une bienséance confinant à l'absurde du droit commun en sytème politique. Ritchy Thibault nous montre avec délices, les affres de toute assignation - et autres rapports de dominations - qu'ils soient éducatifs, issus du monde les ronds de serviettes et des pantoufles, voire des patins pour cirer les Parquets. Blague à part, la bascule judiciaire, voire carcérale peut vite arriver, une incarcération, des amendes, des menaces de mort à la pelle montrent que le fil est ténu mais il tient la ligne. A nous tous de le sortir de là.


#FreeRitchy

What Would Replace the Wage System?

The Industrial Workers of the World believe in a better life for all. In considering what’s right and what’s wrong with our present society, the IWW naturally includes how we are paid for the work we do: wages and salaries.

Wages or salaries are the money given to us by the boss in return for a set amount of time we spend at the job. We get so much an hour, or so much a month. Whether we’ve spent the day working hard or had to “look busy” much of the time, we receive exactly the same amount.

But for the same eight hours of employment, people are paid greatly varying amounts. We are paid different rates for doing the same job in different locations (i.e., truck assemblers get paid more in Windsor than in Vancouver) and for doing different jobs in the same location (i.e., in Vancouver accountants are paid more than daycare workers). Even when we’re employed by the same company in the same building, various tasks are often paid at varying rates (i.e., electricians, assembly line workers, secretaries);

These differences in pay are mostly a result of events which happened in our past: our history. Certain jobs get a particular rate of pay because of some decisions by the boss. Other jobs get a particular rate of pay because of actions taken by our forefathers and foremothers. As teachers grew more militant. for example, that task changed from a low-paying to a better-paying one. Overall, unionized jobs show the results of past fights for better pay and conditions.

On the other hand, a failure to stay militant results in lower comparative wages There was a time in B.C.‘s history when woods workers overall were among the highest-paid blue-collar employees. No longer.

On every job, a number of excuses are offered to explain why I should get more pay than you, and why he or she receive more than both of us combined. Years of education and training are often cited, though this education is largely supported out of taxes we all pay. So those who receive this education really benefit twice. Meanwhile, should employees with four years of university receive more than employees with seven years of an apprenticeship?

Another argument is that some people have more responsibility or take more risks. This can be in connection with our own life or others’ lives, or concerned with valuable items or money. But then, why aren’t those who work at the most hazardous jobs (as determined by Workers’ Compensation Board statistics) the most highly paid? Or, why don’t bank tellers earn a lot of money?

Should the people who produce what society needs most be the best paid? This would mean that farmers and agricultural laborers who produce our food would be among the highest paid people. They aren’t now! And those who manufacture our clothing are still often immigrant women working for very, very low pay in sweat-shop conditions. And the host of non-union carpenters and others building our housing aren’t very well reimbursed for their work, either.

title: Rote Hilfe freut sich über erneuten Mitgliederzuwachs
content:
Rote Hilfe freut sich über erneuten Mitgliederzuwachs


Nachdem die Kündigung aller ihrer Konten der Roten Hilfe

e. V.

 zum Jahreswechsel 2025/26 bereits eine große Welle der Solidarität eingebracht hatte, kann sich die linke Schutz- und Solidaritätsorganisation nun über einen erneuten Schwung an Neueintritten freuen. Hintergrund ist eine Kampagne gegen die Spitzenkandidatin der Partei Die Linke in Berlin, Elif Eralp, die nach eigenen Angaben bis 2025 Mitglied des Vereins war. Große Teile der bürgerlichen Presse nutzten dies dazu, eine Kampagne gegen Eralp zu lancieren und unterstellten ihr und ihrer Partei die Nähe zu einem „Terrorhilfe-Verein“ oder „Extremisten-Nest“. 

Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe ordnet die Kampagne ein: „Den hohen Wellen, die Elif Eralps frühere Mitgliedschaft plötzlich schlägt, sehen wir gelassen entgegen. Es scheint doch ein recht hilfloser Versuch zu sein, eine linke Bürgermeisterin in Berlin zu verhindern, die der Bevölkerung unter anderem die Vergesellschaftung großer Wohnungskonzerne versprochen hat. Wenn nun ihre ehemalige Mitgliedschaft in der Roten Hilfe einer der größten Skandale um ihre Person sein soll, haben ihre politischen Gegner*innen wohl nicht viel Material für die Diffamierungskampagne gefunden«. 

Das tagelange Medienecho brachte der Roten Hilfe einen weiteren Anstieg der Mitgliederzahl auf über 21.000. Auch der Fraktionsvorsitzende der Partei Die Linke im Bundestag, Sören Pellmann, verkündete demonstrativ seinen Beitritt. 

„Wir freuen uns, dass sich erneut so viele Menschen solidarisch mit der Roten Hilfe zeigen. Wir erinnern uns an prominente Mitglieder wie Clara Zetkin oder Kurt Tucholsky in der Roten Hilfe Deutschland zur Weimarer Zeit,« so Brückner weiter. »Wir unterstützen Menschen etwa bei Gerichtsverfahren und setzen uns gegen den Abbau von Grundrechten ein. Dass diese offen und transparent geleistete Arbeit immer wieder zum Anlass für Diffamierungen und politische Angriffe genommen wird, zeigt umso deutlicher, wie wichtig eine starke linke Schutz- und Solidaritätsorganisation ist. Deshalb unterstützt uns, tretet bei, schafft Rote Hilfe!«

title: Assemblée ouverte de la caisse de solidarité Kaliméro
content:
Kaliméro est une caisse et une assemblée solidaire des prisonnier·e·s de la guerre sociale. La prochaine aura lieu le jeudi 8 octobre à 18h et se tiendra au 19, rue burnouf à Paris (19

e

).


La prison est un des rouages de ce système basé sur l'exploitation et la domination que nous voulons raser au sol, c'est pourquoi nous envoyons des mandats à celles et ceux accusé·e·s d'actes de révolte dont nous sommes solidaires.


Une caisse de solidarité a besoin de continuité. Nous n'avons ni sponsor, ni mécène, aussi avons-nous convenu d'un rendez-vous par mois pour collecter des sous pour alimenter la caisse. Ces rencontres sont également l'occasion d'échanger sur nos pratiques face à la répression, d'assurer le suivi des différentes histoires et de discuter des situations qui se présentent. Elle est également un moment de discussion autour des possibles moyens d'esquive, de résistance et d'auto-organisation offensive contre la machine judiciaire et carcérale.


Dans un souci de régularité, ces rencards ont été fixés le 2

e

 jeudi de chaque mois.


Pour envoyer de l'argent, pour demander des informations, ou pour être tenu·e·s au courant des prochains rendez-vous de la caisse et être inscrit·e·s sur la mailing-list de Kaliméro, écrivez à kalimeroparis(at)riseup.net

title: Répression du mouvement lycéen - bilan des premiers jours marseillais
content:
Le mouvement lycéen est massif. Et les CRS et équipes de la BAC sont sur les dents. On propose ici un rapide bilan des derniers jours sur Marseille.


Mais déjà 1ere chose : on pense à vous les lycéen.nes de martigues, aix, tarascon, port de bouc, salon, miramas, seyne sur mer, etc. Force à vous ! Nos conseils face à la police, et l'institution dite « Justice » sont aussi pour vos villes. Mais on peut difficilement demander à des avocats marseillais d'aller jusqu'à vous en garde à vue. Pour préparer la suite (une convocation, un procès, etc) ça se rediscute, écrivez nous !


2e chose nous c'est la Legal Team Marseille, tu peux lire notre présentation en bas de la page.


A Marseille donc, niveau chiffres ça parle de environ 30interpellations jeudi (84 dans le département). Et vendredi pareil : 30 interpel selon Ici provence. Jusqu'à encore 19h en centre ville, métro Réformés, où il y avait un cortège voulant aller devant le comico de noailles pour soutenir les personnes arrêtées…


On a vu beaucoup de CRS déployés , avec camion boucliers lanceurs de grenades lacrymogènes.


La CRS 53 qui dort dans le 14e avenue claude monnet/impasse florida. La CRS 54 qui dort à St Pierre dans le 5e près du dépôt de tramway. Ou encore les CRS qui dorment dans la caserne près du parc de la ravelle dans le 13e.


Mais aussi beaucoup d'équipes de la BAC ces « brigades anti-criminalité » des flics en civil avec matraque, grenades, flingues, cagoules, et menottes dont de nombreux collectifs de Résistance contre la violence policière et le racisme demandent le démantèlement ! (lire Mathieu Rigouste, La Domination policière. Une violence industrielle, Paris, La Fabrique, 2012)


Le Préfet du Département est venu parader dans les médias et il a sorti ses armes genre état d'urgence : des arrêté préfectoraux instaurant l'interdiction de rassemblement près des lycées, interdiction vente carburant au détail, interdiction port de protections individuelles (masques et lunettes ?), etc : de quoi justifier fouilles et amendes et contrôles préventifs et faire peur bouh ! On verra ces fouilles par les flics de sac à dos des lycéens dans la rue aux abords du lycée Simone Veil dans le 13e.


La police municipale est aussi toujours là, de plus en plus nombreuses (mais combien de flics il y a en fRance ??) A Port de bouc on a vu la municipale foncer en voiture sur la foule de lycéen.nes grrr.


La police nationale aussi dans leur fourgon banalisé (camion style jumpy noir, vitres teintées, avec gyrophare bleu sur le tableau de bord). Avec la cynophile aussi.


On a aussi vu l'utilisation des caméras de surveillance dans les arrestations. Elles servent à guide les flics dans leurs interventions mais aussi à rassembler des preuves pour des arrestations futures. On a vu des arrestations suite à des analyses de vidéosurveillance et la dénonciation par des proviseurs et des surveillants qui identifient leurs élèves sur les vidéos que les flics leur montrent.


(plus d'infos sur les caméras sur ce site :

https://www.laquadrature.net/2020/01/20/safe-city-a-marseille-premier-recours-contre-la-videosurveillance-automatisee-de-lespace-public/

)


Les personnes mineures, arrêtées par les flics et placées en garde à vue ont droit de demander un avocat (le commis d'office est gratuit, et si tu donnes un nom d'avocat tu vois avec lui c'est là que la LT peut intervenir), voir un médecin et aussi que ses parents ou représentants légaux soient prévenu. Ils peuvent eux aussi de l'extérieur désigner un.e avocat.e.


La garde à vue peut durer 24h, jusqu'à 48h maximum. Certains lycéens sont sortis de garde-à-vue avec une convocation chez le procureur/ou la PJJ pour dans 1à3mois.

author: groundxero
title: Barricades, Internet Shutdown, Mass Detentions: Delhi Police Violent Crack Down on Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and SIR
content:
Thousands of protesters gathered around Delhi’s Jantar Mantar on 2 October, defying the denial of police permission and a sweeping security clampdown imposed to prevent the protests from taking place. Barricades sealed the designated protest site from all four directions, mobile internet was suspended across central Delhi, several Metro stations were shut, and riot-control forces were deployed in large numbers. What followed was a day of mass detentions, many involving the use of force against women, students, journalists and other protesters. The violent crackdown came amid a renewed call for mobilisation for a ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’ and ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, with organisers calling the 2 October action only the beginning of a wider protest movement.


 


New Delhi, 2 October 2026


by

Mouli Sharma


 


“Thousand is a lowballed estimate,” said a lawyer’s group called

Lawyers for Detainees

, one of several such collectives formed after the historic protests that shook the national capital a mere three months ago after uproar against repeated failures and irregularities in the conduct of public examinations under the tenure of former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Now, recent history is attempting to recreate itself as a similar uproar against the government’s Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, and the recent revelations of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s alleged role in the same has led to widespread national outrage.


 


“85 people have been detained in this station alone,” said Adv. Surya Prakash, who was present at the Badarpur police station. “We have reports that at least 20 buses filled with detainees left the protest site during the day. Many detainees were released informally at random locations far away from the centre of the city, while still more were taken to stations like this one. The actual number of detentions is much higher than whatever numbers will be produced here at the stations,” he said.


 


The figure, though, may include repeat detentions, the most prominent case being of AISA president Neha Bora herself, who was detained at least three times from the same location outside the Royal Plaza Hotel, near the East entrance of the protest site near the Kerala Bhawan canteen, first alongside psephologist and activist Yogendra Yadav, a second time with several student protesters of other parties, and a third time again with fellow AISA leader Anjali of the Delhi University. Former Delhi CM Atishi, independent journalist Harsh Yadav, and at least 700 more students were detained through the day.


 


“700 is the count we have so far from police stations taken across the city,” said Adv. Vertika Mani, also a part of the lawyers’ collective. “But that obviously cannot account for the many detainees who were released at unofficial locations.”


 


The CJP’s ultimatum to the government of witnessing a ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ should Gyanesh Kumar fail to resign within 48 hours (given on 25 September, the deadline for which had long since passed) kicked off with a bang on Friday, as an identical call for the police-defying protest in Shivaji Park, Mumbai was given by countless student, labour, farmer and other political organisations at the eponymous Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, led by prominent activists including Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, Nandita Narain, and Prashant Bhushan. Hundreds of civilians took to the streets on the morning of 2 October, on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, only to be met with armed state forces deployed in massive numbers and a once-designated protest site cut off from their access through curfews (Section 163 of the BNS was declared in the region, without any justification beyond prevention of a ‘crowd forming’) and police barricades blockading entrances to the site from all four directions, dispersing protesters across a wide 2km radius.


 


What followed was a circus of media, police, and protester, as for four hours following the 11 am time given for the assembly, bus after bus was filled with peaceful protesters ‘detained’ under the simple justification of following ‘orders from above’. At least one protester, a young man named Roveen from the All India Students’ Association (AISA) (of whom Neha Bora is national president), was grievously assaulted by the police and had to be taken to a …

author: Katharine Trendacosta
title: Site-Blocking Will Not Defend IP, No Matter the Bill’s Name
content:
There has been a raft of site-blocking bills in the latest Congress, and the latest is called the “Deterring Extraterritorial Foreign Exploitation of Networks Damaging Intellectual Property” aka the “

DEFEND IP Act

.” The problem is that instead of “defending IP,” this bill will incentivize censorship, overblocking, and bad faith attempts to block access to a website. DEFEND IP Act, and all of these site-blocking proposals, threaten the open web.

 


We keep seeing attempts to pass site-blocking legislation–from SOPA/PIPA in 2012 to

Block BEARD

,

FADPA

, and

ACPA

 this year. Every one of them has at its core the rotten idea that enforcing copyrights requires building a censorship machine for websites into the architecture of the internet. This is, of course, a disaster for a free and open web. There is no way to create a mechanism for blocking access to an entire website that does not invite both deliberate abuse and lots of collateral harm to free and lawful speech.


DEFEND IP deputizes every service provider into a copyright cop, so long as a rightsholder has accused a website of copyright infringement. Let’s be clear: this isn’t about removing access to an infringing work–that already exists via the DMCA. This isn’t about getting damages from the website or the uploader. It is about making an entire website inaccessible for everyone trying to visit it.


DEFEND IP lets any rightsholder go to a court and get an order requiring service providers to block access to an entire website after alleging copyright infringement. What DEFEND IP does not have is any deterrent for someone seeking to block a website in bad faith. There are no punishments for getting a website blocked for protected speech. There are no meaningful remedies for those whose speech is vanished from the internet due to an entire website being disappeared. It creates a one-stop shop for getting an entire website–again, not an instance of infringement but an entire site hosting all sorts of user content–removed. But for those whose business, speech, or access to information is affected, there is no easy way to get the site restored.


DEFEND IP scales up the extraordinary legal structures that already exist for copyright enforcement. In doing so, it likewise scales up the problems those regimes pose to protected speech.

 


We see this with DMCA takedowns all the time. We see it with bad faith

takedowns

 used to silence criticism or commentary. We see it with the voluntary use of copyright filters by sites like YouTube, where seconds of sound matching seconds of sound in another video can prevent an entire work from reaching its audience. In these existing systems, there are at least some mechanisms of challenge available to the targeted creator. DEFEND IP has none. Instead, site owners, users, or readers will have to find a lawyer and go to court and hope to challenge the order, a slow, expensive, and daunting process


Those existing systems are already frustrating for the targeted creators and users, but under DEFEND IP a whole class of people doing protected speech will find themselves deplatformed because of the actions of others


This bill is not a defense of creativity or creators. It is a way to reshape the internet by building a vast new infrastructure of censorship. Congress should put aside DEFEND IP and the failed idea of site-blocking laws, for good.

author: Sofia Little
title: Get the Flock Out
content:
On September 23rd, the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing titled “Always Watching: Flock’s Nationwide AI Surveillance Network,” examining the privacy risks, data sharing, and misuse of private automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks.

The hearing was chaired by Sen. Hawley (R-MO) and featured five witnesses, including Lindsey Isaacs, a wrongfully accused driver, Alasdair Whitney from Legislative Counsel Institute for Justice, Sheriff Ross Teeple, Benn Jordan, a self-proclaimed “hacker”, and policy counsel analyst Chad Marlow from the ACLU, where they have coined a campaign called “Get the Flock Out.”

The hearing highlighted pertinent concerns about how ALPR technology can be used and shared. Public concern about Flock cameras has also grown in recent months. A September 2026 Navigator Research survey found that 62% of registered voters were concerned about Flock camera use, including 66% of Democrats, 55% of Republicans, and 70% of Independents.

Flock Safety was founded in 2017 by CEO Garrett Langley, operating as a small startup meant to provide ALPR cameras to homeowners associations and neighborhoods looking to reduce petty theft and local property crimes. Now, it has grown into something alarmingly dystopian: an AI powered network of over 120,000 cameras across 49 states that photograph, scan, tag, and log every driver that passes, whether or not they are suspected of any crime.

License plate reader technologies have existed since the 1970s, in the form of speed, toll, and red-light cameras. These are only triggered by a specific action, such as running a red-light or driving through a toll booth, and only track license plate numbers. The entry of venture capitalist funding and advanced AI technology into the mass surveillance industry has transformed these automatic traffic enforcement cameras into a complex web of invasive surveillance tools.

During the hearing, ACLU’s Mr. Chad Marlow argued that companies operating ALPR systems are profiting from the collection and sharing of information about people’s movements. The ACLU has called for greater limits on how ALPR data can be collected, accessed, and shared.

Privacy concerns extend to how ALPR data can affect people seeking reproductive health care. During the hearing, Sen. Booker (D-NJ) raised concerns that states could use ALPR technology to track people traveling to obtain reproductive care. The concern comes amid documented cases of law enforcement using vehicle surveillance systems to investigate people seeking or suspected of seeking abortion care.

Unfortunately, this ‘hypothetical’ scenario has become the reality for women across the country.

Witnesses Alaster Whitney and Sheriff Ross Teeple both testified about the overreach of Flock’s ALPRs, with Whitney highlighting jurisdiction concerns which police officers have already been accused of taking advantage of.

In Texas, a sheriff’s deputy used 83,000 Flock ALPRs to track a woman who allegedly performed a self-administered abortion, at the behest of her abusive partner. In Massachusetts, a police officer used Flock networks to stalk a former romantic partner who said she had changed her identity to escape from his abuse. In Kentucky, a police officer was accused of searching his child’s mother 1,000 times through Flock’s network, though she has a protective order. The Institute for Justice has catalogued more than 200 incidents of these ALPR abuses, including romantic stalking, wrongful stops and detentions, non-law enforcement use and other types of misconduct.

These encroachments do not just stop here, as Sen. Padilla (D-CA) spotlights the use of loopholes within Flock, which ICE officers take advantage of to track immigrant communities. While Flock has guaranteed no direct access to the Border Patrol subagency, Witness Marlow points out all it takes is one sympathetic person connected to ICE for the agency to obtain access to billions of pictures of citizens, including facial properties.

Concerns about ALPR surveillance have crossed traditional political lines. During the hearing, Sen. Hawley noted that supporters of the Second Amendment have “long feared national databases of any kind.” This has drawn criticism from across the political spectrum highlighting the bipartisan opposition.

While Flock operates as a leading company which produces ALPRs, they are not the sole producers. Companies like Axon and Motorola have slowly begun increasing …

author: EDRi
title: The KIDS Act will make the internet less safe
content:
On 16 September, the European Commission presented the KIDS ACT, its plan for making online experiences safer for young people. Far from being a move to lead the EU towards better digital environments, this move is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. This blog analyse the proposal’s shortcomings.

During her annual address to the European Parliament, the President of the European Commission announced her intention to protect young people from platforms and services that deprive children of their childhood and of their focus. The next day, the Commission published the KIDS ACT (an acronym for ‘Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy’). This announcement arrives after a period of much debate around protecting young people online, and even announcements of social media bans from countries across Europe. As a response to this discussion, on April 22, youth organisations across Europe came together to demand real change, instead of exclusions and bans, from EU lawmakers.

The Commission had the opportunity to change the rules of the dangerous game that makes people unsafe online. Instead, it’s mostly restricting who gets to play. Not only is the KIDS ACT a terrible proposal, it’s also a missed opportunity for the European Commission to lead the EU towards a safer digital environment for children and everyone else. The proposal instead determines who is allowed to use services built upon harmful design choices, and clumsily tries to make some of these choices safe for a narrow age bracket, rather than addressing why they can be harmful in the first place. In doing so, it leaves largely untouched the business models that put us all at risk, and sets complex standards for safety which will cement Big Tech dominance. Let’s unpack the proposal.

The KIDS ACT mostly delays young people’s exposure to online harms. On the one hand, it would ban social media accounts for those under 15*. On the other hand, it would require companies to apply certain protections to minors’ accounts against pervasive exploitative tracking, intrusive default settings, and AI companions designed to create emotional dependencies, among other risky features.

What is striking is that these protections apply only to people aged 15*-18. It’s as if these services, practices and functionalities will magically cease to be harmful on someone’s 18th birthday. We all remain vulnerable to manipulative design and unfair personalisation even as adults: not even the most digitally literate person can examine every single default setting, decode every recommendation system, or resist every strategically timed prompt designed to get us to keep clicking. Fairness must be built into the environment itself, not left to the skills of the people using it. Many of the measures proposed in the KIDS ACT address harms that are not specific to childhood and were therefore meant to be tackled through the forthcoming Digital Fairness Act (DFA), which the Commission said will address addictive design for all consumers. The risk is that by treating these practices primarily as child-safety problems, the Commission is lowering the ambition of the rules still to come. Under the appearance of acting on online harms, the KIDS ACT may rob us of stronger protections for ALL of us, including children.

The underlying logic of the KIDS ACT is that, while some risks can be mitigated for people aged 15-18, those under 15* years old should be banned from social media altogether. This blanket age-based exclusion treats children’s online presence as the problem, rather than following young people’s own call to examine the conditions under which digital services expose them to harm. Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, young people — including those under 15 — have the fundamental right, online and offline, to participate in society, access information, communicate with others, play, and develop their identities. Age-gates undermine these rights.

They would also fundamentally change the open nature of the internet: services would have to treat users as children by default unless they prove their age. The Commission’s approach would create a two-tier internet in which children but also adults who cannot or do not wish to pass an age check are excluded from spaces that have become important for education, socialisation, access to information and participation in public life. People …

Open Source Is Not the Same Thing as Liberation

Open Source Is a Tool, Not a Commandment

There is a peculiar form of ideological dogmatism that has emerged within parts of the FOSS movement. Even in anarchist circles, some people seem to believe that opposition to intellectual property must take precedence over virtually every other ethical consideration. After all, if copyright, patents, and other forms of intellectual property are inherently illegitimate, then any attempt to place limits on how the things we create are used or distributed must necessarily be reactionary, right? Even when those limits are intended to protect workers, creators, and wider communities from exploitation by capital?

Anarchists do not seek to abolish one particular category of property while leaving other relations of domination untouched. Nor do we advocate stripping workers of control over the fruits of their labor in the name of an ideological dogma that ultimately has little to do with fostering anarchism.

The rise of so-called “generative AI” has made this contradiction impossible to ignore. My recent essay on this technology was criticized by some open-source diehards because, in their view, no one has the right to restrict the flow of information — even when that flow gushes directly from the minds and labor of workers and creatives into the bulging bank accounts of Silicon Valley billionaires.

To be clear: I am not opposed to free and open-source software. The forum I run (Raddle.me) was built on software (Postmill) that my cofounder released into the commons from the outset under a FOSS license. Even when fascists forked her code to spread hate and harassment, and when a scummy developer violated the license and tried to pass her work off as his own for profit, we did not respond by retreating behind a closed-source license. As anti-authoritarians and anti-capitalists, we certainly could have justified doing so when her work was being used to harm marginalized communities and enrich capitalists, but the license was kept open.

The same principle applies to my own writing. I release all of my essays freely, and I give zine-makers permission to reprint them without restriction. I believe in sharing knowledge and making creative work accessible. People have the option to donate to support my work if they want to. What I oppose is capital taking that generosity, enclosing it within a for-profit ecosystem, and turning it into another mechanism for extracting wealth from the people who created it.

This is not an argument that copyright is inherently liberatory. It is an argument that the abolition of intellectual property is not, by itself, liberation.

I feel compelled to take a stand against the increasingly rigid open-source absolutism that has taken hold in parts of the milieu: against the ruling class taking our collective knowledge, privatizing it, and selling it back to us. I do not consider this a pro-IP argument, but I’m sure plenty of people will disagree. It is an argument against AI slop …

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Live in the Real World
content:
Our dependence on our phones isn’t an accident. We depend on them logistically for our navigation, payment, and communication. But our phones and the apps they contain are also designed to build emotional dependence — there are entire teams of top-of-their-field psychologists, engineers, sociologists, and designers getting paid hundreds of thousands of dollars a year to make apps even just a little bit more addictive. The emotional and logistical dependence on our phones intertwine in a mutual feedback loop, making it difficult to reduce either.

Every interaction we have with our phones deepens opportunities for state surveillance. Our online activity creates a database of our interests, purchase history, friend networks, location, and activism that the FBI of yesteryear could only have dreamed of. But the biggest problem, as with any addiction, is how something that is fun and useful in small doses can start to take more and more of our time and attention, preventing us from doing other things that we value. So what is there to do?

For most of us, the apps that most deeply build psychological dependence on our phones are social media apps and games. These often take, in some ways, the place of cigarettes in our society today — we do them on a quick break, or when we need to ‘unwind’. But like nicotine, they mostly sate the need that they themselves create. After unwinding in this way, do you feel deeply rested and reset?

If there is an app that you feel wastes your time, or you dislike how much you use, just delete it! You can always re-download it. Note down in your organizer the date and time you deleted the app, and why. If you redownload the app, note that down too. It’s helpful to understand our own patterns of use, to help us understand where we use “tools” or “toys” out of necessity or fun, versus out of psychological dependence.

Think about other activities you can do when you would have used your phone. If you delete an app, it’s easy for some other app to quickly replace it. Be realistic about what might feel fulfilling and restful while deprogramming, in those times and in that headspace. Watching landscapes slide past, noticing the people around you, thinking about your present, past or future, having a conversation with a friend or stranger, reading: each of these might feel more wholesome or restful than your phone. Your Slingshot organizer may be able help you… Don’t you think the edges of the date pages could use additional intricate doodles? Or perhaps you can journal a bit, filling in past date entries with what you remember doing, seeing, eating, or thinking on that day? Use the blank pages in the back to write poetry or outline a manifesto or draw art. Let your boredom be a canvas, a portal to discovery, not something to avoid.

These activities won’t feel as stimulating or give you the same dopamine rush as the apps you’re used to. It’s normal to feel a sense of confusion or loss in this process. Perhaps at some deep level the bright, shifting light of the screen feels like a flickering fire: a thousand generations of finding safety and community in campfires draws us inexorably to this bright cold flame. Try changing your phone’s settings to have the display be in black and white, or switch to a dimmer, less attractive color palette.

We can also feel emotional dependence on the instant knowledge and communication phones provide. What if we can’t respond right away to a friend or loved one? It’s so easy to ask a question to AI like Siri or Google and get an affirming answer! Like puppies or young children, we become anxious without the constant presence of that communication or knowledge. Try consciously pushing your limits more often — if you don’t know something, discuss it rather than looking up ‘the answer’ right away. Delete search bars and AI assistants from your phone and download the Wikipedia app, so if you do need to look something up, you will break that instant gratification loop, finding your own answer and giving yourself context along the way. And try setting aside a specific time of the day to answer your messages. Let friends or loved ones know you might not respond quickly outside of that time.

Logistical dependence is hard in a different way. Practical uses for our phones are often the most problematic sites of government and corporate surveillance, and reinforce emotional dependence by repeatedly forcing us back to our screens.

Try leaving your phone on airplane mode …

author: Dion Nissenbaum
title: SCOTUS Greenlights Use of Federal Citizenship Tool to Vet Voters
content:
The ruling was a rare victory for Trump in his effort to impose more federal control over the country’s electoral system.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Supreme Court cleared the way Friday for election officials to resume using a federal immigration status verification system to check voter rolls for potential noncitizens — a significant victory for President Donald Trump’s administration, but one that’s likely to have little impact on the November midterm elections.

The unsigned opinion hit pause on a lower court’s ruling from June while the case works its way through the appeals process. The lower court had found that the Department of Homeland Security had violated voter privacy by expanding the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements system, better known as SAVE, so that states could run their voter rolls through it to check for any noncitizens.

Friday’s ruling is not expected to lead to any widespread removal of voters before the November election because federal law prohibits election officials from systematically unregistering voters within 90 days of an election.

However, as a result of the ruling, the Trump administration will be able to restart use of the SAVE system to scrutinize state voter rolls after the election, and election officials will be able to use the SAVE system to check the citizenship of individual voters in the meantime as well.

The Department of Homeland Security has maintained the SAVE system for decades to check immigrants’ eligibility for public benefits. But in 2025, the Trump administration revamped the tool to allow election officials to check voter rolls in bulk against federal citizenship and immigration records and to search using Social Security numbers, making it far easier to screen registered voters for potential noncitizens.

The case against the expanded SAVE was brought by a coalition of groups, including the League of Women Voters and the Electronic Privacy Information Center, that argued that the Trump administration violated Americans’ privacy by expanding how the system is used.

“Today’s decision is profoundly disappointing, as it puts Americans at risk of being unlawfully targeted by the administration’s unreliable voter purge database weeks before the midterm elections,” Abigail Kunkler, an attorney for the Electronic Privacy Information Center, said in a statement on behalf of the plaintiffs.

She said the case “is not over” and noted the lower court had ruled that the expanded SAVE violates multiple laws. “We will be doing everything in our power to protect Americans’ voting and privacy rights by ensuring that the district court decision stands.”

Trump administration officials celebrated the court victory.

“Yes, you read that right. We had to file an emergency petition in the Supreme Court just so we could use government data to help states stop noncitizens from illegally voting,” James Percival, the Department of Homeland Security’s general counsel, said on X in reaction to the decision.

The Department of Homeland Security has said that election officials in 25 states, mostly Republicans, have run their voter rolls through the SAVE system. Some of those officials praised SAVE as a valuable tool for weeding out ineligible voters, but others have found it to be unreliable.

A ProPublica investigation from earlier this year found that the Trump administration’s rush to turn the system into a voter verification tool made it prone to false positives. In at least five different states, the system has flagged people as noncitizens who were actually citizens.

In Texas, Votebeat reported that the system flagged hundreds of people who had registered to vote through the state Department of Public Safety, which requires proof of citizenship from any prospective registrants. State and local election officials have confirmed that several of those people are indeed eligible to vote.

In a dissent to Friday’s opinion, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson cited the problems in Texas as a main reason she opposed the Trump administration’s use of the SAVE system to check voter rolls. Jackson noted that one plaintiff in the case had her voter registration revoked without her knowledge and that two others had to provide proof of citizenship to remain on voter rolls.

“The harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the Government experiences …

author: Monica Atieno, Angela Chukunzira and Athandiwe Saba
title: Inside Kenya’s Hidden Deals with Big Tech
content:
When an outsourcing company working for Meta found itself being sued in Kenya, it took its problem to the President.


The dispute had begun in May 2022, when former Facebook content moderator Daniel Motaung sued Sama and Meta over working conditions. Another 43 moderators brought a case in March 2023. The workers had been employed by Sama to moderate Facebook content, work that required them to repeatedly view disturbing material. They argued that Meta, which ultimately benefited from and controlled aspects of their work, should also be held responsible.


Sama was not a minor contractor in Kenya. It was part of the labour pipeline that allowed a global technology company to outsource some of the most harmful work of the internet to Kenyan workers. Meta fought to remove itself from the litigation, arguing, among other things, that Kenyan courts did not have jurisdiction over the foreign company. But on 20 September 2024, the Court of Appeal rejected that argument.


Then on 11 November 2024, less than two months after that ruling, the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill was published. It proposed new rules for Kenya’s outsourcing industry, including provisions dealing with who should carry responsibility for workers employed by outsourcing companies.


Less than a month later, on 9 December, President William Ruto publicly said Sama had approached him about its legal troubles. “Now I can report to you that we have changed the law,” he said, adding that “nobody will take you to court again on any matter.”


But the bill was still before Parliament, where a fight was unfolding over who should be held responsible for outsourced workers. Business groups including KEPSA and the Kenya Association of Manufacturers

argued

 that responsibility should largely remain with the outsourcing company. Tech workers argued that companies that control or benefit from their work should also be held responsible. This was very important for workers trying to sue companies such as Meta rather than only their local contractors.


Figure 1: Africa Tech Workers Movement members during a joint press conference in August 2025, raising concerns about the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024.


The workers also went to court to try to stop the bill. In June 2026, the High Court

declined

 to intervene. On 19 August 2026, the National Assembly passed the amendments. It now awaits for presidential assent. 


For James Oyange, a former content moderator, Ruto’s statement sent a clear message about whose side the government was on. Workers had gone to court seeking protection from some of the world’s most powerful technology companies; instead, he said, the government appeared to be changing the rules in the companies’ favour.


“We are on our own. It is the responsibility of the government to protect us, but they are taking Big Tech’s side. It means the companies can do what they want.”


Oyange fears that if technology companies can turn to the government when workers sue them, while workers are left with fewer ways to hold those companies responsible, the balance of power shifts even further away from workers.


The Sama case is one part of a much wider relationship between Kenya’s government and global technology companies.

The Continent

 identified at least 12 publicly documented meetings, agreements, regulatory engagements and partnerships between the Kenyan government and Microsoft, Google, Amazon, TikTok and Starlink since 2023.


The investigation also found a pattern across these relationships. Major technology companies are being brought into public services, infrastructure and policymaking, often through agreements the public cannot see. At the same time, laws and policies are being developed that can make it easier for these companies to operate. What is much harder to find is who negotiated these arrangements, what Kenya agreed to in return, and who is checking whether they serve the public interest.


Agriculture is one example. In 2020, the Ministry of Agriculture signed an agreement with Microsoft to use technology to

improve farming and food security.

 Microsoft would provide cloud technology for digital tools using information about weather, pests, farming inputs and production.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Does China Intend to Target Taiwan With New National Security Legislation?
content:
TAIWANESE GOVERNMENT officials, speaking under conditions of anonymity to the media, have warned that China may roll out national security legislation directed at Taiwan in the coming months. Such national security legislation would follow up on China’s recently passed ethnic unity law.

The law criminalizes actions aimed at disrupting a vaguely defined “national unity”. Although initial warnings were that the law was mainly aimed at Tibetans and Uyghurs, the Lai administration has framed such national security legislation as potentially a threat to Taiwan. Under such laws, after all, support for Taiwanese independence–or even just maintaining Taiwan’s current democratic freedoms and its de facto independence–could be construed as illegal and criminal under the law.

Such Taiwanese government officials have pointed to a number of laws, some of which are still in the review process, as potentially impacting Taiwan. This includes the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration, Measures for the Supervision and Inspection of Cyberspace Security, and National Defense Mobilization Law.

In particular, the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration could be used to prevent Taiwanese who have traveled to China from leaving. This already occurred in the past, however, most prominently in the case of activist Lee Ming-che, who spent over five years in Chinese jails on charges of seeking to subvert the state. Lee is thought to have been detained over exchanges with Chinese friends on Taiwan’s experiences regarding democratization. Others imprisoned, however, have been noted to include pan-Blue academics, who seem to have fallen afoul of espionage charges in spite of pro-unification viewpoints.

Measures on cybersecurity take place at a time when the Chinese government has attempted to depict Taiwan as engaged in cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. Such allegations seem to be an attempt to depict Taiwan as engaged in the same activity it routinely accuses China of being engaged in, seeing as China consistently conducts cyberattacks on Taiwan and probes key infrastructure. Importantly, such allegations could also be used to cement a casus belli to justify war.

Indeed, to this extent, the National Defense Mobilization Law has been warned as potentially intended to provide the legal grounds for wartime mobilization. Indeed, such a law might be necessary ahead of a Chinese invasion, particularly if the Chinese government intends to move Chinese society as a whole toward war footing, and mobilize all of society to conduct an invasion.

Still, at a time of highly polarized politics between the KMT and DPP, it can be expected that the KMT will probably deny that China has intentions for future national security legislation. KMT chair Cheng Li-wun has, of course, attempted to depict China as only having goodwill toward Taiwan, while depicting the DPP as, in fact, the ones who have sought to provoke China. As such claims to the media are made ahead of elections in November, they will be depicted as simply intended to drum up public fear for the sake of electioneering.

title: Protest in Ranya Against environmental destruction and Turkish military presence
content:
Numerous people in Ranya protested against the destruction of Kurdistan’s natural environment and the continued Turkish military presence in Southern Kurdistan. The rally, held in front of the city’s People’s Garden, was organized by the Koşan Group under the slogan “Êdî bes e dagirkerî û xirabkirina jîngeha Kurdistanê” — “Enough with the occupation and destruction of Kurdistan’s environment.”


Speaking on behalf of the group, Şadiye Samed said that for years the Turkish state had militarily occupied large areas of Behdînan under the pretext of waging war against the guerrillas of the Kurdish freedom movement. In addition to the deaths of numerous civilians, she said, the war had caused severe damage to the environment, nature and infrastructure of Southern Kurdistan.


With the peace and democratic society process launched in February 2025, there was no longer any justification for continuing the war and military occupation in Southern Kurdistan, the Koşan Group stated. Nevertheless, it said, the destruction of the natural environment and the Turkish military presence have continued. “Protecting the borders and forests of Southern Kurdistan is not merely an environmental issue. It is also part of protecting our land, our culture and our identity,” the statement said.


Criticism was also directed at the government of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI). Its silence in the face of the destruction of the forests was described as part of the problem. In conclusion, the Koşan Group called on citizens, institutions, activists and environmental movements both inside and outside Kurdistan to take a stand against the destruction of nature and the Turkish military presence. The group demanded the withdrawal of the Turkish army from Southern Kurdistan and an end to interventions in the region.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Meet Issa Amro: Palestinian Human Rights Advocate Attacked by Settlers, Detained by Israeli Army
content:
We speak with Palestinian human rights defender Issa Amro after he was detained at an Israeli military base for seven hours on Friday. Amro, the founder of the Hebron-based group Youth Against Settlements, was helping a Palestinian family that he says had been attacked by armed Israeli settlers at their farmhouse outside Hebron in the occupied West Bank. Amro says when Israeli soldiers arrived, they ignored the settlers and instead targeted the Palestinians, including him. Amro tells

Democracy Now!

 that soldiers handcuffed and blindfolded him before transporting him to the base in the back of a military vehicle. He was freed after an international outcry over his arrest.


“What happened to me is happening to many Palestinian families and many Palestinian human rights defenders and many Palestinian journalists,” says Amro. “It’s not the first time. It’s not the last time. We have to keep working to make occupation [and] apartheid costly and make this kind of human rights violation costly for the offenders.”

content:
„

Respekt für unsere Arbeit! Wir holen, was uns zusteht“ – unter diesem Motto treffen sich rund 250 delegierte Mitglieder der IG BAU vom 27. bis 30. September in Kassel. Als Gewerkschaft wissen wir: höhere Löhne, 8-Stunden-Tag, Lohnfortzahlung im Krankheitsfall – nichts davon wurde uns geschenkt. Für jede Verbesserung haben Arbeitnehmer*innen gekämpft. Auch jetzt, wo soziale Errungenschaften und Arbeitnehmerrechte plötzlich wieder zur Debatte stehen, geben wir nicht auf!.

..“

Sonderseite der IG BAU

 

 mit allen Infos zum Gewerkschaftstag und hier die wichtigsten Beschlüsse:


IG Bau: „Die Abrüstung muss wieder auf die politische Agenda“ Gewerkschaft fordert klare Absage an Aufrüstungsspirale und Wehrpflicht – Rüstungsindustrie stärker kontrollieren


„Die Welt wird unsicherer – doch die Antwort darauf darf nicht immer mehr Aufrüstung heißen. Auf dem 24. Ordentliche Gewerkschaftstag der Industriegewerkschaft Bauen-Agrar-Umwelt (IG BAU) in Kassel fordert eine große Mehrheit der Delegierten eine klare politische Kehrtwende: Frieden, Abrüstung und Diplomatie statt einer immer schneller drehenden Aufrüstungsspirale. „Wir wollen keine Gesellschaft, die sich auf Krieg vorbereitet, sondern eine Gesellschaft, die Frieden möglich macht. Mehr Waffen und immer größere Rüstungsausgaben sind kein Selbstzweck. Sicherheit muss den Menschen dienen – und nicht den Profiten der Rüstungsindustrie“, lautet der Tenor. Die IG BAU will sich künftig verstärkt für Frieden, Abrüstung und internationale Zusammenarbeit einsetzen. (…) Ein klares „Nein“ sagt die IG BAU auch zur Wehrpflicht. Gerade angesichts des Fachkräftemangels dürfe die junge Generation nicht zum Dienst an der Waffe verpflichtet werden. Wer einen Wehrdienst leisten wolle, müsse dies freiwillig tun können. Kritisch sieht die Gewerkschaft zudem die geplante Stationierung weitreichender US-Waffensysteme in Deutschland. Sie fordert eine gesellschaftliche Debatte über die Folgen einer Politik, die Deutschland zunehmend zum Schauplatz einer militärischen Eskalation machen könne. Auch bei den Rüstungsausgaben verlangt die IG BAU einen Kurswechsel: Nicht starre Prozentvorgaben oder die Interessen von Rüstungskonzernen dürften über Umfang und Ausstattung entscheiden, sondern der tatsächliche Auftrag zur Verteidigung des Landes. Beschaffung und Rüstungspolitik müssten dem Primat der Politik und einer demokratischen Kontrolle unterliegen. „Wir akzeptieren nicht, dass für immer mehr Waffen angeblich kein Geld fehlt, während bei sozialen Aufgaben, der Bildung, bezahlbarem Wohnraum und der Zukunft unserer Gesellschaft gespart wird. Sicherheit ist mehr als militärische Stärke. Sicherheit bedeutet auch soziale Sicherheit, gute Arbeit, Demokratie und ein Leben in Frieden.“ Die IG BAU fordert deshalb eine Politik, die Friedensfähigkeit stärkt, Abrüstung wieder auf die internationale Tagesordnung setzt und Rüstungsausgaben strikt auf notwendige Verteidigungsfähigkeit begrenzt. Übergewinne der Rüstungsindustrie sollen zudem mit einer Steuer belegt werden.“

author: Poetry Collection
title: A War Song to the Person Who Told Me to Die by Raine Ajani
content:
I just thought you should know I’m doing okay now,


I’m shielded by hardened sweat and scum,


Wielding a sword of my broken fingernails,


Voice rupturing with my vengeful war song.


I am forged by the failure to be perfect,


The pressure to exist with precision cracks my knees,


Self-assured strides callous my feet,


All while being told to die.


I just thought you should know what I’ve been through,


Furious deserts and loveless tundra,


The sweet, prickly fruit of addiction,


The ice shards of words I’ll never forget.


Since the last time I saw you,


I’ve been pricked by needles,


Forced to breathe acid-laced air,


Draped in blue scrubs,


And drugged to the point of stability.


I found my dignity in the fetal position,


I needed my breasts to warm my chest,


Needed to put my head to my knees…


To cry,


To think,


To let the spite bubble like stomach acid.


I just thought you should know what I wish for the future,


Black ink shaped to form the letters of my name,


The hard edges of words,


Words I’ll write,


Words that hug and choke my readers,


And make you regret your cruelty.


I hope your regret castrates you and your confidence.


I just thought you should know how your wish for my death used to make me want to grant it,


I thought death could make me feel seen,


Make me a scene on the city block,


For what screams see me more than the crunch of my bones under your flip-flops,


And the smack of vultures feasting on pink human flesh.


So here I stand,


Ready to cleave your arrogance,


Swinging with the might of jagged pills and my hatred for you,


Ready to taste the sweetness of justice…


But why do I taste bitterness?


What’s making me gag and sputter?


After all, you’re bad,


Bad to your bloodstream.


But what if… badness isn’t a stone?


Static,


Unmoving,


Unchanging.


What if… it’s oil?


Slippery,


Flowing,


Seeping.


What if… it has seeped into me?


Maybe, this war song needs to be an inquiry…


What is it that you want me to know?


What is it you’ve been through?


What have you braved?


What do you wish for the future?


I’m taking off my armor,


Dropping my sword,


And crying with you.


We are both aching.


* * *


Raine Ajani is a young student of the writing craft based in Portland, Oregon who hungers for growth. The daughter of an Ethiopian immigrant, she enjoys fantasy books, making jewelry, and exploring the nuances of the human experience through language and conversation.
