author: Mahdi Niksefat Motlagh
title: Ending the war requires accepting Iran in the Middle East
content:
The hardest question about ending the war with Iran belongs in Washington. What place can Iran occupy after the fighting stops? A country left economically excluded, unable to rebuild and exposed to renewed attack has little reason to regard a ceasefire as a durable ending. The war cannot be politically settled while Iranian recovery remains an unacceptable outcome.

The latest diplomacy leaves that question unresolved. Tehran has received US feedback, through Qatar, on a seven-day trust-building proposal. Yet on 1 October, the US Treasury expanded sanctions against Iran’s automotive and rail sectors, alongside manufacturing and steel networks. Talks about ending the confrontation are proceeding alongside measures that further restrict Iran’s capacity to sustain its economy.

The Islamic Republic connects these claims to a revolutionary and religious account of its purpose. Ali Khamenei’s 2019 Second Phase statement, with its emphasis on building an Islamic civilisation, expressed that connection explicitly. Security, within this understanding, includes the capacity to continue a political project.

Israel also brings historical and theological claims to its modern statehood. Netanyahu has described it as the Middle East’s sole true democracy. In his September UN address, he invoked the Jewish people’s three-thousand-year history and biblical attachment to the land while anticipating the Iranian government’s fall.

Different understandings of statehood do not make war inevitable. The contradiction arises when Israeli security is defined through the dismantling of Iran’s capacity to remain an independent regional power. Under that definition, even Iranian reconstruction can appear threatening because recovery restores the resources through which Iran can act. Iran’s continued existence and Israel’s preferred regional order then become politically incompatible.

This gives the war its ontological dimension. For Iran, survival involves retaining the ability to decide its future and sustain its place in the region. For Netanyahu’s government, an Iran capable of recovering may signify the return of an existential threat. Military operations can damage Iranian capabilities. They cannot resolve this dispute over what Iran is allowed to become after the bombing.

The June 2025 war and the present confrontation make a distinction between surviving an attack and securing a durable ending especially consequential.

Its strategic implication is nevertheless clear: economic recovery itself can become a reason to preserve pressure.

A settlement built on permanent Iranian weakness would therefore contain the grounds for renewed confrontation. Iran needs the capacity to rebuild. An Israeli government that treats this capacity as intolerable would retain an incentive to obstruct it. More accurate weapons or more sophisticated surveillance cannot reconcile these positions.

Washington must confront that contradiction because the costs of the war reach beyond Israel’s objectives. Energy markets, shipping through Hormuz and the security of American partners make indefinite confrontation costly. An American exit requires persuading Israel to accept the survival of an independent Iran with an economic future in the region. It also requires Washington to accept that outcome itself.

Trump’s interview with TIME, published on 1 October, exposes the difficulty. Explaining why he had continued the campaign, he said he did not want Iran to return “in some different form”. An ending that depends on preventing Iranian reconstitution keeps the political purpose of the war open even after military objectives are declared achieved.

The tension also appears in the 2025 US National Security Strategy. It advocates accepting Middle Eastern countries’ historical forms of government while prioritising Israel’s security and the expansion of the Abraham Accords. The practical question is whether such acceptance extends to Iran, or whether Iran must remain the exception against which the region’s political and economic integration is organised.

Other regional states have a decisive role here. Their political acceptance of Iran need not involve adopting its institutions or sharing its revolutionary commitments. It means recognising that Iran’s historical and political form has a legitimate place alongside their own. Regional stability requires room for different states to pursue development without making one state’s permanent exclusion the condition of …

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: From Tigray to the Red Sea: Ethiopia’s War in a Wider Regional Struggle
content:
I am not a military expert, but I do not read the withdrawal of Tigrayan forces from towns as straightforward evidence that their military position has weakened. An army can leave towns, roads and airports without losing its ability to move, reorganize, coordinate and strike. The more important questions are whether the force remains intact, how mobile it is, whether it can coordinate across different fronts, and whether it can still choose where and when to engage.

That is how I look at what is happening around Mekelle. Reuters reported on October 2 that federal and allied forces were moving toward the Tigrayan capital, and the following day reported that they had retaken Alula Aba Nega Airport. On a conventional military map that looks like a major federal success. But the map may be giving us a false sense of what is actually happening.

Debretsion Gebremichael who is the president of Tigray had already announced a counteroffensive and said Tigrayan forces would not fight according to the government’s dictates. I therefore do not see their movement out of Mekelle as a setback. I see an orderly and deliberate withdrawal from a fixed urban position by a force whose leadership had already told us that it intended to choose a different battlefield.

That distinction is important. Under conditions of federal air and drone superiority, concentrating fighters and equipment inside a city can make them sitting ducks. Moving out can preserve forces, stretch the opponent and create possibilities elsewhere. During the struggle against the Derg, the TPLF repeatedly relied on mobility rather than treating possession of every town as the measure of military strength. Today’s circumstances are different, especially because of drones and surveillance, but that experience should not simply be forgotten.

As I argued in The Geography of Asymmetric War, military power cannot be measured only by territory. Terrain, mobility, strategic depth and the ability to force a stronger opponent to fight differently also matter. A counteroffensive does not have to begin by immediately retaking Mekelle. It can strike supply lines, isolated units, communications systems, airfields or another front entirely.

This is why I am cautious even about the language of a federal “advance.” Federal forces are certainly moving into places Tigrayan forces have left. But that does not necessarily mean that one army is advancing while the other is simply retreating. If one side is deliberately giving up fixed positions in order to preserve mobility and shift the war elsewhere, the territorial map can create an illusion of momentum that may turn out to be temporary.

Focusing only on Mekelle also misses how much the war has changed. Fighting extends through Amhara and Afar, and armed movements that were enemies only a few years ago are now cooperating against the same federal government. Afar matters because it lies between Tigray, Eritrea and the routes toward Ethiopia’s Djibouti corridor. Amhara matters because Fano and Tigrayan forces, who recently fought a devastating war against one another, are now cooperating. These are not secondary developments. They change the political and military meaning of the war.

I began writing about this changing landscape in Tsimdo and the Changing Politics of the Horn. The creation of the seven group Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival took that process much further. The political map that existed when Pretoria was signed no longer describes Ethiopia, which is why I later argued that Pretoria Cannot Explain Ethiopia Anymore.

The map can show federal troops entering Mekelle. It cannot easily show former enemies learning to fight together. Nor can it show what has happened hundreds of miles behind the supposed front line in Bishoftu and Addis Ababa.

For years the federal government could use aircraft and drones against its opponents while assuming that its own air bases, military command and political center were safely beyond their reach. That assumption has been shattered. Drones have reportedly struck Harar Meda Air Base at Bishoftu, headquarters of the Ethiopian Air Force. Ethiopia Observer reported explosions inside the base and described considerable alarm among military personnel.

This is much more than another attack on a military installation. Drone warfare was one of the decisive advantages that helped Abiy Ahmed’s government survive when Tigrayan forces approached Addis Ababa in 2021. Now the …

author: Jim McIlroy
title: Snap protest demands Labor pressure US to stop its war on Cuba, Venezuela
content:
The Australia-Cuba Friendship Society (ACFS) and the Australia-Venezuela Solidarity Network (AVSN) called a snap rally on October 3 to demand the United States stop threatening and blockading Cuba, Venezuela and Latin America.

It was part of an international day, called by the US United National Anti-War Coalition, to defend the sovereignty of Latin America, particularly Cuba and Venezuela.

US peace organisation CODEPINK said on September 30 that it had information that the US Army Reserve was preparing to invade Cuba, in three to four months’ time. The US Southern Command is allegedly massing military police, engineers, medical units, battlefield surgical capacity and major logistics forces.

The rally demanded that the federal Labor federal government call on the US government to stop its invasion plans of Cuba and lift the 60-year blockade, and end the 10-year blockade on Venezuela.

It also called for Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and Cilia Flores’s release from the notorious US Federal Prison in Brooklyn, where they have imprisoned for eight months on trumped-up charges of drug trafficking.

Coral Wynter, from AVSN and Socialist Alliance (SA), told the rally: “All of Latin America is now under threat from a resurgence of the 19th century Monroe doctrine, with fascist-leaning, US-dominated puppet governments agreeing to US military bases and foreign interference.

“The US commits silent genocides on the people of Latin America with its illegal sanctions. We cannot let this happen. We cannot remain silent in the face of imperialist aggression. History is written by people who rise up and fight for justice,” Wynter said.

Other speakers included Patrick Newbold from ACFS and Red Spark, and myself from AVSN and SA.

title: Pervin Buldan’dan “süreç” açıklaması: “Ekim ayıyla birlikte somut bir gelişmeye tanıklık edebiliriz”
content:
DEM Parti İmralı Heyeti Üyesi Pervin Buldan, Abdullah Öcalan’ın hem silahsızlanma sürecinde hem de siyasal ve demokratik inşa sürecinde koordinatörlük görevini üstleneceğini dile getirdi. Buldan, “Önümüzdeki günlerde bu konuda somut bir gelişmeye tanıklık edebiliriz” dedi.

MA’dan Adnan Bilen’in sorularını yanıtlayan Pervin Buldan, yaptıkları son görüşmede PKK Lideri Öcalan’ın, sürecin ilerlemesi için herkesin inisiyatif alması ve siyasi feraset göstermesi gerektiğinin üzerinde durduğunu aktardı. Buldan, “Süreçte pozitif barış aşamasına geçmemizi sağlayacağını söyledi. Yani yüz yıllık meselenin silahlı kısmıyla değil, siyasal kısmıyla ilgili müzakerelerin olacağı ve adımların atılacağı aşamaya geçeceğiz” dedi.

Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan ve Meclis Başkanı Kurtulmuş’un bugüne kadar sürece pozitif katkı yaptığını belirten Buldan, “Silah bırakma meselesinin sürecin temel başlıklarından biri olduğunu biliyoruz ve bu konudaki hassasiyeti anlıyoruz. Ama bu durumun karşılıklı adımlarla çözülebileceğine inanıyoruz. Burada önemli olan, bu tür söylemlerin sürecin önünde bir ön şart olarak değil, birlikte yürüyen adımların bir parçası olarak ele alınmasıdır” diye konuştu.

Abdullah Öcalan’ın hem silahsızlanma sürecinde hem de siyasal ve demokratik inşa sürecinde koordinatörlük görevini üstleneceğini dile getiren Buldan, şöyle devam etti: “Bunun için kurulan kurulun koordinesini sağlaması, toplumun farklı kesimleriyle görüşmesi, özgür çalışma ve iletişim koşullarının sağlanması kaçınılmaz bir gerekliliktir. Kurul, sürecin ilerlemesinin deyim yerindeyse atar damarı olacak. Kurul hem silahsızlanma süreçlerini yönetecek hem de siyasallaşma sürecinde aktif rol alacak. Bu iki alanın aynı kurul çatısı altında ele alınması, birbirini tamamlayan adımların eşgüdüm içinde atılmasını sağlayacak. Silahsızlanmada atılan her adım siyasal alanı genişletecek; siyasal alanda sağlanan her güvence de silahsızlanma sürecine güven katacak. Bu yönüyle kurulun başarısı, sürecin bütününe duyulan güvenin de teminatı olacaktır. Ekim ayıyla birlikte bu görüşmelerin başlaması ve hukuki güvencelerle sürekliliğinin sağlanması gerekiyor. Önümüzdeki günlerde bu konuda somut bir gelişmeye tanıklık edebiliriz.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Lucas
title: Veganes Wichteln
content:
Veganes Wichteln mit ARIWA geht in die nächste Runde

Danke an über 500 Wichtel beim veganen Wichteln 2025!

Bei der Aktion „Veganes Wichteln 2026 von ARIWA“ senden sich unbekannte Personen Überraschungspakete. Was verschenkt wird, ist dabei komplett offen, unterliegt aber zwei Bedingungen: Der Inhalt muss komplett vegan sein und das Geschenk soll von Herzen kommen.


Es kann gebastelt, gehäkelt, genäht, gebacken werden, du kannst zum Laden um die Ecke gehen und eine Kleinigkeit kaufen – Hauptsache ist, dass du dich ebenfalls über den Inhalt freuen würdest! Deiner Kreativität ist daher keine Grenze gesetzt!


So funktioniert das Vegane Wichteln von ARIWA

1.

Anmelden

: Trage dich im Formular unten mit deiner E-Mail-Adresse ein. Teilnehmen können alle Menschen mit einer Postanschrift in Deutschland.


2.

Bestätigen

: Nach dem Absenden bekommst du sofort einen 6-stelligen Code per E-Mail. Gib ihn direkt im Formular ein – fertig! Kommt keine Mail an, schau im Spam-Ordner nach oder fordere im Formular einen neuen Code an. Solltest du dich vertippt haben, kannst du deine Adresse dort korrigieren.


3.

Adresse erhalten

: Nach dem Anmeldeschluss wird jedem Wichtel per E-Mail die Adresse einer anderen Person zugeteilt – auf magische Weise (und ein bisschen IT-Zauber).


4.

Paket verschicken

: Pack dein Überraschungspaket und schicke es bis spätestens 10. Dezember 2026 los.


5.

Freuen

: Jetzt heißt es abwarten – bald erreicht dein Überraschungspaket die Postadresse deines Wichtels und du bekommst im Gegenzug ein Paket voller Überraschungen.


6.

Danke sagen

: Ist dein Paket angekommen? Über den Link in deiner E-Mail gibst du deinem Wichtel Bescheid und kannst ihm eine kleine Nachricht schicken.


7.

Teilen & verbreiten

: Hilf uns, das vegane Wichteln noch bekannter zu machen! Verteile unseren

Aushang

 oder erzähle deinen Freund*innen auf Social Media davon. Vielen Dank für deine Unterstützung!

2024 und 2025 sogar jeweils mehr als 500 Menschen

 beim veganen Wichteln von ARIWA mitgemacht!

Damit hätten wir nicht gerechnet – umso schöner zu sehen, wie viel Freude es euch bereitet, Überraschungspakete zu packen und zu verschicken.


Wir – das Wichtelteam von ARIWA – sagen von Herzen

Danke

 an alle Teilnehmenden. Eure lieben Mails, Dankesworte und guten Wünsche haben uns sehr berührt.


Darum ist klar: Auch 2026 wird es wieder ein veganes Wichteln geben!


Anmeldeschluss: 23. November 2026


Hinweise zum Paket

Was ist vegan?


Veganes enthält keine tierischen Bestandteile wie Milch, Fleisch, Eier, Honig oder auch Bienenwachs, Leder, Wolle. Es ist so hergestellt worden, dass dafür kein Tier leiden musste.


Solltest du dir nicht ganz sicher sein, dann schreib uns unter

wichteln@ariwa.org

.


Wie hoch sollte der Wert des Geschenkes sein?


Der Paketinhalt sollte bei ca. 10 € exklusive Verpackungs- und Versandkosten liegen. Selbstgemachtes ist immer schön, jedoch kein Muss. Wenn du eher nicht zu den Do-it-yourself-Menschen gehörst, freuen sich die Händler*innen bei dir vor Ort.


Können Lebensmittel verschickt werden?

Dies ist möglich, jedoch mit Einschränkungen:


Bitte beachte die jeweils individuell angegebenen Allergien, diese erhältst du direkt mit der Versandadresse.


Bitte verschicke keine Kühlware!


Verpacke die Lebensmittel ordnungsgemäß und am besten luftdicht.


Verzichte bitte gänzlich auf Alkohol! Das Vegane Wichteln steht allen Personen offen und es können auch Kinder unter den Beschenkten sein.


Bitte beschrifte deine Geschenke eindeutig, sodass die beschenkte Person weiß, was sie da gerade genießt. Lege auch gerne das Rezept bei! Wenn du zum Beispiel selbst gebackene Plätzchen verschickst, empfehlen wir, die Zutatenliste beizulegen – für den Fall, dass Allergien bestehen.


Wann solltest du das Paket verschicken?


Spätestens zum 10. Dezember solltest du das Paket versendet haben. Wir erinnern dich daran via E-Mail. Es wäre sehr schade und traurig, wenn eine Person sich auf dein Paket freut und nichts ankommt!


Kann ich mich mit meinem Wichtel austauschen?


Ja! Wenn du bei der Anmeldung zustimmst und dein Wichtelpartner ebenfalls, bekommst du mit der Adresse auch die Mailadresse – so kannst du z.B. nachfragen, ob alles angekommen ist.


Außerdem findest du in deiner Mail einen Link „Paket ist angekommen“. Darüber sagst du der Person, die dich beschenkt hat, Bescheid und kannst ihr eine kleine Dankesnachricht schicken …

author: webadmin
title: Lessons in Hare Hunting: Inside Britain’s School Beagle Packs
content:
The private schools schooling children in a masterclass of wildlife criminality.


Recently we revealed the

full footage of the Stowe School Beagles

 during what school headteacher, Dr Anthony Wallersteiner, describes as a

“huge variety of activities”

 available to pupils, including

“field games…beagling”

.


Kennedy giving direction to the pupils


The school’s Games Coach, Phillip Kennedy, was in the fields surrounding Crockwell Farm, alongside school pupils, ‘coaching’ them as the Stowe School Beagles hunted a hare.


The school lesson ended with a dead hare and a criminal conviction for its Games Coach.


The now-deleted reference to Kennedy’s role at the Stowe School.


Kennedy pleaded guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs after drone footage captured his pack chasing the hare, first through the farmyard and then across open fields before catching and killing her against a fence.

Police said

 that Kennedy knew allowing his dogs to chase and kill the hare was cruel and illegal.


Just as importantly, the footage shone a spotlight on something that has gone on behind the closed doors of some of Britain’s most prestigious private schools: children being introduced to illegal hunting, more than twenty years after hunting wild mammals with dogs was banned.


There are serious safeguarding questions which Stowe School, in particular, appear determined to ignore. What risk assessments are made before children are taken out with packs of hunting dogs? What are staff instructed to do when those hounds begin pursuing a live animal? What safeguarding procedures kick in when pupils witness that animal being caught and killed?


Nothing in the footage suggests this was some unexpected aberration. They all know the routine, the kids congratulate each other, congratulate the dogs. Nobody looks shocked. The huntsman joins in with the handshaking. They’ve clearly done this before haven’t they!


Games Coach Philip Kennedy congratulating pupils as the hounds rip the remains of the hare apart close by.


Stowe is not alone.


There are other school beagle packs still taking children out into the countryside, maintaining the hounds and traditions of hare hunting.


Eton College has one of the oldest and most famous school beagle packs in the country.


Its history stretches back to the nineteenth century

. Long before the Hunting Act, generations of Eton boys learned their “hound lore” by pursuing hares with the school pack. Boys became Masters and Whips, and learned to handle hounds.


The Hunting Act came into force in 2005, but school lessons in hare-hunting continue.


In 2013, eight years after the ban, the Hunt Saboteurs Association

revealed plans

 for a Young Hare-Hunters’ Day at Eton. This was no historical re-enactment of hunting, children were actually being offered coaching in the skills and traditions of hare hunting.


Pupils were to receive training in hare hunting from experienced huntsmen, including Steven Duckmanton, the huntsman of the Dummer Beagles.


Steven Duckmanton, hare-hunting huntsman of the Dummer Beagles. Image: West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs.


In 2024,

West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs

 put a drone above those same Dummer Beagles. The footage they captured showed a hare breaking from the field and the pack pursuing her line across field after field, whilst hunt staff watched.


In October 2015,

footage was filmed

 at an Eton College Beagles meet in North Yorkshire, which showed a live hare fleeing across a field with the pack in pursuit. The footage was handed to North Yorkshire Police in January 2016 and Eton announced an urgent investigation.


Eleven years after hunting with dogs had supposedly been consigned to history, one of Britain’s most prestigious schools was having to investigate its own beagle pack over footage of a hare being hunted.


This year, Sir Jacob Rees-Mogg revealed his eldest son had brought 41 Eton beagles home with him during the school holidays.


His son, Peter Theodore Aphege Rees-Mogg, left Eton this summer. He wasn’t a mere follower of the hunt – he had been a Master of the Eton College Hunt during his final year.


Peter Theodore Aphege Rees-Mogg at home out with the Mendip Farmers Hunt. Image: Mendip Hunt Sabs.


Peter’s mother Helena, herself a regular fox hunter and meet host for the

recently-charged

 Mendip Farmers Hunt, went even further in an article published in September 2026.


Writing about why she believes Eton should remain an all-boys school …

title: Dixon Mink Farm in Bluffdale, Utah will be Forced to Close
content:
Dixon Mink Farm at 15028 Pony Express Road in the town of Bluffdale, Utah will be forced to close.

The city council of Bluffdale has eliminated fur farming as a permitted use. Fur farms will be unable to operate in Bluffdale.

The councilperson who pushed for the change said:

“I saw the serious issue the mink farm had on the lives of our residents. As I knocked on doors of our independence area there were so many flies people couldn’t open their door to talk to me. Because of this ordinance change the city can not approve the business license for this or any other mink farm.”

To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on site it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.

In fact the animal abusers in white coats have become so secure in their belief that no one is watching that they sometimes don’t even bother locking their doors! Use this negligence to your advantage. And while they sleep, go and do your work.


THE LAB RAID IS BACK.


Nine go free…


Another victory for the animals,


ALF”

author: winter oak
title: Never Accidentally Offer Luxury Recycled Cream Cakes to Portuguese Vegan Punks!
content:
This is the fifth and final chapter from the book 

King of the Squatters

 by jaybo which we are delighted to be able to share on Winter Oak. The whole text can be found as a pdf

here

.


I had enjoyed going for food at the social centre twice weekly. But it became tiresome for me to recognise blatant hierarchies and leaders when their on-line blurb claimed that they were anarchists against leaders, organised along horizontal lines, not vertical, top-down power structures. But my relationship with the social centre was completely destroyed one afternoon, after I had just recycled some expensive, fancy cream cakes.


In front of our house, a fiesta had been happening all weekend, so lots of drunken revellers engulfed our usually quiet home. Our squat had been under siege for the three days, being attacked by young adults who threw stones and came into our building looking for trouble. I had not been sleeping well and was very tired one day as I ate some luxury recycled cream cakes in the city centre. Then the social centre’s leader passed me and stopped to speak. We had only ever seen each other previously at the centre, never in public. I offered yer man a fancy cake, without thinking that they were patently not vegan.


He refused and asked me exactly where our squat was. I innocently told him directions to our home. Then he left to go on a demonstration against workers’ exploitation. That night as I walked home, I was stopped dead in my tracks by fresh graffiti on the bridge just before our squat. In big white letters it simply stated, “vegan limit!!!” I had no doubt that the vegan punk anarchist leader had just sprayed the graffiti as some kind of attempted bullshit intimidation directed at me. Because I had offered to share my hard-earned cakes with him.


I never went back to the social centre after that. I was so angry that I knew if I had returned then I would have certainly made trouble and probably have given the leader an excuse to ban me anyway. I hate egos and authoritarians. However, as always, I tried to turn a negative into a positive. That incident inspired one of my most popular signs for The Whimsical Atrocity Theatre (TWAT): “I only eat vegans”.


The next day, TWAT proudly unveiled its new message to the world. It worked immediately. The show was good. I was a little bit worried that one or more of the social centre vegan punks would pass by, see the sign and beat me up. I was probably safe in my theatre, as I usually had a police escort at one side, looking out for the tourists’ safety. But they knew where I lived.


Some brave souls came and spoke to me during or after my cardboard shenanigans. But things reached dizzying heights for TWAT when an American woman came up to me and asked me how much my signs were. I was absolutely flabbergasted. Someone wanted to buy my recycled carton signs. I replied to her spontaneously that, if she wanted to buy a sign, then she had to tell me how much it was. She put four euros into my hat for “I only eat vegans”. Black permanent marker pen on quality recycled cardboard.


Women were flirting with me almost every day when I performed, but I was caught completely off guard when an extremely attractive, well-dressed young French woman came up to me with her friends, picked up the condoms and said, “OK, let’s go!” She was absolutely serious and in a pathetic response, I replied, “You’re wearing a wedding ring.” She countered with, “It’s only an engagement ring. This is my last chance. Are you coming?” Her friends’ looks assured me that she was absolutely serious. I did not go. One of her friends looked at me as though I must have been insane. One of several potentially delicious sexual opportunities that I missed in life.


As the summer really heated up, it felt as though all of Portugal’s crazy folk were coming out of the woodwork and heading for fun in Lisbon. As I worked one day, a sun-drenched, handsome, young man swaggered up the steps towards me. He wore rags as clothes, had matted, unkempt hair flopping all over his face and had a long stick over his shoulder, with a cloth bundle tied up at the other end. He asked if he could write something on one of my signs. I told him he could, so he picked up “this sign was my bed” and wrote on it, “but I washed it in my jacuzzi first”, which killed me and the audience. Then he shouted for all to hear, “We are homeless because we choose to be.”


Before his departure, he asked me if he could take a condom because …

author: PETA-Team
title: Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren
content:
Symbolbild


Die neue „37°“-Dokumentation „Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“ geht der Frage nach, was eigentlich mit Tieren in Versuchslaboren geschieht – und warum die Öffentlichkeit so wenig davon sehen darf.


Am 

29. September 2026 um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF

 sehen die Zuschauer:innen hinter die Kulissen einer Branche, in der Mäuse, Ratten, Hunde, Affen, Kaninchen, Schweine und viele weitere Tiere für Experimente missbraucht werden.


Millionen Tiere leiden für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“


Nach den offiziellen Zahlen wurden in Deutschland

im Jahr 2024 über drei Millionen Tiere

 für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“ missbraucht. Einen großen Teil nimmt die Grundlagenforschung ein, in der Tieren zum Beispiel der Schädel aufgebohrt wird, um Elektroden in ihr Gehirn zu setzen. In regulatorischen, gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Tests werden die Tiere teils vergiftet und getötet.


Solche Experimente finden nicht irgendwo weit entfernt statt, sondern an verschiedenen Forschungseinrichtungen in Deutschland.

Experimente an Affen

, die in der Dokumentation ebenfalls thematisiert werden, sind in der Hälfte der Bundesländer vertreten.


Was passiert in den Versuchslaboren?


Für die Dokumentation hat der Journalist Manfred Karremann mehr als ein Jahr lang versucht, Einblicke in deutsche Tierversuchslabore zu bekommen. Trotz angebotener Anonymität erklärte sich nur eine Einrichtung bereit, ein wenig Einblick zu geben.


Die Dokumentation macht damit ein Problem sichtbar, das Tierschützer:innen seit Jahren kritisieren: Tierversuche finden weitgehend im Verborgenen statt. Sie werden verharmlost und die wenigsten Menschen erfahren, was den Tieren tatsächlich angetan wird. Dabei geht es um Lebewesen, die Angst und Schmerzen empfinden wie wir – und die schlichtweg nicht dazu da sind, dass wir an ihnen experimentieren.


Die Dokumentation zeigt unter anderem Aufnahmen aus einem britischen Labor. Zu sehen sind Hunde,

Affen

, Kaninchen und Ratten, die für sogenannte

Giftigkeitstests

 missbraucht werden. Die Versuche gelten als standardisierte Verfahren und werden nach internationalen Richtlinien durchgeführt – auch in der EU. Tiere müssen dabei beispielsweise Chemikalien einatmen oder bekommen Testsubstanzen über einen Schlauch direkt in den Magen verabreicht.


Jetzt lesen


Forschung und Medizin


Tierversuche in Deutschland: Was wirklich in den Versuchslaboren passiert


In deutschen Tierversuchslaboren werden Affen, Hunde, Katzen, Nagetiere, Fische & Insekten gequält. Erfahren Sie hier mehr über die Versuche!


Jetzt lesen


Tierversuche sind keine gute Wissenschaft


Tierversuche werden oft als „wissenschaftlich notwendig“ gerechtfertigt – doch die Dokumentation zeigt, dass die Wissenschaft längst mit Methoden arbeitet, die ohne Tiermissbrauch auskommen. Expert:innen aus Industrie und Wissenschaft kommen zu Wort und erklären, warum modernste Methoden wie menschliche Zellkulturen oder Organs-on-a-Chip Tierversuchen nicht nur ethisch, sondern auch wissenschaftlich überlegen sind.


Diese Ansätze arbeiten direkt mit menschlichen Zellen und menschlichem Gewebe. Dadurch können sie bei bestimmten Fragestellungen auch Erkenntnisse liefern, die sich besser auf Menschen übertragen lassen.


Jetzt einschalten und hinschauen!


Die „37°“-Dokumentation gibt einen seltenen Einblick in die abgeschottete Welt, in der Tiere in Laboren ihr Leben lang gefangen sind – und zeigt gleichzeitig, warum es längst überfällig ist, dass sich Wissenschaft und Forschung von Tierversuchen abwenden.


„37°: Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“

 läuft am

Dienstag, 29. September 2026, um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF.

 Ab 5:00 Uhr ist die Dokumentation auch über das ZDF-Streaming-Angebot abrufbar.


Jede Unterschrift zählt


PETA fordert von nationalen und internationalen Entscheidungsträger:innen einen strategischen Ausstieg aus Tierversuchen und eine Modernisierung der Forschung. Unterstützen Sie den Research Modernisation Deal und helfen Sie uns, grausame Tierversuche endlich zu beenden.


Jetzt unterschreiben


The post

Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

title: Nourrir ou trahir. Comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France.
content:
On doit changer de modèle, découvrez comment :

Peu importe qui vous êtes et ce en quoi vous croyez : l’élevage intensif trahit vos valeurs.

Nous mangeons 85 kilos de viande par personne et par an, le double de la moyenne mondiale. Ni accident ni dérive, cette consommation de masse est le produit d’un système dont l’élevage intensif est la pierre angulaire.

Souveraineté alimentaire, santé publique, déforestation, biodiversité, ressource en eau, revenu des agriculteurs, sort des animaux : sur chacun de ces fronts, l’élevage intensif nous trahit. Il nous rend dépendants d’engrais et de soja importés, endette les éleveurs, favorise pandémies et antibiorésistance, nuit à l’environnement et entraîne l’abattage de plus de 3 millions d’animaux chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Nous n’avons pas choisi ce modèle. D’autres l’ont choisi pour nous. Ce livre, rédigé par Brigitte Gothière et Sébastien Arsac, cofondateurs de L214, défend une proposition pour reprendre la main ensemble : donnons-nous l’objectif de réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030. Parce que c’est possible. Parce que c’est vital.

d’animaux abattus chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Vous entrez dans un supermarché. Vous prenez un caddie. Vous suivez un itinéraire balisé. Vous voyez ce qui doit être vu, à la hauteur qu'il faut, au prix qu'il faut. Vous croisez la viande partout, les légumineuses presque nulle part. À la sortie, vous avez le sentiment d'avoir choisi.

« On nous a fait croire qu’il fallait choisir son camp : pour les agriculteurs ou pour les animaux, pour le climat ou pour la souveraineté alimentaire. Mais l’élevage intensif ne défend aucun de ces camps, il les renie tous en même temps. C’est ce que ce livre documente, chiffres à l’appui. »

« C’est un livre sur une impasse dont nous devons sortir collectivement. Réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 est une nécessité, soutenue par une majorité de Français. Ceux qui croient que l’élevage intensif peut durer se bercent d’illusions. »

Nourrir ou trahir, comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France paru le 30 septembre 2026 aux éditions Payot, disponible au prix de 19 € sur notre boutique en ligne et en librairie.

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[1] https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cattle-sheep-and-pig-slaughter

[2] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12431619/Animal-Rising-protesters-charged-stealing-Kings-sheep-royal-Sandringham-Estate-driving-away-animals.html

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

[3] https://www.cambsnews.co.uk/peterborough-court-acquittal-animal-rescue-beagles/

[4] https://www.animalrising.org/post/not-guilty-verdict-for-beagle-puppy-rescuers-in-landmark-legal-case

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

Earlier this month, Animal Rising released first-of-its-kind hidden-camera footage following a mother pig through a month of confinement in a farrowing crate on a factory farm. This month, their campaign lead Michelle Farnham spent 24 hours a day inside a real pig farrowing crate in …

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als Huhn in der Fleischindustrie leben zu müssen
content:
Die Hühnermast ist ein grausames System, das auf maximale Schnelligkeit, Wachstum und Profit ausgelegt ist und mit einem gewaltvollen Tod für die Tiere endet.


Wie fühlt es sich an, als „Masthuhn“ geboren zu werden

, ohne die Möglichkeit, der leidvollen Industrie zu entkommen

?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Du sollst so schnell wie möglich so schwer wie möglich werden – und wirst dann getötet.


Du kommst in einem Hühnerschlupfbetrieb mit tausenden anderen Küken zur Welt. Um dich herum piepsen sie verzweifelt. Und auch du suchst nach Nähe und Wärme. Aber da ist keine Mutter, in deren Gefieder du dich kuscheln kannst – und du wirst sie auch niemals kennenlernen.

Noch am ersten Tag deines Lebens wirst du über Förderbänder geschleudert und in eine Kiste gepackt. Dann beginnt die oftmals stundenlange Fahrt zum Mastbetrieb – eingepfercht mit Dutzenden anderen Küken, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Du kommst in einer riesigen Halle an. Hier wirst du die nächsten rund 5 Wochen verbringen – die einzigen Wochen deines Lebens.


Um dich herum Tausende andere Küken. Du teilst dir einen Quadratmeter mit bis zu 23 anderen Tieren. Jetzt seid ihr noch klein, doch das wird sich schnell ändern.


Du wächst. Unnatürlich schnell. Das Futter steht dir Tag und Nacht zur Verfügung – hochkalorisch, proteinreich, entwickelt für maximales Wachstum in kürzester Zeit.


Du hast keinen Platz, um dich natürlich zu bewegen, es gibt nichts zum Erkunden. Keinerlei Möglichkeiten, deine natürlichen Verhaltensweisen auszuleben. Es ist trist und laut. Da ist nur diese Enge.


Die Luft ist stickig. Der Ammoniakgeruch von den Ausscheidungen Tausender Tiere brennt in deinen Augen, in deinen Lungen. Du bekommst Atemwegserkrankungen. Jeder Atemzug tut weh.


Dein Körper wurde durch jahrzehntelange Züchtung so manipuliert, dass du in wenigen Wochen das Gewicht erreichst, für das ein Huhn unter natürlichen Bedingungen Monate bräuchte.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Deine Brustmuskeln wachsen so schnell und werden so schwer, dass deine Knochen dein Gewicht nicht mehr tragen können. Deine Beine verformen sich. Dein Herz ist zu klein für deinen massiven Körper, es hat Probleme, deine Organe mit ausreichend Blut zu versorgen. Du hast Schmerzen beim Gehen und deine Gelenke sind entzündet.


Um dich herum sind Hühner, die gar nicht mehr aufstehen können. Sie liegen in ihrem eigenen Kot und leiden unter extremen Schmerzen. Sie verdursten und verhungern.


Andere Hühner werden aufgrund der Enge von ihren Artgenossen versehentlich totgetrampelt und erdrückt – ihre Körper verwesen zwischen dir und den tausenden anderen Tieren. Auch du hast keine Chance, den anderen Hühnern auszuweichen.


Dann ist es soweit. Menschen kommen und packen dich. An deinen Beinen, kopfüber, werden du und deine Artgenossen gegriffen und in enge Transportkisten geworfen. Deine ohnehin schon schmerzenden Beine brechen unter der groben Behandlung. Du hast Schmerzen und Todesangst.


Zusammengepfercht, ohne Wasser, ohne Futter, geht es zum Schlachthof. Die Fahrt kann Stunden dauern. Manche Hühner sterben bereits im Transporter – vor Stress, vor Erschöpfung, erdrückt von anderen Tieren.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Im Schlachthof riechst du Blut. Du hörst die Schreie anderer Hühner. Dann bist du selbst an der Reihe. Unter grausamen Bedingungen wirst du betäubt und getötet. Du bist gerade einmal 35 bis 42 Tage alt geworden.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Hühner in der Fleischindustrie erleiden müssen.


Die Wahrheit hinter „Hähnchenfleisch“


Wie grausam das kurze Leben von sogenannten Masthühnern ist, haben wir schon mehrfach bei Undercover-Recherchen aufgedeckt, beispielsweise in einem (jetzt ehemaligen) Zuliefererbetrieb der großen Marke Wiesenhof. Hier erfährst du mehr über unsere Aufdeckungen und kannst unsere Petition für strengere Tierschutzvorgaben, -kontrollen und -strafen unterzeichnen:


Jetzt für Hühner unterschreiben 


In Deutschland wird mehr Fleisch von Hühnern konsumiert als produziert – und die Nachfrage ist in den vergangenen Jahren stetig gestiegen. Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht: Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel.


In den meisten Supermärkten findest du mittlerweile eine Vielfalt tierfreundlicher Alternativen, die hervorragende Proteinquellen sind – probiere sie aus. Oder koche unsere zahlreichen pflanzlichen Rezepte von Love Veg nach, wie unsere

knusprigen Tofu-Nuggets

.

author: webadmin
title: Eggesford in the Dock: Huntsman Convicted of Illegal Hunting
content:
Eggesford Hunt huntsman Jason Marles has been convicted of illegally hunting a fox with hounds following an incident captured on drone footage during the hunt’s Boxing Day meet in December 2025.


Jason Marles, huntsman of the Eggesford Hunt.


Marles, 44, pleaded guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs at Pudson Farm, near Okehampton, when he appeared before Exeter Magistrates’ Court on 23 September 2026.


His conviction followed footage recorded by Devon County Hunt Saboteurs which showed a fox being bolted from an area of rubble before being pursued by hounds. Hunt saboteurs positioned on a farm track nearby were in position to stop the hounds from chasing the fox, and they confirmed that the fox managed to evade capture.


The footage shows Marles standing beside the area where the fox had taken refuge, close to a cattle barn. Two men with spades are moving rubble and digging at the site, while a child, who had dismounted from their pony, also watches what is happening.


Huntsman Jason Marles looks on as landowner Lloyd Heard and terrier-man Tom Bounsall dig and remove the rubble protecting the hunted fox. Image credit: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.


Devon County Hunt Sabs identify the two men digging as Eggesford terrier man Tom Bounsall and landowner Lloyd Heard.


WATCH THE VIDEO


After Marles realised a drone was overhead, and they had walked back to the farmyard, Marles and Heard swapped coats in a comical, and ultimately futile attempt to avoid identification.


Huntsman Jason Marles wearing Lloyd Heard’s jacket after the dig out. Tom Bounsall follows behind on a quad. Image: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.


Bounsall is a terrier-man for both the Eggesford Hunt and the Spooners & West Dartmoor Hunt. Pictured here at a Spooners meet in March 2026. Image: Plymouth & West Devon Hunt Sabs.


After several minutes, the fox bolts from its refuge and runs for the surrounding cover. The hounds follow, beginning the chase. No attempt to call the hounds back was made.


Heard was also charged alongside Marles with hunting offences relating to both the Boxing Day incident at Pudson Farm and a second incident near Crediton in February 2026.


As the landowner of Pudson Farm, Heard also faced a further charge under Section 3 of the Hunting Act of knowingly permitting his land to be used for hunting a wild mammal with dogs.


Lloyd Heard, landowner of Pudson Farm, where the fox was dug out and subsequently pursued by hounds. Image: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.


The proceedings against Heard were

subsequently withdrawn by the prosecution

. No reason for that decision has been made public.


Heard also has a close family connection to the leadership of hunting’s governing body. He is the son-in-law of British Hound Sports Association

Executive Director Julian Barnfield

.


Barnfield is himself a former huntsman with previous Hunting Act convictions. Whilst huntsman of the Heythrop Hunt, he pleaded guilty to

four separate counts of unlawfully hunting foxes

 between 2011 and 2012.


Julian Barnfield (right), who turned up to Crewe Magistrates court in 2022 to support another convicted fox hunter – former Quorn Huntsman Ollie Finnegan (left). Image: Cheshire Against Blood Sports (CABS).


Barnfield also has a longstanding connection to former Prime Minister David Cameron. In 2008, when Barnfield was facing an earlier prosecution under the Hunting Act, Cameron – then leader of the Opposition and Barnfield’s constituency MP –

wrote to the Attorney General on his behalf

 following a private meeting between the two. Those proceedings against Barnfield were subsequently discontinued on a technical issue.


The connection is worth noting. The Heythrop was David Cameron’s local hunt, and

he rode with it on numerous occasions

 before the Hunting Act came into force. It is also reported that David Cameron is ‘friendly’ with Barnfield, Heard’s father-in-law.


David Cameron

 pictured with the Heythrop Hunt in 2004. Image: Daily Mail.


Cameron remains a vocal supporter of fox hunting. As recently as September 2026,

he described the incoming ban on so-called ‘trail hunting

’ as “completely wrong”, urging the minority within the rural community who support hunting to “stand together and fight together”.


None of this establishes that political connections played any part in the decision to drop the charges against Heard. But it does illustrate something that has long characterised fox hunting – those who enjoy hunting …

title: Case at Supreme Court Could Have Profound Consequences for Other Climate Suits
content:
With help from the Trump administration, Suncor Energy and ExxonMobil have asked the court to quash the lawsuit.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Attorneys representing two Colorado local governments are set for a high-stakes legal showdown over climate change Monday at the U.S. Supreme Court, where they’ll ask justices to allow Boulder’s lawsuit seeking monetary damages from two fossil fuel companies to proceed in state court.

With help from the Trump administration, the two companies, Suncor Energy and Exxon Mobil, have asked the court to step in and quash the lawsuit, which was filed in 2018 by Boulder County and the city of Boulder. The plaintiffs are seeking monetary damages under state tort law “for the substantial role (the companies) played and continue to play in causing, contributing to and exacerbating climate change.”

Monday’s Supreme Court hearing in the case, known as Suncor v. Boulder, follows another unprecedented summer of record heat, extreme drought conditions and destructive wildfire activity impacting communities across Colorado. Boulder’s suit is one of more than 30 similar cases filed to date by state and local governments nationwide as human-caused climate change, mostly the result of fossil-fuel combustion, pushes average global temperatures to dangerous new highs.

“This case is really about who’s going to bear the costs of all of these accelerating effects that we’re experiencing on the front lines here in Colorado,” Chris Winter, an environmental attorney and executive director of the Getches-Wilkinson Center at the University of Colorado School of Law, said in an interview. “Are those costs just going to fall on the shoulders of all of the taxpayers and citizens and our local governments? Or is the oil industry going to be at least partially responsible for their role in contributing to this crisis?”

Exxon and Suncor, a Canadian oil giant that operates Colorado’s only fossil fuel refinery, argue that federal law preempts Boulder’s efforts to hold the companies accountable in state court. The defendants have tried and failed repeatedly to have the case dismissed or removed to federal court, most recently in May 2025, when the Colorado Supreme Court issued a ruling allowing the case to proceed.

Soon after that ruling, however, the companies asked the U.S. Supreme Court, where conservatives hold a 6-3 majority, to step in. Their petition asks the nation’s highest court to rule that federal statute “precludes state-law claims seeking relief for injuries allegedly caused by the effects of interstate and international greenhouse-gas emissions on the global climate.”

In February, justices agreed to hear the case, which is set to be among the most closely watched proceedings on the court’s docket for the 2026-27 term, and one of its highest-profile climate change decisions ever. A ruling from the court could have profound consequences for the dozens of other lawsuits seeking climate-related damages from fossil fuel companies, as scientists warn that catastrophic impacts from higher temperatures will continue to accelerate.

In an unusual move, President Donald J. Trump’s administration filed an unsolicited brief in support of Suncor and Exxon’s petition shortly after it was filed, urging the court to overturn the Colorado Supreme Court’s decision, which it called “contrary to the Constitution.” Alongside petitioners and respondents, U.S. Solicitor General John Sauer will be given time during Monday’s oral arguments to represent the Trump administration’s position in support of the companies.

“We’ve seen this administration really bend over backwards to serve the interests of the fossil-fuel industry, and this case is just one of many examples,” Winter said. “A lot of us who watch the court and have studied these issues for a long time are quite troubled by some of the legal arguments this administration has used, to try to undercut the ability of the states to protect (their) citizens, and to insulate the oil industry from liability for its actions.”

In another unusual development, Justice Samuel Alito, one of the Supreme Court’s most conservative members, recused himself from further proceedings in the case last week.

Though the court’s announcement did not explain why, environmental advocates had called for Alito’s recusal because he owns stock in at least two oil …

title: Purulia’s Bero-Chandi Pahar Faces Renewed Threat from Granite Mining
content:
Community-led ecological restoration and a centuries-old cultural landscape face destruction as quarrying resumes; villagers allege criminalisation of resistance


 


Purulia, West Bengal:

 The Bero-Chandi hillocks in Purulia’s Raghunathpur subdivision are facing renewed threats from granite and stone mining, with local communities and environmental activists warning that continued quarrying could destroy a landscape shaped by decades of ecological regeneration, traditional worship and local cultural history.


 


An appeal issued by those supporting the local resistance has called on civil society organisations, environmental groups, human rights organisations, student movements and cultural activists across West Bengal to intervene against what it describes as the “aggressive granite stone mining” now threatening Bero-Chandi Pahar. The appeal demands an immediate and unconditional halt to all granite and stone mining activities and the withdrawal of criminal cases against villagers and environmental activists.


 


Ecological Restoration and Wildlife Resurgence


 


According to the appeal, the Bero-Chandi hillocks are far more than geological formations. They represent a vibrant, living landscape in which ecology, community life, traditional practices and literary history are closely intertwined. The area had suffered extensive loss of tree cover for decades. Local residents subsequently undertook sustained community-led afforestation, gradually restoring the green cover and reviving the local ecosystem.


 


The restoration reportedly brought back a range of wildlife, including striped hyenas, wild pigs, Indian pythons, jackals and two species of rabbits, alongside numerous resident and migratory birds. The return of avifauna, the appeal states, also contributed to improved soil enrichment, water retention and the local micro-hydrological cycle.


 


This fragile ecosystem and the peaceful lives of the local communities protecting it face imminent destruction due to resumption of aggressive granite stone mining.


 


Living Cultural Heritage and Historical Roots


 


The Bero-Chandi hills are deeply intertwined with the spiritual and cultural identity of the region. The sacred worship of Devi Chandi at this site dates back at least 300 years, anchoring the traditional spiritual practices of the local populace.


 


The landscape holds profound literary value for Bengal. It served as the central backdrop for Bibhutisbhusan Bandyopadhyay’s classic Bengali masterpiece,

“Rankini Devir Kharag”

 written over 80 years ago.


 


The hills harbour ancient natural cave systems that form an integral part of the local terrain and ecosystem.


 


It is this historical and cultural heritage that villagers say is now at risk from renewed quarrying.


 


Villagers’ Resistance

to Mining and Criminalisation of Dissent


 


Low-intensity granite quarrying in the region began around 2014. Facing the threat of ecological devastation, local villagers mounted a peaceful yet resolute resistance, eventually succeeding in stopping operations by 2018.


 


Commercial mining operations, however, resumed in 2024. The resumption was preceded by the targeting of local leadership and environment activists. At least 14 villagers were implicated in fabricated criminal charges, thrust into police custody, and incarcerated for 14 days before securing bail. The use of state force and intimidation to silence environmental defenders and suppress local resistance to mining is a gross violation of democratic norms and community rights.


 


For the communities resisting the mining, the issue is not simply one of land use or quarrying. They argue that the destruction of the hillocks would also mean the loss of a regenerated forest landscape, wildlife habitat and water catchment areas on which surrounding agriculture and community life depend. They warn that continued industrial-scale granite and stone extraction could permanently damage sacred sites, cultural traditions and geological formations associated with the hills.


 


Urgent Appeal to Civil Society


 


The appeal argues that local communities have shown exemplary courage in safeguarding their environment, but they cannot be expected to confront politicians backed powerful commercial mining interests on their own, particularly amid a reign of intimidation and repression.


 


It calls on democratic organisations, environmental and human rights groups, students, cultural …

author: Igor Ojeda
title: Brazil’s elections and environmental policy: A choice between continuity and dismantling
content:
Never before in the history of this country has the climate crisis been as relevant to a presidential election as it, very likely, will be in the 2026 vote. Once again deeply polarised, this year’s electoral contest between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers’ Party and Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party is taking place against a decisive climatic and geopolitical backdrop.

Less than a year ago, in November 2025, Brazil hosted the United Nations’ annual climate summit, COP, that restored the country’s status as a key player in the global climate debate. This was a particularly important development given that Brazil currently ranks among the top five contributors to greenhouse gas emissions, primarily due to agriculture, cattle ranching and deforestation.

Four years after the last Brazilian presidential election, in which Lula defeated Jair Bolsonaro by a razor-thin margin, the effects of the climate crisis have intensified. As scientists and environmental, social and civil society organisations have been warning for years, the planet is increasingly suffering the severe consequences of this reality, with a rise in the frequency and intensity of extreme natural events, in addition to the increase in average global temperatures. In Brazil, the historic drought in the Amazon in 2023 and the unprecedented floods in Rio Grande do Sul in 2024 were just a few examples.

The arrival of the El Niño weather phenomenon, forecast to last until early 2027 and once again cause severe droughts and above-average rainfall, alongside rising food prices, contributes to the growing importance of the climate debate in the electoral landscape.

In the geopolitical arena, the Brazilian presidential election will serve as yet another stage for the struggle for global hegemony between the United States and China — a contest currently focused largely on the race to control reserves of so-called critical minerals and rare earth elements. Beyond their strategic value for a clean energy transition, these resources are essential inputs for the defence industry.

“The election will reflect this struggle for hegemony,” says geographer Bruno Malheiro, a professor at the Federal University of Pará (UFPA).

“One side, Flávio Bolsonaro’s, will be clearly structured around a policy of alliance and total alignment with the United States over critical minerals and rare earth elements,” Malheiro says. “On the other side, President Lula’s, we see a more open, multifaceted diplomatic policy, yet one clearly tethered to China in terms of economic strategy.”

An analysis of both candidates’ platforms, as well as their speeches, stances and track records, including Lula’s third term and Jair Bolsonaro’s administrations alongside Flávio’s tenure in the Senate, reveals two different paths. While the incumbent president signals a continuation of policies, with equally significant advances and limitations, his rival envisions a return to his father’s administration, grounded in the dismantling of environmental policies and a disregard for the climate agenda.

Political scientist Maureen Santos is a climate justice activist and international relations professor. In terms of the Paris Agreement negotiations, she believes that the fight against deforestation and illegal mining, and other issues, President Lula’s platform for the 2026 elections “doesn’t change much” compared to the proposals from the previous election or his current administration’s policies.

“However, it seems to me there is an attempt to forge a stronger connection with other areas of the government,” she notes.

To her, however, the platform does introduce some new elements. In particular, Lula places greater emphasis on policies concerning critical minerals and rare earth elements. Yet, Santos criticises the lack of measures ensuring greater state control over the exploitation of these resources.

“Rhetoric about sovereignty obviously matters, but how can Brazil exercise sovereignty, for instance, given the new environmental licensing law, which relaxes licensing requirements, or the absence of a state-owned company for this sector?” she warns. “It is very difficult to envision sovereignty if the country continues to merely sell commodities.”

According to Santos, although Lula’s platform mentions technology transfer, processing and value addition, there are doubts about whether this will actually materialise, given the negotiations the government has been conducting on this …

33. Adana Altın Koza Uluslararası Film Festivali'nde

ödül alanlar

kapanışta bir arada 


Ergüçlü: “Biz adaletsizlikle mi yaşayacağız?”


Ödül töreninde gecenin en güçlü konuşmalarından biri En İyi Kadın Oyuncu ödülünü alan Hazar Ergüçlü’den geldi.


Ergüçlü, “kendin olmanın böylesine tehlikeli olduğu, hatta yasaklanmaya çalışıldığı” bir dönemden geçildiğini söyledi; ardından sözü Soma’daki son maden kazasında yaşamını yitiren 37 yaşındaki Kerim Ören’in oğlu Yaşar’a getirdi.


Ergüçlü büyükannesi ve büyükbabasının madenci olduğunu aktardı ve şöyle dedi:


Benim nenem, dedem kömür işçisiydi. Dedem bakır madeninde çalıştı. Her madenci gördüğümde gözümün önüne kendi dedem, kendi nenem geliyor. İnsanca yaşayabilmek için, çocuklarını okutabilmek için verdikleri emek geliyor.


Madenci çocuklarını ağlarken gördüğümde ben yaşamaktan, aldığım nefesten utanıyorum. Bunu vicdanımı rahatlatmak veya bir şeyin sözcüsü olmak niyetiyle de yapmıyorum şu an. Sadece bu adaletsizlikler bana fazla geliyor ve ne yaparsam yapayım bu üzüntüyü içimden atamıyorum


Ergüçlü, konuşmasını umudu bırakmama çağrısıyla bitirdi: “Elimizde bir tek umudumuz kaldı. Onu da vermeyeceğiz.” 


“İçeride ve dışarıda olan dostlarımızla”


“Bir Arada Yalnız” ile Umut Veren Genç Erkek Oyuncu Ödülü’nü alan Onur Gözeten ise konuşmasını cezaevindekilere uzattı:


“İçeride ve dışarıda olan dostlarımızla film yapmaya devam ederiz.”


Ödül konuşmalarında tutuklu sinemacı Çiğdem Mater’in yanı sıra Selçuk Kozağaçlı, Can Atalay ve Berkin Elvan’ın adları da anıldı.

title: Göksu: Lasting peace requires stronger democratisation
content:
Musician Yasemin Göksu told ANF that lasting peace could only be achieved through democratisation and said, “Replacing violence with dialogue and weapons with politics offers an invaluable opportunity for society.”


Göksu said music was one of the most powerful carriers of memory and that an environment of lasting peace would also contribute to the freedom of the arts. She also said: “Once lasting peace is established, artists will be able to create more freely and people will have greater access to one another’s cultures.”


How can artists contribute to building peace and making it part of society during this period? What role can music play in ensuring that peace resonates not only at the negotiating table but also in everyday life, in people’s minds and consciences?


I do not see peace as an issue that should be discussed only at the negotiating table by political actors. The real test of peace, and of the parties involved, takes place in everyday life. How we see one another, how much we listen to and truly hear each other’s stories, and how well we manage to live alongside one another with our differences are all vitally important.


Art, and music in particular, undoubtedly has a very special power in this respect. Music has the ability to bridge in an instant distances that cannot be overcome through words alone. I have been singing songs in different languages for years. Every language contains a different story, a different pain and a different joy.


I see something very clearly on stage: even when people do not understand one another’s languages, they can still understand the emotion of a melody, and this can change the way they see one another. The real challenge is to resist obsessive and toxic political arguments and internalise the beauty of hearing a sentence or a word expressed in every language, rather than insisting on hearing only one.


For me, this is precisely where art can contribute to peace: not by making us all the same, but by allowing us to hear one another through our differences and come together through shared emotions.


We should now be able to speak freely about living in a more democratic society in which all citizens of Turkey can feel equal, free and safe, and where differences are not regarded as a threat. For me, that too is part of what peace means.


It is also said that the path to peace requires confronting past suffering and the truth. How does music serve as a space of memory in this process of reckoning?


Music is one of the most powerful carriers of memory anywhere in the world. You can read about certain events in books or see them documented in records, but music can make you feel the full emotion of what happened deep within you. It can also heighten the impact of an image even without being its central element.


The music of our region also carries an immense memory: migration, separation, loss, love, poverty, war, longing and massacres. All of these continue to live through music as life goes on.


Memory, of course, is not simply about remembering pain. I believe confronting the past begins with acknowledging the existence of different forms of suffering without setting them against one another.


Our role here is not to pass judgement like historians or politicians. What you can do politically is help people hear, understand and feel one another’s past and present. When you sing a folk song, you may touch the pain or happiness of someone you have never met. I believe genuine reckoning begins with being able to look impartially at the mistakes and wrongdoings of individuals or states, without taking ownership of them, and say, “Your pain is as real as mine.”


Conflict and violence place the heaviest burden on women. Militarism and male domination seem to reinforce one another. What can a women’s perspective contribute to peace and to the language of peace?


Women’s experience of war and conflict is often not limited to what happens on the battlefield. It has profound consequences at home, within families, in children’s lives, and through displacement, poverty and loss.


But I do not want to reduce women’s contribution to peace to a statement such as “women are more peaceful”. There are, after all, many women around the world who willingly serve patriarchal structures and see themselves as actors within that system.


I believe women’s different experiences and the lessons they draw from everyday life need to play a greater role in shaping the factors that …

author: Charlize Tomaselli
title: Not Energy, But Power: why Geothermal Energy Benefits Everyone in Iceland but not Kenya
content:
This article draws on in-person interviews at Mt Suswa, Olkaria, and Menengai with


Coalition for Human Rights in Development

 (CHRD) members and partners directly affected by geothermal projects. Interviews were led by the Coalition’s Research and Learning Facilitator and interviewees identified through the


Community Resource Exchange

 (CRE),

a system to facilitate collaborations and co-develop strategies with and among communities defending their rights in the context of international investments and development projects. The analysis also incorporates a review of Kenyan and Icelandic energy policy documents and insights from the Coalition’s roles in the


AfDB Civil Society Working Group

 and its Energy Sub-Group.


 

In Iceland, geothermal energy – one of the cleanest solutions to the climate crisis – is widely hailed as a success story. It supplies

65 % of the country’s electricity

 and heats

nearly 90%

 of its households. Everyone benefits from it.


Thousands of kilometres away, in Kenya, steam rising from the Rift Valley drives one of Africa’s

largest geothermal programmes

, supplying

nearly half of the country’s electricity

. According to recent data, Kenya is the world’s

sixth-largest geothermal producer

. Yet, its projects are entangled in disputes over land, livelihoods and rights, with local communities left grappling with acid rain, noise pollution and toxic soil.


Steam pipe in Hell’s Gate natural park, Kenya. 2017. Photo credit: Wikimedia Commons.


So how can geothermal energy be celebrated as a success story in one country, and a source of conflict, contestation and environmental harm in another? The difference lies not in the energy resource itself, but in how this resource is governed, financed, and embedded within different social and political contexts. It’s not about energy, it’s about power.


Different technologies, different risks


Different technologies used in geothermal systems, particularly with regard to the management of by-products such as brine and emissions, can lead to different levels of environmental risk.


In Iceland, geothermal operations are characterised by high rates of reinjection to reduce water use, minimal use of open brine storage, and increasing efforts to capture and reinject emissions such as hydrogen sulphide. Environmental challenges are largely approached as technical problems, with the resources and institutional capacity to address them and minimize harm.


In Kenya, while water reinjection does take place, it is not always consistent or effective. In some cases, particularly during drilling or testing phases, geothermal fluids are stored in open, unattended ponds. Infrastructure limitations, cost constraints, and poor monitoring lead to air, water and noise pollution, which has a harmful impact on the health and livelihoods of affected communities.


Communities living near the Menengai Geothermal Power Project in Nakuru County, for example, complain of loud noises disrupting sleep and school activities, hydrogen sulphide emissions, dust, and water pollution. Respiratory problems, particularly among children and older people, are common. Community members are also concerned that geothermal emissions and open brine ponds could be linked to acid rains in the area, which are corroding their house roofs, water tanks and farm equipment.


A different geography, a different history


In Iceland, geothermal resources are largely located in sparsely populated volcanic zones. Land tenure is relatively stable, and there is little legacy of large-scale dispossession shaping current development.


On the contrary, the Rift Valley is a

highly populated lived space

, where pastoralist communities have deep historical and cultural ties to their land. Here, geothermal projects sit atop layered histories of

colonial and postcolonial land alienation

 and violent evictions. Maasai communities still lack deeds to their land and are treated as guests of the government without their own rights. In this context, the expansion of geothermal projects has led to further resettlement, restricted access to grazing areas, loss of livelihoods, and ongoing disputes over compensation and participation.


In 2014, for example, a group of Indigenous Maasai pastoralist communities submitted a complaint to the accountability mechanisms of the

World Bank

 and

European Investment Bank

 for their investment in the Olkaria IV geothermal project, which caused the …

author: Curtis Johnson
title: Trump’s Repeal of Roadless Rule Would Declare Open Season on Protected Forests
content:
A public policy expert described the move as “the largest evisceration of public lands protection in American history.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

On August 18, Donald Trump’s United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) officially proposed eliminating the national Roadless Rule. If finalized, the repeal would strip protections from 44.7 million acres of wild intact forest.

The rule, passed in 2001, protects in total 58 million acres of forest from road building, logging, fossil fuel extraction, and other development. Forests in Idaho and Colorado, which have their own state roadless laws, would be exempt, at least for now.

The USDA, which oversees the U.S. Forest Service, initially gave the public only 30 days to comment on the plan. They were forced after public pressure to allow 15 additional days, until October 6. Opponents are aiming to mobilize 1 million public comments during this short period, as well as sponsoring public events speaking out against the repeal.

One hundred and eighty environmental, conservation, and citizen’s groups have been joined by tribes, sportsmen, wildland firefighters, and businesses dedicated to tourism, in submitting a joint public comment or otherwise speaking out against this decision. A letter in support of the Roadless Rule and opposing recission has been signed by 164 congressional representatives.

The recission is “the largest evisceration of public lands protection in American history,” according to Randi Spivak, public lands policy director at the Center for Biological Diversity. Spivak told Truthout the Roadless Rule shelters “hundreds of threatened and endangered species. It provides incredible recreation opportunities — hunting, fishing, hiking. These were really the last of the forests outside of wilderness that had not been opened up to industrial development.”

The roadless-area forests contain immense old-growth trees, pristine rivers that are filled in the summer and fall with some of the last healthy salmon runs in the country, and trail through some of the U.S.’s grandest scenic beauty. These forests help protect some of the country’s remaining wild species — grizzly bears, wolverines, and endangered lynx. They host key migration corridors for antelope, elk, and mule deer. They protect headwaters of streams providing clean drinking water to 24 million people in the country.

The current protections include 9.3 million acres of the Tongass rainforest in Alaska. The Tongass contains incredible landscapes — rugged ocean coastlines, glacial fjords, snow-capped peaks, wild rivers, and old-growth forest. Concentrated in the Tongass are Earth’s largest remaining intact stands of coastal temperate rainforest, making it a vital carbon sink for curbing climate change. Its trees capture approximately 44 percent of all the carbon stored by U.S. national forests, absorbing 1.5 times more carbon than the U.S. emits annually.

Opening the Tongass and all roadless forests to destruction would be a crime against nature. And further opening the Tongass to development would be yet another crime against Native peoples. The Tongass is the ancestral homeland of the Tlingit and Haida Indigenous peoples. A joint statement from the tribes condemns the decision to rescind the rule, saying it was taken “without any prior consultation with our Tribe or other Southeast Alaska tribes. As a sovereign tribal nation, we do not recognize the validity of federal actions impacting our traditional homelands when undertaken without meaningful government-to-government consultation, as required by law and respect for our inherent sovereignty.”

The statement continues, “The Tongass is more than an ecosystem — it is our home. It is the foundation of our identify, our culture, and our way of life.”

The USDA proposal claims to “reduce regulatory burden and return decisionmaking for the management of inventoried roadless area to the land management planning process at the individual national forest level…. Recission of the national-level prohibitions provides responsible officials with flexibility to better guide management of the National Forest System lands and respond to changing local resource conditions.”

Describing these relatively untouched forests — rich with species, habitat, and natural wonders — as “resources” is a dead giveaway to the proposal’s actual intent.

Despite claims to “return decisionmaking” to local …

Seit etwa vier Jahren importiert Deutschland Flüssigerdgas über schwimmende LNG-Terminals. LNG steht für „Liquefied Natural Gas“ (Flüssigerdgas) und gelangt derzeit hauptsächlich aus den USA, wo es durch Fracking gewonnen wird, über Norddeutschland in deutsche Haushalte. Mit Beginn des Krieges zwischen Russland und der Ukraine hatte die Bundesrepublik begonnen, Alternativen für russische Gaslieferungen zu suchen. Nun zeichnet sich eine ähnliche Tendenz durch Spannungen zwischen den USA und Europa ab. Die deutsche Bundesregierung muss jetzt entscheiden, ob sie für den dafür notwendigen Ausbau der Infrastruktur im Golfo San Matías in Patagonien eine ungebundene Finanzkredit-Garantie (UFG) erteilen will, wie die deutsche NGO urgewald berichtet. Palabras del Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés en la reunión del 3 de octubre del 2026 a las 1100 hrs.

Llevamos muchos años esperando el momento de encontrarnos con ellas.

Entonces, la prioridad o lo más importante en nuestra agenda o programación son las reuniones, encuentros y actividades con las Buscadoras, el día y la hora que ellas establezcan.

Cualquiera otra propuesta de actividad o reunión, deberá ser cuando no haya encuentro o actividad con buscadoras.
