content:
Alors que la jeunesse française embrase le pays, nous avons interviewé Christian Ingrao pour son nouveau livre

Le Temps des promesses

. La situation présente est le produit d'une lente glaciation de l'espérance qui avait été annoncée non par des prophètes, mais par des historiens, des économistes, des ingénieurs agronomes, et toutes ces littératures grises qui enregistrent, en même temps qu'elles font, l'espérance et ses vacillements. Nous vivons les derniers moments d'une série de promesses nées aux lendemains de la mutation anthropologique des guerres mondiales, et dont la force d'élan et d'entraînement s'est tarie au tournant des années 1980. En réactivant une méthode matérialiste inspirée de Engels et Marx, Ingrao parvient à reconstruire la « sociogenèse de l'espérance », depuis une multitude d'observatoires, dont le temps présent nous dit la fin.

author: Paul Messersmith-Glavin
title: A Lifelong Organizer Shares Lessons on Sustaining Activism for the Long Haul
content:
Organizer Chris Dixon discusses how we can sustain our collective efforts over years of social and political struggle.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Writer and organizer Chris Dixon has his fingers on the pulse of North American grassroots movement. Dixon has extensively and repeatedly traveled throughout North America, talking with people working for social change — engaging with activists concerning their successes and heartbreaks, their frustrations and dreams. His first book, Another Politics: Talking Across Today’s Transformative Movements, published in 2014, focused on antiauthoritarian organizers and politics across a range of movements of the 2000s and early 2010s, including migrant justice, prison abolitionism, and Occupy Wall Street. His new book, For the Long Haul: How to Stay in the Fight for a Better World, focuses on how we can sustain our collective efforts over years of social and political struggle.

Movement elders I am close to — now in their 70s — who maintain radical political commitments developed in their youth, benefitted from both the intense community that formed around movements for Black Power and liberation, the youthful counterculture and the New Left, and anti-war movements, as well as from their own inner convictions that served as an animating passion. For these elders, political engagement is a kind of vocation. Though they continue to maintain relationships with those comrades who are also still alive and committed to political struggle, those vibrant communities they once thrived in are gone. Only their specific commitment to the possibility of freedom and liberation keeps them going.

Coming of age politically in the 1990s, we also had strong bonds of friendship born through relentless organizing meetings, demonstrations, and coalition work. It seemed we could collectively change the world. Thirty years later, only a handful of us remain involved. Why? Why do people stop organizing, beyond and in addition to the realities of acquiring increasing responsibilities as we age? Why do people give up on the possibility of creating fundamental social and structural change together over the long term? How can we cultivate and sustain caring radical communities that support us all, while drawing new people in, or welcoming them back? These are some of the questions Chris Dixon sets out to answer in For the Long Haul: How to Stay in the Fight for a Better World. The interview that follows has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Paul Messersmith-Glavin: Who should read your book?

Chris Dixon: I wrote For the Long Haul as a practical guide with two main audiences in mind. On the one hand, I wanted to warmly welcome people who have recently become involved in radical political efforts, especially those who have joined movement upsurges since 2020. I’m particularly thinking of the Movement for Black Lives and Palestine solidarity organizing, but also renewed labor militancy and collective defense of queer and trans people. A lot of people I talk to who are newer to movements — many but not all of them younger people — are hungry for conversations about how to sustain lifelong political commitments.

On the other hand, I wanted to speak lovingly to my peers — long-time activists and organizers who have been involved in movements for decades. Many of us talk informally with our friends about the challenges we face in staying actively involved on the left. We’re working a lot to pay our bills, reckoning with disabilities and chronic health conditions, and holding significant care responsibilities for kids, elders, and others in our lives. So many of us are deeply exhausted and hungry for realistic advice about how to stay steady in the fight.

I also wanted to sympathetically address people who participated in movements of the left at one time or another and then moved away from active involvement. I know many people who have followed this trajectory. Rather than being moralistic or dismissive, I wanted to remind them that they’re always welcome back. And I wanted to suggest that perhaps, together, we can build some better structures and practices for helping people stay engaged.

You have spent a tremendous amount of time travelling around the U.S. and Canada, listening to on-the-ground organizers. What have you learned?

title: 'Aile Sağlığı Merkezleri, satılacak bina değil, sağlık merkezidir'
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

Türkiye’de koruyucu, birinci basamak sağlık hizmetlerinin yurttaşla buluştuğu en önemli noktalardan biri olan Aile Sağlığı Merkezlerinin (ASM) geleceği, merkezlerin fiziki koşullarından kira giderlerine, deprem güvenliğinden personel eksikliğine kadar risk altında. Kamuya ait binalarda bile kiralarına yüzde 300’e varan zamlar istenen ASM’lerde aile hekimleri zor durumda.

Birlik ve Dayanışma Sendikası Genel Başkanı Dr. Ahmet Mehlepçi, ASM’lerin mümkün olduğunca kamuya ait, depreme dayanıklı ve sağlık hizmetinin gerektirdiği fiziki standartlara uygun binalarda hizmet vermesi gerektiğine vurgu yaparak “ASM’ler yalnızca hekim, ebe ve hemşirelerin görev yaptığı binalar değildi. ASM’ler; koruyucu sağlık hizmetlerinin, gebe, bebek ve çocuk izlemlerinin, bağışıklama hizmetlerinin, kronik hastalık takiplerinin ve vatandaşın sağlık sistemiyle ilk temasının gerçekleştiği temel sağlık kuruluşlarıdır” hatırlatmasını yaptı. Bu nedenle ASM’lerin geleceğine ilişkin kararların yalnızca bina, taşınmaz veya bütçe konusu olarak değerlendirilemeyeceğini dile getiren Mehlepçi, “Konu doğrudan sağlık hizmetine erişim, hizmetin sürekliliği ve kamu yararıdır” diye konuştu.

Sağlık Bakanı Kemal Memişoğlu’nun Kasım 2025’te 1000 yeni ASM yapacaklarını açıklamasından bu yana sadece 278 ASM’nin hizmete girdiğini, 370 ASM’nin inşaatının sürdüğünü ve 352 ASM’nin proje aşamasında olduğu bilgisini veren Mehlepçi, Türkiye genelinde ise yaklaşık 8 bin 300 ASM bulunduğunu söyledi.

Yeni ASM yatırımlarının elbette önemli olduğunu belirten Mehlepçi, mevcut merkezlerin ise kentsel dönüşüm, deprem riski, yüksek kiralar veya taşınmaz satışları nedeniyle hizmet dışı kalmasının önlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

Bir taraftan yeni ASM’ler yapılırken diğer taraftan mevcut merkezlerin kentsel dönüşüm, deprem riski, yüksek kiralar veya taşınmaz satışları nedeniyle hizmet dışı kalma tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya olduğuna dikkati çeken Mehlpeçi “Mart 2026’da TBMM’ye sunulan soru önergesine verilen cevapta İstanbul Kadıköy’deki 33 ASM’den 7’sinin kentsel dönüşüm nedeniyle yıkıldığı ve hizmet veremez hale geldiğini söyledi. Mahlepçi kaç yeni ASM açıldığı kadar, kaç ASM’nin kapandığı, yıkıldığı, tahliye edildiği, taşındığı veya başka bir ASM’nin içine sıkıştırıldığının da kamuoyuyla paylaşılması gerektiğini aktardı.

ASM binalarının deprem güvenliğinin de önemli bir sorun olduğunu belirten Mehlepçi, 2025 yılında yapılan bir çalışmada ASM binalarının yaklaşık üçte birinin 1999 öncesinde inşa edildiğinin ortaya çıktığını söyledi. 6 Şubat 2023 yaşanan depremlerde ortaya çıkan tablonun bu konuda vahim olduğunu hatırlatan Mehlepçi “2026 yılı başında sahadan elde edilen verilere göre Hatay’da 96 ASM konteynerlerde hizmet veriyor. 103 ASM kendi binasında hizmet vermeye devam ediyor ancak bunların bir bölümü deprem güvenliği açısından risk taşıyor. Yaklaşık 56 ASM ise tahliye veya yıkım sürecinde” dedi.

Öte yandan ASM’ler için sorunun yalnızca deprem güvenliğiyle sınırlı olmadığını, ASM’lerdeki sağlık hizmetinin niteliği ve çalışanların koşullarını etkileyen başka fiziki sorunların bulunduğunu da dile getiren Mehlepçi durumu şöyle anlattı: “Penceresi, yeterli mekanik havalandırması bulunmayan kan alma odaları, lavabosu olmayan, iki veya üç sağlık çalışanının aynı odayı kullanmak zorunda kaldığı ASM’ler de var. Hatta bazı çalışma alanları hasta mahremiyetini sağlamaya da elverişli değil.”

Yıkım veya tahliye kararı verilen merkezlerde görev yapan sağlık çalışanlarının başka bir ASM’nin mutfağına, dinlenme odasına veya ortak kullanım alanına yerleştirilerek yeni bir aile hekimliği birimi oluşturulmasının kalıcı bir çözüm olmadığının altını çizen Mehlepçi, “Bir sağlık hizmetinin verilebilmesi için yalnızca bir oda bulunması yeterli değildir. O alanın sağlık hizmetinin niteliğine, çalışan güvenliğine ve hasta mahremiyetine uygun olması gerekir” dedi.

Kamusal sağlık hizmeti sunulan ASM’lerde yükün önemli bir bölümünün aile hekimlerinin üzerine yıkıldığına ve özellikle büyükşehirlerde uygun bina bulmanın giderek zorlaştığına işaret eden Mehlepçi “Kiralar da ASM’lerin sürdürülebilirliğini tehdit eden seviyelere ulaştı. Aylık 100 bin TL ve üzerinde kira ödeyen ASM örnekleri var. Elazığ’da bazı ASM’ler yüzde 350’ye varan kira artış talepleriyle karşılaştı. ASM’ler birer ticarethane değildir. Burada yürütülen faaliyet kamu sağlık hizmetidir” uyarısını yaparak buna rağmen yüksek kira bedellerinin yanı sıra elektrik, su, doğalgaz, temizlik, bakım-onarım …

author: Ndivhuwo Mukwevho
title: Limpopo district hospital ‘filthy’, ‘broken’ and leaderless
content:
Filthy conditions, a shortage of warm water, a broken emergency communications system, and unresolved complaints from nurses are some of the adversities being faced by both patients and healthcare workers at Nkhensani hospital in Giyani, Limpopo.


The root cause


According to healthcare workers stationed at the hospital, the woes at the public facility are fuelled by a lack of leadership. For the past eight years, the hospital has not had a permanent CEO. Five individuals have, in ten years, acted as CEOs on a temporary basis but were never permanently appointed.


The Limpopo department of health has blamed a lack of suitable candidates as the main reason for not appointing a permanent CEO. The CEO position has been vacant since 2016 following the removal of Themba Mhlanga.


“We are leaderless at this hospital and everyone does what they want; hence everything is a mess at Nkhensani. I can confidently tell that at night, patients at this hospital bath using cold water as warm water gets finished in the early hours of the morning; and the kitchen does not operate during the night and those who want tea or coffee are always left wanting,” said a staff nurse stationed at Nkhensani hospital.


Lives of patients at risk


The nurse further said that the hospital is filthy and rarely cleaned: “This hospital is never cleaned, we often go for days without it being cleaned and no one cares and cleaners are also never reprimanded as there is no one to reprimand them and they do as they like. This puts the lives of patients and healthcare workers at risk.”


The emergency communications system has not been working for months at the hospital and nurses are forced to use their personal cell phones during emergencies. “Alerting doctors of emergencies at this hospital has become extra difficult as we have to use our own personal cell phones because the hospital does not have a working emergency dial; it has not been working for months. What if I do not have airtime and a patient is in need of a doctor urgently? It might lead to an avoidable death of a patient,” she said.


The nurse also told

Elitsha

 that she has personally raised most of these issues with previous acting CEOs but nothing has ever been done to address her concerns. “Even if you complain to those superior to you, nothing is ever done to address your concerns. No one is prepared to take responsibility and all this has got to do with the lack of leadership at Nkhensani hospital,” she said.


Derrick Mashaba, a local community member in Giyani residing about 2 kilometres away from Nkhensani, told

Elitsha

 that he has witnessed the tumble of the hospital over the past decade. “We have witnessed the fall of our precious hospital over the past ten years. We have seen overcrowding, dilapidating buildings, shortage of water and lack of leadership, and all this has contributed to the fall of the mighty hospital,” said Mashaba.


It hurts him to see the fall of the hospital which is so close to his home. “This is a district hospital and it is supposed to be the best in our region but it is not being prioritised. A hospital as big as this one cannot operate without a permanent CEO; it is wrong and it is something which is supposed to be addressed immediately,” he said.


Limpopo health spokesperson, Neil Shikwambana said that the department is working towards appointing a permanent CEO. “The recruitment process is underway and an acting CEO has been appointed to ensure continuity during this process,” he said.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Mental Health Reminders
content:
These are dark times. It is, in fact, the world that is crazy – despair and anxiety are natural responses to watching society destroy itself for the wealthy and powerful. But by reaching out to each other, we can find the courage to stay engaged with the world, to survive, and to fight back. Mental health and mental health crises vary a lot between people, and are often intertwined with class, race, gender, and activism. These suggestions are generic, but may be useful for yourself or others. If you find yourself or someone you love having delusional thinking or consider self-harm or other violence, these suggestions probably aren’t enough. Remember that it is okay to reach out for professional help!

• Our brains are connected to our bodies, so physical health can help with mental distress. Eating healthy food on a regular schedule and getting enough sleep are necessary for mental stability and sustained activism. Exercise, dance, and physical movement help, too. So can fresh air and having a stable, calming place to stay. Try to recognize if you’re missing one of these, and if that’s causing distress.

• An important component of mental health is the ability to know ourselves, understand our needs, and be able to talk about them to the other people in our lives. This can be really challenging and can often take guidance from others who have learned how to do it with one another.

• It can help to have language for mental crisis that feels comfortable and makes more sense than the dominant medical language. Transmission of language often happens in groups. Talk to friends about the different ways you can feel “off” and develop your own shorthand to describe them.

• Joining a mutual support group of peers listening to and helping peers as equals can be validating, while not necessarily endorsing your feelings. You can form one yourself or join an ongoing group.

• If possible, find a therapist or counselor who supports your self-determination. Ask about confidentiality if someone else — such as your parents, boss, or governmental program — is paying.

• Drugs and alcohol usually make mental health problems worse.

• Psychiatric drugs such as those for depression or bipolar disorder can help some people reduce distress and maintain stability, while other people with similar symptoms may experience distress or harm from the same drugs. Figuring out what works for you can be a process because people differ.

• Nature and wilderness can be our greatest healers. Spend some time outside the city to get centered. Get away from pollution, which is in itself mind-altering. Look up “Ecopsychology” to learn more.

• Allow social, political, and environmental crises unfolding around you to radicalize you, rather than driving you to despair. Actually articulate the world you would want to be living in; work towards it. Remember change happens collectively – look for ways to plug in. Small acts like talking to neighbors or submitting art to Slingshot can help you feel political agency between larger or more radical actions.

• Many communities have 24 hour a day crisis hotlines or crisis centers. Call 800-SUICIDE if you’re thinking about killing yourself or 800 646-HOPE to reach a rape crisis line for survivors of sexual violence. Warning: if you call and say you want to kill yourself police may arrive at your door.

• Things that can help your mental health day-to-day might not be as effective when you’re in crisis. Review the above reminders, and try to eat, exercise, journal, etc., but it’s okay if that isn’t helping.

• Distracting yourself from depressed or anxious thoughts can help: listening to music, making art, washing dishes, doing a project alone or with others. Embrace sensation: use your hands or massage your fingers. Hold onto an ice cube, or take a hot or cold shower. Give yourself time to gather resources.

• Some current emotional crises may be caused by traumas from the past, which may need to be emotionally and consciously processed in order not to keep recurring; that processing might take time.

• When in crisis, it may help to realize that the feeling will eventually pass and your life will begin to feel manageable and meaningful again later. Depression may feel like lack of feelings and a lack of connection to feeling. Anxiety may feel like rapidly cycling concern for what might happen. Both inhibit your ability to perceive and understand the world correctly. Your perceptions of hopelessness are NOT …

We join women, girls, and human rights defenders across Africa and the globe on this 28th day of September to commemorate the 2026 International Safe Abortion Day, reaffirming a simple truth: safe abortion is essential healthcare.

We are reminded of the transformative power of the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), which is lauded as one of the most progressive and comprehensive legal instruments for the promotion and protection of women’s rights globally, particularly in the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). Adopted in 2003 by the African Union, the Protocol goes beyond existing international human rights standards by explicitly articulating a wide array of SRHR protections that are often left ambiguous or unstated in other international and regional human rights instruments.

Article 14 of the Maputo Protocol guarantees women’s rights to health and reproductive autonomy, including the right to control their fertility, decide on family size and spacing, and to choose their method of contraception. Most critically, Article 14 makes the Maputo Protocol the first and only binding international human rights treaty to explicitly guarantee access to safe medical abortion in specific circumstances—namely, where the continued pregnancy endangers the mental or physical health of the mother or the life of the mother or the fetus, or in cases of sexual assault, rape, or incest. This Article also mandates access to comprehensive reproductive health services, including antenatal care, safe delivery, family planning, and sexual and reproductive health education. In doing so, the Protocol moves abortion access from a matter left to state discretion to one of binding treaty obligation — a distinction that remains central to the advocacy for its full domestication across the continent.

Currently, 46 of the 55 African states have ratified the Maputo Protocol, while nine – Burundi, Chad, Egypt, Eritrea, Madagascar, Morocco, Niger, Somalia, and Sudan – are yet to ratify it. Bringing these final states on board is vital because over 150 million African women and girls currently live outside the protective legal framework of the Maputo Protocol.

Despite its progressiveness, 9 out of the 46 member states have placed reservations to various provisions of the Maputo Protocol, with Article 14 being the most reserved provision. A reservation lowers the minimum human rights standards contained in a particular treaty for the reserving states and enables the reserving states to escape accountability for human rights violations.

Currently, Africa accounts for 70% of global maternal deaths. These preventable deaths are compounded by persistent gaps in access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, which are essential to safeguarding the lives and dignity of women, children and adolescents. Unsafe abortions continue to claim the lives of thousands of African women and girls, while millions more are left with severe injuries and long-term health complications. According to the World Health Organization, nearly half of all abortions worldwide are unsafe, with Sub-Saharan Africa carrying the highest burden. author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Quebec Liberal Sandrine Rioux prioritizes health care, housing, cost of living
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux had to share with us.


Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux said the reason she decided to run for office is simple: she wants to help people.


“My main goal is to help people, to be there, to be present, and to write good legislation at the National Assembly of Quebec,” said Rioux, speaking to Nunatsiaq News Tuesday from Chibougimou, where she was born and raised.


She’s among five candidates running in Ungava, the largest riding in the province geographically.


Her main priorities are improving access to health care, constructing more homes, addressing the cost of living and ensuring profits generated from resource development benefit communities.


Her party has a goal of building 100,000 homes per year in Quebec, she said, and wants to implement deadlines for housing authorities to encourage quicker development.


Each community, no matter how remote, should have a baseline 24-7 access to front-line health care services like doctors, nurses and pharmacists, she said. Telemedicine can fill gaps when specialists aren’t available.


At least five per cent of Quebec’s health budget should be dedicated to prevention, she said, and if elected, she wants to reduce Nunavik’s reliance on fly-in-fly-out health-care professionals.


Rioux has been involved with the Liberal party since 2019 and was president of its Ungava association.


She has a degree in business technology management from Université de Sherbrooke and a professional background in business analysis and marketing.


But she always held an interest in politics, she said, working for Élections Québec during the 2018 provincial election as an administrative assistant. It was one of her first jobs out of university and one that allowed her to visit each of Nunavik’s villages.


So far during the campaign, Rioux has visited Chapais, Chisasibi, Oujé-Bougoumou, Matagami, Mistissini, Radison, Waskaganish and Waswanipi. Travelling to Nunavik isn’t in the budget, but she said Kuujjuaq is first on her list if she gets elected.


“I really genuinely hope, if the people trust me, and invest in me, to be able to represent them at the National Assembly,” she said. “I want to make sure the lines of communication are always open.”

title: Pourquoi et comment brûler la psychiatrie ? Discussion pour des perspectives antipsy anticarcérales
content:
Le mercredi 23 septembre 2026, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs organise une discussion antipsychiatrie anticarcérale à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

, qui se trouve à la Parole Errante à Montreuil.


Mercredi 23 Septembre à 18h : Discussion antipsy anticarcérale à la

BARK

 

!


Depuis son lancement, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs s'efforce de s'organiser contre l'enfermement psychiatrique. La psychiatrie nous apparaît naturellement comme un maillon important de la domination : que ce soit par les moyens par lesquels elle enferme des personnes, par son utilisation répressive et pacificatrice dans les autres lieux d'enfermement, ou par ses dispositifs carcéraux de contrôle dans la société. Dans une optique de s'informer sur les luttes contre la psychiatrie et d'y intervenir, on veut prendre en compte le fait que nous n'avons pas toustes les mêmes expériences et connaissances sur le sujet.


L'idée de cette discussion est donc de poser des bases, ensemble, sur ce qu'est l'antipsy pour nous, que ce soit pour découvrir ses courants ou pour développer ce qui nous parle dedans. Quels sont les dispositifs d'enfermement de la psychiatrie

 

? Pourquoi viser à sa destruction

 

? Quels liens faisons-nous depuis nos perspectives anticarcérales

 

? Comment la domination psychiatrique est elle étendue ces dernières années

 

? Comment s'organiser pour la brûler

 

?


Une base d'infokiosque sera aussi proposée pour approfondir certaines questions spécifiques, mais il ne faut pas hésiter à apporter toute brochure que l'on voudrait discuter, conseiller, diffuser, etc.


La discussion commencera dès 18h à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

 (5 rue francois debergue à la Parole Errante à Montreuil, en passant par le jardin à gauche de la librairie Michèle Firk). La permanence de la bibliothèque commence elle dès 16h, et l'infokiosque y sera installé en avance

 

!

La propaganda no es y no puede ser más que la repetición continua, incansable, de aquellos principios que deben servirnos de guía en la conducta que debemos seguir en las varias contingencias de la vida.

Repetiremos, pues, con palabras más o menos diferentes, pero con un fondo constante, nuestro viejo programa socialista-anarquista-revolucionario.

Nosotros creemos que la mayor parte de los males que afligen a los hombres dependen de la mala organización social, y que los hombres, si quisieran y supieran cómo, podrían destruirlos.

La sociedad actual es el resultado de las luchas seculares libradas por los hombres. No comprendiendo las ventajas que podrían sacar de la cooperación y de la solidaridad, viendo en los demás hombres (excepto lo más vecinos por los vínculos de la sangre) un competidor y un enemigo, han procurado acaparar, cada uno para sí, la mayor cantidad posible de disfrutes sin preocuparse por los intereses de los demás.

Dada esta lucha, naturalmente debían salir vencedores los más fuertes o los más afortunados, y de una u otra forma, someter y oprimir a los vencidos.

Mientras el hombre no fué capaz de producir sino lo que necesitaba para su sostén, los vencedores no podían hacer otra cosa que matar al vencido y apoderarse de los alimentos por éste cosechados.

Más tarde, cuando con el descubrimiento del pastoreo y del la agricultura un hombre pudo ya producir mas de lo que necesitaba para vivir, los vencedores encontraron mas ventajoso reducir a los vencidos a esclavitud y hacerles producir para sus dueños.

Más tarde aún, los vencedores se dieron cuenta de que era más cómodo, más productivo, y más seguro explotar el trabajo ajeno con otro sistema: retener la propiedad exclusiva de la tierra y de todos los medios de trabajo, y dejar nominalmente libres a los despojados, los cuales, no teniendo ya medios con que vivir, venían obligados a recurrir a los propietarios y a trabajar para éstos en las condiciones que éstos querían.

De este modo, poquito a poco, a través de toda una red complicadísima de luchas de todo género, invasiones, guerras, rebeliones, represiones, concesiones arrancadas, asociaciones de vencidos unidos para la defensa y de vencedores unidos para la ofensa, se ha llegado al estado actual de la sociedad, en la cual unos cuantos detienen hereditariamente la tierra y toda la riqueza social, mientras la gran masa de los hombres, desheredada de todo, se ve explotada y oprimida por unos poco propietarios.

De este estado de cosas depende el estado de miseria en que generalmente se encuentran los trabajadores y por consiguiente todos los males que de la miseria derivan: ignorancia, delitos, prostitución, la abyección física causada por la desnutrición, la depresión mental, y la muerte prematura. De este modo depende la constitución de una clase especial (el gobierno), la cual, provista de medios materiales de represión, tiene la misión de legalizar y defender a los propietarios contra las reivindicaciones de los proletarios, sirviéndose, además, de esta fuerza, para crearse a sí misma ciertos privilegios y para someterse, cuando se puede, incluso hasta la misma clase propietaria. De esto depende la constitución de otra clase especial (el clero), la cual, con una serie de fábulas sobre la voluntad de Dios, sobre la vida futura, etc …

: Röda flammor

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #5 1913


 Röda flammor heta stiga

 upp mot skyn, som färgas matt.

 Stadens kyrktorn stå och tiga

 i den mörka, svarta natt.


 Röda flammor dåvt ni spraka

 i er hårda, vreda strid.

 Nu palatsens väggar knaka,

 lossna, brista snart därvid.


 Röda flammor, ur ert fängsel

 äntligen ni sluppit ut,

 kvävda bakom mur och stängsel,

 eder frihet kom till slut.


 Röda flammor, praktfullt röda,

 hur jag längtat efter er!

 Intet kan er kraft nu döda,

 mänskor tröttnat lida mer.


 Röda flammor, härligt röda

 såsom eld och purpurfärg,

 gör nu slut på sorg och möda,

 skänk åt livet must och märg!


 Röda flammor, väl ni veta

 målet, som ni brinna för.

 I er eld, den klara, heta

 lyser hoppet, som ej dör.


 Röda flammor, nya tider,

 ni min längtans ljusa dröm!

 Nu ni brinna sent omsider,

 kämpande mot våldets ström.


 Röda flammor, flammor sköna,

 hur jag längtat efter er!

 Lycka skola alla röna,

 mänskor tröttnat lida mer.

author: Unknown
title: Pierre Kropotkine - L’État, son rôle historique
content:
Auteur·e

: Pierre Kropotkine

Titre

: L’État, son rôle historique

Date

: 1906

Notes

: Texte de Pierre Kropotkine publié en 1906 dans le journal anarchiste Les Temps nouveaux

Source

:

fr.wikisource.org/wiki/L%E2%80%99%C3%89tat,_son_r%C3%B4le_historique


 I


 En prenant pour sujet de cette conférence

[1]

 l’État et son rôle historique, j’ai pensé répondre à un besoin qui se fait vivement sentir en ce moment : celui d’approfondir l’idée même de l’État, d’étudier son essence, son rôle dans le passé et la part qu’il peut être appelé à jouer dans l’avenir.


 C’est surtout dans la question de l’État que se trouvent divisés les socialistes. Dans l’ensemble des fractions qui existent parmi nous, et qui répondent aux différents tempéraments, aux différentes manières de penser, et surtout au degré de confiance dans la prochaine révolution, deux grands courants se dessinent.


 Il y a ceux, d’une part, qui espèrent accomplir la révolution sociale dans l’État : maintenir la plupart de ses attributions, les étendre même, les utiliser pour la révolution. Et il y a ceux qui, comme nous, voient dans l’État, non seulement sous sa forme actuelle, mais dans son essence même et sous toutes les formes qu’il pourrait revêtir, un obstacle à la révolution sociale : l’empêchement par excellence à l’éclosion d’une société basée sur l’égalité et la liberté, la forme historique élaborée pour prévenir cette éclosion. Ceux-ci travaillent en conséquence à abolir l’État, et non à le réformer.


 La division, vous le voyez, est profonde. Elle correspond à deux courants divergents, qui se rencontrent dans toute la philosophie, la littérature et l’action de notre époque. Et si les notions courantes sur l’État restent aussi obscures qu’elles le sont aujourd’hui, ce sera, à n’en pas douter, sur cette question que s’engageront les luttes les plus obstinées, lorsque — bientôt, je l’espère — les idées communistes chercheront leur réalisation pratique dans la vie des sociétés.


 Il importe donc, après avoir si souvent fait la critique de l’État actuel, de rechercher le pourquoi de son apparition, d’approfondir la part qu’il a jouée dans le passé, de le comparer aux institutions auxquelles il s’est substitué.


 ⁂


 Entendons-nous d’abord sur ce que nous voulons comprendre sous le nom d’État.


 Il y a, vous le savez, l’école allemande qui se plaît à confondre l’

État

 avec la

Société

. Cette confusion se rencontre chez les meilleurs penseurs allemands et beaucoup de français, qui ne peuvent concevoir la société que dans la concentration étatiste ; et c’est pourquoi on reproche habituellement aux anarchistes de vouloir « détruire la société », de prêcher le retour à « la guerre perpétuelle de chacun contre tous ».


 Cependant, raisonner ainsi, c’est entièrement ignorer les progrès accomplis dans le domaine de l’histoire durant cette dernière trentaine d’années ; c’est ignorer que l’homme a vécu en sociétés pendant des milliers d’années, avant d’avoir connu l’État ; c’est oublier que pour les nations européennes, l’État est d’origine récente — qu’il date à peine du XVI

e

 siècle ; c’est méconnaître enfin que les périodes les plus glorieuses de l’humanité furent celles où les libertés et la vie locale n’étaient pas encore détruites par l’État, et où les masses d’hommes vivaient en communes et en fédérations libres.


 L’État n’est qu’une des formes revêtues par la Société dans le courant de l’histoire. Comment donc confondre le permanent et l’accidentel ?


 ⁂


 D’autre part, on a aussi confondu l’

État

 avec

le Gouvernement

. Puisqu’il ne peut y avoir d’État sans gouvernement, on a dit quelquefois que c’est l’absence de gouvernement, et non l’abolition de l’État, qu’il faut viser.


 Il me semble cependant, que dans l’État et le gouvernement, nous avons deux notions d’ordre différent. L’idée d’État implique bien autre chose que l’idée de gouvernement. Elle comprend non seulement l’existence d’un pouvoir placé au-dessus de la société, mais aussi

une concentration territoriale et une concentration de beaucoup de fonctions de la vie des sociétés entre les mains de quelques-uns

. Elle implique certains nouveaux rapports entre les membres de la société, qui n’existaient pas avant la formation de l’État.


 Cette distinction, qui échappe, peut-être, à première vue, apparaît surtout quand on étudie les origines de l’État.


 Pour bien comprendre l’État, il n’y a, d’ailleurs, qu’un moyen : c’est de l’étudier dans son développement …

Весьма тяжёлые личные и семейные обстоятельства отвлекли меня от своевременного ответа на последнюю (насколько я знаю) статью Пардайяна.

Прошу прощения за задержку и отвечаю теперь, полагая, что лучше поздно, чем никогда.

Итак, Пардайян согласен со мной и со всеми анархистами в том, чтобы «абсолютно отвергать» правительство, которое есть то, что вообще понимается под правительством и которое было и есть всякое существовавшее и существующее правительство, то есть орган, который создаёт закон и навязывает его всем посредством материальной силы.

Только у него есть слабость к слову «правительство», и, оставаясь анархистом, он хотел бы сохранить его, изменив его значение.

Он спрашивает меня: «Могут ли анархисты, не переставая быть таковыми, допускать правительство, которое не имело бы антилибертарного значения обычного правительства?»

Отвечаю: да. Если я, например, изменю значение слова «палач», я вполне могу допустить существование палача с доброй и чувствительной душой, который не обидел бы и мухи; или если я придам слову «шёлк» значение «электрическая лампа», я вполне могу допустить существование стула, который бы светился.

Но к чему было бы так революционизировать словарь? Очевидно, к тому, чтобы понимать друг друга ещё меньше, чем прежде.

И почему Пардайян, который хотел бы, чтобы анархисты составили силу, способную мощно влиять на ход событий, не колеблется вступить в противоречие с массой анархистов и создать новые поводы для раскола, а значит, для слабости, – из-за причуды называть правительством то, что правительством не было бы?

Он рассуждает так: народ привык быть управляемым и подчиняется правительству, каково бы оно ни было; в определённые моменты он может свергнуть данное правительство, но делает это с мыслью увидеть его заменённым лучшим правительством. Кто проворнее займёт место, оставленное павшим правительством, и скажет «правительство – это я», тот немедленно будет признан и ему тут же будут подчинятся. Сделаем так, чтобы мы первыми сказали «правительство – это мы», и сможем сделать не анархию, но столько добра, сколько удастся, а тем временем отнимем у политиканов возможность воспользоваться ситуацией.

Пусть простит меня товарищ Пардайян, если я скажу ему несколько резко: его рассуждение и его намерение кажутся мне настолько наивными, что почти инфантильны, ибо, конечно, не было бы серьёзным делом называть себя правительством и не делать того, что должно делать правительство и чего люди от него ждут, то есть издавать указы и заставлять их исполнять посредством полиции, армии, судей и тюремщиков.

Пардайян говорит, что у него сложилось впечатление (не знаю, откуда взятое), будто я, принимая предложение придать слову «правительство» либертарное значение, чтобы пользоваться им по-своему, уже готов искать вместе с ними (ревизионистами) лучший способ помешать этому правительству стать тем, чем оно абсолютно не должно быть.

Но если правительство будет состоять из анархистов, кто возьмётся удерживать его в пределах, назначенных ему Пардайяном? Это могли бы быть только анархисты, не находящиеся в правительстве, – то есть анархисты должны были бы сдерживать правительство, сформированное их товарищами, так же, как сдерживали бы любое другое правительство. Ну и что тогда!

Нет; это вина моего способа выражаться, но Пардайян понял меня совершенно наоборот.

Я полагаю – не считая игры слов – что мы не сможем стать правительством иначе, как в сговоре с авторитарными партиями и после того, как анархисты утратили бы то пламенное стремление к свободе для всех, которое составляет их специфический смысл существования. И полагаю, что если бы в силу исключительнейших обстоятельств нам удалось казаться правительством, вскоре мы захотели бы быть правительством всерьёз и не были бы …

author: Unknown
title: Axel Holmström - Skräckväldet på Långholmen
content:
Författare

: Axel Holmström

Titel

: Skräckväldet på Långholmen

Källa

: Tidningen Brand #5 1913


 I avslagsyrkandet på nådeansökan från Tomelilla för Algot Rosberg, Anton Nilsson och Alfred Stern skriver direktör Wollin att Rosberg uppfört sig »dåligt under strafftiden».


 En stor del av bevakningspersonalen på Långholmen och flera frigivna påstå motsatsen; de säga att det i flesta fall är Wollin som brutit mot Fångvårdsstyrelsens instruktion. De beundra Rosberg att han kunnat behärska sig som han gjort. Och man måste ge dem rätt.


 Från första dagen Rosberg kom till Långholmen har Wollin uppträtt på ett brutalt, utmanande sätt mot vår kamrat. Det ser ut, som om hans avsikt vore, att genom att raffinerad grym behandling få Rosberg så bitter och uppretad att han till sist skulle »förgå sig» mot direktörn. Ty gjorde Rosberg aldrig så lite våld mot Wollin, kom han nog aldrig ut med livet. Och av allt att döma, tycks detta vara Wollins önskan. Men Rosberg har nog genomskådat dessa planer, och det är säkerligen därför han kunnat resignera och genomgå så ohyggliga lidanden som han gjort på Långholmen.


 Då Rosberg i februari 1909 kom till Långholmen hittade man som bekant en liten sågklinga i den brödkaka han hade med sig. För detta dömdes Rosberg till 30 dagar utan arbete, därav 8 dygn utan sängkläder. Under de 8 dygn, då han låg på golvet, var cellen alldeles tom. Det enda som fanns var en vattenmugg och ett nattkärl. Men man nöjde sig ej med detta, utan man stängde av värmledningen till den cell Rosberg låg eller rättare gick i. Och detta mitt i kalla vintern. Konstaplar ha sagt mig, att isblommorna antogo allt vackrare former på den lilla fönstergluggen. Ett tydligt bevis för, att värmledningen verkligen var avstängd. Själv har jag två vintrar haft tillfälle se, att det ej blir isblommor på fönstergluggarna, då cellerna äro uppvärmda.


 Det påstås, att Rosberg under dessa dagar förvägrades tala med läkaren.


 Innan denna 30 dagars tortyr var slut hostade Rosberg blod. Det dröjde ett och ett halvt år innan han repade sig efter denna knäck.


 Det första brev jag fick från Rosberg från Långholmen är skrivet 29 maj 1910 och däri skriver han:


 »Du frågar hur jag mår, om jag är frisk. Ja, käre broder jag vet det knappast själv. Under vissa tider överfalles jag av en mattighetskänsla, som gör att jag knappt kan hålla mig uppe. Tvänne gånger har jag måst lägga mig till sängs, några dagar varje gång. Nu pågår just en sådan period. Jag är så kraftlös ,att jag knappt förmår lyfta prässjärnet. Du vet väl att jag är skräddare? Så desslikes har jag emellanåt obehagliga stickningar i bröstet.»


 Är det inte dåligt, direktör Wollin, att behandla en fånge som ni har för att »uppfostra» så omänskligt grymt? Är det meningen att Ni skall ödelägga fångarnas hälsa?


 När direktör Wollin hade semester på sommaren 1910 sjukskrev Rosberg sig och frågade doktor Sällberg om han inte kunde få flytta in i en sjukcell. Detta låvade läkaren strax. Dag efter dag gick, men Rosberg fick ej flytta in i sjukcellen. Då frågade han löjtnant Vik, vilken tjänstgjorde som direktör under Wollins semester, varför läkarens order ej verkställdes. Rosberg fick det svaret, att de ej

tordes

 förrän Wollin kom hem. Detta visar väl tydligt, vilket strängt och självrådigt regemente Wollin för därute.


 När Wollin så äntligen kom hem, fick Rosberg flytta in i sjukcell. Därom skrev Rosberg i ett brev till en annan pärson den 7 augusti 1910:


 »Men först bör du veta att jag fått en cell med stort fönster. Kan du tänka dig hur det käns att komma från graven upp i ljuset? Vidare har jag fått sjukmat, en halv portion. På de sista tre veckorna har jag ej ätit annat än gröt. Nu börjar jag snart få matlust igen. Luften gör mycket.»


 Rosberg fick så sitta i sjukcell till i februari 1912. Således ett och ett halvt år. Ett ojävigt bevis för att det ej var en tillfällig sjukdom. Nej, under de åtta dygnen han låg på golvet, då värmledningen var avstängd, hade hans hälsa fullständigt brutits.


 Under den tid, Rosberg i fjor var på »gemensamheten» kryade han till sig ganska bra. Men så kom den grymma tortyren den 4 sept. med åtföljande strapatser. Detta har åter för en tid knäckt hans svaga hälsa.

Было это в конце лета 1872 года в Неаполе.

Неаполитанская федерация Интернационала трудящихся делегировала Кафьеро и меня представлять её на конгрессе, который должен был состояться в Швейцарии (и действительно состоялся в Сен-Имье, в Бернской Юре), для соглашения между всеми секциями Интернационала, восставшими против Генерального совета, который под руководством Карла Маркса хотел подчинить всю Ассоциацию своей диктаторской власти и направить её не к разрушению, а к завоеванию политической власти.

Я был весь воодушевлён этой борьбой, от которой должна была зависеть судьба Интернационала и будущее революционного и социалистического действия.

Молодой человек, делающий первые шаги, я был, естественно, совершенно счастлив от возможности поехать на конгресс, вступить в прямое общение с товарищами из всех стран и, быть может, даже горд от того, что заставлю услышать свой голос. В том возрасте, когда ты не болван, всегда бываешь слишком полон собой! Но больше всего меня возбуждала[1] мысль, что я познакомлюсь с Бакуниным, что я стану (я в этом не сомневался) его личным другом.

Бакунин в Неаполе был своего рода мифом. Он был там, кажется, в 1864 и в 1867 годах и произвёл глубокое впечатление. О нём говорили как о необыкновенном человеке и, как обычно бывает, преувеличивали его качества и его недостатки. Говорили о его гигантском росте, о его чудовищном аппетите, о его небрежной одежде, о его пантагрюэлевской неряшливости, о его государевом презрении к деньгам. Рассказывали, что, приехав в Неаполь с крупной суммой в тот момент, когда туда часто прибывали польские революционеры, бежавшие от репрессий, последовавших за восстанием 1863 года, Бакунин просто отдал половину всего, что у него было, первому встреченному нуждающемуся поляку, затем половину оставшейся половины – второму поляку и так далее, пока – и ждать этого пришлось недолго – не остался без единого гроша. И тогда он брал деньги у друзей с тем же господским безразличием, с каким отдавал свои. Но это и многое другое было легендой, более или менее обоснованной, которая всегда складывалась вокруг имени того, кто по той или иной причине выделялся среди прочих. Важно было то, что во всех передовых кружках, или считавших себя таковыми, много говорили вокруг идей Бакунина, который пришёл расшатать все традиции, все социальные, политические, патриотические догмы, считавшиеся до тех пор массой неаполитанских «интеллектуалов» истинами несомненными и не подлежащими обсуждению. Для одних Бакунин был варваром Севера, без Бога и без Отечества, без уважения к чему-либо святому, и представлял опасность для святой итальянской и латинской цивилизации. Для других он был человеком, который внёс в мёртвый застой неаполитанских традиций глоток здорового воздуха, который открыл глаза молодёжи, приблизившейся к нему, на новые и широкие горизонты; и эти – Фанелли, Де Лука, Гамбуцци, Туччи, Палладино и другие – были первыми социалистами, первыми интернационалистами, первыми анархистами Неаполя и Италии.

И так, от постоянных разговоров о нём, Бакунин стал и для меня персонажем легенды; и познакомиться с ним, приблизиться к нему, согреться у его огня было для меня пламенным желанием, почти навязчивой идеей.

Мечта должна была осуществиться.

Итак, я отправился в Швейцарию вместе с Кафьеро.

Я в то время был болезненным, плевал кровью и был признан чахоточным, или около того, тем более что я потерял родителей, сестру и брата от грудной болезни. Переваливая Готард ночью (тогда не было туннеля и нужно было пересекать снежную гору в дилижансе), я простудился и прибыл в Цюрих, в дом, где жил Бакунин, вечером, с кашлем и жаром.

После первых приветствий Бакунин устроил мне кроватку, пригласил, почти заставил меня лечь на неё, укрыл меня всеми одеялами и пальто …

author: Chris Walker
title: Vance Sees “Nothing Unusual” in Taxpayer-Funded Ads Promoting Trump
content:
Some critics have decried the ads as likely illegal, and potentially an impeachable offense.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Vice President JD Vance told reporters on Monday that he sees no problem with the campaign-style TV ads featuring President Donald Trump that are being produced using taxpayer dollars and airing ahead of the midterm elections.

In defending the ads, Vance compared them to informative government-funded commercials, like those that promoted the Affordable Care Act (ACA) during the Obama and Biden administrations. However, those ads provided information about enrollment, eligibility, and more, while the Trump ads in question primarily promote the president and attack his perceived political enemies.

“I don’t think there’s anything unusual or unorthodox about it,” Vance said, recognizing that “some people probably don’t like it.”

“But if you look at the message of those advertisements, they are not partisan; it’s not like we’re advocating for a particular candidate,” he added.

Vance also claimed the ads are “trying to tell a story about how great the United States of America is.”

JD Vance defends Trump's taxpayer-funded propaganda videos: "If you look at the message of those advertisements, they are not partisan, it's not like we're advocating for a particular candidate"

According to sources speaking to The New York Times with knowledge of how Trump’s ads were produced, the funding for the ads came from the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) budget. The ads have so far run on cable news networks, nationally broadcast sporting events, and other programs.

Federal law prohibits the use of taxpayer funds to produce promotional, overtly political material. Notably, some of the taxpayer-funded ads in question have featured audio of the president, then as a candidate, giving a stump speech during the 2024 presidential election.

The ads feature attacks on so-called “communists” and “Marxists” — terms Trump has errantly used to describe Democrats in the past. An upcoming ad also describes Trump in disturbingly glowing terms, and is reportedly entitled, “God made Trump.”

These ads include disclaimers at the bottom that read: “Paid for by the U.S. Government.”

Critics and observers have described the ads as political, not informational.

“The timing cannot be ignored: five weeks ahead of congressional elections in which Republicans fear defeat in the House and the Senate,” CNN senior political reporter Stephen Collinson said. “The video’s hero narrative is exactly the kind of messaging that might drive out quintessential Trump voters whom the GOP needs to turn out in droves, even when Trump isn’t formally heading midterm tickets.”

The TV spots likely run afoul of federal laws forbidding the use of taxpayer funds for political advertising, others have noted. One former White House ethics lawyer, Richard Painter, pointed out that it may be an impeachable offense.

“This is very dangerous. We do not allow government-sponsored propaganda in the United States,” Painter said last month.

The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

The only way we can keep publishing is with strong reader support. We are asking you to start a monthly donation to Truthout today — anything you can do, whether $5 or $25, makes a difference.

author: Sophia Sheera
title: Burnham Scraps Starmer-Era Plans to Roll Back Jury Trials
content:
Andy Burnham’s government has scrapped plans to curb jury trials, after months of outcry from lawyers, MPs and the public. 


New justice secretary Alex Norris said on Sunday that his government inherited a court system “on the brink of collapse” – but that the answer to driving down backlogs was not to roll back jury trials. 


He added that scrapping the plans, which were introduced by former justice secretary David Lammy under Keir Starmer, would enable the Ministry of Justice to find better ways of addressing the courts backlog. 


“

I have heard the strength of feeling on the proposals for increasing the number of judge-alone trials in the Crown Court and have made the decision to change course,” he said. 


The government has instead promised to invest millions in new technology to modernise the sluggish courts system and give greater resources to judges.


Campaign group Defend Our Juries said the move was “a step in the right direction”. The group has argued Lammy’s plans were a deliberate attempt to stop protesters being acquitted by juries who believe they acted on their conscience when breaking certain laws.  


But the group criticised the government for

 announcing that courts

 will “have the final say over where cases should be heard” in order to prevent “criminals accused of relatively minor crimes trying to game the system by electing a jury trial in an attempt to avoid prison.” 


“The centuries-old democratic principle of trial by a jury of one’s peers is not an attempt to ‘game the system’”, the

group said

 on X.


The justice ministry has also said it will give magistrates the power to hand out longer sentences under the new plans. 


Last month, the Crown Court backlog reached a record high, with 81,000 cases awaiting trial and a third of them for longer than a year. 


Lammy’s plans would have meant cases where the sentence is less than three years would not be tried by jury. They also called for lengthy fraud and financial cases to be tried by only a judge, a policy that Norris will keep.


Critics of Lammy’s plans included

39 of Starmer’s own Labour bankbenchers

 and

Shami Chakrabarti

, former director of advocacy group Liberty Shami Chakrabarti. 


“The drastic restriction of the right to trial by jury is not a silver bullet,” the rebel MPs wrote in a letter to Starmer last December. “To limit a fundamental right for what will make a marginal difference to the backlog, if any, is madness and will cause more problems than it solves.”

author: Stéphanie de Sève
title: 350 km à pied et à pagaie : une expédition pour la réconciliation
content:
C’est sur le territoire anishnabe de la communauté de Kitigan Zibi que l’expédition Mamu Nikantetau a débuté, cette année. Une traversée qui se veut une rencontre entre des participants de différentes nations et des allochtones.


Initiée par le Dr Stanley Vollant, l’expédition en est à sa 4e édition. Pour le Dr Vollant, « la réconciliation doit être plus qu’un simple mot ou un concept. » Mamu Nikantetau en innu veut dire « avançons ensemble ». Cette année, l’aventure s’est déroulée à pied mais surtout en rabaska pour un total de 350 kilomètres.


Un an avant l’expédition, Guylaine Gros-Louis s’entraînait déjà dans l’espoir de se joindre au groupe. Elle a appris la bonne nouvelle en juillet et s’est munie d’un entraîneur privé pour travailler le haut de son corps : « C’est la fierté de faire ce périple-là, c’est un dépassement de soi. »


« Si je peux être un exemple, une source de motivation pour d’autres personnes, pourquoi pas. »


Derrière sa participation se cache une quête d’équilibre des quatre sphères : « il y a des sphères qui sont plus fragilisées, puis c’est d’aller travailler là-dessus. »


Une marche symbolique a marqué le début de cette aventure de dix jours.


Dr Vollant : « une 2e journée plus chargée avec une traversée de la rivière des Outaouais, appelée la kichi sibi et occupée par les communautés anishnabee depuis des millénaires. »


Rencontrée au cimetière Beechwood à Ottawa, la sénatrice Michèle Audette a encouragé les participants : « Alors votre pagaie que vous faites à chaque, que vous faites à chaque jour. Vous le faites pour nos ancêtres, pour vos ancêtres. »


Cinq kilomètres de marche séparaient le cimetière Beechwood du parlement d’Ottawa.


Dr Vollant : « les choses ne changent pas rapidement, on le sait, mais un pas à la fois, on arrive à la fin »


Maman de trois grands enfants, à 52 ans, Guylaine est considérée comme « une jeune aînée ». Selon le Dr Vollant, le lien sacré de la transmission entre les aînés et les jeunes a été rompu en raison des pensionnats : « Aujourd’hui, on doit le rétablir et en ayant des aînés dans notre expédition avec des jeunes, on rétablit cette lignée d’enseignement qui a été brisée. »


Guylaine espère tisser des liens avec les plus jeunes et compte rester connectée à des êtres chers qui ne sont plus de ce monde : « les quatre plumes, évidemment, qui représentent les quatre sphères et les quatre anges gardiens qui me suivent à travers l’expédition, qui veillent sur moi. »


Guylaine Gros-Louis


« Je me sens fébrile. On prend la route de la navigation, on va se laisser porter par la mer.


bien, la mer, le flot de l’eau. Et c’est magnifique. Je pense qu’il va y avoir un vent de légèreté dans tout ça. »


Cette année marque le 325e anniversaire de la Grande Paix de Montréal. Ce qui rend cette traversée encore plus symbolique pour le Dr Vollant : « la rivière des Outaouais a servi de route pour les 42 peuples des Premières Nations se réunir et faire une grande paix pour que tous les gens, peu importe leur culture, leur langage, puissent avoir le droit de développer leur plein potentiel. Et je pense que c’était une des premières réconciliations. »


Dans les jours qui ont suivi, dame Nature a été clémente, mais au jour 7, l’équipe a vécu un revirement : un des rabaskas a chaviré à cause du vent. Guylaine était dans celui-là et elle insiste pour dire que l’organisation a su gérer la situation avec efficacité et qu’elle s’est sentie en sécurité : « mais c’est ça, je n’étais vraiment pas inquiète. Puis moi, mon plan, quand j’étais dans l’eau, je me suis dit, je vais bouger, bouger, bouger mes jambes pour ne pas souffrir d’hypothermie. Mes doigts, je tenais le rabaska, puis mes doigts, j’allais faire… je faisais bouger mes doigts, mon corps. »


La résilience du groupe a été testée : « puis de voir l’unicité de l’équipe, c’est comme une famille. C’est vraiment beau. C’est vraiment beau. Puis, c’est ça, on est tous là, l’un pour l’autre. » Guylaine a tout de même passé un coup de fil à sa mère, Louise Martel Gros-Louis, pour la rassurer : « elle a dit, “moi, je suis correct,

mom

, inquiète-toi pas”. J’étais contente. Je savais qu’elle était correcte. » Après discussion, tous ont choisi de poursuivre l’aventure.


Au dernier jour, famille et amis les attendaient aux abords du canal de Lachine, dont une mère, fière de sa fille : « Sur toute la ligne. …dans sa vie de tous les jours. » Un sentiment partagé par Guylaine à son arrivée, en plus d’une bonne dose de …

author: Mike McDonald
title: ISC minister, chief of Namaygoosisagagun First Nation meet to discuss rebuild
content:
A recent meeting between Namaygoosisagagun First Nation (Collins Lake) and the minister of Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) left the chief with questions.


“What are we rebuilding?” Helen Paavola told APTN News of the Sept. 29 meeting with Minister Mandy Gull-Masty. “And that is a good question. What are we rebuilding? Are we just going back to what our community was? How many structures? So, they’re very good questions.”


In July, community members barely escaped with their lives after a wildfire swept in. People escaped in boats and posted dramatic photos on social media of their flight.


Namaygoosisagagun isn’t under the Indian Act, so unlike other First Nations, the millions needed to rebuild wasn’t guaranteed.


The community has been negotiating its status with the federal government since 2018.


Gull-Masty told APTN that Ottawa will help – but the community needs to come up with some answers.


“What kind of support does she need? How do you work with your members to define how that rebuild is going to look like? And, most importantly, how do you support them through also living through a very traumatic experience of losing the community?” Gull-Masty said.


The summer of 2026 saw some of the worst wildfires in recorded history. A number of communities in northern Ontario had to evacuate because of oncoming flames and smoke.


Read More: 


First Nations stuck in ‘spiralling cycle’ during wildfires: federal housing advocate 


Namaygoosisagagun is located on the northern edge of Collins Lake, about 250 km north of Thunder Bay. People from the community are still not home – but did go back to see what was left.


“They went up to clean the community; they did some cutting, clearing some fallen trees,” Paavola said. “We had ordered six huge prospector tents that they set up for us.”


The tents are for members who want to go back.


“We are planning a trip to go home. How long we stay there, we’re not sure yet,” she said. “Because, we are taking our Elders up there and we’ll see how safe it is for them. And, even the rest of us… we want to go home. And we know how that looks right now, you know, but… but still, to be on the land, to be near our lake, you know, I think that’s going to help us to heal.”


Paavola said her members have been doing their best to cope with the situation, often coping with depression and loneliness.


She said they’re looking forward to going home.


“It sounds like there’s a whole bunch of us going back,” she said. “It’s going to be a big party.”

APTN News

title: London Conference's conclusions: Peace must be guaranteed by rule of law and democratic institutions
content:
Following the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference, held in London on September 29–30, the Centre for Kurdish Affairs published its conclusions from the conference discussions, along with recommendations for the period ahead.


During the two-day conference, representatives of Kurdish political and civil society organizations, as well as figures involved in peace processes in different parts of the world, academics, politicians, and experts came together. They discussed a wide range of topics, from the democratic resolution of the Kurdish issue in Turkey to international experiences of peacebuilding; from legal guarantees and local democracy to the role of women, as well as developments in Syria and the wider region.


The Centre for Kurdish Affairs stressed that "this communiqué presents the Centre’s analysis of the conference discussions. The views, interpretations and conclusions contained herein should not be understood as a collective statement on behalf of every speaker, participant or supporting institution."


The text said: "The Centre for Kurdish Affairs convened a two-day international conference in London, bringing together peace practitioners, academics, political representatives, policymakers and civil society representatives to examine comparative experiences of conflict resolution, peacebuilding, constitutional accommodation, power-sharing and self-government, and to consider their relevance to contemporary discussions concerning the Kurdish question.


For the purposes of this communiqué, democratic integration refers to rights-based and voluntary participation within a plural democratic order and should not be understood as cultural, linguistic or political assimilation. Furthermore, the phrase ‘the Kurdish question’ is employed to encompass the full spectrum of legal, political, cultural, economic, and social issues impacting Kurdish populations."


Summarizing the two-day conference, the text said: "The first day focused on comparative international experiences through three panels: ‘Why Peace Processes Succeed or Fail’; ‘Peace, Power-Sharing and Constitutional Accommodation: Lessons from the UK’; and ‘Autonomy, Devolution and Self-Government’. Drawing on a range of conflict-resolution and constitutional experiences, the discussions considered the political and institutional conditions under which negotiations can be sustained, settlements can acquire legitimacy and durability, and differing territorial and political claims can be accommodated within democratic frameworks.


The second day turned more directly to the Kurdish question through three panels: ‘Post-Conflict Kurdish Democratic Politics’; ‘The Kurdish Question Across Borders’; and ‘Inclusive Peace: Women, Minorities, and Systems of Justice’. The discussions examined the possible evolution of Kurdish politics in a post-conflict environment, the regional and transnational dimensions of the Kurdish question across Türkiye, Syria, Iraq and Iran, as well as within the diaspora, and the role of women, minorities and the media in broadening participation and embedding peace within democratic political life."


Conference Context and International Engagement


The text continued: "London offered a particularly resonant setting for these discussions. The United Kingdom’s constitutional tradition has evolved over many centuries, with Magna Carta of 1215 among its historic reference points in the development of law, political authority, representation and consent.


Its more recent experience of devolution, power-sharing and negotiated settlement provides a further point of reference for considering how established political systems can adapt to diverse identities and political aspirations. In this context, PDIC provided a forum for diplomatic and policy discussion in which Kurdish perspectives could be considered alongside wider international experience on conflict resolution, democratic accommodation and the prospects for a durable political settlement.


The conference received expressions of support and engagement from Catherine West MP, Bambos Charalambous MP and the Rt Hon David Lammy MP, underscoring the importance of sustained engagement between Kurdish perspectives and the United Kingdom’s political and policy community at a time when questions of peace, democratic participation and regional stability are assuming renewed significance.

Adır'ın açıklaması şöyle: "TİP Milletvekili Ahmet Şık'ın daha önce dile getirdiği iddialara ilişkin kendisinden somut bilgi ve belge sunması istenmiş; ancak bugüne kadar iddialarını destekleyen tek bir belge dahi ortaya konulamamıştır. Dayanaktan yoksun ve gerçeği yansıtmayan paylaşımları nedeniyle hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunulmuş ve tazminat davası açılmıştır. İddiasını ispat edemeyen bu müptezelin iftira ve hakaretleri tarafımızca muhatap alınmamaktadır. Gerekli cevap yalnızca hukuk önünde verilecektir. Kamuoyuna saygıyla duyurulur."

Ahmet Şık, 26 Eylül'de X hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda "Akın Gürlek, tutuklu şüphelilerden E.Tezmen ve M.Yarız ile tutuksuz E. Özel ile Adalet Bakan Yardımcılığı döneminden bugüne kadar 2024, 2025, 2026'da İstanbul’daki belirli otellerde kaç kez görüşmüştür? Görüşmelerin tarihleri, yerleri, amaçları ve içerikleri nelerdir?" sorusunu sormuştu.

Şık ayrıca New York'taki BM Genel Kurulu sırasında çekilen bir fotoğrafı paylaşarak "Geçen hafta New York’taki BM toplantısı sırasında çekilen bu fotoğrafta, solda Akın Gürlek’in yanında duran kişi fon soygunu soruşturmasında hakkında yakalama kararı bulunan Bilal Çalışkan" demişti.

Eğer menfaat ilişkisi yoksa en hafifinden “görevi ihmal/kötüye kullanma” suçlamasından şüpheli olan ve bu tür soygunları önleyici/denetleyici kurum olan SPK yönetiminde eşiniz varken sizin soruşturmayı yürüten yargının başında olmanız çıkar çatışması değil midir?
