title: Aposta online: 12 dos 17 parlamentares da Bancada das Bets seguem mais 4 anos no Congresso
content:
Esta reportagem é parte de uma investigação especial da

Agência Pública

 financiada pelos nossos Aliados, sem nenhum dinheiro de bet. Apoie mais reportagens como essa

clicando aqui.


Um total de 70% dos parlamentares mapeados pela

Agência Pública

 como integrantes ou aliados da “Bancada das Bets” segue com mandatos no Congresso Nacional até 2030.

Dos 17 nomes identificados na investigação como parlamentares que contemplaram interesses das casas de apostas ou foram aliados importantes nas articulações desse mercado, 11 foram eleitos no último domingo (4)

. Um deles, Romário (PL-RJ), só enfrenta nova disputa por eleitores na próxima disputa para o Senado.


A

bancada

, que não existe formalmente no Congresso, reúne parlamentares que atuaram em pautas relacionadas à regulamentação, tributação e expansão do mercado de apostas online.


A influência do setor não se restringia à apresentação ou votação de projetos: passava também por conversas diretas com líderes partidários

, articulações para alterar propostas em tramitação e encontros com representantes e empresários do mercado, como revelado no especial

Jogo Perigoso: O Brasil das Bets

.


Entre os 11 parlamentares classificados como nomes de base que, direta ou indiretamente, contemplaram interesses das casas de apostas, sete foram eleitos. Luiz Philippe de Orleans e Bragança, foi reeleito pelo PL em São Paulo. Kim Kataguiri, que mudou do União Brasil para o Missão, também conquistou uma vaga pelo estado. Em Minas Gerais, Weliton Prado foi reeleito pelo PSD com 129.366 votos.


Na Bahia, Adolfo Viana (PSDB) foi reeleito com 119.865 votos e João Bacelar (PL), com 107.232. O outro Bacelar da lista, João Carlos Bacelar Batista, concorreu pelo PV e ficou de fora dos vitoriosos, mesmo obtendo 102.654 votos. Em Roraima, Gabriel Mota (União-RR), conquistou vaga com 10.195 votos. Na Paraíba, Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL) e Hugo Motta (Republicanos), presidente da Câmara, também foram reeleitos.


Dos seis parlamentares identificados pela

Pública

 como “líderes da Bancada das Bets”, além de Motta, outros três foram eleitos: Doutor Luizinho (PP-RJ), Isnaldo Bulhões (MDB-AL) e Felipe Carreras (PSB-PE), que renovaram seus mandatos na Câmara.


Seguem no Congresso


							–


A atuação dos quatro foi destacada em diferentes momentos da investigação. Luizinho e Bulhões foram identificados como articuladores de iniciativas para impedir aumento da tributação das apostas. A dupla também participou das articulações que retiraram a Cide-bets, contribuição de 15% prevista no debate do PL Antifacção, do texto aprovado pela Câmara. Felipe Carreras, por sua vez, foi descrito por interlocutores ouvidos pela reportagem como um dos principais nomes procurados pelo setor, enquanto Hugo Motta foi citado nas negociações que levaram à retirada da Cide-bets.


Dois dos principais nomes ligados às casas de apostas online, no entanto, ficaram pelo caminho.

 Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI), que disputou a reeleição ao Senado, terminou em terceiro lugar, com 24,68% dos votos, atrás de Marcelo Castro (MDB) e Júlio César (PSD). O mesmo ocorreu com Ângelo Coronel (Republicanos-BA), que teve 2.898.885 votos, 20,11% dos válidos, e ficou atrás de Rui Costa e Jaques Wagner, ambos do PT baiano.


Além dos dois, três nomes da Bancada das Bets não chegaram a tentar uma renovação de mandato:

Jorge Kajuru (PSB-GO), e Irajá (PSD-TO) ficaram fora das urnas e encerram o mandato nos próximos meses.


Saem do Congresso


							–


Correndo por fora


Nomes importantes dos bastidores da costura desse setor na Câmara, que não compunham diretamente a bancada, mas influenciam nas suas conquistas também tiveram desempenho irregular no pleito de 2026.

Arthur Lira (PP-AL) deixou a Câmara depois de mais de uma década e conquistou uma das duas vagas de Alagoas no Senado, com 946.970 votos, 28,87% dos válidos. Rogério Carvalho (PT-SE) foi reeleito senador por Sergipe, com 509.608 votos.


Enquanto isso, Efraim Filho tentou, sem sucesso, a cadeira do governo da Paraíba pelo PL. Já Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) não chegou a ir às urnas, uma vez que seu mandato no Senado segue até 2030.


Outro lado


À época da publicação da reportagem sobre a Bancada das Bets, procurado pela Pública, Doutor Luizinho afirmou ser contrário aos aumentos de impostos e à extinção das plataformas de apostas online e negou ter recebido qualquer contrapartida de empresas do setor. Felipe Carreras defendeu a regulamentação e a arrecadação sobre as …

author: Cierra Bettens
title: Beyond the ballot: Why the Alberta referendum is about more than separation
content:
On Oct. 19,

Albertans will vote

 on whether the province should remain in Canada or begin the legal process to hold a binding provincial referendum on separation from Canada.


They’ll also be answering “yes” or “no” to nine additional questions, ranging from immigration to abolishing the Canadian Senate.


This week on APTN News InFocus, journalist Danielle Paradis joins us to dig deeper into the Alberta referendum.


Paradis spent the summer travelling across Alberta with journalist Tim Querengesser for their podcast, Separation Anxiety. They found themselves in church boardrooms and hot dog picnics, talking to organizers about the roots of the separatist movement.


When it comes to understanding Indigenous sovereignty and Treaty rights, Paradis said Albertans are generally “no different from the rest of Canada”.


“You just don’t see people understanding that the First Nations understand this as an agreement to share the land. Not ceding the land, but that there is this acknowledgement that we’re going to be living together, that we have this ongoing relationship,” Paradis said.


“It’s all of a sudden apparent that there are some real rights for the land and power that the First Nations communities hold when it comes to whether or not Alberta would get to separate.”


Meanwhile, four provinces east, Quebecers are voting for their next premier. The Parti Québécois promises to hold a referendum on separation by 2030 if elected.


It’s a reminder that this isn’t the first time First Nations and Inuit have challenged separatists.


In the second half of this episode, APTN’s Montreal web reporter,

Jesse Staniforth

, discusses how the

Cree of Eeyou Istchee

 asserted their rights during Quebec’s separatist referendums of 1980 and 1995.


“The most striking thing the Crees did in 1995 was that they organized their own referendum,” Staniforth said. “They flew out onto the land and found people on their traplines and brought out ballots saying, ‘Do you consent, as a people, that the Government of Quebec separate the James Bay Crees and Cree traditional territory from Canada in the event of a Yes vote in the Quebec referendum?”


“And 96.3 per cent voted no.”


The post

Beyond the ballot: Why the Alberta referendum is about more than separation 

 appeared first on

APTN News

.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Sanikiluaq daycare moves so facility can expand
content:
Sanikiluaq’s daycare is moving as renovations begin on the community’s existing child-care facility.


Starting Oct. 26, the daycare will move into a temporary space at Nuiyak elementary school, according to an Oct. 1 update that the Sanikiluaq

 District Education Authority posted on Facebook.


The DEA initially told families the daycare building would be demolished Oct. 25 to make way for a new facility.


“We wish to clarify that the daycare is closing to allow for renovations,” said Tyler Kraft, the DEA’s office manager, in a statement posted to Facebook on Monday.

“We recognize that the incorrect information may have caused concern and confusion among families, staff, and community members.”


“We regret this error and any distress it may have caused,” he said.


The project involves renovations to expand the number of licensed child-care spaces, said Kuthula Matshazi, director of stakeholder engagement for the Department of Education, Sept. 29 in an email to Nunatsiaq News.


Construction is scheduled to begin Oct. 25 and is supported by early learning and child-care infrastructure funding from the federal government.


The department did not provide a cost estimate for the project.


The renovation is expected to be complete by Sept. 1, 2027, Matshazi said.


The daycare is currently licensed for four infant spaces and 16 preschool spaces. The renovated facility is expected to add two infant spaces and eight preschool spaces, bringing the total to six infant spaces and 24 preschool spaces, Matshazi said.


Kraft had previously said in an interview that 12 children were on the waitlist to enrol at the daycare.


The temporary location at Nuiyak School will allow daycare services to continue during renovations, ensuring the seven employees — six full-time and one part-time — can continue working.


The larger facility would also allow the daycare to hire more staff and include technology intended to support early education, Kraft said.

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: « La vie est un choix difficile » : un chirurgien innu termine un parcours de 350 km à la pagaie avec des jeunes et des aînés
content:
Avertissement : cet article parle de suicide et d’abus sexuels.


La foule rassemblée autour du canal Lachine, au sud du centre-ville de Montréal, a éclaté en acclamations et en applaudissements lorsque les quatre rabaskas (grands canoës de style algonquin) se sont approchés de la rive, marquant ainsi la fin du périple de 350 km de l’

expédition Mamu Nikantetau

 de cette année, à l’occasion de la Journée nationale de la vérité et de la réconciliation.


Dirigée par le Dr Stanley Vollant, un Innu de Pessamit et le premier Autochtone à devenir chirurgien au Québec, la cinquième expédition Mamu Nikantetau a réuni 29 participants, pour la plupart autochtones.


Le groupe est parti de la nation algonquine de Kitigan Zibi, a descendu jusqu’à Ottawa, puis s’est rendu dans les communautés mohawks de Kanehsatà:ke et Kahnawà:ke, avant d’atteindre sa destination : Montréal.


« Au début, les gens ne se connaissent pas du tout », a expliqué Le Dr Vollant à APTN Nouvelles nationales en anglais. « Ils doivent discuter, apprendre à se connaître, découvrir leur passé, leurs traumatismes, ce vers quoi ils se dirigent et leur objectif, puis on doit se respecter les uns les autres, respecter nos différences. »


Pour que l’expédition réussisse, a-t-il expliqué, le groupe doit cerner les forces et les faiblesses de chacun et apprendre à se connaître suffisamment bien pour pouvoir travailler ensemble et atteindre l’objectif commun : mener ce voyage à son terme.


« On doit pagayer tous en même temps », a déclaré Le Dr Vollant. « C’est très difficile au début de pagayer tous en même temps. »


Le Dr Stanley Vollant accueilli par ses supporters après l’arrivée de l’expédition Mamu Nikantetau à Montréal le 30 septembre 2026. Photo : Jesse Staniforth/APTN


La marche


Mamu Nikantetau, qui signifie « ensemble, on avance » en innu-aimun, a commencé quand Dr Vollant s’est lancé dans une marche de six ans et 6 000 km qu’il a baptisée Innu Meshkenu (ou « sentier innu ») et qu’il a réalisée entre 2010 et 2016.


Le Dr Vollant a parcouru ces 6 000 kilomètres dans l’espoir d’encourager les jeunes autochtones à adopter des habitudes de vie saines et à rester à l’école. Mais il a aussi expliqué que ce projet était né d’une grave dépression en 2007, qui l’avait laissé aux prises avec de fortes pensées suicidaires.


« La colère peut transformer votre vie en misère ou vous mener à la mort », a-t-il déclaré.


Il a raconté comment il avait affronté ses sentiments autodestructeurs et réussi à les surmonter.


« Je suis tellement heureux », a-t-il déclaré. « Dix-neuf ans plus tard, je peux dire que c’était le choix le plus sage. La mort est partout. Elle finira forcément par vous rattraper. On dit que les impôts et la mort sont inévitables, mais parfois, la vie est un choix difficile. »


Ce n’est pas un hasard si l’expédition s’est terminé le Jour national de la vérité et de la réconciliation.


Le Dr Vollant a raconté que sa mère avait survécu aux pensionnats, mais qu’elle ne lui en avait jamais parlé. Quand il parle de sa dépression, tout comme quand il évoque le taux élevé de violence dont sont victimes les femmes autochtones, il explique que tout ça est lié à l’héritage des pensionnats.


« Ma mère est allée dans un pensionnat ; elle a subi des abus, j’en ai souffert, et, quand elle était jeune, je ne comprenais pas pourquoi elle buvait jusqu’à en mourir », a-t-il expliqué. « Elle est décédée à 52 ans, et j’étais malheureux. J’avais beaucoup de colère envers ma mère. Pourquoi était-elle comme ça ?


« Mais quand la Commission vérité et réconciliation a commencé ses travaux, tout le monde s’est mis à parler, et mes tantes et oncles m’ont dit : “Ta mère a subi des abus sexuels au pensionnat.” C’est là que j’ai commencé à comprendre pourquoi elle était comme ça, pourquoi elle buvait. »


Malheureusement, a déclaré Le Dr Vollant, il n’a appris ces faits cruciaux sur le vécu de sa mère que dix ans après sa mort, une décennie durant laquelle il a été en proie à la souffrance, à la confusion et à la rage.


« On doit changer de paradigme et transformer cette colère en quelque chose de positif, de constructif, et ce genre d’expédition a changé des vies », a-t-il déclaré. « En voyant les gens [de l’expédition] parler de l’impact sur leur vie, mes compagnons de marche de ces dix derniers jours m’ont dit : “Ça a changé ma vie” et “je veux changer ma vie.” »


Le Dr Vollant a raconté qu’un jeune lui avait confié avoir arrêté de boire et consommer de la drogue …

author: Ed Wanderley
title: O tempo das bets e a hora da luta: a perda familiar que não está em jogo no STF
content:
Esta reportagem é parte de uma investigação especial da

Agência Pública

 financiada pelos nossos Aliados, sem nenhum dinheiro de bet. Apoie mais reportagens como essa

clicando aqui.


O tempo é uma das ferramentas mais poderosas de perspectiva. Em apenas um segundo, as plataformas de apostas online ganharam mais dinheiro do que 33 milhões de brasileiros fizeram em um mês no ano passado. Literalmente.

Por cada segundo de 2025, as famílias brasileiras perderam para as bets R$ 1.982, mais do que o salário mínimo atual, de R$ 1.621

 – uma realidade, por exemplo, de três a cada cinco trabalhadores no Maranhão. 


Os dados são do Comitê Nacional de Secretários de Fazenda dos Estados e do Distrito Federal (Comsefaz), que, em agosto deste ano, estimou o esvaziamento do orçamento das famílias em R$ 62,5 bilhões em 2025 – um mercado cuja hora de “trabalho” ficou acima dos R$ 7 milhões. Na política, é justamente o tempo que muitas vezes dita urgência, relativização ou esquecimento.


Por quase uma hora, uma mulher se mantinha encolhida em um sofá na sala do apartamento da família em Uberlândia (MG). Era 25 de setembro. Em silêncio absoluto, cortado apenas por um respiro ansiosamente pesado. O som da TV preenchia o ambiente embalando a mulher, seu marido e sua filha mais velha. Evitavam falar, talvez até se mexer. As próprias vidas em suspenso.


O relógio marcava exatamente 19h07 quando um misto de riso, lágrimas e alívio tomou conta de seu semblante. Na tela, o presidente da República

assinava

 a Medida Provisória (MP)

1.394/25

, que proibia não apenas a propaganda, mas o funcionamento das plataformas de apostas em todo o território nacional. 


Ao longo dos sete minutos seguintes, viu Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, com quem havia se encontrado dias antes em Brasília, endossar o discurso que ela ajudou a popularizar, ao comparar a jogatina ao crack, e classificar a

ludopatia

 por jogos online como um risco ainda mais invasivo.

“O país trouxe o jogo para dentro de casa. O cassino está na sala, o cassino está na cozinha”, disse antes de citá-la “eu conversei com a ‘mãe que perdeu o filho de 26 anos’”.

 E ela sorriu, sem se incomodar com a alcunha.


“Foi uma sensação de dever cumprido”, resumiu a professora Vânia Borges do Amaral, de 54 anos, emocionada, ao ver sentido em compartilhar o luto de seu filho, Rafael Borges do Amaral, que tirou a própria vida após perder todas as economias acumuladas para as bets. É o mais recente marco na linha do tempo interrompida pela última aposta que o rapaz fez, à 1h48 de 23 de março de 2024 – um novo capítulo de sua história, agora provido de sentido.


Professora Vânia segura a foto de seu filho Rafael


A MP das bets determinou o fim da oferta dos jogos online, tanto em ambientes físicos quanto virtuais, abrangendo concessões federais e estaduais. Loterias tradicionais não foram atingidas pela mudança.

 Na prática, os sites e aplicativos das empresas devem ser retirados do ar nesta terça-feira (6) e as publicidades, mesmo em outdoors e outros meios físicos devem ser removidos. As multas pelo descumprimento da regra podem chegar a R$ 2 bilhões.


Não há previsão de indenização para as empresas detentoras das 85 outorgas para explorar a atividade legalmente desde 2023 no país. Cada outorga custou cerca de R$ 30 milhões, o que significa um investimento de R$ 2,55 bilhões por parte das companhias para ofertar plataformas reguladas no Brasil – valor quase 25 vezes inferior ao montante gasto pelas famílias em bets apenas em 2025.

Estudo da Universidade de São Paulo (USP) estima que as plataformas retiraram R$ 141 bilhões do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) nacional, enquanto renderam R$ 9,9 bilhões em tributos em contrapartida.


“Eu não imaginava que chegaria a esse ponto, porque quando eu comecei essa luta, eu fui recebida com muito descaso. Primeiro pela Polícia Civil, depois pelo Ministério Público. Eu dei entrada, mas tudo foi demorando tanto… e eu sempre buscando uma resposta que nunca vinha. Eu vi ser instaurada a CPI das Bets e acabar naquela farra. Me gerou muita frustração, muita tristeza. Eu tive a impressão de estar abandonada”, pontuou Vânia sobre testemunhar a proibição, com a qual vinha sonhando há meses. “Eu me senti ouvida”, resumiu.


A história de Vânia e Rafael foi apresentada originalmente pela

Agência Pública

, que identificou uma carta que ela enviou ao Senado durante a CPI das Bets, em que narra a tragédia familiar. Os impactos da

reportagem

 noticiados até fora …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Se cumplió un nuevo paro docente en las Universidades nacionales y en la PBA
content:
El personal docente y no docente de las universidades públicas realizó el 30 de septiembre, 1° y 2 de octubre un nuevo paro por 72 horas para exigir la aplicación inmediata de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario y la recomposición salarial del 33,4%. Mientras tanto, el juez Cormick le dio un nuevo plazo de cinco días al Estado nacional para que cumpla con la ley de Financiamiento Universitario, que Milei insiste en ignorar. Paro en PBA por violencia en las escuelas y reclamo salarial.


Por Mario Hernandez


La medida fue votada por la CONADU y la CONADU Histórica, dos de las federaciones docentes más grandes del país, que se sumó a los diversos planes de lucha que organizaron la Federación Argentina del Trabajador de las Universidades Nacionales (FATUM) con paros regionales, la Asociación de Docentes de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (ADUBA), la Asociación del Personal de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (APUBA), el Sindicato de Trabajadores Docentes de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (Feduba) y con la Unión de Trabajadores de la Educación (UTE), con un esquema de paros por 24 horas en cada una de las sedes.


Asimismo, el jueves se realizó un abrazo simbólico en la Facultad de Medicina como una “acción de visibilidad”. También se organizó una radio abierta y actividades participativas para los ciudadanos.


El reclamo por la aplicación de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario comenzó a finales del año pasado, cuando el Consejo Interuniversitario Nacional (CIN) presentó acciones de amparo debido a que el Poder Ejecutivo no ponía en práctica la norma bajo el argumento sobre falta de fondos, que aún mantiene.


Las medidas de fuerza de la semana pasada son la antesala de lo que será

la 5ª Marcha Federal Universitaria programada para el próximo jueves 15 de octubre

.


La Justicia intimó al Gobierno

 


El Juzgado Contencioso Administrativo Federal N°11 volvió a intimar al Gobierno de Javier Milei para que cumpla con la Ley de Financiamiento de la Educación Universitaria (LFEU).


En una resolución firmada el miércoles, el juez federal Martín Cormick le dio cinco días de plazo al Estado Nacional para que cumpla con la medida cautelar dictada por él en diciembre pasado, que ordena la actualización de los salarios de docentes y no docentes de las universidades públicas y la recomposición de los programas de becas estudiantiles, “bajo apercibimiento de astreintes”, es decir, de multas.


El pasado 22 de septiembre, Cormick ya había intimado al Gobierno de Milei-también dándole un plazo de cinco días-para que cumpla con la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario. Ante esa primera intimación, el Gobierno presentó un pedido de revocatoria, que fue rechazado el miércoles.


La medida cautelar para que el Gobierno pague lo adeudado fue dictada por Cormick el 23 de diciembre del año pasado. La decisión del juez fue confirmada por la Sala III de la Cámara en lo Contencioso Administrativo Federal y ratificada por la Corte Suprema el 25 de junio pasado.


Foto: Data Trenque


Docentes bonaerenses


El miércoles, luego de un nuevo hecho de violencia en el distrito de Trenque Lauquen, las conducciones del Frente de Unidad Docente se vieron obligadas a convocar al paro para el 1° de octubre. La lista Multicolor ya había convocado a la medida, a partir de asambleas y mandatos de escuela. Es necesario imponer un plan de lucha frente a la miseria salarial y falta de respuesta del gobierno provincial de Kicillof en las paritarias, el endeudamiento y las situaciones de violencia en las escuelas.


Las y los trabajadores de la educación vienen protagonizando importantes muestras de descontento y movilización frente a una situación salarial y educativa que se vuelve cada vez más difícil de sostener.


Los paros y las convocatorias impulsadas por la Multicolor son un canal de expresión de un descontento que también aparece por diferentes vías en los distritos. En La Plata se realizó una importante movilización al Banco Provincia contra el creciente endeudamiento docente y las tasas que golpean nuestros salarios.


Mientras tanto, distintas situaciones de violencia en las escuelas dieron lugar a medidas de fuerza y movilizaciones en Ensenada, San Miguel, Hurlingham, Almirante Brown y Florencio Varela.


Luego de los graves hechos de violencia contra los docentes de la EP Nº 13 de Ensenada, la exigencia de asambleas y de una medida de fuerza se impuso desde abajo. Tras el paro de 36 horas, y en el marco de una movilización de más de 300 …

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Says Iran War “Should Help” Republicans in Midterms
content:
Recent polling shows more than 6 in 10 Americans want the war to end as soon as possible.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

In remarks to reporters at the White House on Friday, President Donald Trump conceded that it is “possible” that his continued war on Iran will drag Republicans down in the midterm elections.

But Trump also claimed the issue could be viewed positively by voters, thus helping the GOP, despite consistent polling data suggesting otherwise.

“It should help,” Trump said of the war.

The president then blamed supposed media spin for Americans’ negative views of the war, saying it could hurt the GOP in the midterms.

“When you say, ‘Is it OK for Iran to have a nuclear weapon?’ I would say 100 percent of the people say no, including worldwide,” Trump said. “So, when you say it that way, it would help. If you don’t say that, it could hurt.”

Trump has pressed the idea that the war is justified due to the nuclear issue. However, his comments ignore reality — Iran was engaging in indirect but productive negotiations with the U.S. and had already said they didn’t intend to pursue a nuclear weapons program before Trump launched the unprovoked U.S.-Israeli war effort against the country.

As talks for ending the war have stalled in recent weeks, Trump has continued to suggest that he may amp up attacks on Iran, at times using genocidal language. In a recent Time magazine interview, Trump said he might seek to “annihilate” the country in the coming weeks, showing little concern for civilians when pressed by interviewers.

In the same interview, Trump complained that Americans are only upset about him breaking his initial promise that the war would last weeks rather than months because the press keeps highlighting that point. Trump tried to justify breaking that pledge by claiming he had new objectives for the war.

Notably, Trump’s decision to launch an attack against Iran while negotiations were ongoing in late February could push more countries around the globe to pursue nuclear weapons, experts have pointed out.

Polling indicates that most Americans are opposed to the war continuing beyond its seventh month. According to an Economist/YouGov survey from last month, 63 percent of Americans want the war to end as soon as possible, with only 15 percent disagreeing.

Other data suggests that Trump is wrong when he implies the media is to blame for negative attitudes about the war. Indeed, a majority of Americans were opposed to the conflict at its very start, with polling in March showing 56 percent opposed to the war and only 36 percent supporting it.

We now have three full months of data since Google changed its search to feature AI results. The numbers are worse than we anticipated. Overall readership that comes to Truthout through Google is down 54 percent against last year. The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

The only way we can keep publishing is with strong reader support. We are asking you to start a monthly donation to Truthout today — anything you can do, whether $5 or $25, makes a difference.

author: Unknown
title: Director Ismail Güneş: Peace should be at the heart of cinema and art - Part Two
content:
Director Ismail Güneş spoke to ANF not only about his own cinema, but also about the current state of political cinema in Turkey and the role of art in the peace process.


Part one of this interview can be read

here

. 


Ismail Güneş' latest movie,

One of the Unplastered Houses,

focuses on the story of a father and mother who, because they are poor, do not want their son to remain in conflict zones. He said: “I made this film not to repeat the artificial rhetoric of heroism produced by those in power or clichéd political slogans, but to tell the raw and naked reality of people waging their own quiet struggle for existence far from front lines and macro politics, in a stagnant town in Anatolia—in other words, the invisible philosophical tragedy of the ‘unplastered houses.’ Because while the themes of homeland and life are abstract concepts on ideological platforms, inside those homes in the grip of poverty they turn into a ruthless ontological contradiction between a child’s life and the family’s bread.


The mother figure before us is the purest manifestation on earth of universal compassion and the instinct to ‘keep alive’; while the desperate father figure, who wants his son to remain in the military and complete his service so that the money he earns there can sustain the family, is a disturbing mirror of how the capitalist system and deprivation subject human dignity and a father’s conscience to a radical test.


The father does not desire his son’s death; on the contrary, while being crushed beneath the vertical pressures of life, he takes refuge in the illusion that his son will be safe within a military order and in the economic relief that this order will provide.”


The director continued: “Therefore, with this film, I saw it as a philosophical moral responsibility to shake the sanitized images of heroism presented by the system or media on glittering screens; to pull the audience away from the comfort of heroic rhetoric and confront them with the silent rupture of a human being trapped between poverty, conscience, and the desire to survive—in other words, with the true sociological cost of war and deprivation.


We can elaborate on this under three headings.


The transformation of money into an ontological threat: On a philosophical level, money is one of the most powerful instruments in the modern world for mechanizing human relationships, commodifying values, and alienating individuals from their own essence. In the film, the bag full of money is not merely a means of economic relief; in the father’s subconscious, it is the ‘price of the soul’ that he has surrendered to the system in exchange for his son’s life, existence, and future. The fact that the bag is accidentally found in a bank, a place regarded as a temple of capitalism, is a manifestation of the enormous suppressed sense of guilt within the father’s soul.


The father needs that money, but deep down he knows of its connection to his son’s blood and the risk of death, so the bag becomes an impossibly heavy burden to carry in his conscience, a philosophical curse.


The moral rupture that begins when the bag is lost: The moment the bag scatters and is lost on a snowy night is the turning point at which the character’s mask falls away and his inner tragedy becomes exposed. When the money disappears, the false balance between the father’s helplessness in the face of poverty and his instinctive love for his son collapses. Karl Marx’s notion of ‘things enslaving human beings’ is reversed here: when the money disappears, the father does not merely suffer a material loss; the refuge he had obtained at the cost of keeping his son in danger has vanished, leaving him completely exposed to his own moral choice and guilt.


The search for money is actually a session of searching for fatherhood dignity, social respect, and, most importantly, inner peace that the father has lost.


The naked truth of the ‘Unplastered House’ and purification (Catharsis): Through the image of the nylon bag, I wanted to show the audience the most dramatic contradiction of Anatolia’s voiceless poverty. Money, which in wealthy homes is merely a number, has the tragic weight of something measured against the length of a child’s life in an ‘unplastered house.’ Storing the money in a tangible nylon bag symbolizes the raw, fragile nature of poverty, stripped of aestheticization. The tension the father experiences around the bag makes the audience ask: What remains of a …

title: South Kurdistan after the Coalition: Kurdish national unity is crucial
content:
The mission of the International Coalition against ISIS in Iraq officially ended on 30 September after 12 years. The date marked not only the end of a military mission, but also the conclusion of the US military presence that had continued since the 2003 invasion and of the air defence system from which South Kurdistan (Bashur) had indirectly benefited. The withdrawal, announced by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Zeydi, was welcomed as a victory in Baghdad and among Iran-aligned Shia groups, while it has been met with concern in Southern Kurdistan and among Sunni communities.


South Kurdistan, which has been targeted by more than a thousand drone and ballistic missile attacks since the US-Israel-Iran war began on 28 February, is entering a new period without air defences. Peshmerga forces have been unified on paper but remain affiliated with the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) on the ground. The Coalition’s financial support for the Peshmerga has also ended. Twenty-three months after the elections, a government has still not been formed in the Kurdistan Region.


The weakness of a common political will has now been compounded by the reality of a Kurdistan Region increasingly exposed to attacks.


23 years from invasion to withdrawal


US forces entered Iraq in 2003 to overthrow Saddam Hussein’s regime. US troop numbers peaked at 170,000, and approximately 4,500 US soldiers were killed. The US withdrew from the country in 2011 but returned in 2014 following the rise of ISIS. The International Coalition against ISIS was established that same year, and its forces were deployed to the country at the formal invitation of the Iraqi government.


In recent years, around 2,500 US troops have been stationed in Iraq, mainly in Erbil (Hewlêr) and near Baghdad Airport. Their number stood at around 2,000 in July before falling to several hundred as the phased withdrawal proceeded. As major bases across Iraq were evacuated, hundreds of troops and air defence systems were concentrated around Erbil. The withdrawal has seen hundreds of troops and military equipment redeployed to Jordan and other countries in the region.


The timetable for the withdrawal was finalised following Prime Minister Zeydi’s first visit to Washington in July, where he met US President Donald Trump.


Security, economic and political gaps in the Kurdistan Region


The most tangible impact of the withdrawal on Southern Kurdistan has emerged in air defence. Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Araji said the withdrawal also covered defence systems in the Kurdistan Region, explaining that the process was being carried out under an agreement signed between the previous government and the Coalition: “The US side has also made it clear that it is ready to implement the agreement and withdraw within the agreed timeframe. This withdrawal covers all defence forces and systems previously agreed upon.”


As a result, air defence systems deployed particularly in and around Erbil, including Patriot batteries and C-RAM systems, were also removed from the region.


Although Southern Kurdistan was not a party to the war between the US/Israel and Iran that began on 28 February 2026, it became one of the regions most heavily targeted by attacks. According to Community Peacemaker Teams (CPT), 196 drone and missile attacks struck the region between the beginning of the war and 8 March. Forty-three of these targeted bases belonging to Kurdish parties from Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat). The targets also included Erbil International Airport and the 70th Forces Command in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî).


CPT also recorded 751 attacks during the three months between 28 February and 28 May, in which 22 people were killed and 112 others injured.


At the end of July, the Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Region said the number of attacks had exceeded 900, with 30 people killed and 140 injured. Figures released by the Peshmerga Ministry at the end of September put the number of drone and ballistic missile attacks at more than 1,000.


Most attacks targeting Erbil had been intercepted by US air defence systems deployed to protect American assets, while Sulaymaniyah did not have comparable protection.


The Peshmerga Ministry described the US withdrawal at such a critical time, without another air defence system being put in place, as “concerning”. The ministry recalled that the Kurdistan Region’s airspace formed part of Iraqi airspace and said: “The federal …

title: Journalist Hemrînî: Baghdad seeks a model for solution in Shengal
content:
The withdrawal of US and International Coalition forces from Iraq, Baghdad’s efforts to bring armed groups under state control and strengthen the central army are reshaping the country’s security architecture. As Iraq seeks a new security balance, Shengal, which developed its own defense and governance mechanisms in the wake of DAESH attacks, has emerged as one of the key issues in this transformation.


The status of Shengal, the security of the Yazidis and the future of their self-defence forces are closely tied not only to Baghdad’s evolving security policies but also to the balance of power among regional actors. Journalist Hîwa Hemrînî said the demands of the Yazidis went beyond administrative or political arrangements: “The Yazidis are demanding a system that will protect their existence and enable them to develop it.”


Hemrînî stressed that Shengal’s future must be addressed on the basis of a solution that guarantees the continued existence of the Yazidis. He spoke to ANF about the talks between Shengal and Baghdad, the demands of the Yazidis, negotiations between Ankara and Baghdad over Bashiqa, and Iraq’s evolving security architecture.


Recent talks between Shengal and Baghdad, particularly the 11 September meeting between Prime Minister Ali Zeydi, the YBŞ and Yazidi representatives, appear to mark a new phase for Shengal’s future. What concrete issues were agreed upon during these talks?


To properly assess the content and outcome of the meeting you mentioned, two fundamental points need to be recalled. First, the Yazidi community has long sought to develop democratic negotiations with Baghdad. Dozens of meetings were held with governments preceding the Ali Zeydi government, and numerous proposals for a solution were presented. The Iraqi government, however, consistently treated Shengal’s status and the existential issues facing the Yazidi community as a military and intelligence matter. It regarded an ancient community such as the Yazidis as a “security problem”.


Pressure and blackmail by the Turkish state and the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) against the Iraqi central government further deepened this approach. We are now seeing a partial shift in this policy, which has developed under the influence of the “Peace and Democratic Society Process” initiated by Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan.


Second, the Baghdad-Shengal talks are important not only for Shengal’s future but also for Baghdad’s. Iraq is being restructured under the Ali Zeydi government, and one of the most critical issues facing the government is the presence of non-state armed groups. Iraq has yet to develop a model for resolving this issue, and the matter remains open-ended. This is precisely where the Baghdad-Shengal talks take on greater significance: will Shengal produce a model for a solution, or a model for conflict? Baghdad essentially wants to develop a model for a solution and present it to the whole of Iraq. According to information we have obtained, Prime Minister Ali Zeydi also expressed this during his latest meeting with the Shengal delegation.


The central issue at the meeting was undoubtedly the status and future of the Yazidi defence forces in Shengal, namely the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ), Shengal Women’s Units (YJŞ) and Êzidxan Asayish forces. Before the meeting with Ali Zeydi, the Shengal delegation held several days of talks with Iraq’s security bureaucracy. The final meeting with the prime minister indicated that this series of talks had produced a positive outcome.


The Shengal delegation maintained that a self-defence force was essential to protect the social existence of the Yazidis and that this force should be positioned in a way that enables it to protect the Yazidi community, while a joint mechanism could also be developed with the Iraqi army. The meeting concluded without any serious objection from the Iraqi side to this position. It was jointly agreed that the details of how Shengal’s self-defence forces would be integrated with the Iraqi army would be determined through fieldwork carried out by a joint committee.


Does integration in Shengal mean incorporating the YBŞ and YJŞ into Iraqi security institutions while preserving their own command and organisational structures, or is individual incorporation into Iraqi security institutions envisaged?


Democratic integration has a different and particular meaning for Shengal compared with other areas, as the Yazidi community frequently …

title: JINNEWS: 27 women and 6 children were murdered in September
content:
According to the September report compiled by JINNEWS, at least 27 women and 6 children were murdered, while 10 women and 6 children died under suspicious circumstances.


Twelve of the women were murdered by their spouses, 3 by men they were in the process of divorcing, 4 by men they had divorced, 1 by a man they had reportedly previously been in a relationship with, 1 by a family member, 1 by her son-in-law, 1 by the man her sister was married to, and 1 by her tenant. The relationship between 3 of the women and the perpetrators has not been clarified.


The cities where the women were murdered were: “3 in Manisa, 2 in Amed (Diyarbakır), 2 in Antalya, 2 in Sakarya, 1 in Adana, 1 in Ankara, 1 in Çorum, 1 in Denizli, 1 in Antep (Dîlok), 1 in Batman (Êlih), 1 in Hatay, 1 in Isparta, 1 in Istanbul, 1 in Kocaeli, 1 in Konya, 1 in Kütahya, 1 in Maraş, 1 in Mersin, 1 in Muğla, 1 in Osmaniye, 1 in Tekirdağ, and 1 woman in Elazığ (Xarpêt).”

author: Unknown
title: Activist allowed final meeting with his mother has been executed in Iran
content:
In a statement posted on social media, Sepahi’s lawyer, Şehrzad Şehbazi, announced that her client had been executed and said, “I will not forget him.”


Sepahi was allowed to meet with his mother, Somaya Afşar, who is also imprisoned, for the last time at Dastgerd Prison on Sunday, October 4 — in other words, shortly before his execution.


Arrests and executions in the country are increasing in connection with the protests that took place at the beginning of the year.


According to the NGOs Iran Human Rights and Together Against the Death Penalty, Iran executed at least 1,639 people in 2025. This figure was described as the highest number recorded since 1989.


According to Amnesty International, Iran is the country with the second-highest number of executions, after China.

author: Unknown
title: Hıdır Öztürk demands investigation into the murder of his daughter Ayten in 1992
content:
Thirty-four years after the abduction, torture and killing of Ayten Öztürk, her father, Hıdır Öztürk, is calling for the case, which was closed due to the statute of limitations, to be reopened. Particularly at a time when peace and a resolution of the Kurdish question are being discussed, the state must investigate and clarify the crimes of the past, Öztürk said.


His daughter’s case is among the grave human rights violations of the 1990s in Northern Kurdistan, when people were abducted, forcibly disappeared and extrajudicially executed by state and paramilitary structures. According to the Human Rights Association (İHD), at least 1,388 people disappeared while in state custody between 1980 and 2001.


Ayten Öztürk’s eyes were gouged out


Ayten Öztürk was 27 years old and worked at a state-owned flour factory in the district of Mazgirt in Dersim (Tunceli) province. On the evening of July 27, 1992, witnesses saw four men drag her into a white Land Rover and abduct her after she left work. Twelve days later, on August 8, her body was found near Kartaltepe in Elazığ. She had been hastily buried, with one hand protruding from the ground.


Öztürk had been so severely tortured and mutilated that her family was able to identify her only by her clothing. Among other injuries, her eyes had been gouged out. Nevertheless, no comprehensive autopsy was carried out, the signs of torture were not adequately documented, and the investigation was closed.


“Yeşil” had previously interrogated the family


The abduction had been preceded by threats against the family. Hıdır Öztürk, who at the time was himself a civil servant in the provincial administration, had been summoned together with his daughters on the orders of then-Gendarmerie Commander Mustafa Sabri Yazgankıran. There, the sisters were questioned by a man who recorded their personal details. It later emerged that the man was Mahmut Yıldırım, known by the codename “Yeşil.” The intelligence operative has been linked to numerous political killings and abductions during the 1990s.


Two of Ayten Öztürk’s sisters were subsequently transferred as a punitive measure to posts in western Turkey. Ayten remained in Dersim. A few weeks later, she was abducted. Later statements from individuals associated with the military intelligence organization JITEM strengthened suspicions that the operation had been organized by state actors. Former JITEM commander Cem Ersever and former intelligence operative Abdülkadir Aygan publicly stated that Öztürk had been abducted by Mahmut Yıldırım and his team. They said a vehicle provided by the emergency rule administration at the time had been used in the operation.


According to their accounts, the young woman was taken to a JITEM interrogation center in Amed (Diyarbakır), where she was tortured and eventually executed. Although these statements became public, they did not result in those responsible being subjected to penalty.


Constitutional Court found a violation of the right to life


After decades of unsuccessful efforts to obtain justice, Ayten Öztürk’s family applied to Turkey’s Constitutional Court in 2013. On April 21, 2016, the court found a violation of the right to life, citing in particular the failure to adequately establish the facts and the shortcomings in the investigation. The ruling ultimately led to criminal proceedings being opened.


The case was later merged with the proceedings concerning the killing of Kurdish intellectual Musa Anter. Nevertheless, no one was convicted. On September 21, 2022, the proceedings concerning the abduction and killing of Ayten Öztürk, like those in the Anter case, were also dismissed on statute-of-limitations grounds. Decades of delayed and inadequate efforts to investigate the case thus once again ended in impunity.


Öztürk: Our only wish is for the truth to be uncovered


Hıdır Öztürk is now calling for the case to be revisited in light of the current political developments. He said he requested an appointment with Turkish Justice Minister Akın Gürlek on August 10 but has yet to receive a response. His demand concerns not only his own daughter, but also the many unresolved killings and cases of enforced disappearance involving state actors.


“Our wish, our only wish as grieving fathers and mothers, is for the unresolved killings to be investigated and clarified during this period of peace. We hope that the interior minister and the justice minister will grant us an appointment, listen to …

author: Unknown
title: Iran steps up military presence in Eastern Kurdistan
content:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has deployed heavy military equipment in the Şaho Mountains near Rewanser in Eastern Kurdistan and closed parts of the region to civilians. At the same time, artillery fire is targeting mountain ridges under the pretext of a military exercise.


According to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN), citing a resident of a village at the foot of the Şaho Mountains, the Revolutionary Guards have deployed a convoy carrying heavy military equipment to the region in recent days.


Residents were informed through village councils that certain areas of the Şaho Mountains are off-limits until October 7. According to a notice issued by the Şiwankar village council, the restrictions apply to the mountain ridges stretching from Bedrawa through Pir-Xidir to the Goliçî Pass. The area around Pir-Xidir, among others, is being subjected to artillery fire.


The Şaho Mountains and the adjacent Kosalan Mountains were officially designated as a protected area by Iran’s Supreme Environmental Council in 2009. Nevertheless, the Revolutionary Guards have been expanding their military infrastructure there for years. At the end of August, the Revolutionary Guards heavily shelled the ridges of the Şaho Mountains in the Kamyaran area with artillery. Footage published by the KHRN subsequently documented extensive fires across the mountainous area.


According to environmental activists, the Revolutionary Guards have been establishing military bases in the Şaho-Kosalan protected area since 2007 under the pretext of combating Kurdish opposition forces. Parts of the forests and grazing lands have reportedly been destroyed during the construction of the bases and military access roads. The activists also say that vegetation and pastureland around some military posts are deliberately set on fire. The Revolutionary Guards justify this by saying they aim to prevent Kurdish forces from using the vegetation as cover for attacks.

author: Unknown
title: ISIS member arrested in Sulaymaniyah
content:
Counter-terrorism units have arrested a wanted member of the “Islamic State” (ISIS) in Sulaymaniyah. The man is said to have moved to Sulaymaniyah following the military collapse of ISIS and continued his activities for the organization there.


According to the Kurdish Counter-Terrorism Group Lexoman-Parastin (CTG), the arrest followed an extended period of surveillance and the analysis of detailed intelligence. The detainee reportedly belonged to a unit designated by ISIS as the “210th Division.”


Following the collapse of the jihadist group, the man settled in Sulaymaniyah. According to the security forces, however, he remained active as an ISIS member within the province until he was tracked down and arrested by counter-terrorism units.


His father had also held senior positions within ISIS. He initially served as commander of a military unit in the so-called “North Baghdad Province” and was later appointed ISIS “governor” of Fallujah. He was killed in an airstrike in the Abu Ghraib district.


A brother of the detainee, who was also a member of ISIS, was killed in the an-Nibāʿī area northwest of Baghdad, according to the security forces. No further information was provided about the detainee’s identity or his specific activities for ISIS in Sulaymaniyah.

author: Unknown
title: Syrian Federation for Human Rights calls for constitutional right to mother-tongue education
content:
The Syrian Federation for Human Rights Organizations and Bodies has called for the linguistic and cultural rights of all communities in Syria to be guaranteed by law and the constitution. The right to education in one’s mother tongue, it said, must not depend on temporary political or administrative decisions.


In a statement issued by its Executive Council, the federation described linguistic and cultural diversity as an integral part of fundamental human rights. Language, it said, is directly linked to identity and culture, the right to education, and equal participation in social life. The rights of Kurds, Syriacs, Armenians, Circassians and other communities must therefore be protected, the federation underlined.


Mother-tongue education does not mean division


According to the federation, the recognition of different languages does not contradict either Syria’s unity or the status of Arabic as the official language. The existence of an official state language must not be used as a justification for excluding other languages from education, culture and social life, it said.


“Protecting and learning one’s mother tongue means neither division nor isolation. On the contrary, it can strengthen a sense of belonging, participation and equality when the shared rights of all citizens are respected. Multilingual education can help preserve cultural diversity, promote mutual understanding and strengthen social coexistence.”


Legal recognition instead of temporary decisions


The federation referred to the 2025 Constitutional Declaration, which establishes Arabic as the official language while also recognizing the cultural diversity of Syrian society and the linguistic and cultural rights of the population. Decision No. 13 of 2026 also designates Kurdish as a national language and provides for Kurdish-language instruction in state schools, particularly in predominantly Kurdish areas. However, implementation by the Syrian Ministry of Education falls far short of the right to mother-tongue education: Kurdish is not recognized as a language of instruction, but is permitted only as a school subject and limited to three hours per week.


Against this backdrop, the human rights federation called for linguistic rights that have already been won not to be rolled back through new education policies. The right to mother-tongue education must be permanently guaranteed by law and the constitution, it demanded.


Recognition must be implemented in practice


The statement continued: “Kurdish, Syriac and Assyrian must be recognized as national languages, and corresponding educational opportunities must be established. Formal recognition alone is not sufficient. Curricula, textbooks and teaching materials must be developed, along with the training of qualified teachers.”


At the same time, the statement added, laws and administrative regulations that discriminate against people on the basis of their language or cultural and national identity must be reviewed. The federation called for institutional mechanisms to monitor the implementation of linguistic rights and ensure their application within the education system. “Changes to the language of instruction must not result in students having to interrupt their education or facing greater barriers to accessing education,” it noted.


“Protecting one’s mother tongue is not a privilege, but part of protecting identity and culture, the right to education, and the principles of equality and non-discrimination,” the statement said.


“For Syria to have a future based on citizenship rights, equality and human rights, all communities must be guaranteed the right to learn their languages, use them in education and pass them on to future generations,” the statement concluded.

author: Unknown
title: Baluken: Öcalan’s status is linked to the status of the Kurdish people
content:
Kurdish politician Idris Baluken has warned against viewing the peace and democratic society process solely through the lens of the current balance of power in Turkey. Speaking at an event in Besançon, France, he said the Kurdish question must be considered in the context of the restructuring of the Middle East and the shifting balance of power in the region.


Baluken referred to dialogue and negotiation efforts over the past decades and emphasized that the search for a political solution is by no means new: “The leadership of the Kurdish people and the Kurdish movement was already seeking an interlocutor 30 years ago in order to resolve this issue and intervene in the course of developments during this historic period,” the former HDP MP said, referring to Abdullah Öcalan.


“The issue goes far beyond the current government”


Baluken described the mistrust toward the Turkish government and criticism of President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, the AKP and the position of MHP Chair Devlet Bahçeli as largely justified. However, he said that focusing solely on these actors is not sufficient to assess the current developments.


“The issue goes far beyond Erdoğan, Bahçeli, the AKP or the MHP. It goes far beyond the current political government in Turkey.”


The decisive factor, he said, is the restructuring of the Middle East. “At a time when regional powers are repositioning themselves, the Kurdish side seeks to overcome the factors that have weakened its position and enabled attacks against it. As a people numbering 50 to 60 million, Kurds must take their place at the political negotiating table. A Kurdish reality that no longer fits within the narrow organizational confines of the past has entered the stage of history. In the emerging balance of power, the aim is to act as a political subject and a force capable of shaping developments,” Baluken said.


"Kurdish rights must be guaranteed by law and the constitution"


According to Baluken, a lasting solution is inseparable from the recognition of Kurdish rights: “Just as this problem was created by denying the rights of the Kurdish people for a hundred years, it must be resolved in the new century by recognizing those rights and guaranteeing them both legally and constitutionally.”


The Kurdish side, he said, does not want to prolong the current process unnecessarily, but seeks to bring it to a lasting peace. To achieve this, he added, the political counterpart must now also take the necessary steps.


“Öcalan’s status is linked to the status of the Kurdish people”


Baluken pointed out that the legal status of Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan, who is imprisoned on the Turkish prison island of Imrali, plays a key role. He rejected attempts to treat Öcalan’s situation as an individual matter, saying: “If Mr. Öcalan’s status on Imrali is placed on a legal footing, this will at the same time amount to legal recognition of the status of the Kurdish people, which has been denied for a hundred years.”


During the 2013–2015 resolution process, Baluken was among the key politicians involved in the dialogue with the Turkish state. He recalled that Öcalan’s position had already been treated at the time as an important component of a resolution in talks with both the government and the opposition. Today, however, Öcalan’s status is sometimes portrayed as though it concerned him alone, Baluken said. He stressed that Öcalan represents the largest politically and organizationally structured Kurdish force across all four parts of Kurdistan.


Four goals for the new phase


For the coming phase, Baluken identified four fundamental goals of the Kurdish movement: strategic renewal, ideological reorientation, organizational restructuring and lasting peace. The movement, he said, can achieve the first three objectives through its own efforts. “Lasting peace, however, also depends on steps taken by the state. The state must not obstruct the path toward a political resolution.”


Warning of plans for attacks


Baluken also linked the urgency of a political resolution to the dangers arising from the current restructuring of the Middle East. He said a process aimed at eliminating non-state forces was underway in the region. “While this process is underway, very serious plans for massacres targeting the most highly organized structures of the Kurdish movement are on the table.”


The Kurds, he said, have maintained their existence through decades of resistance. “The task now is to secure an …

title: Kaşif Kozinoğlu soruşturması: Mezarından alınan örnekler geri konuldu
content:
Silivri Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığının talebi üzerine 2011 yılında hayatını kaybeden eski MİT görevlisi Kaşif Kozinoğlu'nun kesin ölüm sebebinin ve ölümünde üçüncü kişilerin müdahalesi bulunup bulunmadığının belirlenmesi amacıyla alınan feth-i kabir kararı kapsamında, mezardan alınan örneklerin incelenmesi tamamlandı.

Örnekler, Kozinoğlu'nun mezarının bulunduğu Ümraniye'deki Kocatepe Mezarlığına getirilerek, uzman heyetin çalışmasıyla defnedildi. Ardından mezar kapatıldı.

Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, sosyal hesabından Kozinoğlu'nun ölümüne ilişkin soruşturmaya yönelik açıklama yapmıştı.

Bakan Gürlek, Faili Meçhul Suçları Araştırma Daire Başkanlığınca dosyanın yeniden incelendiğini belirterek yeni soruşturma kapsamında gizlilik kararı alındığını, özel bir soruşturma ekibi oluşturularak olayın tüm yönleriyle yeniden aydınlatılmasına yönelik kapsamlı çalışmalara başlandığını ifade etmişti.

Soruşturmadaki ilk operasyonda olay tarihinde ceza infaz kurumunda görev yapan 10 kişi gözaltına alınmış, 1 kişinin ise “FETÖ” kapsamında firari olarak yurt dışında bulunduğu tespit edilmişti. Gözaltına alınan 10 kişiden 1'i tutuklanmış, 7'si adli kontrol şartıyla olmak üzere 9'u serbest bırakılmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Natalia Viana
title: Flávio Bolsonaro e o risco de um presidente com esqueletos no armário
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui.


O Brasil que sai do primeiro turno está flertando com uma crise institucional permanente. Flávio Bolsonaro teve 2,2 milhões de votos a mais que Lula, ficando em 47% dos votos versus 45,1% do atual presidente.

Se eleito, Flávio teria uma bancada de 28 nomes no Senado e 121 na Câmara dos Deputados apenas do PL, seu partido, um desempenho histórico. 


Mas

Flávio Bolsonaro é um candidato com muitos esqueletos no armário. Está enredado em vários escândalos e corrupção

 dos quais, hoje, conseguimos ter apenas um vislumbre, mas que vão se aprofundar nos próximos meses. E

isso levará necessariamente a um governo maculado por revelações do seu primeiro ao seu último dia. 


A jornalista Flávia de Oliveira

chamou

 a atenção para o fato de que,

por conta da ação de


André Mendonça


de manter sigilo do caso Master, Flávio é o único candidato investigado por corrupção, lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas – e o eleitor não foi informado disso a tempo. 


Mesmo que você esteja acompanhando as notícias, é possível que tenha perdido as revelações mais recentes.  


Pois vamos a elas. 


Primeiro, as rachadinhas, esquema de desvio de verba pública dos mandatos de Jair Bolsonaro e seus filhos através de saques em dinheiro vivo de funcionários, que depois repassavam à família, das quais Flávio sempre foi figura central.

 O resultado foi demonstrado há alguns anos pelos jornalistas Juliana Dal Piva e Thiago Herdy: 51 imóveis dos Bolsonaro foram pagos parcialmente em dinheiro vivo. O processo judicial das rachadinhas foi extinto pelo STJ, que questionou a quebra de sigilo fiscal, mas as evidências existem e podem gerar novas investigações.  


Segundo, vamos ao caso Master. Ainda hoje sabe-se apenas parcialmente sobre a relação entre Flávio e Daniel Vorcaro. Além do financiamento generoso do filme


Dark Horse


e dos muitos diálogos resgatados do celular de Vorcaro

, não sabemos qual o valor real dos depósitos, que tipo de dinheiro criminoso foi usado para o pagamento pela empresa Entre Investimentos, que

lavava

 inclusive dinheiro para o crime organizado, e nem para que fim o dinheiro foi usado nos EUA.

Não se sabe, ainda, que outros favores e apoios foram prestados pelo banqueiro para Flávio – com quem ele tinha uma relação de amizade

,

segundo demonstram os diálogos completos publicados pela revista


piauí

: são 50 mensagens de Flávio, 46 de Vorcaro e 14 ligações – oito delas atendidas.

ᒫᓃᐸᓗᒃᑐᑦ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᑐᑦ 22 ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᕐᕕᖕᓂ ᒫᓂ ᑭᕙᓪᓕᖅᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᕿᑎᕐᒥᐅᓂ ᐅᓪᓛᕈᒻᒥᑕᖅᑎᑕᐅᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᐊᖅᑐᑦ ᐊᑭᖃᙱᑦᑐᓂ ᑎᑭᓪᓗᒍ 2031, ᖁᔭᓐᓇᒦ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪ ᐅᔭᕋᒃᓯᐅᕐᕕᒃ ᑐᓂᓚᐅᕐᑕᖓᓐᓂ $5 ᒥᓕᐊᓐ ᑕᓚᐃ.


ᐅᓇ ᐅᓪᓛᕈᒻᒥᑕᖅᑎᑦᑎᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᖅ, ᑕᐃᔭᐅᓯᒪᖕᒥᔪᖅ ᐃᓄᙳᐃᓂᖅ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᖅ, ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᖅ ᐅᓪᓛᕈᒻᒥᑕᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ, ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᓕᕆᔨᓄᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᖅᑐᓂ ᓂᕿᖃᙱᓗᐊᔭᓐᓂᕐᒥ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ.


“ᑕᑯᓯᒪᒐᑦᑕ ᐅᓇ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᖑᔪᖅ ᐱᒻᒪᕆᐅᓂᖓᓂ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓄᑦ, ᐃᓚᒌᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓄᑦ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᒫᒃ-ᐅᓕᕕᐃ ᕙᓵᓐ, ᐊᐅᓚᑎᔨᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐊᒡᓂᑯ ᐄᒍᓪ ᒥᓕᐊᑏᓐ ᒎᓗᒧᑦ ᐅᔭᕋᒃᓯᐅᖅᕕᒃᒥ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 23-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᐅᖃᓪᓚᒃᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑭᕙᓪᓕᖅᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᓄᑦ ᓴᖅᑭᔮᖅᑎᑦᑎᔪᑦ ᑲᑎᖃᑎᒌᒃᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ.

author: dev
title: Les leçons des lycéens en révolte
content:
Leçon surprise

. C'était la surprise de la rentrée, que personne n'avait vu venir et encore moins prédit. Alors que tout le monde semblait résigné à attendre les prochaines élections du président-monarque pour espérer un changement, les lycéens ont fait irruption sur le devant de la scène et ébranlé toutes les agendas politiques. Partie de quelques lycées de la banlieue parisienne, la révolte s'est rapidement diffusée dans toute la France. Sans aucune organisation dirigeante, sans un parti ou un syndicat à la manœuvre. Juste des groupes de lycéens qui s'auto-organisent, qui bloquent l'entrée de leur école et qui diffusent l'information autour d'eux et sur les réseaux sociaux. Signe que sous les cendres des braises commençaient à se raviver et n'attendaient qu'une étincelle pour déclencher l'incendie.


Une révolte spontanée, imprévisible et soudaine, comme toutes les révoltes. Comme pour l'émergence du mouvement des Gilets Jaunes, à l'automne 2018, et tant d'autres révoltes sociales auparavant. En cet automne 2026, toute l'attention politique semblait devoir se focaliser, obligatoirement, sur les prochaines élections présidentielles et encore une fois réduire les aspirations de changement au triste choix du bulletin de vote, à la délégation à autrui du pouvoir sur son propre destin.


Déjouant tout pronostic, se jouant avec insouciance du calendrier électoral, les jeunes lycéens ont voulu dire, d'abord et simplement, qu'ils existaient, que leur vie présente et future avait de la valeur. Même si, mineurs, ils n'avaient pas droit de vote et aucune valeur ajoutée pour les partis politiques.


Des raisons de se révolter ils en avaient. Celles qui ont été mises en avant, relayées par les syndicats lycéens, dénonçaient des classes surchargées, des emplois du temps saucissonnés et contraignants, des enseignants non remplacés, des édifices scolaires vétustes et insalubres. Ils décriaient aussi la vexation et l'incongruité de l'interdiction du portable à l'école, alors que leurs professeurs comme les parlementaires qui avaient voté cette interdiction étaient tout le temps scotchés à leur téléphone. Traités comme des gamins qu'il fallait punir et discipliner, alors qu'ils étaient jeunes adultes et ne voulaient pas se résigner à un avenir sombre et indésirable.


De toute évidence, derrière les raisons structurelles du manque de moyens et de désinvestissement de l'Etat pour l'Education nationale, il y a des critiques plus profondes. Au fond la dénonciation du système scolaire d'une soi-disant République qui, sous couvert d'une égalité formelle, ne fait que reproduire et entretenir les privilèges et les discriminations de classe et de « race ».


Leçon de sociologie

. Ce qui apparait tout à fait nouveau dans l'histoire des révoltes des étudiants, de 1968 à nos jours, c'est que le mouvement de l'automne 2026 n'est pas portée par des étudiants du centre-ville, par des rejetons de la bourgeoisie déviant (provisoirement) de leur classe sociale, mais par des lycéens des quartiers populaires. D'ailleurs les plus mobilisés dans la lutte paraissent les élèves des lycées professionnels, déjà orientés vers le travail et exclus à l'avance des études supérieurs. Aussi, les images des blocages montrent que, parmi les lycéens en révolte, nombreux ont la peau noire ou basanée. Des jeunes français, bien entendu, correspondant à cette nouvelle France qui, à défaut d'être reconnue et appréciée par des Blancs suprémacistes (sauf, à la marge, pour les performances des joueurs du PSG et de l'équipe nationale de foot) représente son histoire et son devenir.


C'est très probablement pour ça que l'Etat et son gouvernement ont pris la décision, dès les premiers blocages, de ne pas écouter la parole, les doléances, les revendications des lycéens en lutte, mais de les réprimer immédiatement, brutalement. C'est tu, caché, surtout pas affiché clairement, mais comment ne pas penser que derrière la décision (nullement nécessaire) de faire donner tout de suite la matraque en réponse aux revendications lycéennes, il y a un racisme profond incarné par le Ministre-Préfet de police et tant de policiers à ses ordres ? Que comme pour Éric Zemmour et bien d'autres descendants de colons d'Oran, Laurent Nuñez soit habité par des rancœurs et une haine viscérale à l'égard des Arabes et des Musulmans ? Que les flics habitués à faire la chasse aux jeunes arabes et noirs des cités, sous prétexte de lutte contre la drogue, ne se croient pas légitimés à taper sur des …

author: dev
title: Affaire Budapest : « Pas une extradition de plus »
content:
Suite de l'affaire Budapest

 [

1

]

. Alors que la cours de cassation vient de valider l'extradition de Gino vers l'Allemagne et que la Hongrie a définitivement condamné l'antifasciste allemande Maja à 7 années d'emprisonnement, la cour d'appel de Paris devra statuer ce 7 octobre sur l'extradition de Zaid A. vers la Hongrie. Après des mois de procédure, marqués par plusieurs renvois, cette audience – la dernière de plaidoirie – est déterminante pour Zaid.


On doit refuser cette idée de coupable ou d'innocent : ce sont des personnes qui se posent comme résistant

·

e

·

s.


Zero Calcare


Si j'avais 30 ans ou 40 ans de moins, j'aurais probablement été aux côtés de Zaid et Gino. Des formes de résistances, de manifestations ou de contre-manifestations sont tout à fait nécessaires.


Robert Guédiguian


Enfant de réfugiés palestiniens vivant en Syrie, Zaid A. s'exile en Allemagne en 2014 à l'âge de 11 ans avec sa famille pour fuir le régime d'Assad et la guerre meurtrière qu'il livre contre le peuple syrien. En 2024, poursuivi par un mandat d'arrêt européen émis par la Hongrie dans le cadre de l'affaire dite « de Budapest », il se réfugie en France en espérant que celle-ci refuse son extradition comme elle l'avait fait pour Gino, un autre inculpé de l'affaire. Cependant, malgré ce précédent juridictionnel, il n'est pas sûr que la justice prenne la même décision. Dans ce cas, Zaid A. perdrait à nouveau la vie qu'il a construite activement depuis un an en France en s'engageant dans de nombreuses activités solidaires et associatives. Il risque en outre un procès inéquitable et des conditions de détention délétères en Hongrie.


En 2023, une vague de mesures répressives transfrontalières à l'encontre d'une vingtaine de personnes a été déclenchée : c'est ce qui a été appelé « l'affaire de Budapest ». La Hongrie les accuse d'avoir participé à des agressions contre des néonazis en marge du « Jour de l'honneur » à Budapest. Ce défilé annuel, rythmé par des saluts nazis, rassemble des nostalgiques du IIIᵉ Reich en uniforme SS. Tandis que le régime d'extrême droite de Viktor Orbán a autorisé et légitimé ces célébrations, une répression démesurée s'est abattue sur les militant

·

es venu

·

es de plusieurs pays pour protester contre cette glorification de l'idéologie nazie.


Mais la traque à laquelle se livre la Hongrie ne se cantonne pas à ce pays. L'affaire de Budapest est l'affaire d'une collaboration entre les États européens, qui prennent le relais à tour de rôle pour tenter de neutraliser les mouvements de contestation. On peut citer le cas de Gino : si la France a refusé son extradition vers la Hongrie en septembre 2025, elle vient de l'accepter vers l'Allemagne, où il sera jugé selon les mêmes accusations. À l'heure actuelle, il n'est pas possible de savoir si de là-bas il sera extradé vers la Hongrie. Par ailleurs, le cas de Maja T., une des autres inculpé

·

es, est emblématique à ce sujet : en 2024, alors qu'iel est incarcéré

·

e en Allemagne, iel est transféré

·

e illégalement en Hongrie par la police allemande quelques heures avant que la Cour constitutionnelle statue sur son recours et qu'elle ordonne de ne pas procéder au transfert. Cela n'a pas empêché la Hongrie de la placer à l'isolement depuis deux ans, sous vidéo surveillance continue, de la soumettre à des fouilles personnelles constantes, des humiliations transphobes, et de la condamner le 30 septembre 2026 à sept ans de prison

 [

2

]

.


Dans ce contexte de collaboration sélective, la répression des militants antifascistes semble primer sur la protection des droits fondamentaux. La France pourrait aujourd'hui accepter d'extrader Zaid en Hongrie sous prétexte du changement de gouvernement. Cependant, l'arrivée au pouvoir d'une droite conservatrice pro-européenne ne trompe personne. Les risques élevés d'atteinte aux droits humains n'ont pas disparu avec le changement de gouvernement et la surpopulation carcérale ainsi que les conditions de détention dégradantes ont largement été dénoncées par plusieurs rapports du comité Helsinki1

 [

3

]

 ainsi que du Comité européen pour la prévention de la torture (CPT) du Conseil de l'Europe. Les témoignages de Maja sur les violences qu'iel subit régulièrement encore aujourd'hui montrent que la situation n'a pas changé

 [

4

]

.


Le cas de Zaid présente une particularité majeure. Il n'est pas citoyen européen, il a perdu son statut de réfugié et sa demande de naturalisation a été suspendue suite à …
