title: Resoconto dell’udienza di sorveglianza speciale a Stefano
content:
Mercoledì 30 settembre si è tenuta una delle ultime udienze della fase dibattimentale riguardo alla richiesta di sorveglianza speciale a carico del nostro compagno Stefano.


Un’udienza lunga, nel corso della quale è avvenuto l’interrogatorio in cui prima l’avvocato e poi il pm hanno passato in rassegna i casi portati dalla questura a sostegno della richiesta. Già dalle scorse udienze, come in questa, è stata da subito evidente l’infondatezza di elementi a sostegno di una misura così grave. Pareva che a essere sotto processo non fossero infatti chissà quali azioni delittuose, ma le idee e la possibilità stessa di essere attivo politicamente. Nel corso dell’interrogatorio quello che è apparso è una persona che fin da giovane si è speso nelle lotte politiche, dai collettivi studenteschi, alla val di Susa fino ad arrivare ai movimenti per la Palestina. Eppure dietro le domande del pm la tesi appariva sempre la stessa, non potendo appellarsi a chissà quali fattispecie di reati, a essere criminalizzata diventa l’attività di speakeraggio. Secondo la questura infatti, fare un intervento in piazza spiegando le ragioni di un corteo, o esprimendo la propria rabbia in un momento concitato, sarebbe la prova che c’è un organizzatore che guida, che istiga e che burattinaia le persone. Una tesi secondo la quale le migliaia di persone che hanno partecipato alle piazze degli ultimi anni, non avrebbero una loro coscienza, o una loro volontà di stare ed esprimersi nelle piazze.

Un tentativo a dir poco ridicolo, che cerca di silenziare e nascondere la rabbia espressa in questi anni da tantissimi giovani, criminalizzando un singolo giovane come esempio e monito per tutti.

Niente di nuovo in una città teatro di processi come Sovrano, in cui anni di conflittualità sociale sono stati imputati a 16 compagni. Ma allora come adesso l’evidenza è una, che in quelle piazze eravamo tutti insieme, e che nessun compagno verrà lasciato solo nel combattere la criminalizzazione di un dissenso che ha ampiamente superato i limiti desiderati dalla questura. A dimostrarlo mercoledì c’era un’aula piena di persone, compagni e partecipanti alle mobilitazioni che non hanno nessuna intenzione di retrocedere di fronte a queste intimidazioni.

Mercoledì  14 ottobre saremo di nuovo in Tribunale per Sara, e fino alla fine di questi mesi di udienze daremo battaglia affinché una misura del genere non possa avere seguito.

author: Isabela Dias
title: Why a Bolsonaro biopic is at the center of Brazil’s presidential election
content:
This article is a partnership with

Mother Jones


In May,

 now-presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former Brazilian far-right President Jair Bolsonaro,

shared

 on his social media a “

leaked

” trailer for an upcoming biopic about his father. The “most anticipated movie of the year,” Flávio said then, would depict the story of a “true hero.” In the trailer, which had a “disclosure prohibited” watermark, a wig-wearing Jim Caviezel

—

the American Hollywood actor perhaps most famous for his role as Jesus in Mel Gibson’s 2004

The Passion of the Christ

—

plays

 Bolsonaro, who is

serving

 a 27-year prison sentence under house arrest for a failed

coup attempt

 after his 2022 electoral defeat. 


Director Cyrus Nowrasteh

described


Dark Horse

 as a “tense political thriller about power, media, and faith under fire.” The movie’s trailer, which centers on Bolsonaro’s first presidential run and rise to power in 2018, frames the ex-president as “the voice of the people” and a leader who “fought the system” that tried to silence him. It includes a dramatic reenactment of his

stabbing

 during the campaign. “IF YOU CARE ABOUT OUR ELECTIONS,” Caviezel, who is

also

known for the more recent

Sound of Freedom

,

posted

 on Instagram earlier this year, “watch my newest film coming out September 11, 2026!” 


The production company behind the movie advertised it on X.

“A trailer that circulated online was enough to put The Dark Horse at the center of discussions for months,” says the post in Portuguese. “Now, anticipation continues to grow for one of the most awaited international productions inspired by events that marked Brazil.”


Um trailer que circulou na internet foi suficiente para colocar The Dark Horse no centro das discussões por meses.

Agora, a expectativa continua crescendo para uma das produções internacionais mais aguardadas inspiradas em acontecimentos que marcaram o Brasil.


#DarkHorse


pic.twitter.com/3y6E422qpL

— GO UP ENTERTAINMENT (@GOUPEntertainme)

June 16, 2026


That September 11 date went by and the movie, which was shot in English, has yet to be released in Brazil; it won’t come out before the first round in a nail-biting presidential race set for Sunday, October 4. These federal elections, which include congressional and gubernatorial  races alongside the presidential contest, have been dogged by accusations of meddling by the Trump administration, prompting incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to send a clear message to the US leader: “Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard.” While Dark Horse has not featured as a centerpiece in that conversation, it has certainly had its own share of controversy even before hitting the big screen.


The Brazil-US joint production has become the subject of an ongoing investigation that has sent shockwaves through the presidential campaign of one of the main candidates in a high-stakes, knife-edge election. Brazilian authorities are actively looking into the financing of the movie by a now-disgraced businessman accused of leading one of the biggest bank frauds in the country’s history. That financial scandal involves banker Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of the liquidated Banco Master, who is jailed for alleged fraud in a complex billion-dollar scheme involving worthless credit portfolios. The imbroglio has rocked the 214-million-people nation and thrown the Brazilian Supreme Court into an unprecedented institutional crisis, ensnaring justices, including Alexandre de Moraes—a polarizing figure credited by some with having stopped Bolsonaro’s coup plot and vilified by others for judicial overreach—and high-profile politicians and public officials with alleged ties to Vorcaro.


Among them is Brazilian senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who is cited in the

investigation

 by Brazil’s federal police into the financing of the movie for “possible participation” in alleged crimes involving “money laundering, illicit capital flight, corruption, and other related offenses.” Last May, the

Intercept

 Brasil

exposed

 audio recordings and

messages

 exchanged between Flávio and Vorcaro in which the senator

asks

 the banker for money to fund

Dark Horse

. Documents from the federal police indicate Flávio was a “direct interlocutor” in negotiating with Vorcaro

about the financing of the movie production. 


The bombshell reporting revealed that Flávio, the primary opponent facing off against President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva …

title: « Renouveau lycéen » : décryptage d'une escroquerie médiatique
content:
Les médias sponsorisent un faux lycéen mais un vrai communicant macroniste pour tenter de casser le mouvement


Publié par Contre-Attaque :


Lecture


«Renouveau lycéen» : décryptage d'une escroquerie médiatique


par

B


https://contre-attaque.net/2026/10/03/renouveau-lyceen-decryptage-dune-escroquerie-mediatique/


Si vous regardez encore la télévision – ce qui est mauvais pour votre santé – vous n'avez pas pu le rater. Il est partout, sur toutes les chaînes de télévision depuis deux jours : Nathanaël Combary, présenté comme le « représentant des lycéens ». Il présente bien, il a un discours modéré, il cogne sur LFI mais pas sur le gouvernement… c'est le personnage idéal pour mettre en scène un « dialogue » entre les lycéens et le pouvoir. Pendant que, sur le terrain, la police massacre le mouvement.


Le 2 octobre, Nathanaël Combary était reçu par le Ministère de l'Éducation devant un parterre de caméras, et a déclaré : « On a maintenant une écoute et un dialogue qui a été restitué et renoué entre nous et le ministère ». Une réalité parallèle, « l'écoute » se faisant à coup de grenades dans la vraie vie. Il a ensuite fait le tour des plateaux des milliardaires, où tous les éditorialistes boomers, ceux qui justifient à longueur de journée les tirs de LBD sur des mineurs, le trouvent formidable.


Alors qui est ce nouveau chouchou des médias, ce « porte-parole » autoproclamé des lycéens ?


Déjà, Nathanaël Combary n'est pas lycéen. Il participe à la campagne électorale de Gabriel Attal. Il a été assistant parlementaire d'une députée macroniste. Et cerise sur le gâteau, il est actuellement employé de Minerva, agence de communication macroniste présidée par Louis Jublin, conseiller d'Attal.


Dès le nom de son « syndicat », on sent qu'il y a embrouille : « Renouveau lycéen ». Ça sonne comme « Renaissance », « Ensemble » et tout le marketing creux du macronisme. Sur Instagram, la page de cette organisation compte 1.500 abonnés, ses publications sont rares et le nombre de « likes » est famélique, alors qu'elle prétend exister depuis 2021. C'est un groupe totalement inconnu, sans militant, sans public : une coquille vide.


C'est pourtant à son dirigeant que les médias donnent la parole, plutôt qu'aux lycéens et lycéennes réprimées. Une pure production du système. À un militant et un communiquant du camp de ceux qui sont en train de mutiler des adolescent·es.


Sur LinkedIn, Nathanaël Combary se félicite de travailler pour l'entreprise Minerva, et affirme « accompagner des personnalités publiques, des entreprises et des dirigeants dans la construction de leur récit, leur image et leur stratégie d'influence ». Novlangue pour parler de propagande et de lobbyisme en faveur des puissants.


Sans surprise, Nathanaël a effectué son stage d'assistant parlementaire chez la députée macroniste Julie Delpech il y a quelques mois seulement… Un « représentant lycéen » qui n'est donc ni représentant ni lycéen sillonne les plateaux pour taper sur LFI et les « casseurs ».

title: Páginas de fofoca no Instagram enaltecem Derrite e Tebet às vésperas da votação
content:
O

Núcleo

 identificou páginas de fofoca de grande alcance no Instagram que fizeram publicações com texto semelhante e quase simultaneamente que enaltecem dois candidatos ao Senado por São Paulo, na noite deste sábado (3.out.2026), às vésperas da votação do primeiro turno. Nenhuma delas sinaliza se o conteúdo se deu mediante publicidade.


Por que isso importa?


O Tribunal Superior Eleitoral proíbe, desde 48h antes até 24h depois da eleição, a circulação paga ou impulsionada de propaganda eleitoral na internet, mesmo se a contratação tiver sido realizada antes desse prazo. Campanha velada, sem sinalização, pode configurar crime eleitoral.


No caso do deputado federal Guilherme Derrite (PL-SP), foram 18 perfis que postaram que o candidato defende que facções criminosas sejam enquadradas como organizações terroristas. Em quatro páginas (@alfinetei, @acerteinoticias, @portalfoquei e @kimfofoca), tanto a legenda quanto a imagem eram as mesmas: “LINHA DURA CONTRA O CRIME! Derrite defende classificar facções criminosas como organizações terroristas”.


Reprodução de post na página @alfinetei, de 3.out.2026, curtida por Derrite e posteriormente apagada


A página com maior número de seguidores que veiculou o post foi a @alfinetei. A publicação teve, inclusive, curtida do perfil oficial de Derrite.

À reportagem, a assessoria de Derrite disse que “a campanha não tem nenhum envolvimento ou investimento nesses canais de comunicação”. Coincidentemente, após contatarmos a campanha, a publicação na página @alfinetei foi excluída. Os posts feitos por @diferentona, @asatualidades e @odiariobrasileiro também foram apagados depois que a reportagem procurou as páginas.


No caso da ex-ministra Simone Tebet (PSB), 11 páginas repercutiram ontem, também quase simultaneamente, um corte de uma declaração dela sobre redução da maioridade penal que foi dada durante

debate

 de candidatos ao Senado na Band, em 9.set.2026.


Reprodução de post da página @fofocas, publicada em 3.out.2026


Ela afirmou ser favorável à medida a pessoas a partir de 16 anos que tenham cometido crimes graves. Duas delas também haviam feito publicações sobre Derrite (@sobrefavela e @noticiasexplicadas).

A assessoria de Tebet não respondeu ao contato da reportagem até a publicação.


Em dez.2025, parte dessas páginas também promoveu feitos da gestão do governador Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), que disputa a reeleição, conforme

reportagem

 da revista piauí, de 12.jan.2026. São elas: @fofocas, @rainhamatos e @vemebuscarhebe, da Agência Buzz, que pertence à Mynd; e @alfinetei.


Tanto a Secretaria de Comunicação do Estado de São Paulo quanto a agência que representa as páginas negaram à revista o pagamento para repercutir as ações do governo.


O

Núcleo

 buscou as páginas mencionadas pelos canais de comunicação disponíveis, como e-mail e mensagem direta pelo Instagram, mas não houve retorno até a publicação.

title: এসআরএফটিআই-তে হিন্দু জাগরণ মঞ্চের হামলা, শিক্ষার্থীদের শান্তিপূর্ণ প্রতিরোধ, প্রতিষ্ঠানে শুরু ছাত্র ধর্মঘট
content:
সত্যজিৎ রায় ফিল্ম অ্যান্ড টেলিভিশন ইন্সটিটিউট-এ হামলা চালাল হিন্দু জাগরণ মঞ্চ। তারা এসেই গেট ভাঙার চেষ্টা শুরু করে এবং এক নাগাড়ে পাথর, ইঁট, বোতল ইত্যাদি ছুঁড়তে শুরু করে। টানা প্রায় দু’ঘন্টা তারা একটানা এই ঘটনা ঘটিয়ে চলে।


 


সুদর্শনা চক্রবর্তীর

 প্রতিবেদন


 


সত্যজিৎ রায় ফিল্ম অ্যান্ড টেলিভিশন ইন্সটিটিউট-এ হামলা চালাল হিন্দু জাগরণ মঞ্চ। ৪ অক্টোবর, রবিবার তারা বিকেল চারটের কাছাকাছি সময়ে মিছিল করে এস আর এফ টি আই-এর  মূল গেট-এর সামনে পৌঁছায় ও সঙ্গে সঙ্গেই হিংসাত্মক কার্যকলাপ শুরু করে। টানা দু’ঘন্টা তারা গেট-এর সামনে যথেচ্ছ হিংসা সংঘটিত করে।


 


এস আর এফ টি আই-এর ছাত্র ইউনিয়ন-এর সভাপতি ব্লসম হাজারিকা এদিনের আক্রমণ বিষয়ে জানান, তাঁরা আগেই যেহেতু এই মিছিল ও জমায়েতের খবর পেয়েছিলেন ও পোস্টার ইত্যাদিও দেখেছিলেন, তাই পুলিস প্রশাসনকে চিঠি দিয়ে আগে থেকেই জানিয়ে রেখেছিলেন, তাঁদের নিরাপত্তা সুনিশ্চিত করার জন্য। প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃপক্ষ তাঁদের শান্তি বজায় রাখতে বলেছিলেন এবং ক্যাম্পাসে থাকা সব শিক্ষার্থীরাই সেই পরামর্শ মেনেই ছিলেন।


 


“আমরা সবাই গেটের ভেতরে অনেকটা দূরে দাঁড়িয়ে ছিলাম। গান গাইছিলাম। তারমধ্যেই স্লোগান শুনতে পাই যে ওরা আসচে। আমরা তখন জোট বেঁধে দাঁড়িয়ে ছিলাম গেটের থেকে অনেকটা ভেতরে। ওরা এসেই গেট ভাঙার চেষ্টা শুরু করে এবং এক নাগাড়ে পাথর, ইঁট, বোতল ইত্যাদি ছুঁড়তে শুরু করে। টানা প্রায় দু’ঘন্টা তারা একটানা এই ঘটনা ঘটিয়ে চলে। আমরা কোনো রকম উসকানিতে পা দিইনি। গেট থেকে অনেক দূরে দাঁড়িয়ে আমরা গান গেয়েছি।”

October 4, 2026


 


আক্রমণকারীদের মুখে ছিল “জয় শ্রী রাম”, ” দেশ কে গদ্দারো কো/গোলি মারো শালো কো” আর পাকিস্তান বিরোধী স্লোগান। বিপরীতে পড়ূয়ারা জয় ভীম, ইনকিলাব জিন্দাবাদ স্লোগান দিয়েছেন শান্তিপূর্ণভাবে। এক সময়ে যখন তাঁরা ‘জনগণমন’ গাইতে শুরু করেন, এমনকি তখনোও লাগাতার পাথর ছোঁড়া চালিয়ে যায় আক্রমণকারীরা। গেট-এ ঝোলানো মহাত্মা গান্ধী ও বাবাসাহেব ভীমরাও আম্বেদকর-এর ছবি ছিঁড়ে ফেলে তারা।


 


“দু’জন ছাত্র মাথায় চোট পায়, তাঁদের হাসলাতালে নিয়ে যেতে হয়েছে। তারজন্যও অনেক ক্ষণ অপেক্ষা করতে হয়েছে। ৬.৩০-র আগে তা সম্ভব হয়নি। আরো অনেকেই দুষ্কৃতিদের ছোঁড়া পাথর, বোতলে আঘাত পেয়েছেন। আহত হয়েছেন উপস্থিত থাকা অধ্যাপকদের মধ্যে এক-দু’জনাও,” জানালেন ব্লসম।


 


প্রথমে ৫০-৬০ জন মিছিলকারী থাকলেও, পরে সেই সংখ্যা বেড়ে আনুমানিক ২০০ জন মতো হয়। গাড়ি নিয়ে এসে তার উপরে উঠে স্লোগান দেওয়া ও হামলা চালাতে থাকে তারা। গেটের সামনের দিকে ১৫-২০ জন পুলিসকে দেখতে পেয়েছিলেন ভেতরে থাকা পড়ুয়ারা। আগে থেকে চিঠি দেওয়া সত্ত্বেও কোনো রকম বাড়তি নিরাপত্তার ব্যবস্থা ছিল না। মূল গেট-এর সামনে জমায়েত ও হামলা আটকাতে কোনো ব্যারিকেড-ও করা হয়নি। দুষ্কৃতিদের একজন গেট টপকে ভেতরে ঢুকেও পড়েছিলেন, যদিও তিনি তারপর একইভাবে বেরিয়েও যান।


 


সন্ধ্যা ৬’টার পর, প্রায় ৬.৩০টার কাছাকাছি পুলিস কিছুটা সক্রিয় হয়ে আক্রমণকারীদের সরাতে শুরু করে ও তারা ধীরে ধীরে চলে যায়। এরপর পড়ুয়ারা উপাচার্যকে ঘেরাও করেন ও আলোচনার পর একটি দাবিপত্র দিয়ে ঘেরাও তুলে নেন।


 


যে দাবিগুলি তাঁরা রেখেছেন:-


 


১) ৪ অক্টোবর ২০২৬ যে ঘটনা ঘটেছে উপাচার্য ও রেজিস্ট্রারকে তার দায়স্বীকার করতে হবে


২) এস আর এফ টি আই-এর শিক্ষার্থীদের সঙ্গে যে হিংসাত্মক ঘটনা ঘটেছে তারজন্য ক্ষমা চাইতে হবে


৩) এই প্রতিষ্ঠানকে অতি দ্রুত সেই সংগঠনের নামে এফ আই আর করতে হবে, যারা এদিনের মিছিল ও পড়ুয়াদের উপর আক্রমণ সংঘটিত করেছে


৪) পুলিসের নির্দিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষকে দ্রুত চার্জশিট দায়ের করতে বলতে হবে


৫) অখিল ভারত জাগরণ পঞ্চায়েত ও হিন্দু জাগরণ মঞ্চের আক্রমণের নিন্দা জানিয়ে সাংবাদিক সম্মেলন করতে হবে


৬) উপাচার্য, রেজিস্ট্রার ও অ্যাডমিনিস্ট্রেটিভ অফিসার-এর ইস্তফা।


 


দাবিপূরণ না হওয়া পর্যন্ত তাঁরা প্রতিষ্ঠানের শিক্ষাচর্চা বন্ধ ও ধর্মঘট শুরু করলেন বলে উপাচার্যকে জানিয়েছেন।

title: Ya en la calle el nº 3 de Esporas
content:
Ya tenemos en la calle el número 3 de Esporas, revista libertaria de crítica de libros.

Esporas es una publicación periódica puesta en marcha por un grupo de editoriales libertarias del Estado español. No solo pretende ser un espacio para la crítica literaria, sino que aspira a convertirse en una herramienta colectiva para la recomendación de libros no viciada por el marketing de los grandes grupos editoriales; empresas que pueden permitirse regalar decenas de ejemplares a periodistas e influencers.

La revista se puede conseguir en las webs de algunas editoriales que impulsan el proyecto, como Calumnia y Piedra Papel Libros, y se puede descargar gratuitamente en la web del proyecto.

title: Journalist Nagihan Akarsel commemorated at her graveside
content:
Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineology Research Center and a journalist who was killed in an armed attack outside her home in Sulaymaniyah in the Kurdistan Region on October 4, 2022, was commemorated at her graveside in the village of Gölyazı in Konya’s Kulu district. The commemoration was attended by Akarsel’s mother and relatives, members of the Jineology Research Center, the Mesopotamia Women Journalists Association (MKG) and the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG), the Konya and Ankara provincial organizations of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), DEM Party Istanbul MP Özgül Saki, and many others.


The commemoration began with a short march from the home of Akarsel’s family to the cemetery, followed by a moment of silence at her graveside. Roses and daisies were placed on her grave, while participants chanted “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal) and “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî (Woman, Life, Freedom).


Saki: An attack on the philosophy of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’


Speaking after the moment of silence, DEM Party MP Özgül Saki described the attack as an attack on the philosophy of ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî,’ and said:


“They wanted to prevent Nagihan from conveying the truth to us by blending emotion and thought in the light of science. That struggle was undoubtedly continuing. In her writings, she said: ‘I am speaking to you from a geography where resistance is synonymous with life. Women’s methods of resistance are also their methods of survival.’


Her approach to life in all its dimensions, her struggle for freedom, her commitment to knowledge, and her work as a member of the free press made her extremely valuable to us. The perspective of struggle and philosophy of life that they left behind will illuminate our path.


We are going through a process. We speak of confronting the truth. The person who fired the bullet that killed Nagihan may have been arrested, but the mechanism behind it has still not been uncovered, and that responsibility remains with us. It is our responsibility to uncover the truth about Nagihan, Nazım Daştan, Cihan Bilgin, the media workers who were killed, and our comrades who lost their lives in the struggle for freedom. We will continue to fight for this.”


‘Their words will not be left unfinished’


MKG member and journalist Diren Yurtsever emphasized that the pens of Nagihan Akarsel and other journalists who lost their lives would not be left behind.


“She waged a long-standing struggle for truth, both through her work in journalism and in the women’s freedom struggle. We will continue along the path opened for us by Nagihan and the other journalists we have lost, striving to be worthy of them. Neither Nagihan’s pen nor those of the other journalists we have lost will be left behind. Their words will not be left unfinished. Our responsibility is to be worthy of them. Şehîd namirin,” Yurtsever said.


‘In Sulaymaniyah, each of Nagihan’s ideas fell to the earth and became a seed’


Reyhan Yıldırımcı, whom Nagihan Akarsel referred to as her “spiritual family,” also spoke at the commemoration.


“The ancient land of Gölyazı does not hold an ordinary death within it. Nagihan was a journalist and writer who, with her head held high and without fear, reached the essence of truth. In my heart, she was like a daughter to me; she was my comrade. We shared life together. In Sulaymaniyah, each of Nagihan’s ideas fell to the earth. Every idea that fell to the earth became a seed in the minds of many women. Those seeds enabled women to reconnect with themselves,” Yıldırımcı said.


The commemoration concluded following the speeches.


Nagihan Akarsel


Nagihan Akarsel (Zîlan) was born in 1976 in the Kurdish village of Gölyazı (kr: Xelîkan) in Cihanbeyli district of Konya province in central Turkey.


Between 2001 and 2007, she was imprisoned for her political activity at universities. After her release from prison, she worked as an editor and reporter at the Dicle News Agency between 2008 and 2014. During this period, she also followed the lectures of Hacettepe University Women’s Studies Department in order to deepen her understanding of women’s liberation. She took part in the establishment of the first women’s press agency, JINHA. For years, she worked as a reporter in the Kurdish press, chasing news. She was a hard worker, a teacher, a friend and comrade in the development of Kurdish women’s journalism.

title: Lawyer Demir: The Hacı Lokman Birlik case is a litmus test for the peace process
content:
Eleven years after the killing of Hacı Lokman Birlik in Şırnak and the subsequent desecration of his body, the police officers responsible have still not been held criminally accountable. Following a ruling by Turkey’s Constitutional Court, the public prosecutor’s office is now set to reinvestigate the case. The family’s lawyer, Ramazan Demir, calls for investigations into all officers involved—from those who fired the shots to those in the chain of command. At the same time, he views the case as a litmus test for the ongoing peace and democratic society process.


27-year-old actor Hacı Lokman Birlik, also known by his Kurdish name Siyabend, was killed on October 3, 2015, during military operations in Şırnak. The city was under curfew and besieged by police and military forces. Police officers subsequently tied his body to an armored vehicle and dragged it through the streets. Footage of the incident was circulated by members of the police themselves.


The autopsy report documented 28 gunshot wounds, 17 of which were classified as fatal. Witnesses reported that Birlik had been sitting by the roadside when shots were fired at him from a passing vehicle. The shooting allegedly continued even after he had stopped moving. Despite the footage, the circumstances of his death, and the family’s years-long demands for justice, no effective criminal investigation was carried out.


Birlik’s body tied to an armored vehicle


Prosecutor’s office ignored key investigative requests


After the public prosecutor’s office failed for years to conduct an effective investigation, the family’s lawyers applied to the Constitutional Court. In July, the court found a violation of the prohibition against treatment incompatible with human dignity and ordered that the case be returned to the Şırnak Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office for reinvestigation.


According to Demir, lawyers previously submitted specific investigative requests on numerous occasions. However, he said, the prosecutor’s office “persistently and repeatedly” ignored them. Instead of investigating the treatment of Birlik’s body and the officers involved, the authorities focused primarily on identifying which police officer had recorded the footage that later became public and who had shared it in a police WhatsApp group.


“The footage was important to us. From the insults and abusive language that could be heard in the recordings, we already knew the motivation of the police officers,” Demir said. Investigations into this aspect were also requested. However, for the lawyers, the main focus was what had been done to Birlik’s body.


“We submitted numerous requests to the prosecutor’s office regarding this. At some point, we realized that they were not interested in it at all.” The defense eventually explicitly informed the prosecutor’s office that it would apply to the Constitutional Court if there continued to be no indication of any willingness to conduct an effective investigation. No response was received.


Lawyer Ramazan Demir


‘All those involved must be included in the proceedings as suspects’


Despite its shortcomings, Demir described the Constitutional Court’s decision as an important and courageous step. He said the court had examined all of the lawyers’ requests and had also addressed the prosecutor’s dismissive and reluctant attitude. Particularly significant, he noted, was the court’s consideration of the extent of the psychological suffering inflicted on Birlik’s family by the inhumane treatment of his body. The court also sharply criticized the fact that the state officials involved had not even been questioned after his death and that no corresponding investigation had been conducted.


Following the decision, the prosecutor’s office must therefore reopen the case from the ground up. “All state officials involved in what happened—those who made or implemented decisions, those who pulled the trigger, and those who ensured that his body was transported and publicly displayed in this manner—must be included in the case file as suspects,” Demir said.


Confidentiality order imposed on an eleven-year-old case


Following the Constitutional Court’s decision, Demir traveled to Şırnak and met with the prosecutor’s office handling the case. However, when he and the other lawyers representing the family sought access to the investigation file, they learned that a confidentiality order had been imposed. Demir described the decision as completely incomprehensible …

title: Journalist Ferda Çetin spoke about Peace and Democratic Society Process in Giessen
content:
A public meeting was held in Giessen as part of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference. The meeting was attended by journalist and politician Ferda Çetin, who discussed with participants the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the steps taken so far, and developments expected in the coming period.


In his remarks, Çetin said the Call for Peace and a Democratic Society issued by Kurdish people's leader Abdullah Öcalan on February 27 had opened the door to a new political period. He said the call had two central dimensions: bringing wars and conflicts to an end through dialogue and negotiations, and building a democratic society.


Çetin emphasized that lasting peace could only be achieved if people were actively involved in the process and had a meaningful role in shaping it. He also underlined the importance of broad social participation in the construction of a democratic society.


‘Baseless claims are being systematically circulated’


Participants at the meeting raised concerns about the spread of what they described as baseless claims on social media platforms including Facebook, YouTube and TikTok. They said misleading narratives targeting Abdullah Öcalan, the Freedom Movement and the peace process were being deliberately and systematically circulated with the aim of undermining the process.


Following Çetin’s presentation, the meeting continued with a question-and-answer session. Participants raised questions on a range of issues, including the peace process, democratic politics, political prisoners, the women’s movement and developments across the region.

title: PYD: Cutting Kurdish language classes restricts the right to education
content:
The Democratic Union Party (PYD) has criticized the decision by the Damascus interim government to reduce Kurdish-language classes to three lessons per week, saying the move restricts the Kurdish people’s right to education in their mother tongue.


Party members Ahmed Suleiman and Beritan Najim read the statement in both Arabic and Kurdish outside the party’s office in Derbesiyê.


The statement rejected the decision by the Education Ministry of the interim government to reduce Kurdish-language classes to three lessons per week, arguing that the measure was incompatible with the requirements of Syria’s linguistic and cultural diversity.


The PYD called for the decision to reduce Kurdish-language classes to be reversed and for an education system to be implemented that guarantees students the right to learn their mother tongue without restrictions or discrimination.


The party also called on democratic forces, civil society organizations and human rights groups to support these demands.

 ΣΤΟ ΣΥΝΕΔΡΙΑΚΟ ΚΕΝΤΡΟ ΣΤΗΝ ΕΚΔΗΛΩΣΗ ΠΑΡΟΥΣΙΑΣΗΣ ΤΟΥ ΠΡΟΓΡΑΜΜΑΤΟΣ


Σε πλήρη σύμπλευση με τα σχέδια κράτους και κεφάλαιου για σταδιακή ιδιωτικοποίηση της εκπαίδευσης, στην Ιατρική Πατρών πρόκειται να λειτουργήσει από φέτος ξενόγλωσσο προπτυχιακό τμήμα με δίδακτρα που ανερχονται στα 12.000€ ανά έτος, ύστερα από την έγκριση-ευλογίες που έλαβε από τη Σύγκλητο του Πανεπιστημίου Πατρών. Μάλιστα την Δευτέρα 5.10 θα πραγματοποιηθεί εκδήλωση στην οποία θα παρουσιαστεί το πρόγραμμα,που βάσει του πανεπιστημίου, οδηγεί σε μια «νέα εποχή διεθνοποίησης για την Ιατρική». Η κίνηση αυτή δεν έρχεται σαν κεραυνό εν αιθρία, καθώς συμβαδίζει πλήρως με την ολοένα και εντεινόμενη εκπαιδευτική αναδιάρθρωση που συντελείται τα τελευταία χρόνια, από την κατάργηση του ασύλου, την είσοδο των μπάτσων στις σχολές, τον νόμο Κεραμέως-Χρυσοχοϊδη και όλων των αντιεκπαιδευτικών διατάξεων που θεσπίζονται ανά τα χρόνια, μέχρι και τον πρόσφατο νόμο Πιερρακάκη που ανοίγει διάπλατα των δρόμο για την ίδρυση ιδιωτικών πανεπιστημίων. Όλα αυτά σε συνδυασμό με την πλήρη υποβάθμιση των παροχών φοιτητικής μέριμνας, την όξυνση των ταξικών φραγμών και γενικά την καθημερινή βία της ακρίβειας, με τις ανατιμήσεις των προϊόντων, τις απλησίαστες τιμές στα σούπερ μάρκετ, την αύξηση των λογαριασμών και των ενοικίων, έχουν ως επακόλουθο μόνο το φετινό έτος, από τους 4.881 επιτυχόντες, οι 266 να μην ενεγράφησαν με 350 να μην έκαναν ούτε την αρχική δήλωση.


Οι δήθεν εξαγγελίες για αύξηση της «εξωστρέφειας», της «ουσιαστικής αναβάθμισης» του δημοσίου πανεπιστημίου μέσω της ίδρυσης επί πληρωμής προγραμμάτων σπουδών μόνο προσχηματικά μπορούν να λειτουργήσουν καθώς η πραγματικότητα είναι πολύ διαφορετική. Δεν είναι τυχαίο άλλωστε που χρονικά έρχονται να συμπέσουν με τη συνεχόμενη προσπάθεια από πλευράς κράτους να προωθήσει την ίδρυση ιδιωτικών ΑΕΙ, την ολική αναδιάρθρωση της πανεπιστημιακής πραγματικότητας, εις βάρος της δημόσιας εκπαίδευσης και των φοιτητών που δεν μπορούν να ανταπεξέλθουν στο αυξανόμενο κόστος φοίτησης το οποίο συνεχώς και μετακυλίεται στις πλάτες μας.


Λίγα λόγια όμως για τον τρόπο με τον οποίο τα ξενόγλωσσα αυτά προγράμματα λειτουργούν. Ήδη βλέπουμε να αξιοποιούν τους ίδιους δημόσιους διδακτικούς χώρους- αν όχι να τους καταλαμβάνουν πλήρως, όπως χαρακτηριστικά γίνεται στην Ιατρική του ΑΠΘ, με τους φοιτητές του δημοσίου προγράμματος να εκτοπίζονται στο νοσοκομειακό αμφιθέατρο κάτω από άθλιες και επικίνδυνες συνθήκες, ενώ το πρόσφατα ανακαινισμένο αμφιθέατρο της Ιατρικής να παραδίδεται αμέσως μετά τα εγκαίνια στους φοιτητές του ξενόγλωσσου προγράμματος. Στην Ιατρική του ΕΚΠΑ ενώ οι δημόσιες υποδομές αφήνονται στο έλεος τους, πραγματοποιήθηκαν κρυφά εγκαίνια αμφιθεάτρου για το επι πληρωμή προπτυχιακό, ενώ είχε επιχειρηθεί η κατάληψη αίθουσας της Νοσηλευτικής που ύστερα από κινητοποιήσεις αποφεύχθηκε. Μια αντίστοιχη πραγματικότητα αναμένεται να αντικρίσουμε και στην Ιατρική της Πάτρας με ιδιαίτερη έμφαση στο κομμάτι της κλινικής άσκησης, η οποία θα γίνεται παράλληλα και για τα 2 προπτυχιακά προγράμματα. Τη στιγμή που η πόλη διαθέτει ένα μόνο πανεπιστημιακό νοσοκομείο, οι ήδη υπέρογκες από φοιτητές ομάδες κλινικών, θα απαρτίζονται από ακόμα περισσότερους φοιτητές, εντείνοντας την ήδη ασφυκτική κατάσταση που επικρατεί στο νοσοκομείο, δυσχεραίνοντας ακόμα περισσότερο την εκπαίδευση αλλά και …

author: Unknown
title: Diecimila in marcia da Sant’Ambrogio ad Avigliana
content:
Ci sono giornate in cui una valle intera decide di mostrarsi per quello che è.

Ieri è successo tra Sant’Ambrogio e Avigliana. Un numero enorme di persone ha percorso insieme la Valsusa, in una marcia popolare che ha attraversato i due paesi portando in strada una cosa che forse è ancora più importante del numero dei partecipanti: la capacità di una Valle di riconoscersi, ancora una volta, nella difesa del proprio territorio.


Da Notav Info


Diecimila persone sono tante, ma a raccontare questa giornata sono soprattutto i volti e la composizione del corteo.

C’erano gli amministratori locali e d’oltralpe e le famiglie, i comitati e le realtà che compongono il Movimento No Tav, persone che questa battaglia la portano avanti da decenni e giovani che hanno scelto di raccoglierne il testimone. C’erano i comitati No Tav francesi, i movimenti legati alla Palestina e chi da anni si batte per la difesa dei territori. C’era una valle intera che ieri ha deciso di camminare nella stessa direzione con la determinazione e l’entusiamo che da sempre accompagnano le giornate di mobilitazione popolare valsusina.


La ragione della marcia era precisa: fermare l’Avigliana-Orbassano. Un nuovo progetto che si inserisce nel quadro più ampio della Torino-Lione e che arriva all’interno di un territorio che da più di trent’anni è obbligato a sentire l’ormai stantio racconto che le grandi opere sono necessarie, inevitabili, strategiche ed indispensabili. Tutto questo mentre sul territorio rimangono aperti temi molto più concreti che attraversano tutti gli aspetti della vita quotidiana: a partire dal caro vita, la sanità sempre più inaccessibile arrivando poi alla mobilità, con il costo sempre più alto del carburante e gli scarsi investimenti nel trasporto pubblico locale. Il tema che porta con sé l’apertura di questi nuovo progetto non è semplicemente costruire nuove infrastrutture, ma decidere quali trasporti servono davvero a chi vive questo territorio e dove devono essere investite le risorse pubbliche. Ieri, insieme alla critica alla tratta Avigliana-Orbassano, è tornata quindi anche la richiesta di investire nel trasporto pubblico e nella metropolitana, invece di continuare a concentrare risorse su opere pensate secondo una logica diversa da quella dei bisogni quotidiani di chi abita la Valle e l’area metropolitana.


I tanti interventi hanno infatti poi anche allargato il ragionamento anche alle altre emergenze che attraversano il territorio e l’intero Paese: la sanità pubblica, le scuole, i servizi, il trasporto per studenti e pendolari, la crisi climatica e la necessità di prendersi cura dei territori invece di consumarli.

È anche su questo terreno che l’Avigliana-Orbassano diventa parte di una discussione più ampia sulle priorità e sul modello di sviluppo.

Sono passati governi, ministri, presidenti di Regione. Sono cambiate le parole utilizzate per imporre la Torino-Lione e il modello che in cui si inserisce e sono cambiate le motivazioni con cui se ne è sostenuta la necessità.

Quello che invece non è mutata è la voglia di chi abita questo territorio, di organizzarsi per difenderlo.

La manifestazione di ieri è il risultato di una storia lunga, nella quale si è costruita una capacità collettiva fatta di resistenza, organizzazione e mobilitazione, alimentata negli anni da migliaia di persone, esperienze e percorsi differenti.

È questa esperienza che ha permesso al Movimento No Tav di andare oltre la semplice opposizione a una singola opera e di costruire, insieme alla critica, un’idea diversa di territorio, di comunità e di futuro.

La giornata ha mostrato, ancora una volta, come la discussione non possa essere rinchiusa nei confini di una singola tratta ferroviaria.

Questa mobilitazione ha sottolineato la capacità di mettere insieme soggetti differenti: amministratori locali e Movimento No Tav, famiglie e giovani, comitati Valsusini e francesi, persone che partecipano da decenni alle mobilitazioni e una nuova generazione che prende parola e spazio.


Insieme a loro movimenti ambientalisti, realtà legate alla Palestina, esperienze di difesa del territorio come Bosco Ospizio.

Una molteplicità di percorsi che non ha bisogno di essere omologata per condividere prospettive e percorsi condivisi.

La presenza dei giovani è stata una delle immagini più forti della marcia. In una mobilitazione che affonda le proprie radici in più di trent’anni di storia, la loro presenza dice che questa non è una storia chiusa, né una battaglia …

author: Unknown
title: Data center: incontro pubblico a Pavia
content:
Sabato 26 settembre a Milano è nata ufficialmente la rete regionale dei comitati stop data center, che scenderà in piazza con una manifestazione a Milano il prossimo 10 ottobre.

Sul tema si terrà un incontro pubblico di approfondimento a Pavia, martedì 6 ottobre alle ore 21, presso la sala conferenze del Broletto.​ ​


Relatori saranno

Enrico Duranti, ambientalista e fondatore del Comitato Ciarlasco

 per la tutela del territorio, già intervistato da Infoaut:

Data center: bolla o nuova rivoluzione industriale?

Intervista al Comitato Ciarlasco per la Tutela del Territorio e

il fisico Sergio Manera, del comitato di Certosa

, che si è interessato in modo particolare del fenomeno delle isole di calore (approfondisci

qui: L’effetto isola di calore dei data center

) Infrastrutture materiali dell’intelligenza artificiale, questi centri stanno recentemente balzando alla cronaca locale e nazionale. Sono numerosi i progetti, a vari stadi di avanzamento, prevalentemente concentrati sul territorio lombardo. ​ Anche

la provincia di Pavia è interessata dal fenomeno: dalla proposta di ampliamento del campus Stack di Siziano, al cantiere Microsoft di Bornasco, passando per Certosa, dove è sorto uno dei primi comitati di cittadini contrari ai data center, e Garlasco, dove si è recentemente costituito un altro comitato.

 ​ Le cronache cittadine degli ultimissimi giorni, poi hanno riportato dell’esistenza di un progetto presentato a marzo agli uffici del settore urbanistica del Comune di Pavia, di cui l’Amministrazione per mesi non ha fatto pervenire nessuna notizia ai cittadini. Sino al 28 agosto risultava dal portale di Terna una richiesta di allaccio alla rete elettrica per un data center nel territorio comunale per 50 MW di potenza. Oggi ne risulta una per il triplo. Verosimilmente è stata avanzata dai proprietari dell’area dismessa ex Chatillon, alla periferia della città. Mentre sindaco, assessore all’ambiente e alcuni consiglieri comunali, dopo mesi di silenzio, assicurano che non autorizzeranno nessun progetto di data center in città, la capogruppo del PD, partito di maggioranza relativa in consiglio comunale, dichiara che «Pavia ha aree dismesse in cui la realizzazione di un data center potrebbe essere un volano di innovazione straordinario». Non resta che dire che, come in altri territori, toccherà ai cittadini pavesi informarsi, attivarsi e dare battaglia per preservare salute e territorio.​ ​

Nel corso dell’incontro verranno analizzati gli impatti ambientali, sanitari, energetici e sociali dei centri dati, ma si parlerà anche della situazione nazionale e di quella lombarda, dell’assenza di un piano strategico e della svendita dei territori alle Big tech americane. ​

author: Kieler Open Source und Linux Tage
title: Nie wieder Copy & Paste: Reporting mit Quarto [24. Kielux 2026]
content:
Ein Vortrag von Gerhard Nachtmann (Gerhard Nachtmann)


Manuelle Berichte und Präsentationen kosten Zeit, sind fehleranfällig und oft schwer nachvollziehbar. Mit Quarto gibt es eine Open-Source-Lösung, die Code, Daten, Analysen und Text vereint.


Der Vortrag zeigt, wie sich mit Quarto reproduzierbare Berichte und Präsentationen erstellen lassen, die ausführbaren Code (z. B. in R oder Python) enthalten und ihre Inhalte automatisch aus aktuellen Daten generieren. Zudem wird gezeigt, wie sich die Erstellung und Aktualisierung dieser Dokumente unter Linux automatisieren lässt.


Der Vortrag richtet sich an Entwickler, Data Scientists und Linux-Anwender, die Reporting und Präsentationserstellung als Code verstehen und wiederholbare Prozesse ohne Copy & Paste etablieren möchten.


Der Vortrag wurde auf den Kieler Open Source und Linux Tagen im Jahr 2026 gehalten.


Für Inhalt und Richtigkeit sind ausschließlich die jeweiligen Referenten verantwortlich.

title: Der Weg zur digitalen Unabhängigkeit mit BlossomOS [24. Kielux 2026]
content:
Ein Vortrag von Leonie Eleanor Ain (Blossom), Yannik Joel Ain (Blossom)


Diese Präsentation zeigt den Weg zur digitalen Unabhängigkeit mit BlossomOS, den aktuellen Entwicklungsstand und die nächsten Schritte. Sie fasst zusammen, was wir bisher geschafft und herausgefunden haben. Im Fokus stehen Datenschutz, Open Source, eine moderne UI/UX und ein konsequent einfaches Nutzungserlebnis mit einem Klick. BlossomOS ist für private Nutzer, Unternehmen und Behörden gedacht und zielt darauf ab, mehr Kontrolle über Daten und digitale Infrastruktur zu ermöglichen.

author: Kieler Open Source und Linux Tage
title: EGroupware - Was mit KI... [24. Kielux 2026]
content:
Ein Vortrag von Stefan Unverricht (

EGroupware.org

)


Auch EGroupware macht etwas mit KI... Aber eben digital souverän (so weit wie man das möchte).


EGroupware integriert KI-Funktionen in seine Anwendungen und stellt Anwender damit entsprechende Werkzeuge zur Verfügung. Dies ermöglicht eine höhere Produktivität und gewisse Automatisierung.


Umfangreiche Konfigurationsmöglichkeiten geben Administratoren die Kontrolle und ermöglichen es, Anwendern mithilfe geschickter Prompts Werkzeuge zur Verfügung zu stellen, ohne dass diese Prompt-Experten sein müssen.


Durch die Integration von Open WebUI, die Anbindung per API an EGroupware für die Automation und die Möglichkeit, eigene LMM anzubinden, kann man den Anwendern ein System anbieten, das man unter Kontrolle hat. Digitale Souveränität eben.


Dieses gesamte Thema wird vermutlich noch längere Zeit WIP sein. Jedoch stehen bereits jetzt viele wesentliche Funktionen bereit.


Es liegt noch ein gewisses Stück Lernkurve vor uns: für uns als Entwickler von EGroupware, für Admins und insbesondere für die Anwender.


Der Vortrag gibt einen Überblick über den aktuellen Stand.


Im Anschluss gibt es eine QA-Runde und gerne auch einen Austausch zu sinnvollen Funktionen für Anwender.


Der Vortrag wurde auf den Kieler Open Source und Linux Tagen im Jahr 2026 gehalten.


Für Inhalt und Richtigkeit sind ausschließlich die jeweiligen Referenten verantwortlich.

author: gavroche
title: XX Congreso CGT: Miguel Fadrique revalida la Secretaría General, pero Nuria Negro obtiene el apoyo de más sindicatos
content:
De

Sindicalismo.org


El XX Congreso Confederal de CGT termina con una organización prácticamente dividida en dos. Miguel Fadrique consigue 689 votos frente a los 639 de Nuria Negro, pero la candidatura alternativa recibe el respaldo de 90 sindicatos frente a los 84 del secretario general reelegido. El resultado llega después del fuerte rechazo que recibió la gestión del Secretariado Permanente saliente durante el propio Congreso.


Victoria por apenas 50 votos


Miguel Fadrique Sanz continuará al frente de CGT después de imponerse en una de las votaciones más ajustadas del XX Congreso Confederal. Fadrique obtuvo

689 votos

, mientras que Nuria Isabel Negro Blanco alcanzó

639

. Solo 50 votos separaron a las dos candidaturas. Sobre un total de 1.328 votos repartidos entre ambas opciones, Fadrique consiguió aproximadamente el 51,9 % y Negro el 48,1 %. Una diferencia de apenas 3,8 puntos que deja lejos cualquier imagen de una mayoría incontestable.


Pero el resultado contiene otro dato especialmente significativo. Los 689 votos de Fadrique procedieron de

84 sindicatos

, mientras que los 639 de Negro correspondieron a

90 sindicatos

. El secretario general gana, por tanto, en número de votos, mientras que su alternativa consigue el respaldo de

seis sindicatos más

. La explicación está en el sistema de representación congresual, en el que los sindicatos no disponen necesariamente del mismo número de votos y su peso depende de la representación que les corresponde.


Fadrique gana en votos; Negro, en número de sindicatos


La diferencia permite dos lecturas que no son contradictorias. Miguel Fadrique gana legítimamente la votación y renueva la Secretaría General, pero Nuria Negro consigue extender su candidatura entre un número mayor de sindicatos.

689 frente a 639 votos y 84 frente a 90 sindicatos

 muestran dos bloques con un peso muy parecido dentro de la organización.


El dato resulta todavía más relevante porque la votación no se produce en un Congreso tranquilo. CGT llegó a Parla con fuertes debates internos acumulados durante los últimos años y las diferencias quedaron expuestas desde las primeras sesiones. La candidatura de Negro representaba precisamente una alternativa a la continuidad del Secretariado encabezado por Fadrique.


La reelección llega después del rechazo a su gestión


El resultado debe leerse también junto a lo ocurrido el día anterior. Como informó Sindicalismo.org, la gestión del Secretariado Permanente saliente encabezado por Miguel Fadrique recibió un

fuerte rechazo durante el XX Congreso

. Una parte importante de las delegaciones cuestionó la gestión realizada durante los últimos cuatro años, dejando una situación poco habitual: el secretario general consigue posteriormente renovar su mandato, pero lo hace después de que su etapa anterior haya recibido una contestación considerable dentro del propio Congreso.


Son, en cualquier caso, dos votaciones diferentes. Una valoraba la gestión desarrollada por el Secretariado Permanente durante el mandato que terminaba y otra decidía quién debía dirigir la organización durante los próximos cuatro años. Confundir ambas sería incorrecto, pero políticamente resulta imposible analizarlas como si no tuvieran relación. La combinación de ambos resultados muestra una organización donde existe un cuestionamiento importante de la dirección saliente y, al mismo tiempo, una mayoría suficiente para que Fadrique continúe.


Un Congreso marcado por las acreditaciones y las críticas internas


Las tensiones tampoco se limitaron a las votaciones. Durante el Congreso diferentes delegaciones denunciaron problemas relacionados con las

acreditaciones, el acceso al plenario y los turnos de palabra

. Según fuentes de los sindicatos afectados, algunas delegaciones inicialmente excluidas consiguieron finalmente entrar, aunque continuaron las críticas sobre el procedimiento seguido y las posibilidades de intervención de determinados sindicatos.


Estas denuncias proceden de los sectores afectados y críticos con la organización del Congreso y deben diferenciarse de los resultados oficiales de las votaciones. Sin embargo, forman parte del contexto en el que se produjo la elección del nuevo Secretariado y ayudan a explicar el elevado nivel de enfrentamiento vivido durante las sesiones.

author: anred
title: Juicio por el transfemicidio de Azul Semeñenko: una vida atravesada por el odio a la identidad
content:
El juicio por el transfemicidio de Azul Mía Natasha Semeñenko comenzó en Neuquén mientras afuera del tribunal permanecía una pregunta que excede la responsabilidad penal de un acusado: ¿qué significa vivir siendo una mujer trans en una sociedad que todavía expone a esas vidas a la discriminación, la violencia y la precariedad? Por Manuela Wilhelm (ANRed).


 


Durante la primera jornada del juicio por jurados, la Fiscalía, la querella y la defensa presentaron sus teorías sobre lo ocurrido durante la madrugada del 25 de septiembre de 2025. Para las partes acusadoras,

Roberto Daniel Sánchez asesinó a Azul Semeñenko

 en un ataque de extrema violencia y la Fiscalía buscará acreditar un

homicidio triplemente agravado por ensañamiento, violencia de género y odio hacia su identidad de género

.


La defensa sostiene otra hipótesis: que la muerte ocurrió durante un episodio de violencia en el que Sánchez reaccionó bajo un estado de emoción violenta. Cabe destacar que el abogado contratado por el acusado, Ezequiel Leanza intentó pasar como prueba un “informe médico” que fue rechazado por el juez de garantias por considerarlo “inexistente” debido a que la mujer que lo firmaba tenía tres condenas por estafas en torno a un título trucho.


Gentileza


Además, el debate continuó con la prueba y el jurado popular escuchó a la primera testigo, Romina Millapán, hermana de Azul, quien reconstruyó una vida marcada por la violencia hacia su identidad que había comenzado mucho antes de aquella madrugada.


Azul Semeñenko fue discriminada y abusada en la infancia


Romina contó que Azul nació en Uruguay y que a los seis años llegó a Neuquén junto a su madre y sus hermanos. Según relató, desde pequeña manifestó que quería ser una niña. Sin embargo, comenzó la escuela con un nombre y una identidad que no eran los que reconocía como propios.


En la Escuela 61, recordó su hermana, era apartada y molestada porque prefería relacionarse con las niñas. Los insultos y las burlas continuaron durante la primaria y la secundaria. “Los compañeros consideraban que no era normal, que era un raro”, relató Romina ante el jurado.


La violencia tampoco quedó encerrada en las paredes de la escuela. Cuando Azul tenía alrededor de nueve o diez años, según el relato de su hermana, sufrió un abuso sexual dentro del hogar. Su madre lo denunció y el hombre que Romina señaló como responsable estuvo tres años preso. Sin embargo, posteriormente regresó a la familia y, según contó la testigo, continuó ejerciendo violencia y rechazando la identidad de Azul.“Mi mamá recuerda que si bien no lo volvió a tocar siempre le reprochó que no era su hijo y que en su familia no tenía un hijo maricón”, relató Romina.


Ese rechazo familiar se superponía con la violencia social. Durante su declaración, la hermana contó que Azul sufrió agresiones físicas y verbales en distintos momentos de su vida. En una ocasión, cuando había conseguido un trabajo nocturno en un puesto de panchos, un grupo de jóvenes la esperó a la salida, la golpeó, le rompió el teléfono y le fracturó un brazo.


“Yo me voy a matar porque soy un fracasado”


Uno de los momentos más duros del testimonio de Romina apareció cuando reconstruyó las consecuencias que tuvieron sobre Azul los años de discriminación, rechazo y dificultades para acceder a un trabajo.


Contó que cuando tenía 14 años encontró a Daniel —como todavía era llamada entonces— con una gillette en la mano y heridas en uno de sus brazos. Semanas después, atravesando nuevamente un período sin trabajo, le dijo que quería quitarse la vida.


“Yo me voy a matar porque soy un fracasado de mierda, nadie me quiere y nadie me va a dar una oportunidad. Yo me voy a tirar al río”, recordó Romina que le dijo.


La hermana lo siguió hasta el río y logró convencerlo de regresar a la casa. Una vez allí, Azul le pidió ayuda. “Ro, por favor ayudame porque yo así no puedo seguir. Necesito que me ayudes”, recordó.


Su madre buscó asistencia y, según el relato de Romina, comenzó un tratamiento psicológico que duró aproximadamente tres años. Después tuvo que interrumpirlo porque, al tratarse de atención en el sistema público, la falta de especialistas hizo imposible continuar.


Esos episodios fueron incorporados al juicio como parte de la historia de vida de Azul. La defensa cuestionó que se incluyeran hechos de su infancia y adolescencia que no estaban vinculados directamente con el homicidio. El juez Luciano Hermosilla, sin embargo, permitió que continuara el …

author: Clare Hymer
title: Greens Pass ‘Zionism Is Racism’ Motion at Party Conference
content:
Green party members have voted to back a motion stating that Zionism is racism, making the Greens the first explicitly anti-Zionist mainstream political party in the UK.


The motion, which was heard at the party’s largest ever conference in Brighton and passed by 1,022 votes to 813, also called on the party to back a single, democratic Palestinian state, to demand freedom for Palestinian political prisoners, oppose the Palestine Action ban and affirm Palestinians’ right to resistance. 


An amendment to mitigate the risk that the motion could be used to target Jewish members affiliated with Zionist institutions was voted down. Supporters claim it wasn’t necessary, as the motion already separates Judaism from Zionism, and it will have no disciplinary impact as it is a political policy motion rather than one to do with internal party procedures.


Gully, a Green party member whose father is Palestinian and whose mother is an Israeli Jew, told Novara Media: “Zionism is racism. It is a racist ideology… Look back at history. Look at the thinking behind Zionism and tell me it is not an ethnonationalist project.


“Every time you confuse Zionism with Judaism, you increase the risk that people think being Jewish means you support the ethnic cleansing and genocide, the checkpoints and the humiliation that my father and millions of Palestinians are subject to everyday.”


The vote followed a conference weekend in which the motion was a controversial issue, with tensions running high.


On Saturday, dozens of pro-Israel demonstraters shouted at party members as they entered the conference centre. Chants included “There is no Palestine, there is no Palestine”, with some protesters holding signs reading “Anti Zionism = terrorism” and handing out leaflets claiming “The Green party is now the most racist party in Britain”.


Senior Green figures were split on the motion. While co-deputy leader Mothin Ali spoke in favour of it on Sunday, former leader Caroline Lucas spoke against, with co-deputy leader Rachel Millward telling Sky News it was “problematic” earlier in the weekend. 


Green leader Zack Polanski did not vote, as he was campaigning in Holborn and St Pancras, central London, where he is standing in a byelection on Thursday in the hope of becoming the party’s sixth MP.


Green party policy already describes Israeli conduct as apartheid and genocide, backs a full arms embargo, sanctions and an end to occupation and illegal settlements, as well as a ban on the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) as a terror group.


Motions voted for by members at conferences set the Green party’s long-term vision and policy platform. They do not determine election manifestos.

author: Mohammed Altaj
title: Israel Above the Law … Palestine Beyond Justice
content:
The world did not lack knowledge of what was happening to Palestinians.

It knew that a people had been living under occupation for decades; that land was being confiscated, settlements expanding, homes demolished, and checkpoints cutting cities and villages off from one another.

The United Nations knew. Governments knew. Parliaments and international courts knew.

The shift now visible across significant parts of Western public opinion did not begin because the world suddenly discovered new facts about Palestine.

What changed was the distance between the news and the human being.

People saw what war means when a child is trapped beneath rubble, what displacement means when a family carries whatever it can and walks away without knowing where it will go.

And the numbers began to acquire names, faces and voices.

One of those names was Hind Rajab.

I do not mention Hind because her story encompasses everything that happened in Gaza. I mention her because some tragedies become windows through which people see what numbers alone cannot reveal.

Hind was trapped inside a car in Gaza in January 2024 after members of her family had been killed. She called for help. Twelve days later, she was found dead inside the car. The two paramedics sent to rescue her were also found dead.

But Hind was no longer a number.

The world also saw seven World Central Kitchen aid workers killed in Israeli strikes while carrying out humanitarian work. And even after the ceasefire announced in October 2025, the killing did not end. According to Palestinian Ministry of Health figures cited by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, by September 23, 2026, 1,402 Palestinians had been killed and 4,881 injured since the ceasefire announcement.

Bodies remained beneath the rubble, while families waited to reach loved ones not to save them this time, but to bury them.

But Palestinian history did not begin in Gaza.

And it did not begin on October 7, 2023.

In 1994, Baruch Goldstein, an Israeli settler and member of the Kach movement, opened fire on Muslim worshippers in the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron, killing at least twenty-nine people. In 2014, sixteen-year-old Mohammed Abu Khdeir was abducted from Shuafat, beaten and burned alive. A year later, the Dawabsheh family home in Duma was set on fire while the family slept; toddler Ali and later both his parents died.

So when a Palestinian is asked to begin the story on the morning of October 7, he is effectively being asked to erase what came before.

None of this makes the targeting of civilians acceptable, whoever they are.

Justice cannot begin halfway through history.

By September 14, 2026, the United Nations had documented more than 1,600 settler attacks resulting in Palestinian casualties, property damage, or both, across 275 Palestinian communities since the beginning of the year. More than 1,500 Palestinians had been displaced because of demolitions of structures lacking Israeli-issued permits, while more than 2,600 had been displaced in the context of settler violence and related access restrictions.

Between September 15 and 21 alone, the UN documented 51 settler attacks resulting in casualties, property damage, or both. At least 800 olive, fruit and palm trees were damaged, uprooted or burned. In the same week, demolitions displaced 147 Palestinians, including 73 children.

These are not isolated incidents.

This is land being transformed, communities disappearing, families being pushed out.

And this is where the phrase “extremist settlers” is no longer enough.

Who plans the settlements? Who allocates the land? Who builds the roads, extends the infrastructure and provides the protection?

At what point does settler violence cease to be merely the act of an individual and become a problem within the system itself?

In September 2026, UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that settlement expansion was accelerating, outposts were proliferating and settler violence was rising to alarming levels. He also warned that advancing the E1 settlement plan would deal a “deathblow” to the prospect of a contiguous and viable Palestinian state.

How, then, can the world continue to declare its support for a two-state solution while the geography on which one of those states is supposed to exist is being transformed?

The problem is not confined to land.

author: Novara Media
title: Trauma Farming: the New Politics of Public Suffering
content:
Are we in the era of trauma Top Trumps? ‘Lived Experience’ has become a byword for standpoint authority and progressive politics. It has allowed people from marginalised groups to speak and be heard, and forced us to confront how power plays out in interpersonal dynamics. But it has also become a way for people to brand themselves online, and excuse antisocial or even downright nasty behaviours. Has ‘lived experience’ helped the left, or turned us into self-obsessed therapy-speakers, incapable of communicating with the majority of people?


At the latest Downstream IRL, Ash Sarkar sat down with Catherine Liu – cultural theorist, professor and author of Virtue Hoarders – to discuss her new book, Traumatized: The New Politics of Public Suffering. Liu argues that as class politics has declined, the language of psychology has stepped in to explain problems rooted in capitalism. But what happens when trauma becomes content and politics gives way to what Liu calls the ‘gentrification of pain’? Is ‘lived experience’ a prerequisite for legitimate political analysis? Why do movements so often end up policing each other rather than confronting power? And if politics becomes about who’s hurting most, who benefits?

author: Paul Buhle
title: The Communitarian Mind of Michael Albert
content:
Somewhere, in the complex and often confused history of anarchist and communitarian movements of the US, Michael Albert resides, now almost 80, a veteran of endless campaigns but still eager to make his familiar points. Communitarianism of some kind can work, can create a substitute for the miserable economic arrangements of the present, and engage ordinary people in the process of changing themselves as they endeavor to change the world.

This sentiment has a more than honorable history even in the US, historically known for its weak and fragile Left institutions. Its origins should properly be placed well before the rise of the Marxist-related movements, mostly German immigrants, during the 1860s-70s. Indeed, the communitarian experiments of the 1820s-40s engaged some of the great figures of the age, from Shakers to Bohemians, and even produced a remarkable literature, including Nathaniel Hawthorne’s rather satirical Blithedale Romance.

The ideas of dress reform (mainly for women), healthy foods, and even freer sexual relations flowed into Abolitionist and Women’s Rights movements. The Civil War swallowed a large chunk of utopianism, but enough survived to prompt a rebirth in successive generations. Edward Bellamy’s best-selling novel, Looking Backward , published in 1887, seemed, by example, to make small-scale cooperative living imaginable, even if colonies nearly always failed in their first (under-capitalization and too few agricultural skills counted heavily). Hope is ever-born or perhaps never really goes away. Skinny-dipping and open curricula for children’s education, known in the 1910s, also found their way into the hippie mini-societies of the 1960s-70s.

It would be hard to say how deeply anarchist and communitarian ideas penetrated the “Counter Culture”—a phrase so dated and imprecise that we now set it off— but the sentiment was sincere and deep. “Share the Land” by the Canadian group Guess Who still resonates on YouTube with a confidence of “Brothers and Sisters Who Care” sharing valuables in common. It just didn’t work out in life.

To his credit, Michael Albert never gave up. Student activist, antiwar protester, launched South End Press in Boston of the 1970s, and the avowedly anarchist/libertarian Z Magazine in 1989. Thereafter, Albert and various collaborators, notably Robin Hahnel, worked out theories of alternatives to the market economy along lines that Prince Peter Kropotkin surely would have approved. At what might be called a literary highpoint, he published Parecon: Life After Capitalism (2003), a book translated into a couple dozen languages. Albert took his message to the world. The specifics of the furious debates over whether his proposal would work in practical economic terms, are now long past and largely forgotten—but the debate inevitably goes on. Beneath the specifics could be found a deeper plan, a vision based more on ethics than practical details.

And here we are twenty-some years later. And, no doubt, with the enriching personal experience of establishing, through an extended Z Media Institute, a world of training for the next generations of media and grassroots activists, now emphatically including podcasters, including Michael and the Z folks.

The conceit of this fat volume is that the Revolution has been successful, as related by an aged activist and SDS veteran to an oral historian. Like the most rigorous of oral histories, it encompasses a life story or rather a number of life stories. These mostly lack—according to me, an experienced oral historian and director of a couple of oral history programs—the deep family and community background that is most useful. But it emphatically includes details of the process of participation and learning, from a couple dozen imagined participants of widely different backgrounds, through lives of many struggles.

A little backstory from my end is useful. Oral history, the practical use of oral history, fell upon me in the 1970s as I realized that the vital living memories of the 1920s-40s Left—what they believed and what they did, far from the centers of Leftwing national leadership—were slipping away fast. The field had emerged around this time, more activist than academic, with some thousands of activists. Amongst these, the Oral History of the American Left archive (NYU), my veritable brain-child. And later more oral history on Rhode Island working people; still later teaching oral history for a decade at Brown.

I mention these …

author: Abe Walker
title: The Battle for the Soul of the UAW: Union Democracy and the Seductions of Power
content:
After years of struggling in relative obscurity, democratic socialists were jubilant to have elected one of their own to high-profile office. With bold rhetoric and meme-friendly soundbites, their candidate captured the hearts and minds of a working-class base eager for an alternative to the establishment’s caustic brand of demagoguery. Ignoring calls for moderation, the campaign took on a defiant, openly confrontational tone. Its outcome shocked the old guard, upended the status quo, and served as a warning to entrenched interests everywhere.

The year was 2023, and Shawn Fain had just won the presidency of the United Auto Workers union. Fain quickly became the public face of a resurgent workers movement that seemed poised to usher in a new wave of labor militancy. But there would be little time for celebration once the weight of the task ahead set in. Indeed – like a certain big city mayor – Fain would quickly discover that his election fight was only a preview of the battles to come.

Fain is now standing for reelection, with ballots set to be tallied next month. Three years ago, few could imagine that Fain would face a viable challenger as he eyed a second term. Yet today, his star has long since dimmed, and his fate now hangs in balance. The upcoming vote will serve as a referendum on his tenure, and while he remains the clear favorite, there is considerably less enthusiasm behind his current bid.

Fain’s dramatic rise and fall can only be understood in the context of the reform movement that propelled him to power. Fain traces his lineage to a long history of rank-and-file agitators who challenged the 74-year reign of the incumbent Administration Caucus from below. In the 1960s, the Revolutionary Union Movement organized Black militants to combat the union’s complicity in de facto factory segregation. In the 1980s, the New Directions caucus fought against the introduction of lean production and concessionary bargaining. These efforts scored some victories in local elections, but the possibility of taking power on a grand stage remained elusive. The established powers proved remarkably resilient, using their vast patronage network to absorb dissidents and marginalize challengers. Dissent was managed, co-opted, or crushed.

Meanwhile, union leaders embraced “jointness” and labor-management cooperation, seeking to align workers’ interests with corporate competitiveness. A series of concessions in the 2000s culminated in two-tier contracts that subjected new hires to substandard wages and reduced benefits, creating artificial hierarchies that fractured shop-floor solidarity. Givebacks at Detroit automakers were compounded by organizing challenges in the South, where the union failed to make inroads at the German and Japanese plants that were overtaking the sector. As membership plummeted, union officials oversaw a managed decline, presiding over plant closures and outsourcing. Insulated from rank-and-file agitation and accountable to no one, it was a short step from sweetheart deals and graft to outright corruption. The breaking point arrived in the late 2010s with the exposure of a scandal involving the misuse of union funds for personal expenses, and officials accepting bribes from the very auto executives they were supposed to bargain against. Two former presidents were sent to prison, and a federal monitor was appointed to oversee the union’s operations under a consent decree. But this legitimacy crisis came with a silver lining, shattering the old guard’s aura of invincibility and creating an opening for change.

Amidst the wreckage, a coalition of frustrated auto workers founded Unite All Workers for Democracy (UAWD). Drawing tactical inspiration and support from broader labor-left networks, including Labor Notes and the Democratic Socialists of America, UAWD presented democracy as an antidote to corruption. Through painstaking grassroots organizing (and an assist from the federal Monitor), UAWD successfully forced a referendum on direct elections in 2021, which passed with 63% of the vote.

After breaking the old guard’s monopoly on power, candidates had to tailor their messaging to appeal directly to the militant rank-and-file base. Shawn Fain ran on the strength of his populist, class-conscious rhetoric. He framed the election as an existential battle between the working class and the billionaire owners, while promising an end to concessionary bargaining and cozy labor-management partnerships.

Following …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Giorgio Agamben: A general demobilisation
content:
“The Worker” by Vladimir Serov, 1964


In 1932, Ernst Jünger published

Der Arbeiter

 [

The Worker

], a work in which this new figure of humanity pointed to the new world order. The centrality of work corresponds to the dominance of technology. Expanding on concepts he had expressed in his book of two years prior,

Total Mobilization

, Jünger writes: “Technology is the way in which the worker form mobilises the world.” This diagnosis, which revisited Marx’s analyses from an entirely different perspective, exerted considerable influence on both the right and the left of the political spectrum.


It is therefore all the more surprising that this decisive figure of the era has disappeared for some decades now. Technology continues to govern the world and has certainly increased its power everywhere, but it is no longer “the way in which the worker form mobilises the world.” On the contrary, in the form of artificial intelligence, it seems to imply rather the decline of the centrality of work that Jünger had in mind. Instead of the servitude linked to exploitation and mobilisation, technology, by progressively blurring the identities of social classes and estates, seems today to be heading towards an unprecedented form of subjugation through a kind of general demobilisation.


Quodlibet

, 01/10/2026

title: DFG publishes September report on rights violations against journalists
content:
The Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) released its “September Report on Rights Violations Against Journalists.” The report stated that, in September, access restrictions were at the forefront in terms of press and freedom of expression.


The report emphasized that access to social media accounts had been blocked and stated: “According to the September data, access to 3,492 digital media content was blocked on the internet and digital media sphere. In addition, access to 15 news reports was blocked, while 4 websites were shut down. In September, the accounts or websites of media outlets such as JINNEWS, Mezopotamya Agency, Evrensel, Kısa Dalga and T24 faced access restrictions and platform interventions. In addition, the personal X accounts of numerous journalists were made invisible in Turkey on grounds such as ‘the protection of national security and public order.’”


The DFG report also included the following points.


“In September, 15 journalists were detained, and 8 journalists were arrested. The homes of 4 journalists were raided, 3 journalists were threatened, journalists were prevented from covering the news in 5 incidents, and 2 journalists were subjected to ill-treatment. During the same period, investigations were launched against 2 journalists under freedom of thought and expression, while cases were filed against 10 journalists. There are 80 journalists involved in 25 ongoing cases. As of 4 October 2026, the number of jailed journalists is 29.


A significant portion of the interventions against journalists in September took place directly over the news reports they produced or their posts on digital media. Journalist Oya Lale Arslan was detained and arrested on the grounds of her digital media posts and YouTube broadcasts. Journalist Selahattin Günday was arrested over footage he reported on as part of the Kaşif Kozinoğlu investigation, and a second arrest warrant was subsequently issued against him. Journalist Tuğba Tekerek was arrested over a report she produced for Kaos GL, while Hüseyin Aykan, Editor-in-Chief of Bolu Gündem, was also arrested over a report he published.


In September, the interventions journalists encountered while covering the news also reached notable levels. In 5 incidents in September, journalists were prevented from covering the news, while 3 journalists were threatened and 2 journalists were subjected to ill-treatment.


One of the forms of attack faced by journalists was judicial pressure. Investigations were launched against 2 journalists in September, while investigations involving 10 journalists were turned into court cases. While the trials of 80 journalists in 25 cases are ongoing, ETHA reporter Züleyha Müldür was sentenced to 6 years and 3 months in prison.”


According to the report, 2 journalists were attacked, 1 journalist was targeted, the homes of 4 journalists were raided, 15 journalists were detained, 8 journalists were arrested, 2 journalists were subjected to ill-treatment, 3 journalists were threatened, 5 journalists were prevented from covering the news, and 1 journalist experienced rights violation in prison.


The report stated that investigations were launched against 2 journalists and cases were filed against 10 journalists; 2 journalists were sentenced to a total of 6 years, 5 months and 24 days; there were 25 ongoing journalist cases, 80 journalists were on trial, and the number of jailed journalists was 30 as of October 3.


The report stated that 10 journalists had lost their jobs and that RTÜK had imposed penalties on 14 broadcasts. It also emphasized that 4 websites had been shut down, access to 15 news reports had been blocked, and access to 3,492 social media posts had been restricted.

title: Geothermal plants and rising costs hit fig producers
content:
Fig producers in Yaykın neighbourhood in the Karacasu district of Aydın are struggling with high input costs and falling crop prices. Gülhanım Tarhan, one of the producers who spoke to ANKA News Agency, said they sorted their figs according to quality, yet the average selling price still failed to reach even 100 Turkish Lira (TL, around 1.81 euros) per kilogram. Tarhan said they were making a loss this season on figs they had sold for between 225 and 250 lira per kilogram last year, adding that their income no longer covered production costs.


Average selling price falls to 67–70 TL


Another fig producer, Yeliz Tüzyılmaz, provided details of this year’s market prices. First-grade figs are sold for around 120 TL per kilogram, second-grade figs for 60–70 TL, and third-grade figs, known among producers as “baby” figs, for around 50 TL.


Tüzyılmaz said that once all grades were taken into account, the average income per kilogram had fallen to between 67 and 70 TL. Last year, she said, first-grade figs sold for 210 TL per kilogram and second-grade figs for between 120 and 130 TL.


Twenty kilos of figs do not cover a day’s wage


Tüzyılmaz said producers were being squeezed by rising fertiliser, diesel and labor costs, while Tariş had still not announced a base price despite the season nearing its end. She said this had deepened uncertainty in the market.


Tüzyılmaz described fig production as an extremely demanding process, involving labor-intensive stages such as shaking the trees, harvesting the fruit, drying it in greenhouses, grading it and selecting the figs individually. She added that producers had to sell at least 20 kilograms of figs simply to cover the daily wage of one agricultural worker.


Producers face market pressures and geothermal plants


Aydın has been a centre of commercial fig production for thousands of years. Even the fig’s scientific name, Ficus carica, derives from Caria (Karya), the ancient name of the region.


Another problem affecting fig production in Aydın is geothermal power plants. Producers and local campaigners have linked geothermal operations to declining yields, while environmental and public health concerns associated with the plants have also intensified across the province.


An environmental impact assessment approving three new geothermal wells on land used for vegetable cultivation has been issued in the Germencik district of Aydın. Leaks and pipeline ruptures at geothermal facilities have brought agricultural production close to a standstill, while it has been reported that the cancer rate in the district has reached four times the national average.


Source: Yeni Yaşam


https://english.anf-news.com/news/economic-crisis-in-turkey-money-barely-covers-basic-necessities-at-the-market-87491
